typefaces.name: 00 Wagram
typefaces.desc: A serif typeface with a large x-height, whose cited influences are Plantin, Times New Roman and Georgia.

typefaces.name: 29LT Idris
typefaces.desc: 29LT Idris is a modern typeface that skillfully combines an Arabic Naskh calligraphic style with a Serif Latin. It offers two versions: Sharp and Flat, each with five weights, resulting in a total of ten styles. As a versatile visual communication tool, Idris provides two distinct typographic voices. Both versions can be used for display type, while the Flat version is recommended for body text. A contemporary Arabic Naskh, deeply rooted in calligraphic logic and inspired by a 1950s typeface, makes it an ideal publishing typeface. Its echoing Serif Latin gives the typeface a unique design approach and high legibility. Idris Sharp and Idris Flat share a common variable font with three axes: weight, contrast, and extension. The added extension axis allows users to adjust the width of Arabic cups and baseline elongation, placing an Arabic calligrapher’s tool in the hands of modern digital typesetters. It enables users to justify specific Arabic texts or find the exact width of desired words. It is a unique variable font tool, and it might be the first of its kind to be implemented to date. [ 29lt.com ] Links for this entry point to Idris Sharp.

typefaces.name: 36 Days of Type 2023
typefaces.desc: Created during the event of the same name, each letter in this font was inspired by a different album from thirty-six unique artists. It’s more type experiment than typeface with all the glyphs combining in an awkward mixture of clashing characters—similar to the note of a serial killer. The final family is cast of diverse glyphs. Some words work surprisingly well but most are a complete mess with zero cohesion. That’s just what happens you design a collection of beautiful letters instead of a beautiful collection of letters. The font doesn’t work because it was never meant to. I’m still waiting for someone brave enough to set their entire job resume in it. Any takers? [ tofutype.ca ]

typefaces.name: 8 Point Lining Typewriter No.1
typefaces.desc: This single style typeface is a digital interpretation of the 8 Point Lining Typewriter alphabet featured in the Barnhart Brothers & Spindler Typeface specimen, published in the US c. 1908. Unusual details, such as the flamboyant leg on the capital R; the pronounced curve of the lowercase t; the exaggerated overhang on the lowercase f; and the flourished numerals, give this typeface a distinct appearance, which is pleasing to the eye, especially when set in small point sizes. [ a2-type.co.uk ]

typefaces.name: A2 Standard Sans Cond. + X Cond.
Abisinia
typefaces.desc: A unicase poster font with extra Galician taste. It comes with some ligatures and alternates. [ rubenprol.gal ]

typefaces.name: Abitare Sans
typefaces.desc: Originally commissioned for the design & architecture magazine Abitare and based on CP Company .

typefaces.name: Absinthe [Black Foundry]
typefaces.desc: Absinthe is a typeface born from the Tavern, the creative and experimental wavy tool crafted by Gaëtan Baehr. This distinctive font draws its inspiration from the free-spirited, vibrant energy of the 1960s hippie era. Its design exudes a playful and fluid aesthetic, featuring rounded, dynamic shapes that feel both lively and indulgent. Absinthe dances across the layout with a whimsical rhythm, making it perfect for projects that embrace joy, nostalgia, and artistic expression. [ black-foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Acai
typefaces.desc: Released with Capitalics in 2025.

typefaces.name: Acceptera
typefaces.desc: Acceptera is a contemporary sans-serif typeface designed with a balance of functionality and restraint. Its clarity and ease of reading make it highly effective for text use, while its versatility ensures it suits a wide range of design purposes. Inspired by Swedish functionalism, the typeface reflects the modernist ideals that shaped early 20th-century Swedish architecture and design. The design draws heavily from the Swedish functionalist movement, particularly the modernist principles showcased at the groundbreaking 1930 Stockholm Exhibition. The name Acceptera is a nod to Acceptera!, the influential manifesto by Swedish architects Gunnar Asplund, Wolter Gahn, Sven Markelius, Eskil Sundahl, Uno Åhrén, and art historian Gregor Paulsson. The manifesto advocated for functionalism in architecture and design—an ethos echoed in the typeface’s clean, practical forms. Available in seven weights with matching italics. [ felicianotype.com ]

typefaces.name: Access
typefaces.desc: Access is a slightly squarish, wide bodied sans serif typeface. With a slight nod to Aldo Novarese’s immortal classic Eurostile, Access has a technical, functional and robust appearance. Access is divided into three different subfamilies defined by their width. Access has classic proportional widths. Access Granted has semi proportional widths, with some letters having more of a monospaced style to them. And Access Code is monospaced. [ playtype.com ] Announced in January 2025, while the foundry page dates the release in 2024. The proportional sub-family ( Access ) is used here for the sample image and links.

typefaces.name: Ace
typefaces.desc: Collegiate aesthetics, professional polish, and no need for NIL—Ace delivers a versatile superfamily in a familiar package. The serifed version of Ace includes seven widths, eight weights, and both upright and left- and right-leaning variants, ensuring a perfect fit and style for any team. This typeface doesn’t cut corners; instead of using caps in the lowercase set, it features thoughtfully crafted, proportionally accurate small caps for added versatility. [ positype.com ] Links on this page point to Ace , the regular-width member of the collection.

typefaces.name: Acme Gothic
typefaces.desc: Acme Gothic (2018) is based on the thick-and-thin gothic lettering style popular in the U.S. in the first half of the twentieth century. There have been typefaces in this genre before, but they were either too quirky (Globe Gothic), too English (Britannic), too Art Deco (Koloss), too modern (Radiant), or too Art Nouveau (Panache). None captures the plain, workman-like, vernacular style of Acme Gothic.

typefaces.name: Aconchego
typefaces.desc: If everything can be cozy, why not invite these good feelings into a typeface? Geometrically cozy encounters. Functionally relaxing forms. Flexible smooth characters. Essentially comfortable strokes. Contemporarily gentle letterforms. Ah, what a lovely thing. [ fabiohaagtype.com ]

typefaces.name: Aconit
typefaces.desc: Aconit is a contemporary sans serif font family that uniquely blends elements of tech and Art Nouveau. [ octotypo.com ]

typefaces.name: Action Grotesque
typefaces.desc: Action Grotesque is a variable-first, reading-first sans serif that continues Erik van Blokland’s exploration of type created in and for the environments where it is most likely to find itself today: screens. Instead of focusing on specific historical models or the conventions that have accumulated around sans serifs, Van Blokland let optics and proofing guide the development process, with the reader firmly at the center of his thinking. His working principle was that if he could ensure that text was readable at the smallest discernible sizes, the rest of the design would fall into place. Extra care was taken to make punctuation, numerals, and diacritics strong and unambiguous. With a large x-height, low contrast, and a generous weight range, Action Grot excels at handling complex, structured information at every size. [ commercialtype.com ]

typefaces.name: Activist
typefaces.desc: Activist is a functional display sans face with a minimalist esthetic. Its macho stance refers to the compressed rectangular forms of the early-20th-century jobbing types, with influences by contemporary license plate lettering. Activist packs a more assertive line than either of these models. This capital-only font is available in one weight based on the Formular font family. [ brownfox.org ]

typefaces.name: Acus
typefaces.desc: Acus typeface is inspired by the hand-painted enamel signs vernacular typography, popular in Poland between the 50’s and 80’s. High-contrast, condensed feel, and quirky details will serve perfectly as a display style. [ capitalics.wtf ]

typefaces.name: Adana
typefaces.desc: The roots of Adana Circular & Initials going back to the year 1930, to the Berlin-based German graphic designer Wilhelm Berg. His typeface can be interpreted as an answer to Lucian Bernhards Schönschrift and was published by Schriftguss A.G. Dresden. [ astype.de ]

typefaces.name: Adapter Mono PE
typefaces.desc: A monospaced type family with an editorial state of mind. It features a range of weights, strongly inclined italics with cursive alternates, and numerous stylistic sets to meet all your fixed-width letter needs.

typefaces.name: ADB Detach
typefaces.desc: ADB Detach is a serif display typeface with exaggerated transitions between strokes. We pushed this idea to such an extreme that the whole project turned into a set of expressive stencil typefaces for usage at large sizes. This typeface is available in regular and italic weights, each containing over 3000 glyphs divided across three scripts (Latin, Cyrillic and Greek). Among these glyphs is an extensive set of swashes easily controllable through eight stylistic sets, making ADB Detach a playground for expressive and dynamic headlines. Appears to be retired as of late 2025.

typefaces.name: ADB Farto
typefaces.desc: ADB Farto is a slab serif display typeface intended to apply in monumental sizes. Despite being only available in uppercase, ADB Farto contains almost 3000 glyphs divided into four scripts (Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, and Hebrew). Two stylistic sets transform the dense shapes into vertical elements, allowing text to set in a sort of Light and Ultra Light. Expressive and geometric, ADB Farto is a font conceived for extraordinary impact and effective visual rhythm and pattern. Appears to be retired as of late 2025.

typefaces.name: ADB Luder
typefaces.desc: Started in 2014 and inspired by the work of Joseph Champion, particularly the “Set Chancery Alphabet”, ADB Luder is a contemporary approach to the Schwabacher style. Vibrant and much closer to formal handwriting, ADB Luder borrows inspiration from the Bastarda and Rotunda types, frequently used in chancellery clerks across European countries. With more than sixteen hundred glyphs, ADB Luder supports over 290 languages, including an extended character set for minor African languages, Greek, and Cyrillic, among dozens of typographic goodies. Appears to be retired as of late 2025.

typefaces.name: Adelia
typefaces.desc: Adelia is a flare serif influenced by Nordic arts and culture of the early 1900s. With romantic and organic yet straightforward characteristics it pays homage to the final decades of classicism. Based on lettering from a poster by Walter Käch for the 1950 exhibition Nutida Schweizisk konst .

typefaces.name: Adelphe
typefaces.desc: Released as open-source.

typefaces.name: Ademo
typefaces.desc: Ademo is a classic, all caps Geralde display font with chromatic layers and is often used for historically reminiscent, elegant packaging, such as for tea, wine, chocolate, or cakes. The design is based on two typefaces designed by Carl Albert Fahrenwaldt, published 1931 — 1932 by the German Schriftguss AG type foundry, Dresden. The font probably originated in connection with the «Minister Antiqua», also by Fahrenwaldt. Ademos special Fill fonts can be used for building multi layered color text or for special finishing needs like blind imaging, embossing, stamping, partial UV coating or laser cutting. [ astype.de ]

typefaces.name: ADHD
typefaces.desc: ADHD is a visual experiment that explores the possibilities of the variable fonts and dynamic grid inspired by the research of Armin Hoffmann. The whole family is based on 4 compatible masters, with a geometric and modular typeface as their base. With interpolation, each letter morphs into an expressive form, making ADHD a living tool that allows the creation of dynamic visual identities. [ capitalics.wtf ]

typefaces.name: Adoquin
typefaces.desc: Appears to be retired as of 2025.

typefaces.name: Adriano
typefaces.desc: Adriano Etc is a contemporary slab serif typeface inspired by the original 1934 Olivetti logo. When Adriano Olivetti took the reins of the typewriter company from his father Camillo, he commissioned Bauhaus artist Xanti Schawinsky to draw the logo, outlining and setting the new art direction for the company. The typeface project evolved from that initial inspiration. After long studies of the slab-serif typographic genre, we merged all the different subgroups of this vast family of styles such as Antique, Ionic, Egyptian, Clarendon, Typewriter, Italienne, Teutonic, Tuscan, Geometric, etc., into one definitive “pan-slab-serif” focusing on the low contrast and large flat slab serifs. We infused also some "Geometric Universal" Bauhaus features in reference and ode to the original Olivetti logo. The result is this contemporary reinterpretation of the slab serif galaxy into a concise compilation of details, handpicked and selected from the many different genres and subgenres of this undefinable typographic universe. [ abc-etc.com ]

typefaces.name: Advocat
typefaces.desc: Christian Schwartz spent most of 2020 on an extended parental leave that made it hard to find time or energy to concentrate on type design. Scattered hours while the kids were in bed went to this typewriter face, a sufficiently low-stakes project, based on a low-res scan of an old IBM Selectric ‘golf ball’ alphabet called Advocate, designed by Howard “Bud” Kettler (best known as the designer of Courier). Rough source material led to a very loose interpretation. Richard Turley has used it for a few small publications with Civilization. [ vault.commercialtype.com ] Not to be confused with Matthew Butterick’s Advocate .

typefaces.name: Aegis
typefaces.desc: https://www.printmag.com/type-tuesday/aegis-is-a-display-typeface-carved-out-of-resilience/

typefaces.name: Aeonik
typefaces.desc: At its core, Aeonik combines the precision of a neo-grotesque with the roundness of geometric letterforms, featuring closed apertures, perpendicular stroke endings, and clean proportions. [ cotypefoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Aeroport
typefaces.desc: Aeroport is a new typeface in the spirit of both German geometric sans serifs and Swiss neogrotesques. Its deliberately wide proportions and relatively short capitals account for the excellent way the type carries the line. Its short ascenders and descenders allow for very tight leading. When used in large point sizes, Aeroport reveals its industrial ancestry and its unconventional design: the somewhat unbalanced top of the lowercase a, the capital B that has deliberately not been compensated optically, the overly wide capital M. In smaller sizes the type creates a starkly different effect: its measured widths and low contrast make a text setting appear neutral and homogenous. This versatility is what makes Aeroport a multipurpose sans serif suitable for a wide variety of typographic applications. The family includes five weights with their italics and a monospased style. Character set includes an alternate lowercase a, two sets of figures and currency symbols, uppercase punctuation, and a set of arrows. Includes Latin and Cyrillic sets supporting over forty languages. [ brownfox.org ]

typefaces.name: Aether
typefaces.desc: Aether plays with light, callenging the uniform grey tone within letters. Derived from 19th Century modern faces, and grounded in a geometric framework, Aether incorporates a set of predefined curves on a rhythmic system. This ensures an identical stem interval within and between letters for a consistent and rational appearance. The family contains two stylistic variations emphasizing the parametric construction: Aether A, without optical adjustments, results in dark brackets and joints for a bold and distinctive look. Aether B incorporates optical adjustments to enhance legibility and refine the overall design. A set of alternative letters allows for further enhancement of the geometric appearance. Additionally, a vast array of ligatures is available to harmonize gaps in the monospaced column. Circled and boxed numbers, along with fractions, add a touch of versatility for various applications. [ ddoott.net ]

typefaces.name: Aether Mono
typefaces.desc: Aether plays with light, callenging the uniform grey tone within letters. Derived from 19th Century modern faces, and grounded in a geometric framework, Aether incorporates a set of predefined curves on a rhythmic system. This ensures an identical stem interval within and between letters for a consistent and rational appearance. The family contains two stylistic variations emphasizing the parametric construction: Aether A, without optical adjustments, results in dark brackets and joints for a bold and distinctive look. Aether B incorporates optical adjustments to enhance legibility and refine the overall design. A set of alternative letters allows for further enhancement of the geometric appearance. Additionally, a vast array of ligatures is available to harmonize gaps in the monospaced column. Circled and boxed numbers, along with fractions, add a touch of versatility for various applications. [ ddott.net ]

typefaces.name: Affix
typefaces.desc: A geometric slab serif.

typefaces.name: Agiro
typefaces.desc: Agiro is a font with no curves at all. Only composed with segment and play with a lot of fractured shapes. Largely inspired by the work of Vojtech Preissig, she is in a first place a revival drawn to represent the energy of a character from Akira: Tetsuo Shima. [ entravaux.framer.website ]

typefaces.name: Agna
typefaces.desc: Drawing inspiration from the refined proportions of Pierre-Simon Fournier’s Petit-Canon, Agna pays homage to the storied tradition and meticulous craftsmanship of 18th-century French typography. While capturing this historical essence, Agna embodies the spirit and philosophy of DSType fonts, designed for editorial excellence. This type system offers four distinct optical sizes—Text, Subhead, Headline, and Display—each tailored to meet the diverse needs of both print and digital media. Complementing these is a meticulously crafted Poster companion, featuring four unique styles, including eye-catching Stencil letterforms and a rich array of swashes and typographic enhancements. Agna seamlessly blends historical elegance with contemporary versatility, making it the perfect choice for discerning typographers and designers who seek the ideal fusion of classic sophistication and modern functionality.

typefaces.name: Ahkio
typefaces.desc: Ahkio is a brushed disconnected script family of 5 fonts. Ahkio’s roots are in 1930s sign painting and showcard lettering but with a modern and distinctive twist. The main characteristics are soft, rounded forms and a bit of curved stems. Ahkio is a friendly and gentle font that suits well in titles, packages, logos, and, for example, posters. 5 weights make Ahkio a versatile font that allows you to add contrast and interest to your typography.

typefaces.name: Air America
typefaces.desc: Air America is a font originally designed by William G. Sherman and based on the Air America logo. My role was to digitize the original drawings and master the letterforms to create the final font. The drawings were quite precise, which made my job relatively straightforward, but I made some recommendations to help improve consistency and balance in the design. [ sajatypeworks.com ] Released as open-source on GitHub.

typefaces.name: Airport
typefaces.desc: Airport is an interpretation of Matthew Carter’s alphabet for London Airport. The original was drawn in 1961 for the wayfinding system in the newly built Oceanic Terminal, today known as Heathrow Terminal 3. For this showcase of modern Britain, designer Colin Forbes wanted something straightforward like Akzidenz, but with all stroke endings made horizontal. Carter also raised the x-height, in order to maximize legibility. While the signs were pasted up from photostats, the alphabet was also produced as a phototype font. Despite being made available from various type providers, it didn’t catch on, and was overshadowed by the similar Helvetica. The digital reimagination expands Carter’s design to seven weights and optimizes it for contemporary use. Airport supports a large number of Latin-based languages and includes numerous extras like alternates, arrows, and circled and squared glyphs. Airport is optionally available as variable font with a weight axis. There is a version with a second axis that contains Airport X, a variant with a lower x-height. [ revolvertype.com ]

typefaces.name: Airport X
typefaces.desc: Airport X is a variant of Airport with a lower x-height, and part of an interpretation of Matthew Carter’s alphabet for London Airport. The original was drawn in 1961 for the wayfinding system in the newly built Oceanic Terminal, today known as Heathrow Terminal 3. For this showcase of modern Britain, designer Colin Forbes wanted something straightforward like Akzidenz, but with all stroke endings made horizontal. Despite being made available from various type providers, it didn’t catch on, and was overshadowed by the similar Helvetica. The digital reimagination expands Carter’s design to seven weights and optimizes it for contemporary use. Like Airport, Airport X supports a large number of Latin-based languages and includes numerous extras like alternates, arrows, and circled and squared glyphs. It is optionally available as variable font with a weight axis. There is a version with a second axis that contains both subfamilies. [ revolvertype.com ]

typefaces.name: Akin
typefaces.desc: Akin is a monolinear script typeface designed in a single weight. Its letters’ designs combine geometric elements with a retro aesthetic, swashes, and a steep slope. Characters’ sides are straight, giving the typeface a condensed feeling overall. Akin’s design language feels reminiscent of both the 1950s and the 1990s, but there isn’t just one specific style that it cites: Akin is a timeless face, which looks like it could have always been a part of graphic design. Like almost every good OpenType script font, Akin has a lot of alternates. The most prominent feature is the font’s swashes. Swashes of various lengths can be automatically applied via an OpenType feature that reads the surrounding characters – in both directions – and inserts swashes that sweep above or below two or even three other letters (the font knows better than to let its swashes collide with capital letters, ascenders or descenders). Another technical feature in Akin substitutes specially-designed ‘final’ glyphs in for letters that come at the end of a word. Akin supports all European languages written with the Latin script. [ indiantypefoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Akke
typefaces.desc: An interpretation of Kumlien Gothic (1943) by Akke Kumlien. Comes in four optical sizes, each with three sets of x-heights.

typefaces.name: Aktiv Grotesk
typefaces.desc: The list of credits incorporates the designers mentioned up to 2016 [ web.archive.org ].

typefaces.name: Alarm
typefaces.desc: Alarm was published in 1928 by the Trennert type foundry in Hamburg-Altona. One of the last designs by freelancer Heinz König. Alarm can certainly be seen as a reworking of Louis Oppenheim's Fanfare, which was published by H. Berthold AG in 1927. The Alarm typeface did not enter the digital realm until 2017. Andreas Seidel digitized the typeface for Fust & Friends, referring several type specimens of the original metal and wood type versions as well as the result of a special 2016 printing session with 72pt Alarm foundry type. After Jan Middendorp closed the micro foundry Fust & Friends in October 2021, this font can still be licensed via astype fonts. [ astype.de ]

typefaces.name: Albaro
typefaces.desc: A serif typeface informed by broad-nib calligraphy.

typefaces.name: Album
typefaces.desc: Justus Erich Walbaum (1768-1837), a confectioner by trade, carved his own cake molds. Quite gifted, he became a specialist, developing an activity as a punch-cutter, and eventually bought Ernst Wilhelm Kirschner’s type foundry. Considered to be one of the foremost creators of his time, he engraved gothic letters and Antiqua type, similar to those of Didot and Bodoni. But his romans had a different flavor, and for some, they contain the origins of the Grotesques that followed. In 2010, Thomas Huot-Marchand and SPMillot were asked to develop the typographic identity of the Musée d’Orsay that had been based on Berthold Walbaum since its very beginnings. They proposed adding distant “cousins” in later typographic styles: a bold grotesque and a thin slab serif, but these typefaces would ultimately remain unused. In 2020, Thomas Huot-Marchand decided to redesign them while developing an extended family. Album is a subtraction of Walbaum: with no serifs for Album Sans and with no contrast for Album Slab. Its silhouette retains some memory of the particular proportions and slightly flattened curves of Walbaum. [ 205.tf ]

typefaces.name: Alch
typefaces.desc: Alch Typeface is a non versatile font family but available in four distinct styles, all in a Regular weight. It transitions seamlessly from a Serif style infused with a Moyen-Age spirit and refined elegance to a more neutral Sans style, distinguished by its spiky endings. The Gothic style harmoniously blends the characteristics of both, creating a timeless fusion. The variable font version offers two axes for added flexibility: one transitions from Serif to Spiky, while the other shifts from Standard to Gothic, giving you the age of Type ahaha! [ typefaces.pizza ]

typefaces.name: Alea
typefaces.desc: Alea is based on the drawings of Maria Balle. The floral, organic look of these bastard script initials will play well together with nearly all Didone designs and will give them a special note. Alea works perfectly with the Adana typefaces. [[astype.de]]

typefaces.name: Alembert
typefaces.desc: Alembert draws its influence from the work of the Maîtres écrivains (master writers) of 17th and 18th century France, particularly the Bâtardes and Coulées script models. It can be seen to bridge the gap between typographic italics, Roman type companions, and the Anglaise1 script (copperplate script) that emerged in the 19th century. Offering a warmer, less rigid alternative to the Anglaise script, Alembert adds a refined touch to graphic projects. It pairs beautifully with historical typefaces in the Typofonderie library like PS Fournier, Ambroise, and Arsen, allowing for sophisticated typographic blends that reflect the richness of vintage packaging, publishing, and posters. [ typofonderie.com ]

typefaces.name: Alfabeta
typefaces.desc: Originally designed by Aldo Novarese in 1988.

typefaces.name: Alhambra
typefaces.desc: In Alhambra, Richard Lipton attacks the static repetition typically found in lines of typographic capitals by offering the inventive typographer a lavish choice of alternative letterforms. They are particularly useful when doubles occur. Having achieved a personal synthesis from a variety of calligraphic hands, he suggests the sensitive mixing of alternate characters as a creative method of obtaining a calligraphic spontaneity. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Alison Head
typefaces.desc: Extravagant, highly-contrasted and finely detailed, Alison Head finds her own way to redefine the Didone. Inspired by Altona’s flair, Alison picks up a hundred years on to combine historic finesse with modern refinement. Alison is an emancipated evolution of the Didone: powerful and expressive. This attitude is most evident in the vertical serifs. Creating a distinct and characteristic image, they enrich the soft strokes and familiar teardrop terminals with a new sharpness. In this way, Alison confidently breaks new ground. [ typemates.com ]

typefaces.name: Alison Text
typefaces.desc: Inspired by the quirky charm of Altona and the refinement of Alison Head, Alison Text is a reliable foundation for her bold, contrasting siblings. Combined in Alison Variable, the two Alison sisters form a system and express the sophistication of a Didone in text and display versions. [ typemates.com ]

typefaces.name: Alizarin
typefaces.desc: Alizarin is a sophisticated serif with a hand-drawn style, imitating references as found in print. Its subtle asymmetry results in a contemporary appearance and function. [ doubledagger.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Alku Handwriting Model
typefaces.desc: Alku Handwriting Model is a part of PISA renowned Finnish national education curricula since 2016. It helps digital native students to form sufficient handwriting skills during their first years at school. Alku fonts play an elemental part in producing teaching materials for handwriting. In a purely typographical taxonomy Alku would be labelled as a rounded humanistic Italic Sanserif. In practice it is based on letterforms drawn on a paper by hand using a pencil. Its lines are digitally cleaned up and then produced into typefaces. Alku letterforms make handwriting easy to learn and provides a process how everyone can develop a life long personal writing style. Many aspects in this model are designed to keep letterforms from mixing into each others when writing catches more speed. Alku typefaces are designed by Jarno Lukkarila in 2015–2016. The method and letterforms are conceptualised with a group of children's writing experts, teachers and young students in the Majakka pilot schools in Finland.

typefaces.name: Almost
typefaces.desc: Italics added in 2021.

typefaces.name: ALT Klarinet
typefaces.desc: A sans-serif stencil typeface in six weights.

typefaces.name: ALT Maria Clara
typefaces.desc: Released as a single style (Light). The character set was expanded in 2023 . Giulia Boggio expanded it to a full family in 2024.

typefaces.name: ALT Picaro
typefaces.desc: ALT Picaro is a bold, modern typeface that blends geometric structure with a touch of playfulness. Designed for maximum clarity and character, it features clean lines, uniform stroke weights, and subtly rounded terminals that add warmth to its otherwise crisp design. [ alt-tf.com ]

typefaces.name: Altona
typefaces.desc: With proud roots in Hamburg, Altona is a bold, distinctive and cosmopolitan display typeface inspired by the original street signs of the Altona district. [ typemates.com ]

typefaces.name: Altro
typefaces.desc: Designed by Francesco Canovaro with Mario De Libero, Altro is a typeface that seamlessly transitions between humanist grotesque and serif old style, offering flawless pairing within a single font family. It allows designers to maintain visual harmony while experimenting with different aesthetics, thanks to its consistent set of proportions and visual weights. In its Grotesk incarnation, Altro is a Swiss-inspired, low-contrast sans serif with a wide range of eight weights. Its slightly lower-than-usual x-height lends it a touch of elegance while preserving its functionality as a workhorse typeface. The Serif version features an old-style transitional design, characterized by distinctive square dots and a brutalist approach to ball terminals. [ zetafonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Alyssa
typefaces.desc: Alyssa is a dynamic single weight display typeface that brings flair and sophistication to any project, whether it’s a striking logotype, a vibrant magazine spread, or refined branding. Balancing calligraphic flair with an incised quality gives it a unique panache, ideal for designers seeking to balance expressiveness with authority. Alyssa thrives in large sizes, where its vivid details can fully unfold, creating distinctive word shapes. Rooted in typographic traditions but with a fresh, contemporary edge, Alyssa pays homage to the iconic ATF Florentine , and follows designer Mark De Winne’s deepening fascination with the work of lettering masters Oscar Ogg, Arthur Baker and Helmut Salden. The design is an exploration of contrast and control, where bold, exaggerated details are offset by subtle, calligraphic gestures. Alyssa sidesteps the cold perfection of digital type design in favour of lively curves and expressive strokes, giving it a whimsical yet structured personality. The typeface’s large x-height, short descenders, and fluid serifs make it ideal for use in headlines, where it can make a strong impact while maintaining elegance. [ typofonderie.com ]

typefaces.name: Amadeo
typefaces.desc: In 1996 I sent a design to the Morisawa Typeface Competition. It won a prize. This is what I said about it at the time: More of our previously Carolingian lettershapes, de-contextualised by writing them with a cheap marker at the wrong pen angle. The weight distribution is uneven too. Most people would say it would never work as a typeface. This is what the judges said: Adopting the pen script method, this typeface fully expresses the good qualities of hand written letters and yet, it is very beautiful in text composition. It is designed to give a texture of calligraphy brush writing and would probably make a good match with Kanji characters. Parts of the letters look as if they have been cut off with a knife. This font has rhythm and is beautiful in typesetting and calculated to show a unique texture, not seen in ordinary Latin typefaces. I thought I was naming the typeface after the painter, Modigliani: I liked the music of his first name but I now realise that I have spelt it incorrectly. No matter: I prefer my choice of vowels and I adore a happenstance neologism! [ shapesforcash.com ]

typefaces.name: Amalgam
typefaces.desc: Amalgam is a bubbly rounded sans, with purposefully colliding and overlapping characters in the heavy weights. David Jonathan Ross once asked me what one of my typefaces would look like if I started with the Greek. Amalgam is the result of that experiment. Originally drawn from lettering found on the Greek sheet music cover for Η Δροσούλα (1946), taking the rounded, top heavy features and expanding it into a playful overlapping typeface. Originally not overlapping, the amalgamation of characters works well in the greek due to most characters being rounded. To help provide a similar yet functional Latin, Amalgam requires a few contextual alternates to help give the paragraph a good colour by opening or closing the space between letters. The design of the Greek informed the decisions for the Latin, and the Black weight has had an impact on the lighter weights. With all the various alternates in the black, these alternates are still present in the lighter weights, giving the text a certain musicality and rhythm. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Aman
typefaces.desc: Aman is a versatile serif typeface family, crafted to perform seamlessly across a wide range of sizes—from striking display headlines to fine, legible captions. Inspired by the lettering from the book Amen, this typeface brings together the timeless elegance of old-style designs like Plantin with the refined sophistication of transitional styles such as Times New Roman. Its most distinctive features are the baroque flourishes seen in the beaks and head serifs, while its gracefully arcing terminals lend a subtle, refined touch to the letterforms. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Amaretto
typefaces.desc: Amaretto is a typeface born from the Tavern, the creative and experimental wavy tool crafted by Gaëtan Baehr. Characterized by its high contrast and sophisticated design, Amaretto stands out as both classic and unconventional. The font offers two sets of capital letters: a traditional option for timeless elegance and an experimental set where circles seamlessly integrate into the letterforms. This unique feature brings an unexpected playfulness and originality to the typography, making it ideal for creating expressive and elegant lettering. Amaretto is designed exclusively in capitals, allowing for optimized wave effects with the Tavern tool. To enhance its versatility, the font includes a width variation axis and four corner axes—top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right—providing precise control over each letter's shape. These features enable the creation of unexpected and visually striking effects. [ black-foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Amarta
typefaces.desc: Inspired by the design of classic typefaces used in sports visuals, the nd Amarta family features styles for two sizes: text and large headlines. While sharing the same essence, their designs are distinct, each crafted for its intended use. Nd Amarta Text works well in both small and larger sizes, with weight and slant variations that help fine-tune paragraph settings. Nd Amarta Poster, designed for large sizes, has narrow counters and, unlike Text, features width variation to accommodate words or title lines. The name Amarta is a tribute to one of the greatest athletes in Brazilian history, football player Marta Silva. [ plau.design ]

typefaces.name: Ambule
typefaces.desc: Huxley Vertical meets Peignot in this stylized cap/lowercase hybrid design called Ambule. The aim was to create a clean, straightforward design that is strikingly effective in both text and display settings. [ octotypo.com ]

typefaces.name: American Grotesk
typefaces.desc: A reprisal of Franklin Gothic in seven weights in upright and italic, across three widths.

typefaces.name: Amnezia
typefaces.desc: Accessible by enrollment into Production Type’s Beta program.

typefaces.name: Ampere
typefaces.desc: With sleek geometry and an uncompromising clarity, Ampere stands out with a refined, grid-like precision that speaks to its modern design ethos. At small scales, it remains legible and crisp, while at larger sizes it commands attention, making it ideal for both immersive reading and powerful headings. Ampere's unique character lies in its subtle yet striking features. Inside corners are softened with squared ink traps, a choice that tempers its sharp angles for a smooth, sophisticated finish without compromising on structure. Adding a spark to its utility, Ampere also includes a set of special "electric" characters inspired by its namesake, infusing a touch of energy into any project. [ black-foundry.com ] The typeface also features a series of electrical symbols.

typefaces.name: Analog
typefaces.desc: This new take on industrial sans serifs embodies the spirit of the solid state electronics revolution. Its energetic, generously wide proportions are balanced by confident, efficient strokes with minimal contrast. [ vectrotype.com ]

typefaces.name: Analogy
typefaces.desc: Analogy is a contemporary interpretation of the timeless elegance found in Nicolas Jenson’s 15th-century type. Rooted in the humanist forms of the 1470s yet refined for modern sensibilities, Analogy balances historical warmth with precision, offering a text typeface that is as readable as it is refined. Its calligraphic heritage shines through in the subtly flared serifs, measured contrast, and flowing rhythm, making it ideal for immersive reading experiences, editorial design, and sophisticated branding. [ positype.com ]

typefaces.name: Angus Hand
typefaces.desc: Angus hand is a set of authentic handwriting fonts remincent of a time before computers when sending hand-written letters was part of our daily lives. Based on samples of love letters written from Victoria, Canada in 1955—Angus Hand subtly conveys the love and care that was written into the content of those original letters. Angus hand is based on the handwriting of my grandfather R.B.Angus. I traced the original letters he wrote to my nana and those drawings served as the casual style, which stays true to the imperfections that bring warmth to these letterforms. I then created a calligraphy style for a slightly more formal version of my grandfather’s writing. [ arcanetype.com ]

typefaces.name: Animo
typefaces.desc: The Animo font was originally created as a display font and also as a potential revival of wall signs from Spain. We created an extensive archive of photographs depicting this local phenomenon, which is often seen on shop and restaurant signs. As we delved deeper into the origins of the font, we increasingly sought out examples that usually lacked the desired consistency in their rendering. Over time, we got into discussions with designers, usually retired, who remembered their days of practice. As they say, it was a time when there were remixes of classic fonts which had already acquired a completely different and new character thanks to the handmade transfer to the sign format. This is a unique phenomenon where everyone in a local environment interacts with each other and a certain ignorance of the principles of type design was able to offer a different point of view on its design. From the first style "Normal" we start to draw other styles, differing now only in proportions, not in thickness. The differences in proportions were also important to us because of the motivation to bring the font back to the local culture. In fact, due to the Covid pandemic, these original inspiratio

typefaces.name: Anon Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Anon Grotesk, specifically designed for display use, was developed over a period of several years and evolved to become a highly refined reductionist neo-grotesque. It is free of dated, historical limitations that many revivals share, while still being shaped by characteristic Swiss design principles. Symmetry, balance, rhythm and nuance combine to create a fresh, contemporary take on this revered genre. All together, Anon Grotesk transcends its individually drawn letterforms with a familial cohesion characterized by isotropic, sculptural qualities. Envisioned through a hypercritical design lens, the aim of Anon Grotesk was to solve various issues found among past neo-grotesque typeface releases. Foremost this includes the burden of reviving overly dated and aggrandized designs. Anon Grotesk distinguishes itself from others in the genre that are bound by relatively crude, imbalanced, or flawed letterforms, all of which, conceptually, are overlooked contradictions of Swiss design principles. Anon Grotesk represents purity of form and intent, not designed by committee, nor compromised by decisions unfounded in a display face. [ aesthetictype.com ]

typefaces.name: Anon Grotesk Text
typefaces.desc: Anon Grotesk Text, specifically designed for text use, was developed in parallel with Anon Grotesk. These two optically designed families and their functionality are maximized in separation, yet unified in their sophisticated design intent. The qualities of symmetry, balance, and rhythm are reflected at a macro scale in text, lending to a cohesive, refined texture. Collectively, the Anon Grotesk Text family was reduced from its parent of twenty display styles to twelve carefully designed text specific styles in a carefully allocated weight range focused on functionality. The letterforms have been optimized by a significant reduction in contrast, in addition to a critical increase in spacing, allowing it to perform in the most demanding, professional text settings. [ aesthetictype.com ]

typefaces.name: Anon Line
typefaces.desc: Anon Line is a detailed hairline display variant of the inimitable Anon Grotesk neo-grotesque typeface. Reduced to its skeletal essence comprised of a near monoline stroke, it represents the purity and refinement of its source in minimalist clarity. Vertical and horizontal strokes were drawn on a 1000 unit grid at six and five points, respectively, utilizing a one unit differential stroke contrast. Curiously, small gestures such as this lend to its refined and sophisticated character. Excruciating care was taken finalizing letterform paths during mastering, as single integer units are the difference between the continuity of a stroke and the compromise of a glyph’s form. [ aesthetictype.com ]

typefaces.name: Anormal Sans
typefaces.desc: Anormal Sans is a condensed, low contrast typeface with a high x-height, slightly angled terminals and an occasional disconnected stroke. The creation of Anormal Sans derived from a two week trip around Northern Italy, which put a spotlight on Italian Art Deco typefaces. These sans were abundant, from contemporary signage, to old wooden type found in printing shops, each one unique, ornamental and striking. Anormal Sans offers a casual, friendly sans and draws inspiration from these Italian Art Deco typefaces without resorting to stereotypes or gimmicks. Anormal's Art Deco heritage is apparent in characters such as /B, /G, /P and /S but many letters break from this stylistic norm. For example, the typeface includes a conservative /A and /N, a proportional /O and a standout lowercase /a. Overall, the combination of past and present creates a unique and eye-catching display typeface. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Anto Rounded
typefaces.desc: Roman designed in 2017 and released in December 2022. Italic designed in 2022 and released in January 2024.

typefaces.name: APK Galeria
typefaces.desc: APK Galeria is a modern day, grotesque typeface family. A featured combination of well known grotesque properties and hard edged cuts and subtleties are the details that make the font visually distinctive and instantly recognizable, while maintaining versatility. A typeface that has the singularity to be used in logotypes and the versatility to be used as a reading typeface as well. APK Galeria comes in seven weights with accompanying Italics. Offering large character sets and four stylistic sets of alternates across the weights. Originally designed as a custom font (Regular) as part of a visual identity for a modern art gallery in the Netherlands. In 2022 it has been revisited, reworked and refined. In 2023, together with Swiss-based font developer Maël Bächtold, the Regular was expanded into a complete font family and released with the launch of APK Type. [ apk-type.com ]

typefaces.name: APK Protocol
typefaces.desc: APK Protocol is a modern day, grotesque typeface family rooted in the Modernist aesthetic. Visually distinctive by an unique combination of well known grotesque proportions, inner symmetry and more hard edged subtleties. Protocol was made with the intention to take the characteristics (neutral, rational) of the modern day grotesque to the extreme. Protocol has a fondness for symmetry and straight lines. All with the intention to take the characteristics (neutral, rational) of the modern day grotesque to the extreme, without losing sight of the very essentials of type design. Next to these aspirations a set of alternates facilitates a more quirky direction in the use of the typeface. Other notable features of Protocol are a high x-height, the termination of strokes on horizontal or vertical lines and a tight spacing between letters, giving it a dense and solid appearance. The outlines of this typeface were designed in 2018. In 2020 a beta version of APK Protocol Regular was made. Together with swiss based type developer Maël Bächtold the Regular was expanded into a complete font family and released in 2021. In 2023 Protocol was revised, improved and the family extended with a Medium

typefaces.name: APK TL25
typefaces.desc: APK TL25 is inspired by the TL25N table lamp by Gerrit Rietveld, with its structure of strictly geometric shapes that barely seem to touch each other. Until recently, the small table lamp L25 was a treasure that only a few had discovered. Rietveld designed this table lamp in 1925. Surprisingly modern for its time and never serially produced. [ apk-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Apoka
typefaces.desc: Originally released with The Northern Block in 2017.

typefaces.name: Archive
typefaces.desc: A modular typeface drawing from the geometry of segmented displays. Originally released by GarageFonts in 2000 [ fontsinuse.com ] and reissued in December 2024 along with the halftone variant Archive Matrix .

typefaces.name: Archive Matrix
typefaces.desc: A halftone dot-matrix variant of Archive .

typefaces.name: Ardena
typefaces.desc: Ardena is a modern sans-serif typeface family. While neutral and clear at first glance, it can be characterized as both pleasant and confident due to its open, rounded forms and vertical terminals. [ fontcuisine.com ]

typefaces.name: Arkbro
typefaces.desc: Arkbro is a variable typeface based on strict geometric principles and proportions. It draws inspiration from Ellen Arkbro’s track ‘Mountain of Air’, with the concept of shapes filling out the space, much like the sound and feeling of the track. The variable axis of Arkbro blends characters of different weights at the extremes, creating a combination of very heavy characters next to ultra-thin ones. With its diverse shapes and strong contrast, Arkbro is perfect for playful, animated typesetting and display applications. To overcome the significant height differences between upper- and lowercase letters, Arkbro is equipped with case-sensitive numerals, punctuation, and other symbols. [ ecal-typefaces.ch ]

typefaces.name: Arkitekt
typefaces.desc: Store Norske Arkitekt is a geometric typeface based on Norwegian functionalist architecture; the shapes of its buildings and the lettering found on them. The first functionalist building in the Nordic countries, was Restaurant Skansen in Oslo (Lars Backer, 1927). Around the same time Trygve M. Davidsen was developing a geometric lettering alphabet, later published in his textbook Typografisk Skissering (1933). Other notable examples are Davidsen’s lettering for Møre Landbruksselskaps Jubileumsutstilling (1931), and Per Grieg’s lettering on Bergens Sjøfartsmuseum (1927). The functionalists wanted their design to be predominantly determined by practical considerations, with the intention to exclude anything visually redundant. Pure forms, and form should follow function. It should not be a style, but a method. But even with that aim, many of the buildings had distinct common attributes. Simple geometric features easy to imitate regardless of understanding their purpose. The superficial imitations that arose, were referred to as Funkis. It seems that the most successful functionalist buildings, were designed by the generation of architects trained in neoclassical architecture. With a

typefaces.name: Arkitekt [Aesthetic]
typefaces.desc: Arkitekt is an avant-garde reinterpretation of Anon Grotesk, that is inspired by applying architectural and sculptural themes in a literal, material direction. Early developmental explorations of Anon Grotesk as a collection of related typeface families led to one particular proof of concept which would ultimately manifest itself in Arkitekt (née Anon Form). In contemplating concepts of dimension, structure, and space–the precise, sharp letterforms, and unified word shapes of Anon Grotesk ultimately fall flat. This is the nature of formal typography, as it is bound by its own limitations within two dimensions. Envisioning a letterform as a tactile, three-dimensional object, such as one shaped from stone or metal, lends itself to details that counter this limitation. It is through this lens that details which ultimately define Arkitekt are manifest. Specifically, a reduction in horizontal contrast, beveled edges, and faceted interior intersections are most defining and prominent. Additionally, certain letterforms have received specific modifications, simplifying, balancing, or reinforcing their form structurally. Separately, these changes are rather limiting in their application, bu

typefaces.name: Arkitekt Text
typefaces.desc: Arkitekt Text, specifically designed for text use, was developed in parallel with Arkitekt. These two optically designed families are unified in their technical, material design attributes. The underlying qualities of symmetry, balance, and rhythm are reflected at a macro scale in text–with a unique, contemporary, machined texture, which is rather unorthodox in a text face. Collectively, the Arkitekt Text family was reduced from its parent of sixteen display styles to twelve carefully designed text-specific styles in a carefully allocated weight range focused on functionality. The letterforms have been optimized by a significant reduction in contrast, in addition to a critical increase in spacing, allowing it to perform in the most demanding, professional text settings. It especially excels in, but is not limited to, settings or themes related to architecture, technology, engineering, process, and innovation. [ aesthetictype.com ]

typefaces.name: Armin Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Inspired by the work of Swiss designer Armin Hofmann.

typefaces.name: Armin Soft
typefaces.desc: A variant of Armin Grotesk with softened corners.

typefaces.name: Armond
typefaces.desc: Taking reference from old fashioned Italian packaging and sign styles, Armond is an old soul with a few trick up its sleeve. It’s born to show up in a tux (Did someone say they were designing a whiskey label?), but destined to impress in more contemporary ways (we’re thinking peppermint flavored holiday alcoholic seltzers.) With an outline style in the caps and a matching solid infill in the lowercase, it’s really two layerable fonts in one. [ badsontype.com ]

typefaces.name: Arrogant
typefaces.desc: Arrogant is a display, single-case typeface that stands out for its expressivity and rounded shapes. [ carmen-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Arrogante
typefaces.desc: There’s no denying that the high contrast and precise geometry of serifs like Bodoni or Didot carry not only elegance but also an unmistakable sense of self-assured grandeur. That subtle edge of self-importance lit the fuse for Arrogante, a typeface family proudly embracing its bold character. Equal parts refined and assertive, Arrogante pairs dramatic contrasts with semi-condensed proportions and razor-sharp serifs to deliver a design that doesn’t just attract attention—it demands it. [ zetafonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Ars Technica
typefaces.desc: A partire da un logotipo commissionato da un'azienda costruttrice di simulatori di guida, il font nasce da un'indagine dei visual utilizzati nei settori industriali: logistica, edilizia e meccanica, tutti accomunati da componenti tecniche ricche di tipografia, soprattutto per quanto riguarda le informazioni poste sui macchinari, come carichi, tensione o velocità. Gli outline sono costruiti con rigore e su base monospaziata e acquisiscono un aspetto digitale molto forte, ispirato agli anime giapponesi di fantascienza – in particolare ai mecha – dove spesso informazioni di natura tecnica assumono un alto valore estetico. [ firm.gs ]

typefaces.name: Arsenica Condensed
typefaces.desc: Arsenica Condensed builds upon the inspiration behind Arsenica, namely early 20th-century Italian poster art. It channels the era’s fusion of typography and illustration, where traditional Old Style letterforms coexisted with Art Nouveau and Deco aesthetics. The design pays homage to artists like Giorgio Muggiani, whose work for iconic brands like Cinzano and Pirelli, as well as newspapers like Il Popolo d’Italia, seamlessly integrated lettering into visual communication. Arsenica Condensed retains the key characteristics of its parent family: Old Style low-contrast proportions and subtle stylistic quirks, reinterpreted through a condensed lens that enhances verticality while preserving the robust, vintage-inspired charm. The condensed version refines the display and text qualities of Arsenica, offering a more compact yet equally expressive solution for designers working with limited horizontal space, such as headlines, posters, or editorial layouts. [ zetafonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Artford
typefaces.desc: Artford is a user-friendly sans serif font designed for versatility. Its slightly wider design and high x-height make it ideal for both impactful headlines and small typesetting. With a touch of North American grotesk style, Artford features subtle thickness contrasts, creating generous counter shapes even in its bolder weights. At larger sizes, you'll notice the shapes are gently rounded, giving a softer, more approachable appearance. [ typography.synthview.com ]

typefaces.name: Arvana
typefaces.desc: Originally released on Future Fonts in 2019, from which it graduated in 2023. Subsequently released with lo-ol type.

typefaces.name: ASM
typefaces.desc: The initials ASM are the acronym for the Arts Santa Mònica cultural center in Barcelona, Spain. ASM was the center's custom corporate typeface from 2008 to 2013. ASM is an energetic, monospaced, highly legible typeface. It consists of two original weights, with an underlined version –used on some of the original corporate applications– all with their companion italics. [ extratype.com ]

typefaces.name: Asoma
typefaces.desc: Asoma aims to revive the sense of wonder and mystery of 1970s monoweight typefaces such as ITC Busorama, ITC Serif Gothic, and Marvin. Loosely inspired by its predecessors, Asoma riffs on aesthetics of the past, embedding new shapes and ideas with an offbeat sense of nostalgia. A plethora of ligatures gives you the option to heavily customize headlines, titles and logotypes. Additionally, Asoma includes a full upper and lowercase character set, lining figures, math characters, punctuation, 5 distinct weights and support for Western European, Central European, South Eastern European and South American scripts. Short for asomatic, Asoma speaks with a voice that is somewhat otherworldly, a step away from the physical realm and existing in a more transcendental space. This makes Asoma a great option for horror film titles. For some reason, it also works surprisingly well on packaging for black beans. At heavier weights, Asoma communicates a nostalgic feeling, emulating the design of the 1970s. Asoma thin offers a more subdued feel, perfect for the contemporary design space. [ jamesplattner.com ]

typefaces.name: Asphalt
typefaces.desc: Who hasn’t admired the energy of Antique Olive Nord ? All other ultrabolds seem sluggish in comparison. Nord exudes Roger Excoffon’s animation and Gallic impatience with the rules. Tobias Frere-Jones cross-bred the weight, proportion, and rhythms of Nord with the casual grace of his own Cafeteria , gaining informality and a dancing vitality on the page. In his words, Asphalt swings with “a lively, if faintly inebriated gyration”. [ store.typenetwork.com ] Originally released by Font Bureau in 1995 and moved to Frere–Jones Type in 2020 [ fontsinuse.com ], available through Type Network and added to the foundry’s website in December 2024.

typefaces.name: Astra
typefaces.desc: Astra is a sophisticated geometric sans serif typeface, offering 9 weights that range from delicate thin to robust bold. Its design beautifully merges geometric precision with subtle humanist details, creating a clean yet inviting appearance. This balance ensures Astra is versatile, making it ideal for both branding and editorial projects. The typeface exudes modernity and elegance, appealing to designers seeking a fresh and refined font to elevate their work. [ positype.com ]

typefaces.name: Asura
typefaces.desc: Asura is a feral, free-flowing display typeface that mixes poster-era elegance with a hint of delightful chaos. Its sharp stroke ends, unpredictable bends, and mischievous letter skeletons make it feel like a 19th-century French sign painter had a caffeine rush and decided to reinvent the alphabet. Every glyph in Asura marches to its own beat, yet somehow they all vibe together like a beautifully disorganised parade. It’s expressive without being messy, wild without losing its manners, and dramatic without taking itself too seriously. From rebellious branding to offbeat posters, cryptic zines, experimental titles, and anything that needs a touch of “beautiful weird,” Asura delivers attitude with a wink. Think of it as a sophisticated troublemaker: unpredictable, elegant, and very much alive. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: At Chrome
typefaces.desc: At Chrome is a sharp, modern sans-serif font that captures the bright, intelligent, yet warm and breathing essence of present and future technology. Designed for precise performance, it renders crystal-clear on digital screens, and it excels in versatility with a wide range of letter alternates for personalized applications. [ arillatype.studio ]

typefaces.name: At Koba
typefaces.desc: At Koba is a capitalis monumentalis typeface engraved in the fashion of the Basque Country.

typefaces.name: At Umami
typefaces.desc: At Umami is where East meets West in typographic harmony. Conceived during a flight from Tokyo to Madrid, this rounded sans-serif was inspired by a plethora of visual provocations experienced in Japan. The result is a savoury and bold typeface that adds depth and dimension to your designs. [ arillatype.studio ]

typefaces.name: ATC Anais
typefaces.desc: Retired as of 2025.

typefaces.name: ATC Bianca
typefaces.desc: Retired as of 2025.

typefaces.name: ATC Doe Collection
typefaces.desc: Retired as of 2025.

typefaces.name: ATC Doubletap
typefaces.desc: Retired as of 2025.

typefaces.name: ATC Hal
typefaces.desc: Retired as of 2025.

typefaces.name: ATC Krueger
typefaces.desc: Retired as of 2025.

typefaces.name: ATC Monarch
typefaces.desc: Retired as of 2025.

typefaces.name: ATC Nasty
typefaces.desc: Retired as of 2025.

typefaces.name: ATC Ripley
typefaces.desc: Retired as of 2025.

typefaces.name: ATC Saturn
typefaces.desc: Retired as of 2025.

typefaces.name: Athena Ruby
typefaces.desc: Athena Ruby is a typeface for transcription of Byzantine seals and coins, commissioned by the Dumbarton Oaks Research Library and Museum. It provides multiple forms of Greek and Latin letters, reflecting more than a thousand years of palaeographic evolution and distinctive sigillographic and numismatic usage. Athena Ruby was selected as a Judge’s Choice in the 2013 TDC Typeface Design competition by Abbott Miller, who noted ‘its ability to aid research and provide typographic expression that, in turn, leads to a stronger set of interpretative tools.’ Version 2.00 of Athena Ruby includes extensions made in recent years and a broader range of font formats, and is released by Dumbarton Oaks under the Open Font License. [ tiro.com ] Version 2.0 released in 2024.

typefaces.name: Atkinson Hyperlegible
typefaces.desc: Updated in February 2025 with an improved proportionally-spaced version named Atkinson Hyperlegible Next , plus a new monospaced version.

typefaces.name: Atlantic
typefaces.desc: Appears to be retired as of 2025.

typefaces.name: Atlas
typefaces.desc: Atlas was originally designed as a corporate typeface for Munich Re, one of the world’s largest reinsurance companies. This typeface deliberately avoided contemporary trends in corporate type design in favor of the clear, optimistic tone of Dutch Modernism. The client produces hundreds of publications, reports, and other documents each year. They required a new typeface capable of maintaining clarity in often complicated typographical situations with a suitably well-considered range of weights. The new typeface also had to be economic in setting, saving space over the previous corporate face and saving significant amounts of paper in the process.

typefaces.name: Augure
typefaces.desc: Augure, designed by Simon Renaud, is based on an a priori paradoxical principal: how to move beyond traditional letterforms without undermining legibility? To this end, this typeface questions the canons inherited from Roman capitals and Carolingian minuscules. Augure freely reflects a range of diverse influences: somewhere between historical forms of the Latin alphabet (including Uncials), forms taken from cryptography, and forms inspired by digital technology and its rationality. The combinations of elementary forms are reminiscent of early twentieth-century experiments with geometric sans serifs. The juxtaposition of these many borrowed elements provides the typeface with a formal singularity, generating captivating typographic compositions. [ 205.tf ]

typefaces.name: Aujournuit
typefaces.desc: Aujournuit is a display font built on calligraphic traits, organic shapes and runny ink. Inspired by a 1956 magazine title “Chemins Perdus” (lost paths), it has evolved into a very condensed to very wide variable font, and includes all the zodiac signs. The name of the font is a play on the French words “aujourd’hui” meaning “today” and “nuit”, night – a reference to biodynamic farming practices which gravitate around the sun, moon, day and night. Expressive and atmospheric, Aujournuit conveys a timeless connection to natural cycles. [ colllettivo.it ]

typefaces.name: Aukera
typefaces.desc: A second version released in August 2024.

typefaces.name: Aukio
typefaces.desc: Aukio (means “square , angular” in Finnish) is a high-contrast display typeface with details inspired by the calligraphic practice of the Nordic countries. Its large squarish structure and angular inner shapes are a direct reference to this crafty and artistic world. Its digital drawing approach combined to its high contrast gives it a contemporary dimension for sensitive yet striking titles. [ typofonderie.com ]

typefaces.name: Auroc
typefaces.desc: Auroc is a pre-historic ‘workhorse’ type family. It comes in five weights, italics and in three optical sizes – Small, Text and Display. The upright roman has sharp incised serifs with strokes that terminate like knife cuts and joints between curves and stems etched with sharp notches. In contrast, the italic has a faster flow, softer curves and imitates pointed-brush lettering. With three optical sizes Auroc is an ideal editorial typeface. It works as well in large headlines as it does in running text, paragraphs, and even footnotes and references. [ eastofrome.com ] Debuted in 2020 on Future Fonts and graduated to v1.0 in 2024. Covers extended Latin, extended Cyrillic, and monotonic Greek.

typefaces.name: Authenia
typefaces.desc: Authenia is a brush script font that has been created with a brush pen and paper, and then carefully converted into vector format. Its texture has been retained to ensure it looks great in both small and large sizes, and gives it a natural, laid-back feel. To add variation and enhance the natural look of your text, Authenia features two sets of lowercase letters. By enabling Contextual Alternates on the OpenType panel, you can make these sets appear randomly. Additionally, there are several stylistic alternates and underlines available to further enhance your text and design.

typefaces.name: Avalon
typefaces.desc: Avalon is a vibrant script with sweeping freedom in the capitals against the vital discipline of a lowercase relieved by alternative ascending characters. Inspired by the work of Friedrich Neugebauer, who was known for the cutting power of his calligraphic invention. For example, as a prisoner of war in Egypt, he wrote with toothpaste when all else failed. The irrepressible style of this Austrian artist inspired a vibrant and dramatic design. Available in three weights. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Avena
typefaces.desc: Avena is a contemporary humanist sans-serif that blends elegance with a friendly, approachable personality. Drawing inspiration from classic humanist proportions, it brings a modern touch to traditional letterforms, making it ideal for branding and editorial projects. [ typeverything.com ] Available in seven weights, Medium shown here.

typefaces.name: Avona
typefaces.desc: Appears to be retired as of 2026.

typefaces.name: Axia
typefaces.desc: Axia is a sans serif uni-widths of concise letterforms. The type consists of ten weights from Light to Black, each with Italics and Small Caps. Two display styles, Stencil Light and Stencil Black feature a unique aesthetic. A distinct fragmentation of the letters gives this stencil design its particular character. The type is perfect for captivating big sizes; shapes of abstract floating parts allure the eye and form nicely proportioned type when united. Originally designed for the Rice University School of Architecture in 2011, this contemporary sans found some inspiration in the TwinCities typeface family created by Sibylle Hagmann for the University of Minnesota in 2003. Axia has been orchestrated from scratch, each the roman and italic weights harmonize perfectly in width without a changing line length. Text set in Light or Black results in the same, economical fit. The inner arched strokes off the stem on the lowercase ‘b’ and ‘d’, for example, progressively open the letterforms and express conceptual clarity throughout the system. A feature doing double duty, it contributes to great legibility in heavier weights, and attributes to versatility of individual styles. Axia includ

typefaces.name: Baga
typefaces.desc: Baga started with a simple sketch looking for a soft and fun typeface for packaging. It began with a bold version, but there will be at least five weights with a light version. An italic will also be part of it. The typeface has a stylistic set for the double storey a and g already in this first version. This soft typeface wants to reach your heart! [ futurefonts.com ] Finalized in February 2025 with the expansion to five weights.

typefaces.name: Balete
typefaces.desc: Balete is a typeface crafted with elegance and precision, blending natural fluidity with geometric refinement. Its design draws inspiration from traditional calligraphic forms and modernist typography, balancing graceful curves with sharp, structured details. This versatility makes Balete an exceptional choice for editorial layouts, branding, storytelling, and digital applications. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Baleze Display
typefaces.desc: Baleze is a contemporary typeface inspired by a Fraktur alphabet dated around 1825-1850, from Pennsylvania. The source material was used as the basis for a pixel typeface, which was then generatively modified via heavy use of custom filtres. The result was then refined by hand, keeping as much as possible the spirit and aesthetic of the original pixel typeface. [ futurefonts.com ] Updated in 2024 with a second, thinner pixel style.

typefaces.name: Banger
typefaces.desc: Banger is a thorny, prickly, and potentially explosive blackletter. A lively and energetic typeface that works great for anything that needs a little extra OOMPH. Loosely inspired by decorative blackletters, Banger is the result of searching for new textures in type and exploring unique methods of making. [ manictype.com ]

typefaces.name: Banto
typefaces.desc: Originally published as an early-access release on Future Fonts, from which it graduated in 2025.

typefaces.name: Barbican
typefaces.desc: Barbican is a typeface inspired by London’s iconic Barbican Centre, a landmark of Brutalist architecture. It blends the bold, utilitarian feel of Brutalism with softer, natural touches, offering a balance between strength and subtlety. The condensed design comes in multiple weights, making it versatile for various uses. Its strong, clear forms are ideal for impactful, large-scale communication. [ rangeleft.co.uk ]

typefaces.name: Barbieri
typefaces.desc: Barbieri is a casual, compressed san-serif family based on German lettering styles from the 1950s and ’60s. The original hand-drawn alphabet appeared on the cover of a Deutsche Grammophon edition of 'Der Barbier von Bagdad', an opera composed by Peter Cornelius. Unlike many typefaces in this genre, Barbieri is a version-rich family of five weights ranging from Thin to Black. These playful, expressive styles work especially well for video games, children’s books, apps, toy brands, T-shirts, logos, packaging, posters, greeting cards, and cover art. [ re-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Barcino
typefaces.desc: Barcino is an elegant sans-serif typeface, inspired by the geometric forms and rational style of 1930s typography. Its clean and balanced design evokes the modernist aesthetics of Bauhaus and constructivism, where precise proportions and uniform strokes create a sober yet bold appearance. The name “Barcino” pays tribute to the ancient Roman name for Barcelona, connecting its classical essence with a contemporary typographic approach. Ideal for branding and editorial design projects, Barcino combines the strength of geometric shapes with timeless modernity. [ typerepublic.com ]

typefaces.name: Bariloche Sans
typefaces.desc: Designed for the unforgettable Villa Beluno in San Carlos de Bariloche, Bariloche Sans takes inspiration from the location’s heritage to evoke the European Vienna Secession, yet with modern appeal. Designed to juxtapose the architectural structure of the hotel with the natural beauty of Patagonia, Bariloche sans balances modernity with softness. Grotesque-inspired boldness is tempered by Nouveau-like curvature accents, Barilcohe Sans is sure to bequeath boldness with a sense of timelessness. [ cantrelltype.com ]

typefaces.name: Barnum
typefaces.desc: Introduced in 1845 by Thorowgood and Co. of London, Clarendon became an instant classic typeface thanks to its robust structure, bold slab serifs and distinctive letterforms. Bridging the gap between traditional serif fonts and the emerging demand for attention-grabbing, bold typefaces in advertising and signage, Clarendon typefaces quickly spread across continents, becoming synonymous with the American Old West and iconic "wanted" posters. In this tradition-steeped lineage, Zetafonts introduces Barnum, designed by Cosimo Lorenzo Pancini as an homage to Clarendon's historical significance. Subtle design innovations rejuvenate this classic model: serifless versions of pivotal characters (C,G,S) add a contemporary flair, emphasizing a departure from tradition with a brutalist approach, while a dynamic weight axis allows Barnum to adapt its letterform to the boldness of the cut. [ zetafonts.com ] Updated in 2024 with italics [ newsletter ].

typefaces.name: Bartok
typefaces.desc: Sarah Kremer’s Bartok redefines the very notion of a type family. Its four styles with their singular designs break with the principle of formal unity usually sought after in such families. Each variant stands out for its expressivity, contributing to the creation of a contrasted whole. The development of Bartok was undertaken in the context of editorial design in order to propose a multifaceted typeface with only four styles. It has been designed to be used for long or short passages of straight text as well as for titles. With the aim of proposing complementary typographic colors, the four styles of Bartok (Regular, Italic, Highlight and Poster) have been designed with different structures and possess distinct weights. Each variant develops formal specificities taken from different moments in the history of typography. Inspired by Humanist typefaces, Bartok Regular is based on the proportions of typefaces derived from incunabula. Its asymmetrical serifs and slanted stems are characteristic of calligraphic script. Its squat counterforms combined with its stability give compositions both pace and balance. Bartok Italic explores the calligraphic model of the chancery hand, to offer

typefaces.name: BC Exalt
typefaces.desc: Exalt has a fascinating family tree. There were two aesthetic starting points at its inception. The first, which has its roots in the early 18th century, is the fascinating book antiqua of English typographer William Caslon and its later imitations. The second point of departure is less refined and showy, a bit of an outcast in the closed world of calligraphy. This work with a flat nib pen, a so-called Atopen, was used in promotional and arrangement workshops in the 1920s and 1960s. Exalt manages to use these two different formative sources consciously and intuitively to create an attractive and, at the same time, usable text typeface. [ briefcasetype.com ]

typefaces.name: BD Karlo
typefaces.desc: BD Karlo is a groovy, cartoony comic titler typeface. It is coming in three flavours: Clean & straight, Clean & wiggly, Subtle distressed & slightly wiggly. The variable font lets you fine-tune the wiggling of the baseline. Some of the capital letters have alternatives to play with. Type your funky comedy. [ typedifferent.com ]

typefaces.name: BD Orange
typefaces.desc: BD Orange is a picturesque scripty grotesk typeface with a large amount of alternatives, discretionary ligatures, variable weights from delicate thin to loud black. With a total of 1025 glyphs BD Orange is a language talent and speaks so many languages including uppercase Cyrillic, Greek and even Japanese Katakana. With its versatility and its balance of classic meets avant-garde this font will serve you as a reliable titling, logotype and bodytext typesetter. [ typedifferent.com ]

typefaces.name: BD Weakon
typefaces.desc: A pixel font that recreates and extends the typeface from Eric Freeman’s 1983 Atari game Weakon .

typefaces.name: Beale
typefaces.desc: Beale is a retro display font that started as a custom lettering project to promote a speaking engagement in Memphis with Creative Works. The letterforms were inspired by the amazing lettering on Blues and Rock ‘N’ Roll records from local pillars, Sun Studio and Stax Records. This display font comes with tons of additional fun characters and glyphs. [ hoodzpahdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Bearklaw
typefaces.desc: Sometimes, creative inspiration is a slow trickle. Other times, it mauls you in a single moment and won’t let go. Bearklaw’s moment occurred when stumbling upon a mail order ad for a ’65 Lyons Maid model Stingray. The title is set in a unique cut of Futura Display—that second cousin once removed of the ever-popular Futura family. As we dove into researching various pre-digital cuts, we found ample space to explore, riff, and expand on that irresistible charm—the oddity that just seems to work. Bearklaw is not a pure revival but a fusion of the ideas we saw at play. These makeshift geometric systems come together to form a powerhouse display family, brought into the modern era. Bearklaw includes various historical alternates, some good ol’ goop, and a wider cut for particular use at small sizes to satiate additional cravings for The ‘Klaw. [ fortfoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Bega
typefaces.desc: Bega is a simplified sans serif typeface. Formal reduction plays a strong role in its design. This is most visible in its ‘spurlessness.’ The visible strokes (or spurs) have been eliminated from the letterforms that would typically feature them. The lack of spurs in Bega is most-clearly visible when you look at the top-left corners of letters like ‘m’, ‘n’, and ‘r’. The Bega family includes eight weights, which range from Thin through Black. Each weight has two fonts on offer: An upright font, and an italic. Bega’s italics are obliques; their letterforms are slanted. The strokes of Bega’s letterforms all appear to be monolinear; that doesn’t mean that Bega is without contrast, however. Thanks to the family’s large number of weights – eight really is a lot – you can combine two or more of them with each other to create headlines that exhibit quite a bit of contrast! Each of Bega’s fonts includes a full range of numerators and denominators, to use when typesetting fractions, etc. The font’s numerals are proportional lining figures; these have the same height as Bega’s uppercase letters. The lowercase letters’ ascenders are tall, and they rise up above the tops of the capital letters

typefaces.name: Belinda New
