typefaces.desc: Belinda New is an updated version of the original Belinda I designed in 2011. Belinda New is a smooth, lining brush script font with a vintage and retro feel. It has two sets of uppercase and many alternates for lowercase letters. It is an excellent choice to use in logos, headlines and packages. You can also match it with a serif or sans serif fonts and use it as a secondary font in web design, magazines and branding.

typefaces.name: Bellucci
typefaces.desc: Bellucci is the redesign of Ramiro Espinoza’s first typeface, Mabella. This experimental alphabet was used for some time as headline font in ‘Jazz’, an e-zine. Being not happy with the original design, he decided to redraw it completely and add 3 new weights. Bellucci is a constructivist, modular, compressed family intended for headlines and posters. The name is an homage to Mabel Bellucci, an Argentinian feminist activist. [ re-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Berkeley Mono
typefaces.desc: Berkeley Mono is a love letter to the golden era of computing. The era that gave rise to a generation of people who celebrated automation and reveled in the joy of computing, when transistors replaced cogs, and machine-readable typefaces were developed, for when humans and machines truly interfaced on an unprecedented scale. It wears a UNIX T-shirt and aspires to be etched on control panels in black synthetic lacquer. It is Adrian Frutiger visits Bell Labs. It is Gene Kranz's command. It operates with calibrated precision and has a datasheet. Berkeley Mono is a typeface for professionals. [ usgraphics.com ]

typefaces.name: Berlingske Typewriter
typefaces.desc: Berlingske Typewriter has converted the essentially elegant and exclusive touch into a style that mimics the look of a typewriter while still living up to the demands of modern use. It is, in contrast to a typical typewriter, not monospaced but proportionally spaced, so that the text appears with identical spacing between letters, thereby maintaining a balanced appearance. It is ideally suited for body text and headlines where it simultaneously expresses a classic and modern style. [ playtype.com ]

typefaces.name: Bertin
typefaces.desc: Designed by Roman Seban, the modular typeface Bertin is inspired by the work of the famous French cartographer Jacques Bertin and Dutch graphic designer Jurriaan Schrofer. In 1967, Jacques Bertin (1918–2010) published Semiology of Graphics: Diagrams, Networks, Maps , a fundamental treatise in contemporary cartographic thinking. In this book, he established a series of parameters for representing information, defining six visual variables which he used to construct his graphical system. In 1973, Jurriaan Schrofer (1926–1990) designed the cover of a reprint of Semiology of Graphics . He proposed a typographic application of Bertin’s graphical system. His typeface, constructed on a grid with a highly rigorous approach, typographically illustrates the six visual variables defined by the cartographer. With Bertin, Roman Seban presents a synthetic and revitalized interpretation of both the cartographer’s and the graphic designer’s work. Thanks to variable font technology, the different styles of the typeface combine multiple axes of visual variables. [ 205.tf ]

typefaces.name: Betània Patmos
typefaces.desc: Betània Patmos has an austere morphology, free of ornaments, to facilitate recognition the ductus of the letters. It isn’t a display typeface; it’s a script typeface intended for early reading texts. [ betaniapatmos.huertatipografica.com ]

typefaces.name: Beverly Drive
typefaces.desc: Beverly Drive is a left-leaning script font from Hoodzpah, Inc. inspired by Beverly Hills: from the posh Rodeo shop signs, to the kitschy apartment complex logos. Beverly Drive is the kind of font you can dress up (holiday cards or wedding invitations) or dress down (can’t you just imagine this on a laminated diner menu?). [ hoodzpahdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Beverly Drive Right
typefaces.desc: Beverly Drive is a retro script font with a low x height, slightly exaggerated cap height, and 2 unique style sets to suit any occasion. You can dress up (holiday cards or wedding invitations) or dress down (restaurant logo or beer labels). Click on the Licenses tab to see how you can use this font. [ hoodzpahdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: BianZhiDai
typefaces.desc: bianzhidai is a font inspired by ASCII art shading character and 编织袋 (woven plastic bags). Initially constructed in GDC (glyphdrawingclub, an online drawing tool made by @heikkiveikko and Ian Tuomi), BianZhiDai thrives in color, especially when you experiment with different fill/stroke combinations. Its modular nature, developed in Glyphs, allows for endless customization. [ notyourtype.nl ]

typefaces.name: Big Issue
typefaces.desc: The Big Issue superfamily is a modern grotesque sans developed with The Big Issue magazine. It started with a bold, single-weight typeface for the 30th-anniversary cover, created in collaboration with Pentagram. Since then, it’s grown into a flexible family featuring Narrow, Standard, Wide, and XWide widths, offering solutions for both print and digital needs. Its design is rooted in historical British grotesque typography, blending classic typographic influences with modern-day functionality. [ blast-foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Big Shoulders
typefaces.desc: Part of the Chicago Design System and released as open-souce.

typefaces.name: Bigante
typefaces.desc: Bigante is a big, giant superfamily with two variants: Solid and Inline, offering six weights and seven widths. Its constructed design interprets rounded corners as three 30° angles, resulting in edged terminals and twelve-sided dots. While it sounds functional, this rounded-like semi-serif enhances the appearance, creating a friendly aesthetic. The lowercase alphabet features a high x-height. For versatile use in display and advertising, the multitude of fonts enables flexibility. Captivating with a linear structure, it associates with modern architecture, tactical sports, space travel, and futuristic technology. [ vibrant-types.com ]

typefaces.name: Bilo Thai
typefaces.desc: The Thai script companion to Bilo .

typefaces.name: Bisbee
typefaces.desc: Arabic added in 2024.

typefaces.name: Bitum
typefaces.desc: Bitum is a new sans that defies conventional classification, with nods to such disparate references as early geometric sans serifs and modular lettering used in wayfinding signage. The former influences lend sheer energy of breaking new ground while the latter supply industrial pragmatism and uniform proportions. In its display version Bitum calls attention to itself in the manner of the carefully-lettered street signs of old West Berlin—its perennial calling card. The type’s strong personality is determined by a quirky lowercase a, the lowercase s with a stubbornly horizontal connecting stroke, and the uppercase M with a conspicuously low vertex. Notwithstanding its idiosyncrasies, the type’s low stroke contrast, consistent proportions, and generous x-height with short ascenders and descenders make it highly readable in small sizes resulting in solid and even setting. [ brownfox.org ]

typefaces.name: Bitzer
typefaces.desc: An experiment in testing boundaries, Bitzer selectively observes and breaks the established rules of Latin flat brush calligraphy. Bitzer speaks with a voice that is equal parts trustworthy and contemporary. Cutting edge without feeling overly irreverent. A visual balance of order and chaos… you get the idea. Bitzer was designed for use in headlines, logotypes and editorial design. Its narrow proportions aren’t exaggerated but allow for succinct delivery within a few lines of text. Sharp twists of the pen give the letters a bottom-heavy quality, adding a sense of gravity into the visual texture, which becomes more pronounced in heavier weights. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Bizzarri
typefaces.desc: Introducing Bizzarri: a dynamic type family drawing inspiration from the sleek lines of racing cars. With two distinct subfamilies – Bizzarri Headline and Bizzarri Text – this versatile typeface bridges the gap between impactful display work and legible body text. Tall ascenders, high contrast, and angular serifs give Bizzarri Headline version a sophisticated and bold presence in large formats. In contrast, Bizzarri Text subfamily softens these features, providing clarity and comfort for extended reading without sacrificing personality. The italics strike a unique balance between elegance and sharpness, enhancing the family’s versatility. [ blast-foundry.com ] Debuted on Future Fonts in 2018, from which it graduated in October 2024.

typefaces.name: Blackbike Two
typefaces.desc: Originally released in 2017 as Blackbike, updated in February 2025 and renamed to Blackbike Two. Note: the sample image shows the original Blackbike, as published by Typeverything.

typefaces.name: Blacker Pro
typefaces.desc: Updated in November 2024 with axes for width, weight, and optical size.

typefaces.name: Blak
typefaces.desc: Blak belongs to a type series designed for the now defunct magazine Suite. Our collection is giving this chubby typeface a second life. Blak has a strong geometric feel, combined with a hard counterform. A confident typeface for big and bold statements. [ extratype.com ]

typefaces.name: Blei
typefaces.desc: Stretching and squishing fonts can distort the relative thickness of horizontal and vertical stems. While this practice is often criticized, Blei views these effects as acceptable from a creative perspective. However, elements like shoulders, bowls, and terminals can suffer, leading to a design that may appear amateurish or rushed, along with potential issues in letter spacing. Blei addresses these concerns with careful corrections, resulting in a more polished typeface. It’s a partially geometric, sans-serif, single-weight typeface that comes in five widths, spanning three distinct styles: Straight, Inflated and Rounded. [ pfa-typefaces.com ]

typefaces.name: BN Arora
typefaces.desc: An interpretation of Dante (Schelter & Giesecke, 1900).

typefaces.name: BN Binder
typefaces.desc: Based on Stan Control (VGC, 1973) [ instagram.com , fontsinuse.com ].

typefaces.name: BN Boxer
typefaces.desc: BN Boxer evokes unapologetic strength and striking visual impact. This bold, blocky display typeface commands attention with its geometric precision and powerful, grid-like forms. Designed for high-impact headlines, branding, and posters. Modeled after vintage type specimen “ Square ” by Mecanorma. [ bnicks.com ]

typefaces.name: BN Crocker
typefaces.desc: With a brutalist yet refined approach, BN Crocker maintains a sharp balance between vintage typographic influence and modern-day utility. Its tightly spaced, high-impact structure is designed to fill space with authority, making it perfect for branding, posters, editorial headlines, and any project that needs a dose of unapologetic boldness. [ bnicks.com ] Inspired by Permanent Massiv (Ludwig & Mayer, 1967).

typefaces.name: BN Danimal
typefaces.desc: A bold display typeface with a quirky & playful spirit. This typeface features strikingly thick characters with a subtle “italic” form that create a visually captivating appeal. [ bnicks.com ]

typefaces.name: BN Gallant
typefaces.desc: An uncredited interpretation of Churchward Typestyle (2002) [ fontsinuse.com ].

typefaces.name: BN Hellmade
typefaces.desc: An interpretation of ITC Honda (ITC, 1970).

typefaces.name: BN Kendall
typefaces.desc: A contrasted sans serif typeface. The design appears to descend from lettering by Eugen Nerdinger and Lisa Beck. [ fontsinuse.com ]

typefaces.name: BN Kossell
typefaces.desc: A loose interpretation of Wiegands Adbold (Berthold, 1974) [ fontsinuse.com ].

typefaces.name: BN Mishmash
typefaces.desc: An uncredited digitization of Kellie / Kathrine [ instagram.com ].

typefaces.name: BN Mitchel
typefaces.desc: BN Mitchel combines bold, blocky forms with a handcrafted edge, giving it a raw and authentic personality. It’s versatile yet unmistakably unique, ideal for conveying strength and creativity with a touch of imperfection. Perfect for projects that demand attention: BN Mitchel is more than a typeface—it’s a statement. [ bnicks.com ]

typefaces.name: BN Numa
typefaces.desc: BN Numa Pro is a newer version of BN Numa with more sharply defined features.

typefaces.name: BN Numa Pro
typefaces.desc: A version of BN Numa with more sharply defined features.

typefaces.name: BN Pooly
typefaces.desc: A display typeface inspired by Rodger , by way of the Public Pool branding.

typefaces.name: BN Rambunk
typefaces.desc: Experience the quirky charm of "BN Rambunk", a typeface that combines playful irregularity with a bold, assertive style. Perfect for brands that dare to be different, "Rambunk" is designed to grab attention with its unique character shapes and strikingly uneven lines. This typeface is versatile enough for eye-catching headlines, standout display copy, or any project that demands a touch of whimsy and a strong visual presence. Inspired by vintage type specimen "Implode" with updated forms and new glyph additions. [ bnicks.com ]

typefaces.name: BN Sailor
typefaces.desc: According to Fonts in Use, an uncredited interpretation of Adriana , a film typeface of unknown origin.

typefaces.name: BN Sammy
typefaces.desc: An interpretation of Corvina Black (VGC, 1973).

typefaces.name: BN Social
typefaces.desc: Appears to be an interpretation of Harry [ fontsinuse.com ].

typefaces.name: BN Ventura
typefaces.desc: BN Ventura blends bold retro energy with a modern aesthetic, creating a typeface that is as versatile and impactful. Its wide, curvaceous letterforms and clean tapered lines evoke a sense of confidence and sophistication, making it ideal for branding, editorial headlines, signage, and expressive design projects. [ bnicks.com ]

typefaces.name: BN Zipline
typefaces.desc: Based on the specimen for a typeface called Apollo-fotoheadline [ instagram.com ], apparently related to Giorgio [ fontsinuse.com ].

typefaces.name: Bogart
typefaces.desc: Updated in 2024 with a range of condensed weights [ newsletter ].

typefaces.name: Bogue
typefaces.desc: Bogue is a soft serif type family of 8 weights and matching italics. The soft forms gives it a friendly and approachable character with a hint of retro feeling. Bogue comes with a lots of stylistic alternates that makes it very versatile in various uses like logos, editorial design, branding, web design, package design and much more. You can use it to create short powerful phrases and headlines and also use it in longer text like lead paragraphs and body texts.

typefaces.name: Bogue Slab
typefaces.desc: Bogue is a slab serif type family of 8 weights and matching italics. Bogue Slab comes with a lots of stylistic alternates that makes it very versatile in various uses like logos, editorial design, branding, web design, package design and much more. You can use it to create short powerful phrases and headlines and also use it in longer text like lead paragraphs and body texts.

typefaces.name: Bolivia
typefaces.desc: This typeface started as an interpretation of Albert Hollenstein’s famous « Brasilia » from 1958. A second version (G) with vertical terminals was drawn in order to let the modernistic feeling collide with a more humanistic expression. The untypical long tails of /f, /j, /r and /t are emphasized and accompanied with stylistic alternatives to give it a more contemporary feeling. [ deinwaller.com ]

typefaces.name: Boogie School Sans
typefaces.desc: Updated in 2019.

typefaces.name: Boogie School Serif
typefaces.desc: Updated in 2022.

typefaces.name: Booklet Serif
typefaces.desc: Booklet Serif is a modern versatile serif, part of the Booklet typeface superfamily. Slender proportions, calm rhythm, elegant ovals and nontrivial glyph designs — as always, we have mixed tradition with relevance, moderation with emotion. This serif can be used as both its own independent typeface and as a pair for Booklet Sans. [ brownfox.org ] Italic style added January 2025.

typefaces.name: Boomville
typefaces.desc: Boomville is a bouncy and upright script font. It is fun and lively with a lot of personality. This script is sketched with quick brush strokes with a pointed brush to achieve this casual and playful feeling.

typefaces.name: Booster
typefaces.desc: Drawing inspiration from the classic Modern Gothic of the late 19th century by Barnhart Brothers & Spindler, this expansive collection reinterprets a wide, massive geometric grotesque with a contemporary twist. With 93 fonts spread across 6 diverse subfamilies — Sans, Rounded, Pixel, Polygonal, Stencil, and Inktrap — Booster Collection offers a rich toolbox that adapts seamlessly to a variety of design challenges. Each of these subfamilies acts as a unique “buff,” enhancing different aspects of a design’s personality and function. At its core, Booster Collection features clean, precise forms enhanced by subtle rounded details — such as softened character tails and capsule-like accents on additional symbols and diacritics — that inject a playful energy into its bold structure. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Booton
typefaces.desc: Booton is a versatile sans-serif typeface engineered for the digital age. Its unique uni-width feature maintains consistent glyph widths across all weights and styles, ensuring stable spacing and alignment—ideal for button designs and digital interactions like hover effects. Booton’s design enhances readability on screens with a high x-height and legibility-focused elements like ink traps and strong tapering at stem connections. Distinctive glyph shapes in the lowercase “l” and uppercase “t”, alongside subtle cropped diagonals, contribute to its adaptability. [ displaay.net ]

typefaces.name: Borel
typefaces.desc: Initiated as a research project at ANRT in 2017 and released as an open-source font in 2023.

typefaces.name: Borges Titling
typefaces.desc: Specially conceived for a bookish atmosphere, Borges Titling is a delicately spirited roman that goes nicely together with the Borges text versions. With more economical vertical proportions than the text version, it has a slightly more accentuated stroke contrast, its serifs are slightly more elongated and its overall appearance is more delicate. The Borges type family pays homage to the fantastic work of writer Jorge Luis Borges. His writing technique, that of a meticulous and tireless goldsmith, in relentless pursuit of the perfect word, suggested a clean, economical but elegant letterform. [ pampatype.com ] Originally released as a pair of solid and open styles named Borges Título. The open style was expanded in 2025 into Borges Open , and the solid style renamed Borges Titling.

typefaces.name: Bork
typefaces.desc: Bork is a display typeface that was inspired by an exercise in blackletter calligraphy. The style’s characteristic dark texture is seen mainly in the lowercase, with uniform spacing (where counterspace equals letterspace), shapes that recall the straight, interrupted strokes used in that style of writing, and the peculiar construction of certain letters. On the other hand, the uppercase aims for a more conventional roman construction, making it more legible for modern-day readers.

typefaces.name: Borogodó
typefaces.desc: Borogodó is a high contrast sans-serif in three optical sizes, bringing couture looks with a tropical feel to any part of your design project. Borogodó in Brazilian Portuguese is often used to describe someone or something that has a special charm, charisma, or appeal, and our Borogodó is meant to add this swag to your branding, packaging and editorial projects in any size you may need it. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Boulevard
typefaces.desc: Boulevard is an homage to Ed Ruscha’s typeface Boy Scout Utility Modern, used by the artist for the majority of his artworks. Through a large study of these works, we have redrawn a typeface maintaining all the proportional irregularities and intuitive non-typographical letter-shapes that Ruscha drew, then expanded into a family of 8 weights. The name is also a reference to the city of Los Angeles and the city's roads so frequently depicted in Ruscha's work. The Outline family variation expands the project further into a revival of US vernacular letterforms of the 1970s. It has a tall x-height and is very functional at tiny sizes for screen usage while maintaining its charm at large display sizes. [ abc-etc.com ]

typefaces.name: Boulevard Outline
typefaces.desc: Boulevard is an homage to Ed Ruscha’s typeface Boy Scout Utility Modern, used by the artist for the majority of his artworks. Through a large study of these works, we have redrawn a typeface maintaining all the proportional irregularities and intuitive non-typographical letter-shapes that Ruscha drew, then expanded into a family of 8 weights. The name is also a reference to the city of Los Angeles and the city's roads so frequently depicted in Ruscha's work. The Outline family variation expands the project further into a revival of US vernacular letterforms of the 1970s. It has a tall x-height and is very functional at tiny sizes for screen usage while maintaining its charm at large display sizes. [ abc-etc.com ]

typefaces.name: Bourget
typefaces.desc: Bourget is a Display-Sans, which is inspired by the Art Déco Typography of the 1920’s, 1930’s years. It has a very characteristic and unique style by its thin line through every letter. [ fontcuisine.com ]

typefaces.name: Bouuuuuh
typefaces.desc: Just like our favorite TV Shows (Brooklyn Nine-Nine, The Office (US), or obviously, The Simpsons), Lift Type has its own “Halloween Special”. Having started in 2017 with the regular weight, Bouuuuuh is now a collection of all cap Typefaces, inspired by old comic tilting. A cool excuse for experimenting a mix between scary and funny. The typeface is available 1 month for free download, and will be back again next year, with maybe an additional piece to the Bouuuuuh collection… [ lift-type.fr ]

typefaces.name: Bremen
typefaces.desc: Bremen is an all-caps display typeface designed in the style of the 1920s and early thirties. All forms of display typography flourished in Europe and nowhere more than in Germany and Austria. German poster design set a high creative standard, stimulating the design of a marvelous group of sinuous and sparkling display letterforms. Richard Lipton designed Bremen for Font Bureau after a set of freehand capitals on a poster designed by lettering artist Ludwig Holwein in 1922. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Brezel Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Brezel Grotesk, a sans-serif typeface, embodies simplicity and draws inspiration from the charm of classic 19th-century Grotesques. Infused with the regular yet organic shapes reminiscent of a Bavarian pretzel («Brezn»), this typeface marries readability in small point sizes with distinctiveness in larger formats, boasting unique terminal details. Designed to excel across diverse text settings, Brezel Grotesk finds its place in a broad spectrum of applications. The typeface family now consists of 8 styles, featuring 4 weights complemented by corresponding italics. Each style encompasses an extended Latin character set, ensuring versatility and adaptability for a multitude of design purposes. [ serpentype.com ]

typefaces.name: Brick
typefaces.desc: Previously released with Colophon Foundry in 2019.

typefaces.name: Brill
typefaces.desc: The Brill types were commissioned in 2008 by the venerable Dutch academic publishing company Koninklijke Brill, with the goal of establishing a consistent house style across the typography of their many book series and journals. Brill began publishing at Leiden in 1683, and the range of humanities subjects they now cover requires many specialised characters, including extensive symbol sets, phonetic notation alphabets, historical letters and numbers, and diacritics for both modern orthographies and transcription of ancient languages. [ tiro.com ]

typefaces.name: Brinkhuis
typefaces.desc: This typeface is a liberal interpretation of the Art-Deco lettering found on several facades of the famous avant-garde Betondorp neighborhood located in Watergraafsmeer, Amsterdam. The original letters were probably designed by the Dutch architect Dick Greiner. Paula Mastrangelo fixed many inconsistencies in the original model, completely redefined several letters, added punctuation marks, and turned a simple alphabet into a striking typeface, suitable for designing outstanding posters, book covers and logos. [ re-type.com ] Moved to the Brutal Types catalog in 2025.

typefaces.name: Brise
typefaces.desc: Brise is a stencil type family inspired by the interplay between air and structure. Like a breeze drifting through space, its forms are shaped by both presence and absence. Rooted in the architectural idea of the brise-soleil, Brise explores how deliberate gaps can give rhythm, clarity, and breath to type. The family started with Text, designed for subtlety and flow; Display, more condensed and assertive; and Extreme, bold but still airy and more expressive. The additional weights Text Regular and Display Bold expand its usability. Stencil and breeze share a paradox: the play between the visible and the invisible. A stencil is defined as much by its strokes as by the voids that interrupt them. These gaps are not losses but intentions, precise pauses that give structure its rhythm, its balance between weight and air. Born from necessity, stencil type has moved beyond the realm of industry and function. [ type-o-tones.com ]

typefaces.name: Brito
typefaces.desc: Inherited from Fañch Le Henaff’s early work (Tir na Nog, in 1995), the Brito typeface is stabilised and increased for the first time between 2011 and 2013 in partnership with Yoann De Roeck & Malou Verlomme. Today, the Brito is fully upgraded with new glyphs allowing to support every European and Celtic languages, it also offers stylistic alternates close to the original oncial designs. It is now available in 6 weights. [ skritur.eu ] Italics added in October 2024.

typefaces.name: Broaduro
typefaces.desc: Broaduro had its origins in type explorations based on cigar branding from the Caribbean region. Its skeleton is based on Morris Fuller Benton’s typeface Broadway (think of the Miami Vice logo). What I ended up with was a Latin-flavored take on Broadway, a sort of calligraphic Art Deco design. Outline, inset, and engraved stroke layers were incorporated as a reference to the cigar box and cigar label influences that inspired the project in the first place. [ midwesttype.com ]

typefaces.name: Bronzo
typefaces.desc: Originally designed by Rick Valicenti and Mouli Marur in 1990 for Gilbert Paper’s ESSE, revived and expanded by Patric King in 2023.

typefaces.name: Brook
typefaces.desc: Originally designed for a theater identity, Brook is a monospaced typeface revisiting old typewriter fonts. The family consists of two contrasting styles that complement one another: a straightforward roman and a fancy italic. [ ma-ma-type.com ] Originally designed in 2017 and made available after the launch of the foundry. Fonts in Use places it in 2022 [ fontsinuse.com ].

typefaces.name: Brubeck
typefaces.desc: While I was having a drink in Rotterdam’s famous «Hotel New York», I stared at one of Dave Brubeck’s best live LPs, wondering what typeface they used on the cover. After days of researching, I still couldn’t find it — so I drew my own version. What you see is an attempt to inherit this distinct 60s, phototype feeling. This set of letters is made to be set tight and big. [ deinwaller.com ]

typefaces.name: Brum
typefaces.desc: A love letter to informal, handwritten shapes, Brum is influenced by writing with both a flat brush and a felt tip marker. With an overall soft character and simplified shape construction, it feels approachable and inviting without losing even one ounce of its core credibility. Its tiny inconsistencies and imperfections round off the off-the-cuff look. Conceived as a headline typeface, Brum thrives the most when it’s set in a grand and bold format. [ hottype.co ]

typefaces.name: Bruna
typefaces.desc: [ behance.net ]

typefaces.name: Brzo
typefaces.desc: BRZO is a 5 style display typeface inspired by the boldness of 90's basketball graphics. Growing up my room teemed with Dream Team posters, Fleer trading cards and Eastbay catalogs. Fast forward 20 years this influential era manifested into a full bodied italic sans serif wanting a jersey to be sewn on. BRZO’s intentionally tight letter spacing gives a headline an additional punch. Stack it, set it diagonally or use a drop shadow… no matter the occasion BRZO’s ready to play. [ nuformtype.com ]

typefaces.name: BST Symbol
typefaces.desc: A geometric sans serif that draws inspiration from DIN-style typefaces and early Bauhaus styles.

typefaces.name: Bugrino
typefaces.desc: Bugrino is a sans serif typeface with a distinctive combination of smooth and structured elements. The typeface is available in a comprehensive range of sixteen weights, from the lightest Thin to the boldest Black, providing flexibility for various design needs. Its design integrates subtle curves and defined lines, creating a balanced and modern aesthetic that adapts well to different typographic settings. In text applications, Bugrino offers a unique visual effect that enhances readability while maintaining a refined appearance. For headlines and display usage, its diverse weights ensure prominence and clarity, making it a versatile choice for projects that require both nuanced detail and strong visual impact. [ gunesmuhittin.com ] The creative journey of Bugrino commenced with the idea of achieving a harmonious balance between sharp and soft lines. The design process took inspiration from the Blur and Huit typefaces, incorporating sharp lines and introducing unique symbols and characters. When utilized in text, Bugrino intends to create a blurred effect, enhancing its visual impact. However, in display applications, the typeface presents itself as unconventional and experimental

typefaces.name: Bull-5
typefaces.desc: Bull-5, designed by David Einwaller, derives from a particular style of typewriter fonts that emerged in the 1960s, presumably introduced through Olivetti—an Italian manufacturer of office products. The project began by digitizing printed type samples spotted on labels of photographic prints from the 1980s, which were sold due to the closure of an American newspaper archive. To preserve its raw and mechanical character, Bull-5’s Mono styles are drawn in coherence with the source material, including all their quirks and irregular proportions. They are accompanied by Proportional styles for greater legibility and Typewriter styles to embrace another iconic characteristic of typewriter fonts. [ tightype.com ] Initially released in 2022 in one weight, expanded in August 2024 to six weights across the three styles: proportional, monospaced, and typewriter. I had seen a sample of this typeface a few years back when I was researching typewriter-designs, but was never able to track down a good source. In 2019 a friend (and talented designer ) purchased photographic prints from a closure of a newspaper archive and who’d believe it, all the images were labeled with this exact typeface. I dig

typefaces.name: Bulo
typefaces.desc: Bulo is a sanserif typeface with clear and concise letterforms. It follows a mechanically based construction, but with a slight humanistic touch, particularly in its lowercase and italics. It has been designed for newspaper and magazine contexts, thus the feature of economy in its use of space, both horizontal –through its narrow proportions– and vertical –with its short ascenders and descenders. In addition it has a generous x-height and reduced uppercase. Bulo Rounded is a Real Rounded. What I mean with real rounded is that not only the beginning and the end of the strokes are rounded, but also the counters and the intersections of the glyphs. The result is a smooth effect that brings warm feeling, and the rounded text is perceived in a logical and natural way. [ typografies.com ]

typefaces.name: Bw Darius
typefaces.desc: Designed by Alberto Romanos, Bw Darius is an elegant wedge serif typeface, halfway between the transitional and didone genres, with a sharper approach to terminals without falling on the stiffness of the didones. The wide skeleton, modern proportions and high contrast, all contribute to the opulent personality of this font. [ brandingwithtype.com ] Updated in November 2024 (announced February 2025) with Medium and Extra Bold weights.

typefaces.name: Cabina
typefaces.desc: Cabina was inspired by the inscription “TELEPHONE” on the K2 & K3 red telephone box (or telephone kiosk) designed by Sir Giles Gilbert Scott, which are found in the streets of the United Kingdom, Malta, Bermuda and Gibraltar. The neoclassic geometry of the letterforms is combined with small sharp wedge serifs, giving this font a look that merges sans serif modernism with a humanist twist. [ abc-etc.com ]

typefaces.name: Cæsura
typefaces.desc: Cæsura is a bold display typeface that draws from a rich blend of influences, seamlessly merging the stoic, structured forms of mid-century European signage with the fluid, expressive strokes of Japanese calligraphy. Available in a single Bold weight, it is crafted specifically for headings where its striking character and high contrast can take center stage. Cæsura’s design plays with exaggerated strokes and sweeping swashes, balancing rigid, upright structures with dramatic, knife-like cuts that slice through the glyphs, creating a dynamic tension that feels both timeless and distinctly modern. The currency symbols, for instance, feature sharp, tailored cuts that offer a contemporary reinterpretation of familiar shapes. [ black-foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Cafeteria
typefaces.desc: The irregularities normally found in handwriting can also enliven sans serif letterforms. In Cafeteria, Tobias Frere-Jones took special care to balance activity with legibility, drawing a freeform sans serif that is condensed but in no way stiff. [ store.typenetwork.com ] Originally released by Font Bureau in 1993 and moved to Frere–Jones Type in 2020 [ fontsinuse.com ], available through Type Network and added to the foundry’s website in December 2024.

typefaces.name: Cake4Freaks
typefaces.desc: Inspired by Gerrit Noordzĳ’s seminal sketching technique, Cake4Freaks explores zigzags as sources of legibility and obfuscation. At large sizes, the zigzags carve the page into abstraction—darting, curving, crossing in a labyrinth of letterforms organic and bizarre. At small sizes, however, they solidify into the silvery shapes of a textface modeled on the broad nib pen, just as Noordzĳ intended. Cake4Freaks is a traditionally crafted typeface, drawn from scratch with outlines and overlaps, not an encoded effect applied to a preexisting design. This labor of love is the secret ingredient that keeps Cake4Freaks unrehearsed and optically adjusted. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Cako
typefaces.desc: What makes Cako unique is its very graphic shapes of letters and serifs and its numerous stylistic alternates – giving the typeface a great rythm. Cako has three contrasted weights, black, regular and thin, offering several degrees of impact. The drawing of Cako black is characterized by big contrasts between thicks and thins, fine details and spiky terminals. [ vj-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Camelion
typefaces.desc: Clear and chiseled, Camelion renders a highly legible paragraph, without sacrificing warmth and humanity. […] It has origins as a slanted roman and upright italic, reversing the attributes of these common roles in an interesting and irreverent way. [ ohnotype.co ]

typefaces.name: Campingo Indoor
typefaces.desc: Campingo Indoor is the perfect counterpart to Campingo. With its bold, blocky style, it celebrates the weightiest of letterforms. Hidden within its robust design are precise, striking typographic details, making it a powerhouse of both form and function. [ typefaces.pizza ]

typefaces.name: Canon Grotesque
typefaces.desc: Canon Grotesque is a playful type family distinguished by its round-sided sans-serif design with slightly closed terminals reminiscent of the grotesques from the early 20th century. Its compressed form and tight spacing make Canon Grotesque ideal for use in posters, billboards, headers, and logos. The type family also includes wide alternates for round-shaped characters, introducing a dynamic change in tempo within compositions and creating a fresh reading experience. [ futurefonts.com ] Published on Future Fonts as two separate projects, one for the Latin-only version and another for the bi-scriptual version . Links for this entry refer to the Latin version.

typefaces.name: Canopée
typefaces.desc: Canopée was created in 2016 by Jérémy Schneider as part of the new artistic direction of the magazine Welcome To The Jungle. It is an uppercase-only typeface and a singular take on New York’s 1960 store signs. The combination of condensed glyphs with large-rounded O, C and G’s as well as the few alternates available give the font a strong rhythm, perfectly fit for titles. [ vj-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Canto
typefaces.desc: Canto is a series of typefaces inspired by Edward M. Catich’s seminal thesis on the origins of the Roman inscriptional style, such as that found on Trajan’s column. Richard Lipton’s design traces the path from an expressive, preparatory Brush (with Brush Open to preserve gestural details at smaller sizes), through informal Pen, to the formal Roman. Classical capitals are accompanied by Lipton’s own calligraphic lowercase, small caps, and swashes. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Cantrell Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Cantrell Grotesk takes inspiration from Benjamin Krebs Nachfolger’s Phönix-Grotesk specimen, yet with a humanist tilt that adds nuance and softness to balance its austerity. It offers an approachable, yet energetic personality with dynamic flexibility that can work with luxury brands and sports brands, ornate packaging or a more modern and minimal aesthetic. From the ashes, Cantrell Grotesk breathes life once again into the grotesk type category and lends air to any type artisan. [ cantrelltype.com ]

typefaces.name: Capek
typefaces.desc: Capek is a blackletter sans serif, whose forms are inspired by the technophile universe and science fiction. With its expressionist and modular style, influenced by display faces created in Europe and the United States on the margins of the “New Typography”, it is a design that plays with contrasts, intended for display and short texts. Capek is atypical, which will bring an undeniably original touch to your projects in the fields of music, art, technology, digital, and even industrial. [ typofonderie.com ]

typefaces.name: Cardinal Elite
typefaces.desc: Cardinal Elite harks back to an era of low-tech typefaces, with a vibe navigating between organic, classic text typefaces, and plastic, of contemporary digital type. Although Cardinal visibly has all the traits of conventional workhorse typefaces, it bears its own dryness and rigidity, giving the text a distinct and somewhat mechanical appearance. Further accentuated by the fixed-width, yet often uneven and irregular spacing between letters, Cardinal Elite’s simple and no-nonsense appearance reflects its somewhat utilitarian nature, just like the machines it is meant to emulate. Rugged, cold and metallic, Cardinal Elite adheres to a rigid grid of digital typography where each character occupies the same fixed width, resulting in a stark, unyielding visual uniformity. The typeface was initially commissioned by art director Mochizuki Akiho of Japanese fashion magazine Dossier. [ productiontype.com ] Accessible by enrollment into Production Type’s Beta program.

typefaces.name: Cardinal Tech
typefaces.desc: Accessible by enrollment into Production Type’s Beta program.

typefaces.name: Cardone
typefaces.desc: Cardone, developed between 2016 and 2021 is a singular interpretation of early so-called Scottish modern faces, later called Scotch Roman. Specifically created for editorial design, this serif typeface seeks an ideal balance between elegance and robustness: its ample curves contrast with the brutality of its lines and the verticality of its axis. The five weights of Cardone ranging from Thin to Bold each with its own italic have been designed separately so as to emphasize the uniqueness of their design. Without sacrificing the elegance of Scottish modern faces, each style is pushed to the point of extreme simplicity and efficiency, both in their structure and in every formal detail. Functional and legible, the typeface has been designed mainly for use with running text. Nevertheless the constant thickness of Thin or, inversely, the stark contrast of Bold allows Cardone to stand out when used in titles. To extend its efficiency to multiple uses, the Cardone type family is also available in a Micro version (Regular and Italic) intended for settings in smaller than eight points. The design displays forms that are radical, mechanical and straightforward. [ 205.tf ]

typefaces.name: Carp
typefaces.desc: Carp is Marie Otsuka’s streamlined take on the humanist sans-serif genre inspired by Excoffon’s Antique Olive , where the tops are heavier than the bottom parts of the letter. In Carp, this asymmetric weight balance and contrast is exaggerated in the heavier styles, while the lighter styles lean toward a more functional monolinear sans. Complete with variable axes across width and weight, the result is a versatile family suitable for both expressive display and robust body text. [ occupantfonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Caryotype
typefaces.desc: Caryotype is a chunky, quirky and geometric font designed by Vicente Granger. This font is primarily inspired by a karyotype, the general appearance of the complete set of chromosomes. This character, with his playful, generous and lively shapes, is very suitable for display use and for body text as well. Caryotype is the «go to» font if you need something bold and charismatic, experimental and retro with a modern twist. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Caslon Ionic
typefaces.desc: Bolder and more robust than the modern, yet lighter and more refined than the Egyptian, the Ionic with its bracketed serif was another innovation of the nineteenth century. Lesser known than Thorowgood’s Clarendon, Caslon’s Ionic No. 2 is a superb example of the form and greatly influenced the newspaper fonts of the next century. With additional weights and a matching Egyptian companion, Antique No. 6, it is a masterpiece of type designed to be robust and legible. [ commercialtype.com ]

typefaces.name: Caslon Ionic Rounded
typefaces.desc: Bolder and more robust than the modern, yet lighter and more refined than the Egyptian, the Ionic with its bracketed serif was another innovation of the nineteenth century. Lesser known than Thorowgood’s Clarendon, Caslon’s Ionic No. 2 is a superb example of the form and greatly influenced the newspaper fonts of the next century. Greg Gazdowicz created the Rounded variant of Caslon Ionic in 2025. [ vault.commercialtype.com ]

typefaces.name: Caslonian
typefaces.desc: Caslonian is an old style influenced by various Caslon metal cuts, including the ones from Fonderie Caslon in Paris. [ caslonian.typofonderie.com ] Produced in four optical sizes (S to XL) in upright and italic, with open counterparts.

typefaces.name: Category
typefaces.desc: Bienvenue au studio. In our routine, our well-organized mess filled with our everyday-work life objects. Category is a sensible and mocking expression of our working process: we started with the will of drawing a useful, legible, balanced, elegant text font. And this inevitable moment happened when we felt the urge to add stronger stylistic details. Almost unintentionally. Category mixes business with pleasure. It’s a sans serif font with utilitarian and stylistic functions. It was designed with this specific balance so it can be used for any kind of content: long texts, body-copy, titles, logotypes. We like to think of Category as a universal and friendly font with a slight touch of eccentricity. It brings something sensitive to the geometric grotesk genre. The design originated from geometrical shapes with low-contrast and it features some graphic singularities that make it pure and elegant but yet reasonably curvy and funny. Lower-cases a g j and y are the best demonstration of that balance. The CBRP bring style to the uppercases set with its original angles. Could we have the audacity to say Category is square yet round? [ vj-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Catorze27 Style 1
typefaces.desc: Catorze27 is a typeface inspired by northern Portuguese modernist lettering. Wrought iron is a widely used element on Portuguese architecture and, as such, the typeface started after collecting several photographs of modernist iron signage in several cities in the north of Portugal, specially in Espinho, Porto, Ponte de Lima and Viana do Castelo. [ fonts.scannerlicker.net ]

typefaces.name: Cedrat
typefaces.desc: Cedrat is initially based on the typefaces called “Hollandaises” from the Berthier & Durey foundry, visible in the 1895 “ Spécimen de caractères ”: a “family” with thick strokes and high contrast, offered in a single weight in roman and italic. Typical of typefaces from this technical and cultural transitional period between the 19th and 20th centuries, the forms of the “Hollandaises” are hybrid: the axis of contrast varies according to the letters (h, o, a have a straight axis while b, d, p, q, e have a slanted axis), some pleasing inconsistencies create identity. Cedrat retains this free spirit but has been refined to be more coherent and functional. In order to reconcile the source that was clearly intended for display and the desire to have a typeface that could function in text, the design space was divided into three optical sizes. Each subfamily is broken down into six weights to cover all needs. Finally, the italic design diverges from the source, drawing from the likes of Times and ITC Caslon 223 instead of using Berthier & Durey’s mechanical slant of the roman, which lacked true cursive characteristics. [ formagari.com ]

typefaces.name: Cera Mono
typefaces.desc: The monospaced companion to Cera Pro .

typefaces.name: Ceraph
typefaces.desc: Piercy began Ceraph in 2018 as an experiment, a sketched word featuring whiplash forms and flared serifs. "It slowly evolved into a more ambitious and refined project. I wanted the typeface to embody grace and strength, and this aim was the north star throughout its development. This is my first serious undertaking of typeface design, and it took a year on-and-off to settle on the concept." "Ceraph’s flared stroke endings give them an engraved quality. The uppercase proportions and construction reference Roman capitals, while the lowercase has more of a calligraphic approach. This is a flared serif typeface, but it doesn’t follow any particular historical model." Even so, Piercy is forthcoming about her influences: "The work of Hermann Zapf, Giovan Francesco Cresci, and Jakob Erbar were significant. Typeface-wise, Canela was a specific reference point, too. Over time, my influences also became more humanistic, so my interest and practice in calligraphy further moulded this project. [ sharptype.co ]

typefaces.name: Chaco
typefaces.desc: Chaco began as a research project to solve specific wayfinding and roadway signage problems in Argentina, expanding to become a signage system based on the international standards of seven additional countries. Since differentiating between easily-confused signs at a long distance or in small sizes is a major concern, many of its solutions account for this issue. Chaco was designed with the rare ability to maintain internal space in word composition, offer better performance, and avoid word shortenings that are naturally illegible on a sign, without using the crutch of faux condensation. After solving for large-scale use, great consideration was given to headings and paragraph text to ensure Chaco met a bevy of common scenarios. These refinements include narrower proportions overall, spacious internal angles, and inktraps that are both functional and aesthetic to improve readability. Particular attention was paid to the shape and proportions of the numerals to differentiate them from small caps and capital letters, making alphanumeric strings foolproof. [ type-together.com ] Originally released around 2008 and reissued by TypeTogether in September 2024.

typefaces.name: Chamberí
typefaces.desc: Chamberí is designed to be Vogue España's bespoke typeface. An ambitious typographic branding project made for one of the most iconic magazine headers of the world, it defines the Spanish edition’s personality through a blending of the functionality of XIX Century Modern Romans (also known as “Scotch" typefaces) and the gestural expressiveness of typographic Baroque. Chamberí is a peculiar combination of the rational and the delicate, the sturdy and the feminine. The family is organised in a broad spectrum of 56 variants in which the transition from the restrained text version to the flamboyant, elegant display is modulated by contrast. [ extratype.com ]

typefaces.name: Chantier
typefaces.desc: The Chantier type family is a blend between Nebiolo type foundry’s Egizio , of which I was able to consult a specimen in the Berlin’s Staatsbibliothek archives, and typefaces from posters specimens recollected in the Brittany’s Museum printed objects collections. It is made of four styles, including an opened variation called “Constructed”. The latter questions the shape to be given to a font “under construction”, and how to display through a letter shape the steps of a typeface’s making. Chantier was developed by Fátima Lázaro. [ fonderiebretagne.fr ]

typefaces.name: Chapman Ave
typefaces.desc: Chapman Ave layered font is a family of 4 dimensional fonts with more looks than the Met Gala. Mix and match styles, access Open Type stylistic sets for a whole new underlined look with contextual alternates, and play with different cases for endless design possibilities. This font was made as a chrome font all caps variation of our font Santa Ana Sans. [ hoodzpahdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Chartwell
typefaces.desc: Chartwell is the innovative award-winning font that easily makes charts. Using OpenType technology it is supported in most design apps such as Adobe and now it is supported in Figma and on the web. The data remains as editable text, allowing for painless updates in designs. [ vectrotype.com ] Initially self-released in 2011, reissued with FontFont as FF Chartwell in 2012. Updated in 2023 and re-released through the designer’s own foundry.

typefaces.name: Chary
typefaces.desc: A high-contrast sans-serif variable display typeface, Chary is an introvert with a lot to say. A tough and composed exterior protects the delicate, expressive curves that make up Chary’s intrinsic character. A fine balance of geometric intensity and smooth, undulating curves, Chary is riding pretty high for a sans. This balance of order and organic personality give Chary a voice that is utterly zany but still somehow composed. [ jamesplattner.com ]

typefaces.name: Chateau Grande Display
typefaces.desc: Commissioned for the luxurious Chateau Grande Hotel, Chateau Grande Display pays homage to the french origins of the hotel architecture. Inspired by french posters and ornamental ephemera, Chateau Grande Display evokes luxury and elegance with its high contrasting weight and pronounced serifs. [ cantrelltype.com ]

typefaces.name: Cheesecake
typefaces.desc: Cheesecake (2024) is an ultra-bold script inspired by lettering of the sixties and seventies. It’s a design that I found myself compulsively drawing during the development of Dreamboat (2022). Cheesecake is simpler and less formal—almost a caricature of the style—with a larger x-height and more extreme forms. It has an alternate to the default cursive-style lowercase “s” and a full set of dingbats. It’s keen for branding, advertising, posters, book covers, packaging, and the like. [ marksimonson.com ]

typefaces.name: Chella
typefaces.desc: Chella is a friendly display type family of 8 weights and matching italics. Chella has soft forms combined with some sharp edges. It includes swash capitals, end swashes for lowercases and a few options for ascenders and descenders. Chella is a great choice for package design, children's books and where ever you’ll need a playful and friendly font.

typefaces.name: Chippo
typefaces.desc: Marked as dormant on Future Fonts.

typefaces.name: Chokecherry
typefaces.desc: Chokecherry is a lively sans for Latin and Cherokee, with influences ranging from handwriting to sign painting. Its shapes are informed by handwriting ductus, including accidental flicks of the wrist that lead to unexpected closed loops with leaf-shaped counters. Chokecherry’s giant x-height and gently eccentric forms make it ideal for logos, headlines, packaging, and other display uses. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Cholla
typefaces.desc: The Cholla typeface family was designed by Sibylle Hagmann in 1998-99 and named after a species of cactus she encountered in the Mojave Desert. Cholla was originally developed for the Art Center College of Design in Pasadena, California. There, art director Denise Gonzales Crisp and associate designer, Carla Figueroa, collaborated with Hagmann to create a series of fonts that would offer a great deal of variation. The variety was needed to echo the school’s nine different departments, yet together the fonts had to exude a unified feel. It was first used in the radically designed 1999/2000 Art Center catalog which won an honorable mention in I.D. magazine and was also featured in Eye No. 31. Originally Hagmann set out to design a typeface that, as she recalls, “I could feel comfortable making, first of all, and one that would serve a purpose and had a clear idea behind it, and something that I would want to use myself.” Stylistically Hagmann set out to create “12 cuts with slightly different person- alities, with different ideas applied. For example the Bold weight isn’t simply the Regular with weight gain, but has bold letterforms with their own peculiar details. What all weights s

typefaces.name: Choriza
typefaces.desc: Initially released with Huy!Fonts, folded into the MTM catalog in 2025.

typefaces.name: Choso
typefaces.desc: Choso ("house" or "home" in the Canary Islands) is a typeface inspired by the kind of symbols that can be found in the frieze section (upper part) of many 20th-century house facades of the Canary Islands, specially on single storey popular houses (known as "casas terreras") but sometimes also on two-storey manor houses. These symbols can appear in an isolated manner or as repeating patterns, but the two kinds of display are sometimes combined. Their different shapes have been collected over a long period of time and on different islands. The use of geometric figures to decorate facades is not exclusive to the Canarian archipelago, but this particular collection of shapes and the way of displaying them is indeed characteristic of local popular culture. Choso is a collaborative project that aims to be extended in the future with the addition of new symbols. [ tunera.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Chroma
typefaces.desc: Chroma is a sophisticated sans serif that combines elegant curves with a bold graphic stance. The slightly extended font covers a wide spectrum of weights, from black display use to bright text applications. The typeface finds early inspiration from a poster discovered in the book Graphic Design Manual (1965) by Armin Hofmann. While the unique graphic letterforms sparked the initial inspiration for Chroma, Selina Bernet re-energized the 60s Swiss aesthetic with her own contemporary design sensibilities. Over years of development the typeface garnered underground notoriety in its pre-released form and has been used for a variety of projects in a mix of industries. We’re proud to present Bernet’s debut font, as she has been part of the Source Type family since day one. Chroma is now officially available, an unparalleled Swiss banger featuring a set of weights crafted for peaktime or afterhours. [ sourcetype.com ]

typefaces.name: Chromatica
typefaces.desc: Chromatica is a clean sans with simple, blocky forms and very low contrast. Geometric construction is combined with more humanistic strokes and angled terminals to add some warmth, and a reasonably large x-height and (mostly) open aperatures allow Chromatica to perform well in text. Crisp and elegant in the lighter weights, sturdy and warm in the heavier weights, Chromatica is a versatile family that works well across a wide range of projects. [ polytype.co.uk ]

typefaces.name: Ciclo Display
typefaces.desc: Finalized in April 2025.

typefaces.name: Cina Sans
typefaces.desc: Cina Sans is the culmination of over thirty years of typographic exploration, drawing from a broad spectrum of experiences rather than adhering strictly to historical precedents. My relationship with Helvetica has been one of both critique and admiration, revisiting it through reinterpretations in 2002, 2009, and 2019, and engaging in conversations about its legacy in publications like Emigre magazine. The seeds of Cina Sans were planted in 2023 when a custom job inquiry sparked the desire to draw my vision of the "perfect sans." This typeface was refined through extensive testing, thoughtful use, and invaluable feedback, leading to multiple iterations and adjustments in the distribution across its nine weights. The design process underscored the importance of adaptability, and technical collaboration with a Google typeface developer ensured that Cina Sans met the highest standards of performance. At its core, Cina Sans is a reflection of my engagement with typographic history—a Neo-Grotesque that feels both new and comfortably familiar. [ publictype.us ]

typefaces.name: Ciron
typefaces.desc: Released late 2023 or early 2024.

typefaces.name: Citadel
typefaces.desc: Weak ovals replace powerful circular forms in the condensed form of most geometric slab serifs. In Citadel, Tobias Frere-Jones follows a stronger alternative, substituting straight strokes for the curved sides of round characters. Flat horizontal curves play against the variety of serifs in counterpoint to the repeating rhythm of verticals. The inline stripe adds to the rhythm of a typeface that offers a powerful and stylish geometry; FB 1995 [ fontbureau.com ] Originally released by Font Bureau in 1995 and moved to Frere–Jones Type in 2020 [ fontsinuse.com ], available through Type Network and added to the foundry’s website in December 2024.

typefaces.name: Citizen
typefaces.desc: Not to be confused with Citizen Grotesk (Altiplano).

typefaces.name: Citizen Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Citizen is a new Grotesk inspired by the typographic movement developed in Switzerland in the mid-twentieth century: the International Style. This ultra-clean style became the symbol of a radical approach to typography and the principle of Swiss neutrality. Today, what meaning can we give to this ideal of neutrality? Citizen applies the methodical spirit characteristic of the International Style to move beyond the fantasy of purity, universalism, and neutrality. It is a Grotesk for the 21st century, proudly displaying the singularity of its vision amidst the homogenizing flows of globalization. [ altiplano.xyz ] Not to be confused with Citizen (Emigre).

typefaces.name: Citizen Grotesk Poster
typefaces.desc: Citizen is a new Grotesk inspired by the typographic movement developed in Switzerland in the mid-twentieth century: the International Style. This ultra-clean style became the symbol of a radical approach to typography and the principle of Swiss neutrality. Today, what meaning can we give to this ideal of neutrality? Citizen applies the methodical spirit characteristic of the International Style to move beyond the fantasy of purity, universalism, and neutrality. It is a Grotesk for the 21st century, proudly displaying the singularity of its vision amidst the homogenizing flows of globalization. [ altiplano.xyz ] Not to be confused with Citizen (Emigre).

typefaces.name: Citywide
typefaces.desc: Citywide is a sans serif family inspired by mid-1900s bus and train destination roll signs. The letterforms draw from a bus roll sign I found at a flea market years ago. […] Citywide is an interpretation of these letterforms, drawing inspiration from both my sign and others like it. I attempted to standardize it a bit by wrangling cross strokes, corner radii, and counters, while also imposing a system for width and weight. [[shop.loudroom.com(https://shop.loudroom.com/products/citywide)]

typefaces.name: Claus
typefaces.desc: The design of new typefaces often involves a delicate dance between honoring tradition and embracing innovation. Mario De Libero's Claus is a festive intepretation of this artistic interplay, as it emerges as a reinvention of the classic Stunt Roman . First gracing the pages of the Speedball Text Book in 1929, this hand-lettered serif alphabet masterfully crafted by the penmanship virtuoso Ross Frederick George blended the classical beauty of Old Style letterforms with the narrow proportions and fluid elegance of Art Deco. Inspired by its iconic proportions, Mario De Libero embarked on the design journey that birthed Claus. With a distinctly elfish flair for harmonizing classic charm with a brutalist twist, De Libero introduced etched serifs and calligraphic quirks, subtly adapting the letterforms to a more contemporary and digital taste. [ zetafonts.com ] Expanded in December 2024 to eight weights.

typefaces.name: Clearly
typefaces.desc: Clearly is a flared typeface for display and headline use. Its tone exists in between moods; soft curls of certain forms bring a warmth and playfulness that is balanced by the sharp terminals of others. Put simply: Clearly can be used in many settings, but doesn’t sacrifice personality just to fit in. [ bigfog.co ]

typefaces.name: Cloître
typefaces.desc: Cloître is a condensed, almost monospaced typeface. Each letter follows a grid and some have variants (M for instance) with a stronger and more direct shape to play with. The spacing has been designed for use in medium character size, otherwise, if used in headings you may need to tighten the spacing. [ entravaux.framer.website ]

typefaces.name: CMM Coda
typefaces.desc: CMM Coda is a warm typewriter font with subtly rounded edges and an analogue aesthetic. It comes in three styles: Mono Sans, Mono Serif and Proportional, each with accompanying italic styles. It is a versatile and unusually structured type family with many alternates that completely change the look of the typeface, giving an array of options across different use cases and text types while maintaining a common design DNA. CMM Coda is based on Dual Basic, a typeface designed in the 1960s for the IBM Selectric typewriter. It was one of the first machines where fonts could be switched via “type balls” and characters could be stored on magnetic band – thus an early analogue word-processor and important bridge technology between typewriter and computer. Interestingly, both “typewriter” and “computer” were once terms to describe the female workforce operating the machines. Starting the late 19th century, typewriters enabled women to pursue careers such as typists, punchcard operators and telegraphists. Because women’s work used to be strongly associated with meticulousness, computing was considered well suited to women. In fact, the first people to write a computer program were women (ENI

typefaces.name: CMM Modul
typefaces.desc: CMM Modul is a constructed geometric display typeface with two personalities: one a child in play, the other rigorous architect. Its potential lies between naiveté and constructivity, looseness and stability, motion and order. Each letter is composed from a small set of simple modules designed to balance simplicity and readability. Stylistic sets offer many options for customisation such as alternative letters, ligatures, a stencil version and placing letters with descenders on the baseline to enable extra compact line spacing. [ commatype.com ]

typefaces.name: CoFo Holz
typefaces.desc: CoFo Holz is an expressive serif typeface with unapologetic character. It counterbalances sharpness and softness, combining triangular wedge serifs with circular dots and terminals. The design creates a playful tension of simple geometric shapes by incorporating a modern modular feel within a classic serif typeface. The ideological and stylistic inspiration behind CoFo Holz come from two sources—18th Century Engravings and American Wood Type—both known for their particularly exaggerated pointed serifs. Reflecting on this historical context of letters carved from wooden blocks, we named it “Holz,” a German word for “wood.” CoFo Holz goes beyond its traditional references and transforms them into a contemporary functional design. [ contrastfoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: CoFo Meteor
typefaces.desc: CoFo Meteor is elegant and a little arrogant due to its extravagant art deco features. Originally designed for movie titles, it is loosely inspired by a bunch of typefaces: DeVinne Roman, Romanisch, Literaturnaya, and even Times Modern. Yet it is narrow in proportions and has a slightly lower contrast than its predecessors, allowing it to work especially well on dark and colorful backgrounds. If you look closer at the details, terminals, and serifs, you can notice that they are sharp but not pointy — this detail makes it appear warmer and friendlier. CoFo Meteor comes in three styles, but we do plan to continue expanding it into a bigger type family with a larger language support. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: CoFo Sans Semi-Mono
typefaces.desc: CoFo Sans Semi-Mono is the ultimate fusion of our iconic CoFo Sans and its monospaced variant: CoFo Sans Mono. We all love the aesthetics of a traditional monospaced typeface—the rigid proportions and technical feel. We equally appreciate the elegant proportions and spacing of classical sans-serifs. And who says we can’t have the best of both worlds? CoFo Sans Semi-Mono captures all the things that designers like about the Mono, but with subtly adjusted character. Letters that look overly-compressed in the Mono (such as m w щ ы), are slightly wider here, while others that are exaggeratedly wide (i j l), are slightly narrower. This allows for smoother typesetting while preserving strong personality. The unusual blend of features gives the designers more flexibility and freedom. [ contrastfoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Collapse
typefaces.desc: Collapse is an austere and melancholic condensed serif, crafted with an air of stark pessimism. Loosely inspired by the iconic serif typeface seen in the opening titles of Neon Genesis Evangelion, it draws upon the haunting atmosphere of that series while quickly diverging into something more expressive, more severe. This typeface embodies a tension between restraint and rebellion, its sharp edges and compressed form evoking an unsettling beauty. Collapse plays with the contrast between elegance and intensity, making it ideal for projects that demand both sophistication and a sense of underlying urgency. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Collier
typefaces.desc: Collier is a wildly versatile flare serif family initially designed for display typography. However, this subtly tapered face has several styles that perform well in text sizes, starting at 8pt. As it happened, Richard Lipton had a chance encounter with a hand-lettered bookplate from the early twentieth century that provided the impetus for this sprawling family of 168 styles, 7 widths, 12 weights, with Italics. Collier occupies that rare zone between serif and sans serif, harnessing the best of both. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Columba
typefaces.desc: Originally released with Colophon in 2020, and re-released through the designer’s own foundry in 2024 after the former joined Monotype.

typefaces.name: CommonSans
typefaces.desc: In 2021, Xiaoyuan became intrigued by the phenomenon of ink bleed as seen in the printed text on mass-produced items, such as the text on eggshells, capacitors, and expiration dates on food packaging. Initially, she wanted to emulate this ink bleed effect on typeface, but due to her technical limitations at the time, she was unable to find a satisfactory way to replicate it. The idea persisted in her mind for a loooong time, and finally, through continuous practice in and sheer stubbornness, she made another attempt. This led to the creation of commonSans. [ notyourtype.nl ]

typefaces.name: Compagnon
typefaces.desc: Compagnon is a typeface family composed of five distinctive styles. It finds its inspiration in the online archives of Typewriter Database specimens and combines different periods of the history of typewriter typefaces. Each weight is based on singular references relating to significant periods aiming to underline the evolution of typewriter characters as they are called. [ velvetyne.fr ]

typefaces.name: Concrette
typefaces.desc: Produced as a variable font with two axes, for weight and contrast.

typefaces.name: Condensed Sans No. 10
typefaces.desc: Condensed Sans No.10 is a free-spirited revival of Stephenson Blake & Co.’s Condensed Sans Serif No.10 and is directly inspired by the cut for their 14 point metal type. The font is available in five weights: Regular, Medium, Bold, ExtraBold & Black.

typefaces.name: Config Mono
typefaces.desc: Config Mono is a monospace sans serif, adapting the modern technical spirit of the Config font family into a fixed-width format. Modified for clarity and utility, it introduces subtle refinements in the roman and italic, enhancing readability across digital and print environments. Stylistic alternates give added flexibility, while the design remains clean and versatile — well-suited for smaller sizes in UI, coding, game consoles, and captions, and for larger sizes in magazines, textbooks, and packaging. [ ladd-design.com ]

typefaces.name: Conforto
typefaces.desc: Conforto is a sans-serif typeface inspired by the feeling of ease, well-being and comfort. Its rounded features and balanced proportions create a friendly and familiar appearance, making it easy on the eyes. Each character is designed for approachability, adding a welcoming touch to any project. [ typeoffeeling.com ]

typefaces.name: Contradictor
typefaces.desc: Design of Contradictor combines several elements such as elegance, tall x-height, high contrast, slightly condensed look and true Italic. Charming details, some unique shapes and very small slanted angle of Italics make Contradictor distinctive font family. [ tourdefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Contro
typefaces.desc: Taking inspiration from early 20th-century Italian modernist typography, Contro embraces global writing traditions. It is not a revival typeface—it does not replicate the past but moves forward through the designers’ unique perspective. Harsh Patel’s initial alphabet, drawn in November 2023, laid the groundwork for Michael Cina’s exploration, resulting in a fully realized glyph set. Together, the designers crafted a typeface that melds multiculturalism and experimentation. Contro’s glyphs and styles were designed with many typographic cultures in mind. The turn of the 20th century, a pivotal moment in industrialization, inspired a focus on universality in typography. The conceptual backbone of Contro pays homage to iconic figures such as Tschichold, Renner, Bill, and Bayer. Contro challenges designers to explore new methods of language construction and rethink their typographic choices. While it supports legible Latin text, its true potential lies in the user’s hands, encouraging intentionality in spacing, layout, and overall design. [ publictype.us ]

typefaces.name: Control
typefaces.desc: Based on the sans serif lettering examples in Walter Käch’s lettering manual Schriften Lettering Écritures (1949). The cursive style, drawn by Miguel Reyes, is loosely based on Van Dijk (Letraset, 1982). Produced in upright, italic and cursive styles as variable fonts with axes for weight, contrast, and apertures.

typefaces.name: Corax
typefaces.desc: Corax is a sophisticated, high contrast, serif typeface that explores the italic construction in up-right letterforms. With calligraphic influences and an unexpected gothic twist, this beautiful Frankenstein will surely add a touch of drama and mystique to most applications. Designed to behave as a digital lettering, the current 3-weight family has several alternates, including a second set of ornamental capital letters. Want more? No worries, Júlia is working on bolder styles and real italics. [ flaviazim.com ]

typefaces.name: Corfe
typefaces.desc: Links in this entry point to Corfe Regular .

typefaces.name: Cornbread
typefaces.desc: A ‘drip’ variation axis was added in April 2025.

typefaces.name: Corpid
typefaces.desc: Corpid was originally commissioned by Studio Dumbar in the Netherlands as a corporate typeface for the Dutch Ministry of Agriculture, Nature Management and Fishing. The font was designed to replace the existing standard typeface (a well-known business-like sans-serif) to provide the organization with a unique and strong identity. Although it was designed to fit strict technical requirements, Corpid has a personality all of its own. This was in part a result of what Luc(as) calls “creating tension” between the inner and outer curves of each character. “I tend to put a little more diagonal contrast into fonts than is the case in most neutral sans serif fonts. This brings a certain humanistic touch to the typeface. Much more subtle here than in Thesis – but although it is almost invisible, it is still palpable.” [ lucasfonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Cortese Sans
typefaces.desc: Cortese Sans is a sans serif responsible companion of Cortese, a 2023 reinterpretation of the seventies classic, Cortez, originally designed by Philip Kelly and published in 1977. While losing Cortese’s characteristic sharp serifs, Cortese Sans maintains the same geometric structure and raw attitude of its predecessor, as well as some signature design elements like its triangular dots. [ markvanleeuwen.co ]

typefaces.name: Cosmos Deco
typefaces.desc: Cosmos Deco is a sans-serif typeface inspired by architect Carlos Crombé's sketches for the original facade of the iconic Cine Cosmos, a symbol of Mexico's golden age of cinema. Its clean lines and bold curves capture the essence of Art Deco style, prevalent in the streets and buildings of early 20th-century Mexico City. The elegance and prominence of Cosmos Deco’s uppercase letters stand out, particularly in headings and titles, especially in heavier weights and larger sizes. Meanwhile, the lowercase characters offer clarity and comfort for extended text, thanks to their wide apertures, which enhance readability. [ sudtipos.com ]

typefaces.name: Cottonhouse
typefaces.desc: Cottonhouse began as a branding project for a new hotel being built from a neoclassical building in Barcelona that was originally used as a cotton house in the industrial market. We were given access to some digital archive in the Spanish libraries where we pulled inspiration from old ephemera and currency. One connection we immediately found between cotton and currency was the guilloche patterns having the appearance of cotton spools. The typographic characters were hence imbued with the regality of the regional coinage and currency. It bestows history yet modernity to any brand it pairs with. [ typeverything.com ]

typefaces.name: Courtside
typefaces.desc: Courtside recalls the 90s era of streamlined efficiency and forward-thinking design. With its tall, condensed letterforms and sleek lines, Courtside embodies a sporty, dynamic vibe. Low contrast and sharp corners create a polished finish that’s nostalgic yet professional. Courtside is offered in two styles, Regular and Italic. [ doubledagger.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Cowgirl
typefaces.desc: This typeface is a slab-serif, only it isn’t really, as the serifs are not too slabby: they rebelliously taper. In fact, there is a whole lot of tapering going on. The design came from the desire to play with the nature of slab serifs, as I once did with a design that became Postino , that was – and still is – published by Adobe. But this time, I wanted something quite skinny, in contrast to Postino ’s chunkiness. The playing with the skinniness led to the attempt at reversing the contrast by making the vertical stem width less than the horizontal. I named it Cowgirl . Now on the subject of naming: firstly, an anecdote: the name I had originally wanted for Postino was Thwacker , however I was overruled by Adobe Marketing wisdom (they felt it was too violent). Now, unfettered by such sensible commercial oversight, I have called it Cowgirl. Several of my mucky-minded friends insist that this is rude. However, I protest my innocence, I was listening to Neil Young’s Cowgirl in the sand at the time of naming. [ shapesforcash.com ]

typefaces.name: CP Company
typefaces.desc: Originally developed for the Italian clothing manufacturer C.P. Company. Later remade into Oook .

typefaces.name: Crespo
typefaces.desc: Starting as an interpretation of a shopfront sign found during one of the numerous strolls through the vias and piazzas of Milano, Crespo’s geometric curves quickly became an exercise in shape variability. Therefore, it comes in three angles: Backslanted, Upright, and Slanted. As far as its weight is concerned, it normally spans from Light to Black—and to top it all off, we’ve added three different extender and cap height sizes for enhanced flexibility. Crespo certainly isn’t your run-of-the-mill geometric sans serif, as there is something quite humanist and unique protruding from those sturdy geometric shapes. [ hottype.co ]

typefaces.name: Crisp
typefaces.desc: Crisp is a humanist sans serif font. It was developed to fill a gap of fonts that look sleek and cool, while not sacrificing anything in terms of readability. [ type.design ] Licenses available on request.

typefaces.name: Crit
typefaces.desc: https://elementtype.co/news/self-crit-on-biases-behind-forms/

typefaces.name: Criterium
typefaces.desc: Criterium is a measured, rhythmic, and condensed typeface family that is an interpretation of the warm, modernist typography found in Emil Ruder’s works for Gewerbemuseum Basel. In an approximation, Criterium adopts these prominent typographic attributes, utilizing them as the basis to shape its form in totality. Criterium is defined by expanded, yet condensed proportions and enclosed terminals, contrasting its considerably rounded contours. Select characters are marked with naturally arced, yet tightly contracted stem joins–an atypical detail that contributes to Criterium’s identity. Struck by the warmth, details and curvature of these particular typographic works, a limited character prototype was produced. With its primary forms realized, references were largely abandoned, while letterform construction logic was applied to each subset of new glyphs. In subsequent iterations, Criterium was further shaped by an effort to capture the general feel of this era, versus direct replication.
