In doing so, it was natural to not only refine, but eliminate the rough quality often found in early, or modern-era condensed typefaces. [ aesthetictype.com ]

typefaces.name: Criterium Text
typefaces.desc: Criterium Text is a text specific variant of Criterium that leverages the characteristics of its source, while adapting it for use in small sizes and dynamic settings. Its texture elicits the warmth and modernism of the era, complimented by an astute functional intent, unique to the condensed sans serif genre. The sixteen styles of Criterium have been reduced to ten styles, with the family weight progression recalibrated to accommodate a diverse range of text requirements. In addition to increased letter spacing, the enclosed terminals of Criterium have been expanded, increasing legibility at text scale, and harmonizing with its open spacing. [ aesthetictype.com ]

typefaces.name: Crysta
typefaces.desc: Crysta is a display typeface that resembles the organic shapes of leaves, flowers, insects and fairies. [ carmen-type.com ]

typefaces.name: CT Gates
typefaces.desc: Designed over the span of 4 years, Gates is a reinterpretation of Arial, a typeface almost everyone has been exposed to. Rather than a strict redesign, Gates is an attempt to exaggerate features of Arial while keeping its wide usability. [ contextype.com ]

typefaces.name: Cure Sans
typefaces.desc: Originally released as Core Mono on Future Fonts. Core Mono has been in development for a long time and has worked to fill my personal monospace needs. I started getting requests to release it so apparently it can fill the needs of other people as well. To that end I've started polishing it up to be a commercial typeface. Core Mono has a neutral overall feel on the surface but the details blend a subtle mix of mechanical and humanist shapes. It’s meant to be kind of a workhorse (as far as a mono can be) but also be fun and interesting to look at. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Cut
typefaces.desc: Cut is a stencil type family inspired by designs from two different historical periods. Its proportions are based on the forms of neoclassical typefaces produced in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries. The sharp vertical stroke contrast of these types has been taken to an extreme in Cut, with hairline cross-strokes dissolved into open spaces that break down its letterforms into individual segments. The systematic construction methods used to assemble Cut’s letters references typefaces created in the early twentieth century where parts of letters were reduced to simple geometric units that could be used as structural components to build alphabets, using scaling, reflection, repetition and redistribution. Although the typefaces produced in these historical periods appear to share few visual attributes, they can be seen as stages in the development of a common heritage that is rational, reductive, elegant and modern. The MuirMcNeil Cut type system is intended to reconcile these disparate points of historical reference. [ muirmcneil.com ]

typefaces.name: Cut Square
typefaces.desc: Cut Square is the straight-edged variant of Cut .

typefaces.name: Cy Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Cy Grotesk is the result of combining the clear forms of mid 20th-century European neo-grotesks and the expressiveness of the 19th-century grotesques. It is display typeface with an eccentric character and a special rhythm. Symbols have sharp long angled spurs and large wedge incision between the bowl and the stem, diluting it with smooth curves and the tight aperture. Built like a multifunctional workhorse that has a wide range of font uses. This type family consists of 27 styles that are adjustable in weight and width. Or one variable font with 2 axes. From pure thin to radically black. From roomy key to catchy grand. All styles include an extended set of Latin characters and a basic Cyrillic. [ zakznak.com ] Originally released in 2021, Unrelated to Cy (Superior Type).

typefaces.name: Dada Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Dada Grotesk is a typeface designed by deValence for the fabulous exhibition, Dada, which took place in 2005 at the Centre Pompidou in Paris. Its design was based on a typeface called Aurora Grotesk, which was used on third and fourth issues of Dada journal. Aurora Grotesk’s origins can be traced to Wagner & Schmidt, a company specialized in punch-cutting and engraving in Leipzig. The company sold matrices to many European foundries in the early twentieth century, which resulted in the same typeface appearing under multiple names and being distributed by different foundries, such as Edel Grotesk from Ludwig Wagner foundry or Cairoli from Nebiolo foundry. Aurora Grotesk was eventually used by Dada artists in some of their avant-garde publications. While maintaining the idiosyncrasies of the original drawing, deValence developed a contemporary typeface, which is available as a complete family. With its modulated stroke curves—resembling hooks—and terminals finishing at varying angles, this sans-serif typeface presents an interesting warmth and dynamism. [ optimo.ch ]

typefaces.name: Dada Grotesk Pan
typefaces.desc: Dada Grotesk Pan offers an extended character set, which supports languages that use Cyrillic and Greek alphabets, in addition to those which use the Latin alphabet. It provides accurate and genuine letterforms created for pan-european communication. Dada Grotesk is a typeface designed by deValence for the fabulous exhibition, Dada, which took place in 2005 at the Centre Pompidou in Paris. Its design was based on a typeface called Aurora Grotesk, which was used on third and fourth issues of Dada journal. Aurora Grotesk’s origins can be traced to Wagner & Schmidt, a company specialized in punch-cutting and engraving in Leipzig. The company sold matrices to many European foundries in the early twentieth century, which resulted in the same typeface appearing under multiple names and being distributed by different foundries, such as Edel Grotesk from Ludwig Wagner foundry or Cairoli from Nebiolo foundry. Aurora Grotesk was eventually used by Dada artists in some of their avant-garde publications. typefaces.name: Dahlia
typefaces.desc: Dahlia typeface grew from a land filled with elegance, 1910’s Italian lake posters and Art Nouveau feeling. Like so many flowers, it translates a sense of perfect balance between eccentricity and delicacy. It was designed in 2021 by Jérémy Schneider for VJ Type. Dahlia typeface is a display serif typeface, useful for headlines or short to medium-length texts. It comes with 3 weights, regular, medium and bold, and 2 widths, normal and condensed. Dahlia is nonconformist, romantic, delicate and has some extravagant alternates. Its atypical curves and refined details create a lot of rhythm, and timeless elegance. The Bold version uses high contrast to be as noticeable as possible. With a touch of Art Nouveau inspiration, its counter forms are highly expressive, particularly the upper cases P, R, K, B, E. Letters endings and curves are inspired by the flower stems, burgeons and spines. We drew 93 stylistic ligatures, like the vegetal world can naturally combine species. Each letter is designed so that the transition from one letter to the next remains melodious. In this context, all circular glyphs (e,c,o) are included in the Standard ligatures, and enabled by default. [ vj-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Daimito
typefaces.desc: Daimito is the result of two years of research into sharp yet stable forms, positioned between the great but relatively young typographic styles of our modern times. The design incorporates elements of uncompromising neo-grotesque and strong stylisation characteristic of humanistic fonts like Gill Sans. Daimito is a child aware of its cultural heritage, looking boldly into the future with the eyes of an explorer. [ bigtype.co ]

typefaces.name: Daletra
typefaces.desc: Daletra is a display slab serif font. Unicase. Twirly. A vernacular Galician letterform on drugs. The very typical pencil doodle that ended up as a font. [ rubenprol.gal ]

typefaces.name: Danfo
typefaces.desc: Drawing inspiration from the iconic 'Danfo' buses of Lagos, Nigeria, Danfo is a Tuscan slab serif that merges design elements from Western and local traditions. This single-weight font features striking ornamental details through variable axes, demonstrating technical and construction ingenuity. It also serves as a documentation of Lagos' vibrant visual culture. [ afrotype.com ] Released as open-source on GitHub.

typefaces.name: Dank
typefaces.desc: Stadium, Transport & Logistics, Warfare, Liberty City… you probably feel like you've already come across this figure, don't you? Dank pays homage to these brutal and rigid typographic shapes which constitute a prominent part of our visual environment since the last century. With a wide silhouette enhanced by angular curves and cleverly conserved irregularities resulting in its singular rhythm, this sans serif font draws inspiration from the infamous Bank Gothic (Morris Fuller Benton, American Type Founders, 1930). Unlike the latter —abusively associated with the fields of construction industry, sports or distopian sci-fi movies and video games— this first instalment of the Dank family intends to gently set new worlds for this particular font style while offering alternates styles (allowing to revive small slab serifs or not). [ ott-foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Daphne
typefaces.desc: Daphne is one of Georg Salden's first typefaces, designed in 1970. It features a large number of calligraphic swashes that can be added to individual characters. The digital version uses OpenType features to apply these swashes. Since many swashes fit different characters, the possible combinations are endless. Alternate and full swash characters provide even more design options, making this a unique tool for designers with a calligraphic instinct. [ ludwigtype.de ]

typefaces.name: Dark Academia (Céline’s Version)
typefaces.desc: Originally released on DaFont in 2022.

typefaces.name: Dash
typefaces.desc: Links on this entry point to Dash Slow .

typefaces.name: Datei Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Datei Grotesk emerged from an extensive exploration of sans serif typefaces that trace their origins back to the categorization of grotesques and neo-grotesques. The design process started in 2017, with the gradual development of the family contextualizing defining design features of legacy grotesque typefaces like Akzidenz, DIN 1451, Breite, Folio, Gerstner Programm, Haas Unica, Record Gothic, and Recta, among others. The design aims for a balanced approach to uniformity, featuring clear shapes, effortless readability, and a progressive system for both roman and italic styles. The final design strikes a balance between restraint with form qualities aiming to blend rationality with friendliness. The slight straight-sided letter forms give the type a subtle industrial flair, creating robust textures without appearing too rigid. [ kontour.com ]

typefaces.name: DD Sans
typefaces.desc: A clean, circular geometric sans serif typeface is offered in three weights, suitable for a limitless number of applications. [ doubledagger.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Dean
typefaces.desc: The Dean family is a vibrant tribute to the musical and cinematic culture of mid-20th century America. These typefaces, rooted in the legacy of wood types and period posters, reflect an era of intense creativity when design served as the voice of a culture in full swing. With its sharp, precise forms, Dean Gothic retains historical subtleties while embodying a timeless and understated modernity. It continues the typographic tradition of combining functionality with strong aesthetics, echoing the rebellious and free-spirited soul of the cultural events of that time. For a complementary design with a strong visual impact, explore Dean Slab, which encapsulates the robustness and authenticity of American wood types. [ blazetype.eu ] The sample image and links on this entry refer to Dean Gothic .

typefaces.name: Dejanire
typefaces.desc: Dejanire is a type family loosely inspired by an anonymous display typeface found in a type specimen by Claude Lamesle, published in Paris in 1742. It takes its name from Deianira, a Calydonian princess in Greek mythology and the wife of Heracles. The font originally introduced under the name of ‘Gros Canon Deux Points de Gros Romain’ was neither handsome nor elegant, suggesting that its punchcutter wasn’t a very talented artisan. In spite of this, Ramiro Espinoza saw enough alluring features in it that he decided to assign himself a design exercise: he would scrub the font of its flaws and ungainliness while preserving its genuine freshness, using it as a starting point for a new editorial family. Dejanire is a transitional roman with a marked contrast and a crisp presence both in print and on screen, making it an ideal choice for robust titles, pull quotes, and decks. Although designed with magazine and newspapers in mind, the family’s clean design and readability also make it an excellent candidate for websites, brochures, annual reports, and corporate identities. The italics were modeled after the polished, rational design introduced by Pierre-Simon Fournier, which was later ad

typefaces.name: Dejanire Sans
typefaces.desc: In November of 2019, Retype introduced Dejanire Headline, a roman type family loosely inspired by an anonymous display typeface found in a type specimen by Claude Lamesle, published in Paris in 1742. In the months that followed, Ramiro Espinoza worked to expand the system with Dejanire Sans, a refined, multipurpose sans family consisting of twelve fonts. Its compact proportions and neutral appearance make Dejanire Sans especially well suited for corporate websites and commercial publications like marketing collateral and advertising campaigns. Its open counters and robust strokes yield a high legibility on paper and screen. Dejanire Sans purposefully departs from overused grotesques and geometric sans. Its humanist forms are imbued with a strong character that will bring inventiveness to any design work. Editorial designers looking for a consistent family with serif and sans counterparts will find that Dejanire’s carefully balanced weights can be easily combined in a wide range of scenarios. [ re-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Delaney
typefaces.desc: Delaney is a five-weight script family from the hand of Richard Lipton. Richard brings wide-ranging historical script forms into practical, contemporary use. The Bold and Black weights stand independently at display sizes, while the three lighter weights pair well with an endless variety of bolder serif and sans serif families. Mixing and matching can be easy with the dynamic attributes of this typeface. Delaney shines at 24 pt and above but is surprisingly tolerant of depths down to 14 pt. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Delegate
typefaces.desc: Delegate explores the grey area between cold European Grotesks and warm American Gothics. It takes inspiration from Chauncey Griffith’s iconic agate face Bell Gothic and various anonymous, highly functional grotesques that remain invisible despite their idiosyncratic shapes. It balances text-friendly features (compact lowercase, wide uppercase, diagonal cuts, and low descenders) with distinctly grotesk elements (medium contrast and flat, truncated terminals). Delegate performs the function of a workhorse agate without relying on stereotypical ink traps or loose spacing, instead focusing on core letter design that exaggerates differences—like eccentric numerals that clearly differentiate 3 from 8, 6, and 9. This results in a typeface where functionalism serves as both a purpose and an aesthetic. [ nvmbr.in ] Delegate Mono attempts to achieve the smoothest possible texture within fixed-width constraints. Delegate explores the grey area between cold European Grotesks and warm American Gothics. It takes inspiration from Chauncey Griffith’s iconic agate-face Bell Gothic and various anonymous, highly functional grotesques that manage to remain unobtrusive despite their idiosyncratic shap

typefaces.name: Delphia
typefaces.desc: Delphia’s design references early 20th century Gothics like ATF’s «Lining Gothic», «Gothic No. 545» and more. With nearly triangular counter-shapes, the lowercase was kept fairly close to the original. The rest of the typeface is headed into a more contemporary and clear style, making it useable for more than print purposes. The clear skeleton also made it possible to expand the typeface with multiple weights and widths, without sacrificing its untypical character. [ deinwaller.com ]

typefaces.name: Demur
typefaces.desc: Demur is a sans inspired by social issues and constructivist aesthetics. It was commissioned by the Winnipeg 1919 Workers Collective and expanded its existing logo into a full font. Demur’s condensed proportions and tight spacing pack letters together like a crowd of marching protesters. The modular construction gives the typeface rhythm and commonality, ensuring the glyphs are cut from the same cloth. This is not your typical boring sans serif. Despite having a generous x-height, this font is best used at medium to large sizes when emphasis is required—like the headlines on a grassroots zine publication. While you can use it however you want, I ask that you avoid using it in anything harmful or hateful towards others. [ tofutype.ca ]

typefaces.name: Densia Sans
typefaces.desc: Densia Sans is an economic sans serif. Its tall x-height and narrow width make it shine whenever there’s very limited space. […] Among its OpenType features it includes small caps, case-sensitive forms, proportional and tabular figures, superiors, inferiors, and fractions. Free for personal and commercial use. An update is in progress.

typefaces.name: Departure Mono
typefaces.desc: Departure Mono is a monospaced pixel font inspired by the constraints of early command-line and graphical user interfaces, the tiny pixel fonts of the late 90s/early 00s, and sci-fi concepts from film and television. [ github.com ] Released as open-source on GitHub.

typefaces.name: Deréon
typefaces.desc: Deréon is a hybrid typeface, sober in the basic version, it unfolds its curves and volutes with its swash letters. Deréon affirms its originality and strangeness by activating its alternative variants, and by its angles that creates like splinters in counter-shapes. The birth of the typeface is prestigious, because Deréon, in its first life was specially designed for the visual identity of the House of Deréon brand launched by Beyoncé Knowles in 2005. […] Typographers will see in Deréon an influence of Caledonia designed by W. A. Dwiggins in 1938 and they will be right, because even if the result is clearly different, Caledonia was the typeface chosen by art director Soohyen Park to build her House of Deréon visual identity project at AR New York. The collaboration with ZeCraft began in 2004 with the House of Deréon logotype, followed by alphabets the following year. [ typofonderie.com ]

typefaces.name: Devinyl
typefaces.desc: Capital letters only.

typefaces.name: Dextur
typefaces.desc: Dextur is a modern interpretation of traditional blackletter scripts. Calligraphic and rugged, Dextur is suitable for those with classical or grungy artistic tastes. [ doubledagger.xyz ]

typefaces.name: DGM Fette
typefaces.desc: DGM Fette is a semi revival of Breite Fette Information . Originally designed by Friedrich K. Sallwey and cast by Klingspor in 1956 as an addition to the Information family, it is probably best known today from its use in Pablo Ferro’s title sequence for “Bullitt” and The Kinks’ – Kinkdom album art. [ giuliaboggio.xyz ]

typefaces.name: DGM Sprinter
typefaces.desc: DGM Sprinter is based on “Röntgen Therapie” [‘X-ray Therapy’], first shown in Walter Käch’s “Schriften / Lettering / Écritures – geschriebene und gezeichnete Grundformen” in 1949. While the Bold weight was designed as quite faithful study of the original Röntgen Therapie cut, the lighter weights are added to retain a similar contrast while expanding the family's scope and adaptability. [ giuliaboggio.xyz ]

typefaces.name: DGM Typeset
typefaces.desc: Drawing inspiration from a selection of typewriter historical typefaces, DGM Typeset blends the vintage feel of a classic Olivetti Type with a digital flare and a modern duality. The two main sets, Soft and Sharp allow for maximum versatility in print and digital contexts. Well suited for a wide range of uses, DGM Typeset has a smooth, readable texture and a simple, direct style. [ giuliaboggio.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Diabase
typefaces.desc: Accessible by enrollment into Production Type’s Beta program.

typefaces.name: Diagraph
typefaces.desc: Diagraph mimics the rudimentary look of Computer Aided Design (C.A.D.) typefaces. During its creation, all the mathematically generated aberrations have been kept in the design to enhance its digital look. The hybrid aesthetic issued from this mix is intentionally irregular to create a sans serif family of 9 weights with variability at hand. [ abc-etc.com ]

typefaces.name: Diagraph Wide
typefaces.desc: Diagraph Wide Etc follows the same concept of his regularly proportioned sibling (Diagraph Etc). It mimics the rudimentary look of Computer Aided Design (C.A.D.) typefaces. During its creation, all the mathematically generated aberrations have been kept in the design to enhance its digital look. The hybrid aesthetic issued from this mix is intentionally irregular to create a sans serif family of 9 weights with variability at hand. The only difference is the addition of a 400 units extention to each glyph and few small optical correction to fit the overall aesthetic. Thanks to Arnaud Milliquet ATMA.world for participating in the development of this typeface, which it has tested and printed on several issues of Bagel Magazine. [ abc-etc.com ]

typefaces.name: Dial
typefaces.desc: Dial originated as a redrawing practice of numbers found on a vintage Quartz wall clock. Its style quickly expanded and evolved, resulting in a caps-only geometric typeface characterized by strict monoline negative spaces. In the pursuit of avoiding the pitfall of repetitive geometry, its outer forms are sometimes devoid of usually-expected minimalism, paving the way for an amplified ambiguous appearance. Dial is meant to be used on a grand scale, and most definitely in environments where legibility is not an issue. It works well for punchy signs, striking headlines, notable logotypes—and so much more! [ hottype.co ]

typefaces.name: Dida
typefaces.desc: Dida is a display typeface full of surprises, designed in 2016 by Jérémy Schneider for the Parisian « Théâtre des Bouffes du Nord » : it is generous through its large rounded shapes, geometric construction and soft lines. Dida is a playful, heavy yet breezy font which was created together with Scalie as an expressive pairing. [ vj-type.com ]

typefaces.name: DINosaur Sharp
typefaces.desc: DINosaur Sharp is an evolution of the original DINosaur. The most relevant stylistic feature of this version is the reduction in the rounding of the terminals and the redesign of various characters. [ type-o-tones.com ] Compared to its predecesor, it features an extended character set, with support for Arabic, Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese.

typefaces.name: Dioda
typefaces.desc: Dioda is a typeface based on an old Radio Shack logo found on a cassette tape. [ store.tekio.work ]

typefaces.name: Diolce
typefaces.desc: Diolce Display is a font inspired by the mascarons from the city of Bordeaux. Made in Italy during the Renaissance, this sculpture type spread throughout Western Europe thanks to trade. Slightly condensed, Diolce Display expresses itself through flared serifs. The calligraphic based design of the font is inspired by the Roman Capital ductus. The contrasts between solid and smooth lines reproduce the plant details finely chiseled by the craftsman's hand and tool. The shapes have been radicalised and the x-height taken up to get a more modern line. [ entravaux.framer.website ]

typefaces.name: Diploë
typefaces.desc: Diploë is a late rendition of a genre of sans serifs that borrows its structure and proportions from Renaissance writing. The typeface’s abrupt transition from stems to branches and its preference for horizontal directionality are traits that derive from these ancestors. Diploë’s arches spout high from the stem — a feature echoed in its large apertures. When combined with a left-leaning contrast axis, the lineal humanist tends to exhibit a pronounced asymmetry. Diploë uses a few tricks to rein in this tendency: the magnet-like arches grow almost horizontally from the stem, reverberating across the horizontal axis to form bowls. The symmetrical distribution of thicks and thins offers additional stability. Finally, Diploë’s proportions tend toward uniform widths in all characters. The resulting shape language suggests a wide stance, but its sturdiness also helps stabilize the narrower styles. [ monokrom.no ] Produced as a variable font with weight and width axes. Static instances in seven weights across three widths, in upright and italics, are also available. Version 2.0 was released in January 2025.

typefaces.name: Discotack
typefaces.desc: Discotack is a reverse contrast slab serif with organic, flowing strokes and a ton of personality. Initially inspired by Benguiat’s Discotheque (1967), the font takes an off-kilter approach to a genre typically marked by straight lines and angles. Set it in all caps for a (mostly) flat top and bottom to your lines of text, or add the lowercase to introduce a playful wavy texture to your type. Discotack is best used large and playfully, and is perfect for headlines and logos. [ bigfog.co ]

typefaces.name: Dolph
typefaces.desc: Graduated from Future Fonts in 2024.

typefaces.name: Dona
typefaces.desc: Dona is a non-boring sans serif. While very legible in text sizes, its friendly details really come to life on headlines, packaging and visual identities. Produced in two flavors with different default forms for some glyphs as Dona and Dona Alt . Available in five weights, in upright and italic, as well as variable fonts.

typefaces.name: Done
typefaces.desc: Comprised of straight lines only, inspired by tape, and moving a broad nib in straight lines. There are a few alternates for E, N, and M, and a set of figures that will leave you absolutely shook. Yes, Mike Giant is a contemporary influence. [ ohnotype.co ]

typefaces.name: Dorival UI
typefaces.desc: Loosely inspired by the engineered geometry of DIN 1451, this family balances a strict structure with subtle humanistic traits like the diagonal terminals and a bit of contrast. Dorival UI has “Multiplexed Spacing”, which guarantees that blocks of text occupy the exact same space in the layout when composed with any of the weights. This is done by establishing the same width and kerning for the glyphs in every weight of the font. This kind of typeface is a great deal for composing texts on digital environments and interfaces, because they avoid text reflow and repositioning – think of UI design, for example. Although it was designed with interfaces in mind, the fact that Dorival UI is equipped with three different widths and their respective italics, makes it a versatile type family. Also, the multiplexed feature does not compromise the letter shapes or indicates design solutions, like monospaced fonts often do. This way, Dorival UI is totally capable of being used in a wide range of situations, including printed material. The name of the font is an homage to the great brazilian musician Dorival Caymmi. [ blackletra.com ] Links in this entry point to the regular width.

typefaces.name: Dorothy Norma
typefaces.desc: Norma is a fantasy dot matrix font base on DIN 6776 lettering for technical drawing (also known as TGL 31034 in the former East Germany, which is in fact the reference for this font). “Fantasy” dot matrix because no printer using this font ever existed. In order to meet the DIN standard requirement for stroke length to be 1/10th of the Cap-height, the Cap-height is 10 dots; the x-height is 70% of that at 7 dots. The underlying design is a sans serif with monoline stroke and a squarish O. The standard style is slightly condensed. [ drj11.itch.io ]

typefaces.name: Dorset
typefaces.desc: Dorset marks Léon Hugues first script typeface and first release with the Positype Flourish label. Built crosscurrent to a strict revival or calligraphic digitization, Dorset’s aim was to understand how a font could interact with various calligraphic influences in a single execution and how that interpretation by Léon would lead to new, exclusive design choices. The design purposely chose to connect various gestures from Spencerian handwriting and copperplate calligraphy and meld that with his initial experiments with fine, flat nibs. The result is wholly unique and useful when clear, open, and legible script typography is desired. OpenType features included in this typeface allow the user to seamlessly move from an italic to connected script, while the various stylistic sets can lead you to variations of texture and rhythm, allowing for a more personal and exact expression. [ positype.com ]

typefaces.name: DOSS
typefaces.desc: Inspired by the logotypes of construction and hi-fi audio brands, DOSS is a collection of four display-oriented typefaces that also reference the aesthetics of ‘90s rave culture and ‘80s sci-fi tropes. The quartet was designed by Marc Rouault over a period of five years, forming a loose confederacy of fonts that reveals his fascination with vernacular typography—in this case, the aesthetics of electronics and their branding. Available all together or as individual styles, the DOSS collection includes Exaflop, Acid, Plexus, and Problem. While each has its own unique flavor, the styles within the Doss collection are unified by their exaggerated geometric structures, unexpectedly round counterforms, and unicase character sets. A graphic designer’s type designer, Marc’s output maintains a balance of inventive curiosity and sharp technical prowess. DOSS is no exception, offering a toolbox of riches to the intrepid designer seeking to explore the limits of ultra-display typography.

typefaces.name: Down
typefaces.desc: Inspired by the purposeful type that we encounter in such places as the auto mechanic’s garage, the laundromat, the county courthouse stairwell and even that cardboard box indicating “this way down”. [ luxtypo.com ] Available as a free download when signing up to the foundry’s newsletter.

typefaces.name: Drafter
typefaces.desc: Inspired by hand-painted signage, Drafter is a bold, all caps typeface built to stand out. [ doubledagger.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Drat
typefaces.desc: Drat is a rock-solid, sturdy slab serif available in 14 static weights as well as a variable version. Drat is Central Type's interpretation of the “Grecian” category of wood type. With examples dating all the way back to the 1840s, it's a style most notable for the absence of curve edges. We took cues from some of our favorites of the genre (Bartuska Satanic, City, ITC Machine) and aimed for something both fresh and hopelessly nostalgic. In others, just the way we here at Central Type like it. [ centraltype.com ]

typefaces.name: Drummond
typefaces.desc: This typeface is the result of work started between 2018 and 2019 during the Expert class Type design course held at the Museum Plantin-Moretus in Antwerp, Belgium. From the initial research in the Plantin-Moretus collection, I was particularly interested in sets of matrices or punches that were incomplete, fragmented, and highlighted in the inventory with hesitant annotations or suppositions about their authorship. I think these sets attracted attention because, like many other well-known pieces, they also highlight the excellence of Renaissance typography, although they may not receive the same distinction as other widely recognized artifacts. Furthermore, dealing with a fragmented object of study would allow more space for research and interpretation – elements that I enjoy exploring in my work. In this context, I was fascinated by the characteristics of the set of matrices Mediane Romaine, which, in the inventory of the Plantin-Moretus collection, is described as "a beautiful face, sixteenth century French in style, resembling but not the same as the Median Romain used by Garamont in the books published with Barbé in 1545, apparently not used by Plantin; deserving of detailed s

typefaces.name: DT Hooke
typefaces.desc: Hooke is a high-contrast condensed typeface designed to balance strength with elegance. Inspired by the functional beauty of hooks, it reflects the tension between fluidity and precision. Its sharp ink traps and even sharper terminals evoke the pointed edges of a hook’s barb, while the bars curve with a natural bend, capturing the dynamic motion of catching or pulling. Hooke’s structured yet expressive design makes it ideal for large sizes, where its refined details and striking contrast come to life with clarity and purpose. [ deathoftypography.com ]

typefaces.name: Dual Casual
typefaces.desc: Dual Casual is a variable font family inspired by casual letters, a popular style in the sign painting trade. Its carefully crafted features create a cheerful, vibrant, and familiar design. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Dug
typefaces.desc: Dug is a bottom-heavy, ultra bold display family that evokes the personality and warmth of the best fonts of the psychedelic era. Dug is available in 3 standard styles as well as matching italic versions. For even more versatility and added control, Dug is also available as a variable font. Dug's general look is inspired by the late 1960s trend towards exaggerated heaviness in the base of the letters. This look can often be found in custom lettering featured on candy packaging, album covers, and book jackets of that era. A number of notable commercial typefaces from that time also feature the look (Village, Bottleneck, Obese, Scorpio). Dug is a contemporary interpretation of the "bottom-heavy" style. Drawn with large round shapes and sturdy geometric sans construction. Dug is big, loud, and friendly. It's boldness lends itself to be decorated with inlines, outlines, shadows, and other shading techniques. [ centraltype.com ]

typefaces.name: Dulcinea
typefaces.desc: Dulcinea is the title of Ramiro Espinoza’s in-depth look at Spanish Baroque calligraphy’s most extreme tendencies, and especially at some of those produced by the writing masters Pedro Díaz Morante and Juan Claudio Aznar de Polanco. These new 17th and 18th centuries alphabets with their plentiful calligraphic flourishes represented a marked break with the harmonic and angular Renaissance Cancellaresca style. It was Morante who first introduced and popularized the use of the pointed quill in Spain, and although his famous text entitled “Arte Nueva de escribir” – first volume published in 1616 – contains alphabets that have much in common with traditional broad nib Cancellaresca calligraphy, most of the examples therein are outgrowths of the new models put forward by the Italian master Gianfrancesco Cresci. The writing’s swashes are complex and intricate, but at the same time they feature a profusion of defects. Many of them sometimes come close to ugliness. However, these pages contain an artistic essence that bears a relationship to the ironic and sometimes somber character of Spanish Baroque. That’s why the name of the font pays homage to “Dulcinea del Toboso”, the fictional beaut

typefaces.name: Dunhill Script
typefaces.desc: A bit of happenstance and accident are always full of possibility — Richard Lipton’s Dunhill Script is based on observations of the work of his left-handed calligraphy students and then from a small detail generated by his own freehand sketching. Like his other script typefaces, Dunhill was born from the desire to achieve a particular visual drama. Many details show the pen at work, like the terminal shapes, caps, and ascenders. It’s a great choice for editorial display or advertising and branding. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Early Sans
typefaces.desc: Inspired by an 1894 metal type specimen by Wilhelm Woellmer’s Schriftgiesserei in Berlin.

typefaces.name: Easy Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Easy Grotesk? It’s confident and optimistic. It’s fresh, friendly and combines the conventional with the surprising; trust and familiarity with a visual twist. Easy Grotesk brings together two opposing aesthetics. There’s the easy-going typographic texture on the one hand, and quirky character on the other. Useful and functional, this cheerful helper is carefree but not careless. It’s Easy, not lazy! Expressive gestures are key to Easy Grotesk’s personality. It may follow a standard neo-grotesque model, but it plays with the principles. Where, ordinarily, the lower parts of a letter are a little larger to make it feel more stable, Easy is dynamic: the top heavy, almost upside down s and signature a are only a few of the details that bring playful character to typography. Easy Grotesk’s unmistakable appearance pulls the reader closer. While its proportions give the typeface distinction and impact at display sizes, they’re subtle at smaller ones. Level-headed proportions, ample body, and spontaneous detailing delivers content with joie de vivre. Originally designed for a tech startup, its seven styles, matching italics and relaxed attitude can organise complex information and make it

typefaces.name: EB Ackerhof
typefaces.desc: A rotalic style was added in 2024.

typefaces.name: EB Reklame
typefaces.desc: An interpretation of Windsor.

typefaces.name: Ecru
typefaces.desc: Ecru is based on four unique capitals designed by Los Angeles graphic artist Margo Chase for a single use. Richard Lipton examined these four letters: E, C, R, and U. To his designer’s eye, they implied a complete typeface, so he expanded them to a full working set of condensed capitals, then designed and added a new lowercase, figures, and punctuation, bringing into being an ornate and lively addition to any display repertory. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Edificio
typefaces.desc: Edificio is a typeface inspired by the façade engraving of the Waldorf Astoria Hotel building in New York City, initially drawn by architects Schultze & Weaver directly on the historic elevations. The architects have intentionally or intuitively subverted the art-deco monumental letterforms to give more room to geometric and modernist design. In the same spirit, Edificio possesses anachronistic and contemporary characteristics, creating a hybrid look that could be defined as something like “deco-modernist." We have expanded this “façade inscription” into a single cut font with an extended latin character set. [ abc-etc.com ]

typefaces.name: Editorial Sans
typefaces.desc: Editorial Sans is a typeface that seamlessly bridges the past and present, embodying a retro-modern aesthetic. Building on the legacy of its serif counterpart, Editorial New , it retains the same proportions and metrics but with a sleek sans-serif design.

typefaces.name: Egads
typefaces.desc: A hearty sans with firm footing on the baseline, Egads is a true exclamation of a display typeface. You'll find it all here: Low stroke contrast, straight-cut terminals and a can-do attitude. Egads leans into the energy of classic geo-sans typefaces like ITC Kabel and Grizzly , but subverts that familiar feeling of order with its highly exaggerated bottom-heaviness. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Eina
typefaces.desc: We designed Eina as a corporate typeface for EINA, University Center of Art and Design. It is more than a functional font – Eina embodies an educational concept that transcends simple typographic use. Eina is a typeface with teaching potential, a way to learn about typography. The publication Four Nuances of a Typographic Standard: A Typeface for EINA reflects the entire design and development process. [ extratype.com ]

typefaces.name: EK Baumer Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Baumer Grotesk is a sans-serif that follows the principles of Neo-Grotesque typefaces. With a strong focus on functionality, it combines a clear, neutral design language with soft curves, creating a harmonious and distinctive look. The blend of rationality and subtle friendliness results in a typeface that is versatile across a wide range of applications. With an efficient selection of four weights and corresponding italics, Baumer Grotesk provides everything needed for the effective use of type styles and hierarchies. It offers a wide range of stylistic alternates, especially suited for brand identity, providing a solid foundation for customization without compromising readability or cohesion. Supporting the full Latin language and featuring modern OpenType functionalities, Baumer Grotesk is not only versatile but also a contemporary, timeless typeface ready to meet the demands of modern typography. [ erkinkaramemet.com ] Initially a digitization of Folio (Bauer, 1957) incorporating elements from various sans serif designs such as Mercator (Typefoundry Amsterdam, 1958), later evolving into a distinct design.

typefaces.name: Elaphus
typefaces.desc: With great support of ↗ Bruce Kennett and others, I was able to get my hands on original drawings of an unfinished typeface by W. A. Dwiggins for Linotype in 1947. I wanted to keep a warm and organic quality within my interpretation for a lively texture, in true with Dwiggins’ intent and style. For the Italics I went back even further in time, to one of the best punchcutters to ever do it: Robert Granjon and his «Gros Romain» from ~1550. This project is in a very early stage and a display version with a modern twist will soon be the counterpart to this classic, soft text-face. [ deinwaller.com ]

typefaces.name: Electric Blue
typefaces.desc: Electric Blue is a rounded pixel typeface derived from Daniël’s experimentation with melting and conjoining pixels. It is a variable font with extremely bold and thin poles and a surprising switch in-between. The look of Electric Blue taps into the nostalgia of retro futuristic design from the Space Age 60’s and Neon Glow 80’s. While it might awake associations to existing typefaces, we can asure you, that these are purely coincidental. The technical challenge to switch from apart elements to conjoined letters, pushed Edgar to the outskirts of variable font engineering. Not every software (looking at you After Effects) might support all features, but we went out of our ways to support as many environments as possible. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Elido
typefaces.desc: Elido (Odile in reverse) is the sans counterpart to Odile, a serif type. Together they form a sans and serif superfamily with a wide range of variations for editorial and display use. Elido follows Odile’s proportions and matches the weight distribution and typographic color of its serif twin. Elido is a sans with classical proportions. Odile’s conceptual approach is echoed in the structure and anatomy of the Elido family. The arched stroke low off the stem reveals a script characteristic most pronounced in the Elido Upright Italic. This particular interpretation is gradually diminished in the Italic and becomes even less emphasized in the Regular style. Six balanced weights, from an elegant Light to a pronounced Black, are in tune with three display solutions and a set of beautiful Ornaments. [ kontour.com ]

typefaces.name: Ellery
typefaces.desc: Ellery is an elegant display typeface inspired by Oscar Ogg’s calligraphed book jackets from the ’40s for Atlantic/Little-Brown & Company. This delicate and warm family has a suggested size range of 14pt and higher. The flowing Italic pairs well with the Roman yet is also truly expressive on its own in large display settings. Richard Lipton’s Ellery is ideal for any typography needing distinction and grace. Available in Regular, Medium, Bold, and Extra Bold, with Italics, or as Variable Fonts. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Elmira
typefaces.desc: Elmira was the final project I did during Typemedia. It is a family inspired by the process that type goes through when being woven in industrial power looms. The styles influenced and inspired each other, so they share similar design approaches, metrics and sometimes letter structures. The family pack consists of 3 main sets of styles, a sans grotesque for small typesetting, and 4 "loom" display versions, two vertical and two horizontal (which indicates the direction of the grid). This is a versatile family that can work well together or be broken apart, because of the styles personalities. All the loom display styles can be paired, juxtaposed or layered giving a lot of choices to the end user. Color fonts have also been added to the pack, so this woven front-back layered characteristic of the font can be featured in web and apps. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Elysian
typefaces.desc: Elysian is a Transitional Serif typeface inspired by the feeling of being creatively & divinely inspired – utterly in a state of blissful delight & perfection. As an ode to the paradisiacal Elysium from Greek mythology, this font has embellished terminals & features, sharp & compelling Serifs, and classically-styled numerals. [ typeoffeeling.com ]

typefaces.name: Empress
typefaces.desc: Empress (formally known as Vilaage) is a versatile flared serif derived from the lettering found around Hackney Village, just north of Victoria Park in East London. The lettering found around the Village ranges in width and weight, but are unified by ornamental and luxurious characteristics, predominantly the drooping crossbar found in the A and H – these are reflected in this typeface through stylistic sets. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Enfilade
typefaces.desc: Enfilade is a condensed grotesk with four optical variations. Each optical variant is optimized to work at half the point size of the previous variant to make establishing hierarchy a breeze. [ futurefonts.com ] Updated in January 2025 to include all optical sizes in a single two-axis variable font.

typefaces.name: Englewood
typefaces.desc: Englewood is an expressive script inspired by the calligraphic hand of Philip Grushkin. Richard Lipton has always admired this somewhat loose but disciplined style and felt it was worth keeping alive in a typeface that could accurately emulate the spontaneity and warmth of these letterforms. Lipton hoped to honor Mr. Grushkin with a design that works exceptionally well for an invitation, a menu, or in any display setting that calls for an informal calligraphic hand. This single-weight display script includes small caps — a rarity in a handwritten script — for flexible typesetting, along with alternates and ligatures to simulate the appearance of spontaneous writing. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: EnjoyFun
typefaces.desc: These letters are an exercise in extremes, historical reference and joyful drawing activity. The initial offering of this EnjoyFun family comprises two quite different, yet related sets of letters: Squodge and Bone. Squodge takes its name from the descriptive text for Hipsterpotamus, but has no wish to steal its bloated thunder. Squodge is a far curvier affair than that fellow: a weighty, slightly italicised counterless collection of rascals, with elements of balloon animals; dough; juicy fruits; slices of yummy pie, whipped cream and er... other things. Bone is the skeleton of Squodge, a slender design that follows many of the mannerisms inherent in its weighty sibling, and has more chance to display its historical influence. Overlayment. as shown in some of the images above, demonstrates that they share many characteristics. The fonts also contain a second set of lettershapes for all capitals and lowercase, special code within these automatically ensures that double letters are not visually repeated, and of course, the whole palette of letters are available to you for your own word compositions. [ shapesforcash.com ]

typefaces.name: Epitaph
typefaces.desc: Drawn around 1880 at the Boston Type Foundry, Epitaph combined slow curves with a boxy sure-footed profile. Its noisy theatrics caught Tobias Frere-Jones’ eye, who created this digital revival. Starting with a handful of alternates from the original, he also built a complete second alphabet, offered alongside the default. [ store.typenetwork.com ] Originally released by Font Bureau in 1993 and moved to Frere–Jones Type in 2020 [ fontsinuse.com ], available through Type Network and added to the foundry’s website in December 2024.

typefaces.name: Ermine
typefaces.desc: Ermine is a typeface inspired by the original Works Progress Administration National Park Service Posters from the early 20th Century, of which there only a handful of designs. The the odd, variable width, hand-painted lettering style on these posters exemplifies a dilligent work ethic, an honesty in its production, a warmth and imperfection of handicraft, and a connection to the land. It was these qualities that compelled us to bring Ermine to life across five widths, all designed to be mixed and matched.

typefaces.name: Ernst
typefaces.desc: Ernst is an elegant but playful slab serif which harks back to some peculiar early 20th-century types but responds to contemporary demands by offering a wide range of applications. Not properly a revival, Ernst blends type details from avant-garde faces such as Ernst Deutsch/Dryden’s Tango and Georg Belwe’s Belwe Antiqua. Its pronounced and frisky details make it a strong candidate for display work, while the big x-height, its design rigour and consistency of proportions also make it suitable for long texts. The name Ernst is a tribute to Ernst Deutsch/Dryden, an Austrian designer who in his younger years did some remarkable lettering besides his Tango typeface released by Schriftgiesserei Julius Klinkhardt in 1913–1916, and later by H. Berthold AG. In German ‘ernst’ means ‘serious’; but our Ernst is anything but serious – especially with its whimsical italic that recalls the lettering of early 20th-century Parisian street theatres and silent movies. [ c-a-s-t.com ]

typefaces.name: Eros
typefaces.desc: Eros lives up to its name. It is the loving fusion of 2 custom typefaces we drew in the past years: a condensed one for Le Théâtre des Bouffes du Nord and a regular one for Pharrell Williams and Jean Imbert’s common project in Saint-Tropez. Eros' aesthetic is inspired by the art movement of Jugendstil and Vienna Secession in the late 19th century and are redesigned with a strong contemporary touch that brings an elegant sharpness to the drawing.Eros has a very refined expression, it conveys a beautiful organic feeling and yet the typeface is still functional. Eros Condensed is consistent with Eros Standard but shows its own characteristics as it is more than just a variation. Eros Condensed has its own design. The condensed « O » is coded to interact with the letter next to it. It will adapt whether it's next to uppercases or lowercases and this special feature gives quite some flow to the typeface. We drew 30 pairs of uppercase ligatures and 30 pairs of lowercases ligatures to ensure the most beautiful sequences of words possible. [ vj-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Eroticon
typefaces.desc: We're all familiar with the concept of sexy curves. Can bézier curves be sexy? Are sophisticated ligatures synonymous with something secretly erotic? Extreme kerning pairs with something intimate? Eroticon is a high-contrast serif typeface with a distinctly narrow shape. Wide alternations of rounded characters and swash variations give the typeface an unmistakable character and dynamic nature. The character set, in addition to the extended Latin alphabet, includes Cyrillic and Greek alphabets. [ suitcasetype.com ]

typefaces.name: ES Park
typefaces.desc: ES Park is a “more or less” baroque serif typeface designed by Xavier Erni (Neo Neo) and developed by Lisa Schultz. Its curves are inspired by the shapes of two famous predecessors: Clarendon and American Typewriter. Due to its design features and thick, block-like serifs, it can be classified as a Slab Serif (also known as Mechanistic, Antique, or Egyptian). However, its serifs are designed slightly narrower than those of other slabs. The thinner weights are drawn with less contrast than the heavier ones, making it highly legible at smaller sizes while remaining very impactful in bolder texts. It is perfectly suited to grabbing the reader’s attention. In its default version, the terminals are designed as mini-serifs, adding a subtle ornamental aesthetic to the typeface. [ extraset.ch ]

typefaces.name: Eternal Collection
typefaces.desc: Eternal Collection is a display font family that is designed for high-impact visual communication, this font family features a striking combination of serif detailing and high contrast proportions. With an extensive range of 162 styles, Eternal Collection offers a broad range of creative possibilities. The family includes variations in width, weight, and slant, allowing for nuanced typographic expression across various design contexts. From bold, commanding headlines to delicate, refined subheadings, this font family ensures that every design element can be tailored to the precise mood and tone you wish to convey. Choose from a full spectrum of widths, from compressed to wide, and a variety of weights, from thin to black. The inclusion of slant styles adds an extra dimension of flexibility for dynamic, forward-leaning typography. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Eterne Display
typefaces.desc: Dynamic, dramatic, and dense with detail, Eterne Display is a compact and springy suite of titling fonts drawn by Kia Tasbihgou. As eye-catching as it is unconventional, its condensed forms have been gracefully articulated with skilled pageantry. Eterne Display began as a direct response to printed magician’s ephemera and reveals its designer’s legerdemain, taking cues from French titling types like Deberny & Peignot’s Elzévir Gras Allongé. Idiosyncratic incisions and gestural twists on convention are deftly deployed to suit editorial contexts in which prestige, pragmatism, and space are at a premium. [ sharptype.co ]

typefaces.name: Eterne Text
typefaces.desc: Eterne Text’s refined clarity of construction imparts impeccable readability to an unconventional model. This polished pop recontextualizes the joie de vivre that makes its display sibling so striking. Taking cues from the Marionette Formula proposed by W. A. Dwiggins, unexpected cuts and curves of the letterforms possess a lively tension and draw attention to the push-and-pull of space and counter-space. Shallow-shouldered arches, low contrast, and evenly proportioned terminals recall Miller & Richard’s Old Style Antique No. 7, translating the drama and gesture of the Eterne family into a system that is eminently scalable. [ sharptype.co ]

typefaces.name: Eudald
typefaces.desc: Released in 2006 as Eudald News, reissued in 2025 as Eudald.

typefaces.name: Euphemia
typefaces.desc: Euphemia in its most recent form is a thorough reworking and extension of Ross Mills’ original design, fulfilling his intent for a harmonised Latin and Canadian Syllabics typeface. The stroke weight, proportions and spacing of both scripts have been carefully revised to better balance in bilingual text, and the Latin character coverage and OpenType Layout glyph variant and feature set has been significantly extended in the full Euphemia and Latin subset fonts, and includes support for all modern European alphabets as well as diacritic letters for the Latin orthographies of indigenous languages alternatively or historically written in Syllabics. The Euphemia Syllabics subset fonts are available under our pay-what-you-want system to support indigenous language use. [ tiro.com ]

typefaces.name: Exact
typefaces.desc: Finalized in 2024. When we were a teenager putting together our first design portfolio, back in the days of rubber cement and X-Acto knives, we were obsessed with Times New Roman. We knew it was prissy and joyless, but we didn’t mind. We were prissy and joyless ourselves. We loved its air of strict, unbending neutrality, and we bought sheet upon Letraset sheet of it and used it for everything we could. But as we grew older and learned a bit about letters, we realised that it actually wasn’t very well made. This is not surprising, since TNR was art directed by Stanley Morison, a man who never pretended he could draw, and drawn by nobody in particular. A lettering artist named Victor Lardent did the initial concept art. This was then turned over to the 1930s hive mind—the Monotype Drawing Office—and expanded into a range of weights and widths with no one, apparently, talking to anyone else throughout the process. TNR did its job as a modern newspaper type brilliantly without ever actually being any good. It subsequently became numbingly ubiquitous because it was less trouble to use than not, and at last was shunned by right-thinking design- ers everywhere. But in recent years typogra

typefaces.name: Exetegue
typefaces.desc: Exetegue is a very narrow, all-caps typeface, where the diacritcs are pushed inside the capitals’ case. It’s ideal for titles with tight leading. [ fonts.scannerlicker.net ] Released as open-source on GitHub .

typefaces.name: Experimo
typefaces.desc: Experimo is an experimental display sans serif font family that celebrates the juxtaposed contrast between the round and rectangle shapes. […] The font conveys a modern and futuristic feel while being playful and distinct. [ r9typedesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Explicit
typefaces.desc: Explicit is a narrow, reverse contrast geometric typeface informed by a disparate variety of past counter cultural typographic sources. The very graphic, unorthodox typographic sensibilities found in these obscure art, music, and street apparel references were the catalyst in its inception. Despite this, it wasn’t derived from any particular reference and was primarily designed from memory. Conceptually, it is defined by an intentionally unconventional, disruptive, and forward attitude, similar to the references that inspired it. Although it shares characteristics with Materiel, Explicit is foremost distinct in concept. Through this distinction, its direction was realized materially, and primarily shaped manually. Letterforms were carefully edited in a particularly reductive manner, increasing their clarity and in some cases their density. Remaining angular details were blunted or squared, providing a neutral counter to its overt expressive posture. As a result, Explicit is more than the sum of its parts or automated processes. It is the culmination of a uniquely conceptual origin, paired with intent, and supported by an acute level of detail. Altogether, these factors impart Expli

typefaces.name: Explorers
typefaces.desc: Sometime in the 20th century, I sent a design to the Morisawa Typeface Competition. It won a prize. I called the typeface Vespucci (I suppose I had been reading something about the origin of America at the time.) You will be able to see the original design – as presented in Morisawa’s brochure – by scrolling the gallery above. At a later date, I found myself drawing more fat grotesques, and as I had named a similar design after an explorer, I carried on (sometimes naming a typeface is harder than designing it). There was no initial plan to make these designs belong together, I was just enjoying the drawing. The collection of sketches eventually grew to the point where a stapler was required, and so it seemed like a good idea to try and impose some order on them. Many of their base characteristics were brought into some kind of alignment with each other, and they were forced to share an x-height and other vertical metrics (extenders [ascenders & descenders]). The years passed, and I continued messing about. I thought it would be nice for each character in the now 20+ designs to share the same widths, so that they could be interchanged to make some interesting interactions of shape.

typefaces.name: Exposure
typefaces.desc: Exposure borrows the eponymous principle from photography, using it to question the possibilities offered by variable fonts in a completely original way. While studying at the Atelier national de recherche typographique (Nancy, France), Federico Parra Barrios took a very unique approach to the technique, developing a singular typeface between 2019 and 2022. Available in Roman and Italic, Exposure is a remarkable feat—both technically and in terms of drawing—that shows how other ways of exploiting variable font technology are possible. While variable fonts—which appeared in 2016—are considered to be a major development in typography, the use of axes of variation to modify weight, set-width, and optical size are all transformations inherited from previous techniques. Federico Parra Barrios breaks away from this conventional approach to propose a new way of thinking. Exposure’s axis of variation ranges from –100 to +100, and gives a feeling of adjusting the intensity of the light to which the typeface is exposed, thus affecting its outline. Some might see this as a nod to another, now defunct, technique: phototypesetting. [ 205.tf ]

typefaces.name: F37 Arcade
typefaces.desc: Leap back in time with F37 Arcade, a typeface inspired by the iconic arcade aesthetic and informed by Wim Crouwel’s grid-based work. F37 Arcade is a modular, mono-spaced, and stencil typeface. With a unique combination of modularity and stencil, the letterforms are reminicent of falling Tetris blocks that appear to be on the brink of slotting together. Also prominent throughout the typeface are rounded corners. These reference the rounding effect CRT glow has on type within arcade games. F37 Arcade is further packed with ligatures and alternate characters to keep you playing for hours. [ f37foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: F37 Atlantic
typefaces.desc: There’s something a little fishy about F37 Atlantic, which manages to be simultaneously curvaceous and spiky, mimicking the peaks, troughs and juxtaposing patterns of the wavy seas. Inspired by Herb Lubalin’s 1972 ITC Serif Gothic font, we’ve exaggerated and emphasised the ocean-going elements, with swooshes or wave-like features on selected spurs and terminals, breaking up the sturdy and otherwise classic geometric strokes. Strong, bold curvature is contrasted with sharp, pointy details. Swooshes abound. The letterforms mimic the movement and rolling motion of the sea as words form and break. [ f37foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: F37 August
typefaces.desc: F37 August is our humble homage to Futura, Paul Friedrich August Renner’s genre-definining geometric sans serif. F37 August is a direct descendant of Futura, one of the all-time great typefaces. Designed by the German designer, author and founder of the Master School for Germany's Printers Paul Renner in 1927, we're totally in awe of Futura here at F37. We even went as far only consulting primary sources of Renner's original cut as reference throughout the design process. Like its distinguished forebear, F37 August uses strikingly symmetrical circular geometric lines in the curves of the letterforms and varied character widths. We've also stayed true to the vertical proportions of Futura, keeping the tall ascenders and descenders that evoke the classical vertical proportions that were popular before the x-height growth spurt of the late 20th century. While the affinity to Futura is immediately apparent, F37 August does contain its own personality. Features like, an overbite on the 'g', blunt diagonals and updated numbers all lend to the F37 August's individuality. We've also developed two alternate character sets. The first is based on experimental drawings by Renner and features e

typefaces.name: F37 Bergman
typefaces.desc: F37 Bergman is a revival of Hans Möhring’s Florida typeface. Swedish film director Ingmar Bergman often used Florida in his films — always in stark black and white. This inspired us to digitalise the font and create a matching lowercase version in four new weights. We love Möhring’s juxtaposition of tapered stems and geometric thick/thin lines. This makes it perfect for luxury branding and editorial work. We’ve also injected some modernity into the design by creating numerous Herb Lubalin-style ligatures, as well as stylistic headline diacritics. [ f37foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: F37 Bezier
typefaces.desc: F37 Bezier exposes what is often hidden, championing the nodes that connect bézier curves as a design element themselves. The F37 Bezier font family is available in three styles. Two styles, Node Large and Node Small, give user control over impact of the nodes. When large, the nodes dominate the letter forms, leaving only an elusive glimpse of the actual glyph behind them. When the nodes are small they appear as a smattering across the letter forms. The third style, is the non-nonsense underlying sans serif, perfect as a text style accompaniment to the two node styles. [ f37foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: F37 Blanka
typefaces.desc: Blanka is F37’s take on a clean, classic Swiss sans. Perfect for body copy, it’s economical, functional and very legible at small sizes. It’s the holy grail — an everyday workhorse sans font that’s a little different, but doesn’t distract when used as body copy. We designed Blanka as an approachable grotesque with nuanced humanist inclinations. It takes its cue mainly from the classic pair of Helvetica and Futura. But the slightly angled terminals are a tribute to Neuzeit Grotesk. Blanka comes in a wide range of weights, from delicately light to imposingly heavy. We’ve painstakingly manually hinted the letterforms to make sure they’re really crisp and clear on screens of all shapes and sizes, regardless of pixel density or render. We like it so much, we’ve used it for our own website. [ f37foundry.com ] Updated in 2023.

typefaces.name: F37 Bobby
typefaces.desc: A warm and friendly headline serif with a subtle geometric twist. F37 Bobby is a contemporary geometric serif. Its design was influenced by the warm serifs that were popular back in the 1970s. We took inspiration from the rounded, friendly feel of fonts like Souvenir, Windsor and Cooper Black. This is a font with brands in mind: if you’re looking for a cool font that’ll work well for identity work, with a bit of standout, Bobby might be your boy. It’ll also work well for the luxury and fashion worlds. The F37 Bobby family comes in six weights with matching true italics. Version 3.0 adds extensive Arabic language support. The soft features and gestural Naskh strokes of F37 Bobby Arabic pair perfectly with the look and feel of the Latin — and work equally well stand alone. [ f37foundry.com ] Updated in 2023 with Naskh-style Arabic.

typefaces.name: F37 Britain
typefaces.desc: What is it that makes something look typically British? That’s pretty hard to put your finger on. Because the nation’s peculiar visual vernacular comprises thousands of small quirks and nuances. Many of these are so commonplace they go virtually unnoticed — they’re around us on the streets, our homes, objects that we pick up and use every day. We take them for granted, they’re just part of the national socio-cultural landscape. This was the idea behind the F37 British Collection, a collection of seven disparate but perfectly patriotic fonts. We’ve taken our inspiration from all nooks, corner and crannies of the land — from Victorian theatre posters and antique maps, to wood-type specimens and Leicestershire typewriter impressions. We’ve paid homage to John Baskerville, the father of transitional typography and Edward Johnston, the man who took letterforms Underground. We’ve referenced the Union flag and Scottish foundries, classic serifs and ever-popular sans serifs. Together, they reflect the hope and the glory of everyday British life. They celebrate our collective character and eccentricities. They nod to our past while looking stiff-upper-lippedly into the future.

typefaces.name: F37 Caligari
typefaces.desc: Blackletter is a genre steeped in history and ripe for modernisation. Unfortunately, while it is a highly evocative genre it is often overlooked these days. At F37 we decided to fill this gap in our library with F37 Caligari. Named after the titular character of the first true horror film, the font is as vivid and expressive as its namesake. We based F37 Caligari on a traditional Textura hand, a style constrained by limitations. However, we embraced these limitations for a modern audience, dialling up the angularity and sharpness of the style well past anything a medieval scribe would dare to do. F37 Caligari is available in six weights. Throughout the weights, the energy of the font changes. The lighter weights are made up of uniform and parallel strokes, while the heavier weights from flared and lively strokes. F37 Caligari also comes with swashed capitals, perfect for drop caps, logos, or your next illuminated manuscript. [ f37foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: F37 Club
typefaces.desc: F37 Club, a typeface that pulses with energy. With slightly condensed proportions, it draws inspiration from sound waves and vibrations, bringing rhythm to every letter. Each character is crafted from two dynamic parts, creating a sense of movement without sacrificing legibility. [ f37foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: F37 Confusa
typefaces.desc: F37 Confusa is a single-weight font with kerning so tight, the letters appear to fuse together. Using a clever and extensive set of alternate characters, the font seamlessly merges as you type. While at first glance, the words might seem indistinguishable, there is a method in the madness. We worked closely with Ceci to strike a careful balance between her reality-blurring vision and the need for readability in practical use. [ f37foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: F37 Fatigue
typefaces.desc: Exhausted by endless sans serifs? Fatigued by too many type choices? F37 Fatigue is a sharp and serene sans serif designed to cut through the grotesque monotony. Based on a humanist sans serif, its sharp vertical terminals provide the perfect foundation for a fresh, visually striking take on the genre. Combined with geometric undertones, F37 Fatigue feels contemporary amidst a sea of choice. [ f37foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: F37 Ginger
typefaces.desc: F37 Ginger’s geometric shapes and unusual near-circular counters, make it an ideal choice for logos and headlines. F37 Ginger is our best seller. Since its birth in 2013, this sleek, geometric san-serif font has been used by some of the world’s biggest companies, becoming a favourite with brands such as Google, Pepsi and Barbour. While we were drawing F37 Ginger, we repeatedly returned to the work of two legendary typographers — Paul Renner and Herb Lubalin. In particular, it was the alternatives in Renner’s Futura and Lubalin’s Avant Garde Gothic, that paved the way for F37 Ginger’s geometric slant. Over the years we have updated and improved F37 Ginger with refined and optimised proportions. We’ve also extended extended the choices of weights and styles, with a Soft variant now available. Currently, F37 Ginger supports a wide range of languages, with over 500 glyphs, covering 252+ languages, including Extended Latin, Cyrillic and Greek writing systems. Version 5.0 further adds support for languages using the Arabic script, including: Standard Arabic, Farsi and Urdu. To pair seamlessly with the original 3 scripts, F37 Ginger Arabic is routed in a contemporary blend of Kufic and Na

typefaces.name: F37 Haggler
typefaces.desc: Introducing F37 Haggler: you won’t find a better quality condensed sans this side of the Atlantic. Don’t pass this up; buy now, and we’ll even throw a unicase set in with the upper and lower cases. Lovely jubbly. F37 Haggler is the last condensed sans you’ll ever need. “Why would I need another sans serif?” you ask. Well, F37 Haggler comes equipped with narrow proportions for those tight headlines, a large x-height to amplify your message, and a steep 14° slant matching italic. Unlike your typical boxy, flat-sided condensed sans, F37 Haggler keeps a roundness in its shapes. This gives the font family a natural and human feel, evocative of hand-painted signage and grocery store lettering. Don’t miss out! Try F37 Haggler now and hawk any of your wares with this clean and bold typefamily. As Del Boy might say, “You know it makes sense!” [ f37foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: F37 Judge
typefaces.desc: Updated in 2021 (v2), then in 2023 (v3) with the addition of Cyrillic and Arabic support.

typefaces.name: F37 Lemon
typefaces.desc: The starting point for F37 Lemon was the M-Formula concept, dreamed up by early 20th century type designer William Addison Dwiggins based on his experience of marionette carving. At F37, we take our inspiration wherever we can find it, like F37 Lemon, which owes it all to a puppet. Or, more accurately, a marionette, the ones operated by strings. US type designer, calligrapher and pipe-smoker William Addison Dwiggins also carved marionettes. He noticed that the ones with more flattened, angular faces were more expressive and suggested that this quality might apply to typographic letterforms too. So F37 Lemon tests this theory out, using an underlying humanist sans construction, along with open apertures, vertically cut terminals, interrupted strokes and moderate stroke contrast. Its counter forms are built around hard edges, which create curious, striking shapes at larger sizes and a really different, but very legible texture at smaller sizes. F37 Lemon is available in four weights with several alternate characters, such as a lowercase a, which is more legible at smaller sizes. It’s our font, but Dwiggins certainly had a hand in it. [ f37foundry.com ] Italic style added in 2024.

typefaces.name: F37 Lothian
typefaces.desc: Inspired by its namesake, Lothian is a landscape of rough crags, lush hills, and turbulent seas. Navigating within the aggressively rugged and enticingly quaint, F37 Lothian fills this space with a fully equipped and versatile type family. F37 Lothian draws structural inspiration from greats such as Garamond, Cloister, and Sabon. However, unlike these classics, F37 Lothian is finished with a blend of hard angles and delicate hairlines, making it perfect for elegant, modern headlines. It is available in 6 weights, covering a wide emotional range – from commandingly bold styles that flaunt their curves, to the unimaginably delicate hairline. To complement the upright styles, F37 Lothian is also available in true italics. These feature sharp in/out strokes and rounded descenders, allowing for a tonally humorous pairing. [ f37foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: F37 Morta
typefaces.desc: F37 Morta is a pixel font available in two weights, supporting both Latin and Arabic. The font takes its name from the game, ‘Children of Morta,’ developed by Iranian game designers, a nod to the designers heritage. Pixel fonts are usually designed on an 8x8 or 16x16 grid. This is a grid that suits the Latin characters well, but poses an exciting design challenge for the Arabic letters, trying to fit them within this limitation. Challenging characteristics of the script include: lettershapes extending below the baseline and multiple dots. Therefore, the Arabic design uses as few pixels as possible to achieve clarity and functionality while adhering to the grid. The Arabic version, based on the Naskh style and includes over 100 ligatures. F37 Morta also includes nostalgic gaming symbols like Pac-Man, a pixelated heart, and a dinosaur. The Latin version offers alternate characters, including four ampersand options. [ f37foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: F37 Neuro
typefaces.desc: F37 Neuro is inspired by neutral Swiss sans-serif fonts such as Akzidenz and Helvetica. But there’s a British influence too, namely Edward Johnston’s classic London Underground font. In fact, F37 Neuro’s shape and structure is based around the contrasting, expressive curves and distinct straight edges of Johnston’s masterpiece. Other subtle, quirky features have been sampled from IBM’s range of Selectric typewriter fonts from the 1960s. For example, the straight crossbar of the a and the downward tail on the top of the 7 take their inspiration from IBM Advocate. F37 Neuro comes in 12 weights. Its aesthetic is accessible, characterful and contemporary — reassuringly Swiss, but with a hint of British eccentricity that sets it apart. [ f37foundry.com ] Support for Arabic was released in 2024 and announced in January 2025.

typefaces.name: F37 Pythia
typefaces.desc: Originally named F37 Oracle, renamed to F37 Pythia in May 2025.

typefaces.name: F37 Qbik
typefaces.desc: F37 Qbik puts a new slant on hardcore geometric sans. It’s bold, powerful and uncompromising… although not so much in its rotalic form. Qbik is born from a brutalist design aesthetic, most of its characters are created out of basic geometric forms and with minimal optical adjustments. It feels hard, pure and confident, a font that knows exactly what it stands for and refuses to budge on principle. Apart from a couple of characterful quirks, like the cap Q, which resembles an upside-down yo-yo. Or the lowercase alternate g, that looks like it has tank tracks. This all starts to change in the companion variant version, which instead of the usual italics come as ‘rotalics’. With italics, the letterforms are slanted, with their feet planted firmly on the baseline. Rotalics however, are rotated to the right, so the characters kind of look like they’re ice-skating, or at least off balance and tottering forward. F37 Qbik is available across five weights, in both upright and rotalic, so 10 styles in all. Medium and regular work best for longer text, while light, bold and black are just the job for display and titling. [ f37foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Fabulosa
typefaces.desc: Fabulosa brings a unique blend of historical and creative influences, combining the bold ‘ fat face ’ typography style with the lively flair of Ed Benguiat’s Caslon Black Swash from the 1960s. The ‘fat face’ style, with its thick strokes, was pioneered by Robert Thorne in the early 19th century. Thorne’s design was a stronger version of modern type styles, known for its strong contrast and heavy serifs. Caslon Black Swash , on the other hand, captures the vibrant typographic creativity of the mid-20th century. Its swashes and decorative flourishes bring a nostalgic feel, reminiscent of ornate letterforms from earlier times, while fitting perfectly into the energetic graphic culture of the 70s. [ type-o-tones.com ]

typefaces.name: Factor A Mono
typefaces.desc: The monospaced companion to Factor A .

typefaces.name: Falconer
typefaces.desc: Falconer is a revival and adaptation of W. A. Dwiggins’ unpublished typeface Falcon . It blends historical sensibility with contemporary functionality to bring a deliberate, literary tone to both text and display typography. With moderate contrast and sturdy serifs, the roman performs well at smaller sizes, while the calligraphically informed italic adds warmth and personality. Falconer is a versatile font family and lends a distinct, classical voice to books, magazines, journals, and advertising. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Fata
