typefaces.desc: The first characters of Fata were originally designed for a pasta-cookbook which was unfortunately refused by the publisher. We turned the font into a 1001 nights experience which gives a lovely oriental feel.

typefaces.name: FDI Kromograph
typefaces.desc: A color font companion to FDI Lettograph , produced in two variants. FDI Kromograph A has 5 layers and features a 3D effect, while FDI Kromograph B has 3 layers and a color change effect activated through the “contextual alternates” OpenType feature.

typefaces.name: FDI Wunder
typefaces.desc: FDI Wunder is based on the typeface Laudahn-Kanzlei originally designed by Heinrich Laudahn and released by Bauer in 1913. FDI Wunder is a carefully crafted revival design based on the original letterpress fonts. [ fdi-type.de ] FDI Wunder is available in two styles, one that follows the original blackletter design and another with romanized letterforms. The fonts include a “dancing baseline” feature. Initially offered in October 2023 as a free download for Typography.guru supporters. Made available for general licensing in January 2025.

typefaces.name: Feint
typefaces.desc: Feint is engineered so every glyph has the same number of vectors and paths as every other glyph. I.e.- they are all 100% compatible with each other. By the numbers, Feint has 26 instances with 26 uppercase letters in each for a total of 676 glyphs. The first instance is the only one in alphabetical order; all 25 other instances are randomized. Confused? Give it a try in the Features section below to see for yourself. Moving the slider along the “CYFR” axis morphs every uppercase letter into every other letter — instance by instance — visually scrambling the original message while the underlying codepoint remains intact (even if the glyph you see is not what you typed. [ delvefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Fenul
typefaces.desc: Italic style added in 2024. Fenul – Originally designed by Jana Papierníková and introduced in 2023, Fenul saw some exciting updates in 2024. With Italic styles added by Viktor Mizera, and True Cursive available through Stylistic Sets, this typeface offers incredible versatility—all in a single Variable Font file featuring three widths: Compressed, Condensed, and Standard.

typefaces.name: Fenway Banner
typefaces.desc: Fenway is a neoclassical serif design initially commissioned by Sports Illustrated. It has excellent copyfit and strong color—precisely the qualities needed for rigorous book typography and demanding publication design. Matthew Carter designed the Romans to be robust and the Italics economic, both holding the potential to be stalwart mainstays for any typographic designer. [ carterandcone.com ] With contributions by Jill Pichotta and Richard Lipton [ linkedin.com ]. Produced in four widths and five weights, in upright and italic styles.

typefaces.name: Feraz Condensed
typefaces.desc: Feraz is a condensed typeface, ideal for headlines, logos and posters. The delicate feel of the thinner weights translates into the bolder ones by softening the curves and relaxing the angles. [ giuliaboggio.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Fest
typefaces.desc: The first basic characters were originally designed in 2013 for the cover of a book for French Masterchef Michel Roux. In 2014 we completed the font and designed some extra glyphs, swooshes and ligatures.

typefaces.name: Fetza
typefaces.desc: Initially named Festa (used for the sample image).

typefaces.name: FH Anorma
typefaces.desc: Originating from calligraphic sketches in 2022, this typeface has been shaped through years of knowledge and experience. Each letter, subtly defined by the calligraphy brush, comes together with a modern aesthetic sensibility. The term "A norma," meaning adherence to standards and rules in Italian, reflects the typeface’s embodiment of order and discipline in a refined manner. […] Respectfully paying homage to "Griffo’s Roman" and "Bodoni" typefaces, this typography offers both traditional and modern aesthetics. [ typografische.com ]

typefaces.name: FH Oscar Pro
typefaces.desc: FH Oscar Pro is an enhanced contemporary typeface that builds upon the foundation of its predecessor, FH Oscar. Drawing inspiration from the iconic structures of Akzidenz Grotesk and Breite Grotesk, this typeface has evolved to meet the diverse needs of modern design. The evolution of FH Oscar Pro includes the addition of new alternate glyphs, as well as the incorporation of Cyrillic and Greek alphabets, making it a versatile choice for global communication. [ typografische.com ]

typefaces.name: Fictional
typefaces.desc: Fictional is a lively and playful typeface with a cartoonesque character, crafted to bring warmth and quirkiness to your designs. [ jonastype.com ]

typefaces.name: Fields
typefaces.desc: Fields, Fields Display, and now Fields Big are a versatile family with three optical sizes blending casual, retro tones with modern touches. The details like rounded serifs, teardrop terminals, and subtle tails make this typeface friendly and approachable. Fields is excellent for branding! Whether you want that vintage 1970s vinyl record vibe or on-trend packaging with a nod to the handmade. Fields Variable can precisely fine-tune the tone of voice and meet your typographic goals and needs. [ ladd-design.com ] Fields Big Ultra added in February 2025.

typefaces.name: Fig Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Graduated from Future Fonts in 2024.

typefaces.name: Finador
typefaces.desc: Finador is a modern and soft sans family. The functional style of a geometric sans has been soften by open apertures and rounded corners. [ fontcuisine.com ]

typefaces.name: Finador Slab
typefaces.desc: A soft slab serif family based on Finador Sans .

typefaces.name: Finder
typefaces.desc: Finder is a versatile sans-serif typeface meticulously crafted for multi-script applications in user interfaces. Designed with an emphasis on clarity at smaller sizes, its open design, large counters, and ample spacing significantly enhance legibility. The typeface's neutrality ensures a seamless user experience, keeping readers focused and undistracted. [ black-foundry.com ] The Arabic script was redesigned in 2024.

typefaces.name: Finnish Pie
typefaces.desc: Finnish Pie is a custom type family designed for, well, said pie. What started as a pie escalated into a whole branding project together with Äari and Werklig. It’s 100% vegan and 100% Helsinki. Which is why the typeface draws inspiration from the architecture as well as street signage of Finland’s capital. The font is slightly odd, quite elegant, a bit classical, a bit peculiar and loves to be set big. It comes in four weights from Light to Bold, nice and compact. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Firula
typefaces.desc: Firula is flourish, ornament, embellishment. It’s swirl, curve, adornment. Firula is our latest font, a typeface that embraces joy. A variable connected script in 7 styles. With simple or cursive capitals, details, and surprises that make each word feel as if it were crafted by the brush. [ plau.design ]

typefaces.name: Fit
typefaces.desc: Fit is a hyper-stylized series of caps designed with one thing in mind: filling up space with maximum impact. To accomplish this task, I drew Fit as a variable font with an expansive range of widths, represented by the ten styles shown here. Beginning with the impossibly narrow Skyline style, each character grows by 3600% (on average) to reach the gargantuan Ultra Extended. In between these ridiculous extremes, you will find a family rich in panache and expressive potential. Fit is anchored by its white shapes: regardless of width, the space within the letters and the space between the letters always remains the same. These white shapes cut dramatically through the letterforms, fusing them into a mesmerizing network of black and white. [ djr.com ]

typefaces.name: Fit Devanagari
typefaces.desc: Fit is a hyper-stylized design with one thing in mind: filling up space with maximum impact. Fit Devanagari is Kimya’s companion to David Jonathan Ross‘ groundbreaking variable font. Ranging from a ridiculously Ultra Compressed to a shockingly legible Regular to insanely Ultra Expanded, Fit can fit into any space!

typefaces.name: Fit U&lc
typefaces.desc: An iteration of the all-caps Fit that adds lowercase characters. Offered in December 2024 to members of the foundry’s Font of the Month Club.

typefaces.name: Fitzroy Display
typefaces.desc: Fitzroy Display was designed for The Fitzroy residence designed by Roman and Williams in New York. The name is taken from the Fitzroy Road that ran through West Chelsea in the late 20th century. Inspired by the iconic art deco style in the zeitgeist of New York architecture, Fitzroy Display offers a modern take on deco by combining gentle curves and edges inspired by art nouveau. [ cantrelltype.com ] Originally released with Typeverything .

typefaces.name: Five
typefaces.desc: The Five system is one of a series of stencil type families first published by MuirMcNeil in 2017. It was extensively revised and republished in 2021 in three different contours, each in two widths, two optical weights and in positive and negative versions. Constructed from basic geometric segments, Five is intended to explore relationships between figure and ground. Instead of assembling glyphs from a minimal set of strokes in the conventional manner, Five has been built around a system of internal spaces that are reduced to thin white lines, resulting in dense and imposing alphabets. The stencil contours and void spaces of the Five typefaces reference designs such Kombinations-Schrift, drawn by Josef Albers’ in 1921, along with compressed rectilinear sans serifs from the 1960s such as Letraset’s Compacta and Walter Haettenschweiler’s Schmalfette Grotesk from 1954. In MuirMcNeil Five the lower case, from baseline to x-height, divides into either two or three horizontal sections. Following principles similar to those used by Walter Ballmer in 1971 for his Olivetti logo and lettering designs, this allows stroke proportions to be modulated more fluently and more naturally than is com

typefaces.name: Fizz
typefaces.desc: Fizz is a friendly but sharp display face with a defining horizontal stroke emphasis. The original concept for Fizz was born during the MATD programme as an experiment with contrast. This redesigned version of the typeface features even smoother curves, sharper edges, and more details. Like a fizzy drink on a hot day, it will breathe life into any flat design. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Flatspot
typefaces.desc: A radical design feature for hinting on small screens, and a love letter to all the Grotesk spinoffs of the 60s — especially influenced by the work of Simoncini for Karlgeorg Hoefers «Permanent», which was then spread all over Italy in advertising and magazines. The typeface has an unusual amount of contrast but carries a default look in small sizes and reveals interesting details when used big. [ deinwaller.com ] Appears to be retired as of July 2025, as it was not included in the foundry’s website redesign.

typefaces.name: Flatspot Nuovo
typefaces.desc: Flatspot Nuovo is a revised version of a high-contrast neogrotesque font that is conceptually located between fashionable references from the 1950s and the visual principle of pixel display on the screen. The font is intended for digital use, but the flattened curves disappear completely in print below 12pt, making it suitable for editorial use as well. The current version of the family comprises six weights with matching italics, which are sufficient for versatile design. [ shop.deinwaller.com ] Appears to be retired as of July 2025, as it was not included in the foundry’s website redesign.

typefaces.name: Flip
typefaces.desc: MuirMcNeil Flip is a collection of seven experimental sans serif typefaces that explore aspects of symmetry in the roman alphabet. The character set of each individual variant font is governed throughout by a single axis of symmetry: either vertical, horizontal, rotational, biaxial or multiaxial. The Flip collection is a development of MuirMcNeil Sans Sans, an extensive typeface programme that seeks to investigate the fundamental attributes of alphabetic form in order to to map the contours of its design space. In Flip each glyph has been stripped down to its simplest symmetrical shape while maintaining legibility as far as is possible in mirrored forms that inevitably bear enormous degrees of redundancy. The Flip typefaces have all been designed in a single common weight and in selected subcomponent font pairs where only half of each glyph is shown. These can be recombined to make composite forms. [ muirmcneil.com ]

typefaces.name: Fliper
typefaces.desc: Fliper is a friendly sans-serif typeface that simultaneously has a geometric core and humanistic details. A feature that sets it apart is the several different stylistic sets that allow the introduction of rotated letters to highlight any headline. [ capitalics.wtf ]

typefaces.name: Folha
typefaces.desc: The serif and sans serif companions Folha Texto and Folha Gráfico are two new co-ordinated type families, commissioned by the Brazilian press group Fohla de São Paulo for the redesign of their newspapers, magazines, and other media, including web solutions and apps. Fohla de São Paulo originally licensed Bulo and Trola Text, both commercial typefaces from the Tipografies catalog, but needed exclusivity. This led us to rethink the designs and create two custom families for the press group. Because their exclusivity is limited to Brazil, Folha Texto and Folha Gráfico are available for commercial licensing in the rest of the world. Our primary aim in the development of Fohla Texto and Fohla Gráfico was to make them inviting above all. To achieve this, we accentuated the humanist traits of the letterforms, and infused the designs with a friendly and warm look. [ tipografies.com ]

typefaces.name: Fontoira
typefaces.desc: Fontoira is a typeface inspired by the traditional style of painting boats in the ports of O Grove and Meloxo, created by Mr. Raúl Fontoira, a retired sailor and self-taught artist. It is a project created hand in hand with my partner Lino Prieto. [ rubenprol.gal ]

typefaces.name: Fork
typefaces.desc: Fork is a monospaced typeface designed as an exploration of geometry and simplicity. The overall sharpness of shapes brings a mechanical tone to the characters as well as a singular typographic color. [ ma-ma-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Forma DJR Mono
typefaces.desc: Spearheaded by Ruggero Magrì, the typeface reconsiders DJR’s revival of Forma for use on a monospace grid. At the same time, it preserves the subtly rounded corners and tapered stems that evoke the physicality of ink on paper that Roger Black sought to preserve when he commissioned the revival. Following its proportionally-spaced cousin, Forma DJR Mono embodies the cleanliness and precision of midcentury design but tempers it with subtle imperfections that come from its origins in metal type. Monospaced typography was shaped by typewriters and early digital displays, but Forma DJR Mono is not a distressed typewriter font nor is it a purely digital creation. It exists somewhere in-between. [ djr.com ]

typefaces.name: Formiga
typefaces.desc: Formiga is a humanist and expressive display typeface, perfect for impactful headlines in modern and contemporary design contexts. It is also ideal for packaging with a fresh, bold, and powerful style. [ tipotype.com ]

typefaces.name: Forta
typefaces.desc: Forta is a new humanist sans-serif typeface designed to excel as a versatile workhorse for a wide range of applications. [ typeverything.com ]

typefaces.name: Fragment Mono
typefaces.desc: Fragment Mono is a monospaced coding version of Helvetica created by modifying and extending Nimbus Sans by URW Design Studio. [ github.com ]

typefaces.name: Fraise
typefaces.desc: Fraise is a fresh and fruity humanist sans typeface with a tall x-height and distinctive round shapes, inspired by the work of Roger Excoffon. [ daltonmaag.com ] The main reference is Antique Olive . Produced as a variable font with a weight axis, in upright and italics.

typefaces.name: Frama
typefaces.desc: https://www.printmag.com/type-tuesday/frama-geometry-after-the-space-age/

typefaces.name: Franziska
typefaces.desc: Originally released in 2014 with FontFont.

typefaces.name: Frasa Display
typefaces.desc: Frasa Display is a additional families based on core Frasa Family, a contemporary serif family with characteristics that arise from the charms of Caslon and a touch of transitional style; the display version design offers distinctive proportions to serve big type headline with more contrast on it. Frasa Display shows that the family is shaped by the traditions of its ancestors through small details that show the personality of the typeface, such as pointed ball terminals and strong shoulders. The italic weights have their own beauty, which is created to humanize the form based on a stylized and natural cursive style with the aim of emphasizing the text's essential elements. The addition of small caps, old-style figures, ligatures, etc. to this type family satisfies conventional typographic requirements. Frasa Display typefaces can eventually lead to the use of powerful design tools to create editorial and casual design styles. [ tokotype.com ]

typefaces.name: Fraunces
typefaces.desc: Fraunces is a display, soft-serif typeface inspired by the mannerisms of the early 20th century such as Windsor, Souvenir, and the Cooper Series. Designed with Phaedra Charles and released by Google Fonts, Fraunces has 4 axes that generate 100+ static styles. Besides the more common Weight and Optical Size controllers, there are 2 custom axes, Softness and Wonk that rule respectively the “wetness” or “inkiness”, and the substitution of “wonky” characters, such as the lean of the h, n, and m in the Roman, and the flagged ball terminals of the b, d, h, k, l, v, and w glyphs of the Italic. [ flaviazim.com ]

typefaces.name: Freizeit
typefaces.desc: Freizeit is a neo grotesque drawing inspiration from the mid-century triumvirate of Univers, Neue Haas Grotesk and Folio – as well as some of the sans that preceeded them. Strictly horizontal or vertical terminals, modern proportions and closed aperatures place it firmly within the genre, while a moderate amount of contrast with a slight angle of stress in places, aggressive stroke narrowing at joins, and some playful forms all emphasize a move away from the neutrality of the Swiss realist style. Freizeit is available in three widths, which can bought as separate subfamilies or together in the Freizeit Superfamily package. [ polytype.co.uk ]

typefaces.name: Friend
typefaces.desc: A condensed serif typeface with softened outlines, co-released by Typeverything and the designer’s own foundry, Beasts of England. The latter lists the regular and italic styles on separate pages.

typefaces.name: FSD Emoji
typefaces.desc: Monochrome emoji symbols designed for usage at small sizes. An ongoing project.

typefaces.name: Futura 100
typefaces.desc: https://www.type-together.com/new-release-futura100

typefaces.name: G2 Airdancer
typefaces.desc: G2 Airdancer was originally conceived for a 7-meter-tall Airdancer installation in the Lichthof of Karlsruhe University of Arts and Design welcoming the students coming back from their summer break. As a formalist approach to bold, compressed, display SansSerifs, G2 Airdancer rather explores technological properties of type design than a revivalist narrative. G2 Airdancer features three distinct families — round, semi-round, and edgy — each offering unique characteristics, yet designed to be interchangeable. This flexibility is further enhanced by its availability as a 2-axis variable font, allowing seamless transitions between families and styles. [ gruppo-due.com ]

typefaces.name: G2 Erika
typefaces.desc: G2 Erika emerged from an early sketch for a semi condensed monospace typeface. It started out referencing historic typewriter lettering, but quickly moved on to something new. Early versions of G2 Erika were used for a number of personal projects (e.g. the gruppo-due.com system font). Through this extended use and testing phase we gradually polished, adapted and expanded G2 Erika to arrive at a sturdy typeface ready for heavy work. Following our interest in expanding the single cut to a font family, we added a proportional version to the original monospace. By working on both styles at once, they started to influence each other’s characteristics. The pair now combines the technical and logical appearance its origins as a typewriter monospace with the details and rhythm of a proportional sans serif. Inspired by an early use of G2 Erika for a publication featuring the logical language LINCOS invented by the mathematician Hans Freudenthal we added a wider range of mathematical symbols and a set of astronomical signs related to interstellar communication. [ gruppo-due.com ]

typefaces.name: Ga Maamli
typefaces.desc: Inspired by the historic handwritten posters found in the vibrant coastal communities of Accra, Ga Maamli is a font that embodies the spirited essence of the Ga people. Originally used to announce social events like concerts, boxing matches, and parties, these original posters exuded a distinct flair and vivacity. Ga Maamli has been adapted and reworked into an extended character set that preserves the dynamism and allure of its traditional counterpart. This font’s variations and nuances exude a charm that pays homage to its vernacular origins while embracing modern typographic standards. Ga Maamli is more than just a font – it captures and celebrates the lively culture of the people of Accra. [ aayalolo.com ]

typefaces.name: Gabriela
typefaces.desc: Originally released in 2019 with Latinotype [ behance.net ], reissued in May 2024 [ behance.net ].

typefaces.name: Gabriela Stencil
typefaces.desc: Released in September 2024 [ behance.net ].

typefaces.name: Gabriela Stencil Cnd
typefaces.desc: Released in May 2024 [ behance.net ]

typefaces.name: Gal Gothic
typefaces.desc: A sans serif whose main inspiration is Morris Fuller Benton’s Franklin Gothic. The links in this entry point to the regular width.

typefaces.name: Galice
typefaces.desc: Galice is a humanistic sans serif typeface that effortlessly balances modern design with the organic forms typical of traditional serif fonts. Inspired by humanist letterforms, Galice features subtle curves and a variety of stroke widths, giving it a warm, approachable feel without sacrificing legibility or clarity. Its design blends the crispness of sans serifs with the slight variation in thickness that echoes the natural rhythm of handwriting, creating a friendly yet professional appearance. Unlike purely geometric sans serifs, which can sometimes appear mechanical, Galice's softer edges and more dynamic structure add a sense of flow and personality to its letterforms. Its subtle curves allow for a more inviting and legible design, making it highly adaptable across a range of applications—from body text to display use. Whether in print or on screen, Galice remains highly readable at various sizes, offering a natural reading experience that maintains its grace and coherence in all types of media. The font is characterized by its refined yet uncomplicated design. The overall feel is contemporary but with a touch of warmth, making it suitable for diverse contexts, including editori

typefaces.name: Gamay
typefaces.desc: [ Release announcement ].

typefaces.name: Gamuth
typefaces.desc: Gamuth is conceived as a multi-faceted work, of which the first panels are two optical sizes (Display, Text) of the same serif typeface. Gamuth borrows from Dutch Baroque faces and their typical breadth: narrower than usual proportions, generous x-heights, and crisp detailing are key features of the typefaces, and contribute to giving a dense, deep texture to running text. Gamuth was initially designed to perform well for on-screen, long-form consultation. Its hybrid origins made it a work of pure syncretism: the Display cuts have a life of their own, and while they work hand in hand with the Text cuts, the rhythm of lowercase proportions dances a different ballet. Meanwhile, they sport an even crisper and sharper texture. Departing from the historical roots of the romans, the italics are normalized towards a more predictable behavior on modern displays and therefore have a constant angle. Gamuth is designed to perform graciously in demanding environments such as content-heavy websites while proving distinctive enough for branding applications where a touch of depth and substance are sought. Gamuth’s next panel is already set to unfold as Gamuth Sans. [ productiontype.com ]

typefaces.name: Gangster
typefaces.desc: Originally released as a single-weight roman/italic pair, expanded in 2025 to several weights.

typefaces.name: Garage Gothic
typefaces.desc: Garage Gothic explores the coarse, unvarnished shapes of ephemeral printing. In the 1980s, Tobias Frere-Jones collected discarded tickets from parking garages in Brooklyn, intending to use them in collages. The numbers on the tickets had a simple matter-of-fact geometry, which contrasted with the smearing and blurring of rapid printing. He was taken with this uneasy combination of voices, and would later use them as a basis for Garage Gothic, adding two extra weights and hundreds of new characters. “I wanted to make this crude vernacular as valid and useful as classic types of past centuries, and also record a genre that is routinely omitted from type history, despite its being part of our landscape for decades.” The truncated centers of M and W recall the monospaced forms often found in mechanical printing, while the rounded corners and joins make blurriness into a central theme. [ frerejones.com ] Originally released by Font Bureau in 1992 and moved to Frere–Jones Type in 2020 [ fontsinuse.com ], available through Type Network. An updated version was published on the foundry’s website in December 2024.

typefaces.name: Garet
typefaces.desc: Garet is a modern geometric sans serif. It is characterised by high x-height, clean and soft letterforms with a smooth masculine tone. Garet derives its distinctive oval shapes from the optically perfect circle and has closed counters to further emphasise that form. [ typeforward.com ] Support for Greek script added January 2025.

typefaces.name: Garibaldi
typefaces.desc: Garibaldi is a text typeface based on humanist calligraphy. It has an organic look and feel, while preserving the traditional construction of roman typography. It all started with a desire to learn more about the origin of the strokes on humanist typefaces. To accomplish that, Garibaldi features a 20° axis, medium contrast based on translation and expansion, asymmetric serifs, and terminals related to the broad nib stroke. Garibaldi Regular was selected for Tipos Latinos 2014. Since then, the family was expanded with more weights and matching italics, making it a solid choice for setting books, magazines and all kinds of long texts. Among many OpenType features, each font contains small caps, ligatures and contextual alternates, totalling more than 750 glyphs and supporting at least 200 languages. Typographica Favorite Typefaces of 2015 .

typefaces.name: Garino
typefaces.desc: Garino is a modern sans-serif typeface family. It gains its expressive character from a dynamic sweep in the curves and high-contrast transitions. [ fontcuisine.com ]

typefaces.name: Gatwick
typefaces.desc: Updated in 2024 .

typefaces.name: Gauche
typefaces.desc: Like a gawky teenager at family dinner, Gauche breaks all the rules—not because it wants to, but because it can’t help it. Its arcs are too shallow, its caps are too wide and its italic slants at a dangerous 28 degrees, while shifting its baseline to accommodate some pretty steep ascenders. We first encountered this bizarre typeface many years ago in a Nikkor Annual photobook and were immediately taken with it. Reviving it has been a long-time wish, but it was difficult to find a way of translating the complete strangeness of this grotesk into a digital font. This year, we finally found the right approach and the time to bring it back to life. Gauche consists of a roman and an (un)matching baseline-shifted italic, as well as a set of “fancy” numerals and punctuation that were part of the font in the original source—fitting Gauche’s vibe of coming to the party overdressed in someone else’s heels. [ celine-hurka.com ] The Roman style was expanded in Oct 2024 to five weights.

typefaces.name: Gayot New
typefaces.desc: Gayot New is a contemporary interpretation of Jean-Pierre Gayot’s eponymous typeface of the 1970’s. The original Gayot was released as dry-transfer lettering in 1973 by Mecanorma as a winner of their International Type-Style Contest. In addition to revised proportions, this new interpretation sees the addition of uppercase characters, extended Latin character support, and new symbols and punctuation. While it deviates from its inspiration, it remains the same in tone; sorta futuristic, sorta retro, a little bit ugly, and a whole lot of fun. [ bigfog.co ]

typefaces.name: GB.
typefaces.desc: GB is a bold sans serif typeface inspired by two single capital letters – G & B – found printed on a single page of the Morgan Press Type catalogue. Having only two random letters to start with, the challenge of creating a harmonious and coherent design was immense and open-ended. Other inspirational touchstones include letterpress printed wood alphabets and early sans serif fonts found in historical type specimens. The font is a striking balance of tradition and modernity. Awards: Tokyo Type Directors Club TDC Prize & ISTD Certificate of Typographic Excellence. [ a2-type.co.uk ]

typefaces.name: Gear
typefaces.desc: Designed by Jeremy Mickel with assistance by Graham Bradley, Sabina Kipară, and Douglas Hayes. Published as a beta release in 2023 under the name Dash, and renamed to Gear in 2024. Released for retail in 2025.

typefaces.name: Gela
typefaces.desc: Gela is an exploration of mixed contrast approaches, seeking harmony in variety and embracing the discord of a playfully fluid angle of stress. Inspired in-part by the funk and flare of 70s typography, Gela brings together naive blobby forms and confident incised details, with a laid-back attitude. Designed for display, with diminutive ascenders and descenders, an enormous x-height, and oversized tittles and diacritics. It is available in three optical sizes, with a variable version included when purchasing the family package. [ polytype.co.uk ]

typefaces.name: Gelati
typefaces.desc: Gelati is a semi-serif typeface that blends soft corners with angular strokes. Subtle variation on the otherwise conventional, bold letterforms make Gelati a standout contemporary display font. [ doubledagger.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Genepi
typefaces.desc: Genepi is a typeface born from the Tavern, the creative and experimental wavy tool crafted by Gaëtan Baehr. It has been inspired directly by the iconic lettering of Central Park’s “Tavern on the Green.” Designed exclusively in capitals, Genepi optimizes the tool's ability to create flowing wave effects, resulting in dynamic and unexpected visual patterns. This linear font, with minimal contrast and delicate flares, evokes the refined aesthetics of the Art Nouveau movement while embracing modern versatility. Genepi features a width variation axis and four unique axes controlling the top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right corners of each letter. These innovations allow for unparalleled customization and creative expression, enabling designers to craft surprising and unique visual effects. [ black-foundry.com ] The design seems to be referencing Kevin Cantrell ’s lettering work for the restaurant.

typefaces.name: Genevoix
typefaces.desc: Based on simple geometric shapes, Genevoix is a new typeface family that pays tribute to Bauhaus aesthetics. Its unique reinterpretation of familiar forms gives it a mechanical yet warm appearance, making it suitable for a wide range of applications. Each style includes alternate letterforms to enhance visual rhythm in compositions. [ thedesignersfoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Gertie
typefaces.desc: Gertie (2024) was inspired by the lettering of comic artist and animation pioneer Winsor McCay—specifically the title lettering in his “Little Nemo” comic strip, which ran in Sunday newspapers from 1905–1927. The name comes from his 1914 animated short, “Gertie the Dinosaur,” which is considered the first to portray a character with personality. Gertie (the font) is an ultra-bold all-caps spur-serif design for display use with an early 20th-century feel and includes a set of matching dingbats, a set of raised caps for ordinals (4th, 5th, etc.), and other situations (the o in Co., the c in McCAY, etc.).

typefaces.name: Gesamt
typefaces.desc: Accessible by enrollment into Production Type’s Beta program.

typefaces.name: Getty
typefaces.desc: Introducing Getty, a fun and friendly typeface inspired by the iconic Cooper Black. Getty is available in two families: normal and italic, each with 9 styles plus variable files, making it versatile for various design needs. Its playful, rounded forms and warm personality make it perfect for logotypes and packaging. While echoing the charm of 70s serif typefaces, Getty stands out with its unique and unconventional letterforms, bringing a modern twist to a classic style. [ typeverything.com ]

typefaces.name: Ghost
typefaces.desc: Not to be confused with TWK Ghost (Weltkern).

typefaces.name: Giboula
typefaces.desc: Debuted in 2018 on Future Fonts, graduated in 2021.

typefaces.name: Gigio
typefaces.desc: Gigio was born in Argentina—as Ana Laydner's graduation project at CDT-UBA in Buenos Aires—and raised in Brazil. A friendly yet strong slab serif, inspired by comic books, that welcomes all kinds of narratives. Combining a mechanical structure with calligraphic strokes and rather condensed proportions, the 5-weight family (from Book to Extrabold) works nicely in text, while uncovering quirky details in larger settings. Version 0.1 has uprights only, but italic companions are coming next. [ flaviazim.com ]

typefaces.name: Gimlet X-Ray
typefaces.desc: An experimental version of Gimlet that exposes the internal mechanics of a variable font, including glyph contours, control points, spacing, and kerning .

typefaces.name: Gimme
typefaces.desc: Gimme is the kid in class with everything, from the latest toy as seen on TV to a tricked out BMX bike. It's the only person you knew with the complete Playmobil Mansion or USS Flagg, and now, this can be you! Gimme is a dazzling ever-growing type family of multi-chromatic and variable display typefaces which will leave you saying: gimme more! And you are in luck, because updates will deliver on that! Inspired by a box full of toys, more type families will be added as we go along, expanding them further and adding new features. And the more allowance, the more it will grow! [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Ginka
typefaces.desc: Ginka is a playful and asserting grotesk typeface. Thanks to the duality of the design of this family it’s possible to have a really good texture in text, but also quirky and specific aesthetics in large sizes for posters! Ginka has pronounced punctuation and funny rebounded curves while it has deep sharp ink traps which create high contrast with a specific pinched. Try to play with Ginka! [ lift-type.fr ]

typefaces.name: Ginny Sans
typefaces.desc: Ginny, an unassuming power player with a delicate touch, is a thin workhorse sans inspired by the clear and open sans types prevalent in 1970’s food packaging, with a little extra zing thrown in for good measure. Set in sentence case or in all caps, Ginny knows when to take center stage, or hang back as a supporting player. [ badsontype.com ]

typefaces.name: Gintona Slab
typefaces.desc: Gintona is an extremely versatile slab serif font with 8 weights, ranging from delicately refined styles to bold and robust options. Additionally, Gintona is available as a variable font, allowing for weight variations within a single file. Its design combines traditional elements, such as thick serifs and pronounced ink traps, used primarily as a stylistic resource. The diagonal terminals and organic shapes give it a warm and dynamic appearance. Gintona is a robust, fresh, and modern typeface that will add a distinctive touch to your projects. It is the perfect choice for editorial work, logos, packaging, or advertising material seeking to make a significant visual impact. [ sudtipos.com ]

typefaces.name: Giornale
typefaces.desc: Giornale is inspired by the alternative interpretations and aberrations of classic Roman serif fonts used in Italy in the 1970s, mainly on newspapers, magazines, and political posters. For this project we reversed the typical process and instead of drawing from historical references, we used a series of vernacular interpretations as the source to redraw a single cut display font. The word "giornale" simply means newspaper in Italian. This typeface has a retro look, condensed proportions and is well-suited for headlines and quotes. A small but unique family is in the works. [ abc-etc.com ]

typefaces.name: Gladiola
typefaces.desc: Gladiola is a smooth and balanced brush script font. It is suitable for logos, titles, t-shirts, packages and where ever you will need this kind of lining and legible script font. Gladiola includes lots of Stylistic Alternates that gives you many options to customize your text. There are two sets of upper case letters. Lower cases has options for initial forms, final forms, end swashes and multiple options for ascenders and descenders.

typefaces.name: Glammo
typefaces.desc: As part of the annual Dublin Bowie Festival, Signal was invited to create a typographic poster based on David Bowie’s eighteenth studio album, BLACK TIE WHITE NOISE. BTWN is a dark and intensely 90s piece of work, inspired by the 1992 Los Angeles riots (which a newly-wed Bowie watched from his hotel window), and we decided the poster deserved a dark, intensely 90s typeface. Glammo blends references to techno, AKIRA, and the Designers Republic to convey a air of sleek modernity gone badly wrong. We set the full lyrics of the title track in red and ran them sideways along the bottom edge of the poster, suggesting both an audio equalizer display and leaping flames. [ signalfoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Glance Sans
typefaces.desc: Geometric, stylish, and not quite a stencil face: Glance Sans is the urban alter ego of Glance Slab—a strong-willed sans-serif with visible gaps between strokes that create a dynamic impression of balance and movement. [ identity-letters.com ] The typeface design was updated in September 2024.

typefaces.name: Glance Slab
typefaces.desc: Glance Slab is an experimental design at the intersection of connection and detachment. Gaps between strokes create a stencil-like effect in large sizes. In small sizes, they work like ink traps. [ identity-letters.com ] The typeface design was updated in September 2024.

typefaces.name: Glotik
typefaces.desc: Glotik is an all-purpose and all-together weird multi-weight humanist sans. As well as a range of historical stylistic alternates made for logos and headlines, Glotik includes upright italics, small caps and all the features of a text type. The uppercase italic matches the roman (just how the early humanist scribes did it) and its generous but irregular curves and rigid stems make Glotik personable and readable at text size as well as memorable and interesting at scale. [ eastofrome.com ]

typefaces.name: Glucosa
typefaces.desc: If Glucosa were a dish, it would fit perfectly into fusion cuisine. Its design recipe combines ingredients from diverse origins, which complement each other to create a bouquet of new flavours and venture into little-explored typographic terrain. Clean on a macro level, Glucosa avoids the risk of appearing static and repetitive thanks to its organic nature: while the underlying structure is composed of firm, decisive strokes, the finish has a sweet, penetrating softness: corners are slightly rounded, dots are squared, and some glyphs even seem to have been dipped in honey. Others resemble objects that were subject to erosion, smoothed by the wind. Glucosa Display offers a variation on the theme. The modulation is taken much further, increasing the overall contrast and bringing vibrancy to the text appearance: where Glucosa is moderately soft all around, Glucosa Display engages in an interplay of fully rounded and razor-sharp. [ tipografies.com ] Glucosa Display was announced in January 2025.

typefaces.name: Glyptotek
typefaces.desc: Glyptotek is a contemporary restoration and revival typeface inspired by lettering found on the Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek in central Copenhagen — a significant museum building designed by architect Vilhelm Dahlerup in the early 1880s. The original alphabet is a peculiar ‘mixed’ design, with serif uppercase and sans serif lowercase letters. The new Glyptotek font is now available in three categories: Sans (A), a matching Serif (B), and a mixed case option (C+D), just like the original source. The Glyptotek font family is free to use for all designers working directly with the museum on exhibition signage, publications, or public-facing campaigns.

typefaces.name: Gonia
typefaces.desc: Gonia is a slab-serif typeface family designed to function at all sizes. With a large range of weights, this family remains functional and legible in small sizes while its use in larger point sizes reveals the finer details of the letter forms. The very heavy Black weight can attract attention, the lighter weights provide a more balance reading experience and the inclusion of a real italic form allows a visual distinction between the roman or italic form. [ typogama.com ]

typefaces.name: Google Sans Code
typefaces.desc: The typeface is dedicated to the memory of Chris Simpkins (1974–2025), who initiated and oversaw the project as a program manager at Google Fonts.

typefaces.name: Gothalian
typefaces.desc: Introducing the "Gothalian" font, a blackletter design influenced by the timeless elegance of Victorian ornamentation. This font takes roots in Henry Brehmer's 1890s metal type published by George Bruce's Son & Co. We have revived the vintage source material with the ornate ironwork of the late 19th century, extrapolating the essence of the past and creating a font that showcases a sophisticated and attractive look. The font boasts elaborate details inspired by the Victorian era, combined with a touch of darkness that adds a unique and captivating aura to your designs. Its unique style makes it stand out and will give your designs a memorable look. The font is available in a flexible variable format, allowing you to adjust the weight, and it also comes as a 9 static style font, including italics and numerous alternates that provide endless design possibilities. The font includes a full set of characters covering a wide range of Latin-based languages. The name "Gothalian" is a mix of two terms: "Gothic," which refers to the style of blackletter typefaces that were prevalent in medieval Europe, and "Italian," which is used to describe reversed contrast typefaces in the 19th century.

typefaces.name: Gothia Serif
typefaces.desc: Gothia is a duo of serif and sans serif typefaces originally designed for the Swedish newspaper Göteborgs-Posten as part of their rebrand by design agency Brandwork. Given its roots as a newspaper type system, Gothia is specifically geared towards editorial and publication design and complex design systems. It covers the entire spectrum from body copy for immersive reading to distinguished, arresting headlines. Gothia’s appearance references Gothenburg’s historical connection with the Netherlands—the city was built by the Dutch in the 17th century. This was the era when a number of classic Dutch types saw the light of day, typefaces that are still role models for many contemporary designs. Gothia builds on this rich tradition, infusing the Dutch style with a modern Scandinavian flair. Studying both historical Dutch typefaces by Hendrik van den Keere and Christoffel van Dijck and contemporary classics by Gerard Unger inspired letterforms that combine a supple, refined elegance with a crisp finish and sharp details. Instead of just being the sans serif counterpart for Gothia Serif, Gothia Sans was given a smoother appearance for additional contrast. Developing Gothia was similar to w

typefaces.name: Gothia Serif Text
typefaces.desc: Gothia Serif Text is a small text-optimized adaptation of Gothia Serif, created for a book project commissioned by Swedish designer and art director Nina Ulmaja. Aiming to harmonize display and text usage, Ulmaja envisioned a typeface versatile enough for both. Gothia Serif Text achieves this with a wider design, reduced contrast, and an elevated x-height, ensuring enhanced legibility and readability in smaller text sizes. [ lettersfromsweden.se ]

typefaces.name: Gotta Scotch
typefaces.desc: It emerged from Marcela’s final project for the Master in Typographic Design at the Eina School of Barcelona, which deals with the first typefaces used in Chile. It is an interpretation inspired by the Scotch Romans formula to which contemporary and transitional influences are incorporated, resulting in a work of great visual interest and, at the same time, offering great comfort in its reading. Ideal combination for use in editorial design. Among its practical attractions, the formal contrast of the calligraphic accent of its Italics stands out. It also has a set of Small Caps, old-style arrangements, aligned, tabular and fractional, among other multiple stylistic options. [ type-o-tones.com ]

typefaces.name: Gradine
typefaces.desc: https://www.dstype.com/newsletter/gradine-next/0a50cfe482e94377c8b01cbcab07e604

typefaces.name: Gramercy
typefaces.desc: A streamlined serif typeface with a set of contrasting swash capitals. Produced in three optical sizes, with eight weights in upright and italic, and as a variable font with weight and contrast axes.

typefaces.name: Grand Central
typefaces.desc: In 1846, the French designer Louis Perrin created a typeface from his own personal reinterpretation of ancient Roman lettering. Soon after, sign painters and typefounders copied this new “French Oldstyle” with their own alterations. In the following decades, signpainters and typefounders would copy and alter this new style, often calling it “French Oldstyle”. When Grand Central Terminal opened in 1913, signpainters used an American take on this style in making notices and directions throughout the building. In 1994, a full renovation of Grand Central Terminal began. To keep new locator maps and signage in harmony with the old lettering, Tobias Frere-Jones was hired to design a typeface in Grand Central’s distinct Beaux-Arts style. He studied decades of archive photography to compile the original lettering for the Light. After consulting trade manuals from the period, he drew the bold to comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act, which established precise rules for signage type. [ frerejones.com ] Originally released by Font Bureau in 1998 and moved to Frere–Jones Type in 2020 [ fontsinuse.com ], available through Type Network and added to the foundry’s website in December 202

typefaces.name: Granda
typefaces.desc: Granda is a sans-serif typeface rooted in the Grotesk genre. Its lively proportions bring warmth to the text. The italic's contrasted structure adds emphasis and reveals personality in paragraphs and headlines. Granda Reclined is a playful alternative, counterbalancing the italic. Additionally, it opens up possibilities for building hierarchy and headline usage, like an extra display style within the system, packaged in a single variable font. Grotesk typefaces became a symbol of modernism in graphic design. They often aim to be clean and even sterile. However, early examples of the genre show lots of quirks and a range of unexpected treatments. That was the inspiration for creating Granda, a type family with multiple flavors. Unlike the uniformly shiny glass skyscraper, Granda is more like a block of flats, revealing the life of individual personalities with the vast variety of every balcony decoration. [ thedesignersfoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Grano
typefaces.desc: Grano is a modern geometric sans-serif designed to make a bold impact. Inspired by the classic Block typeface by Hermann Hoffmann (1908) and Schwere Block (Berthold, 1920), Grano takes these influences and reimagines them with a contemporary twist. [ typeverything.com ]

typefaces.name: Grantig
typefaces.desc: Grantig is a bold serif display typeface. Inspired by the opening titles of old western movies, the genre of western slab serifs has been translated into a modern context and adapted to today's needs. As a result, it breaks free from the chains of its genre and opens up to many themes. With its massive serifs and strictly rounded curves, it comes particularly close in character to the grumpy Western heroes of days gone by, always in the presence of his two leaning companions, Slant and Backslant. [ fontcuisine.com ]

typefaces.name: Graveur
typefaces.desc: Initially released with Huy!Fonts, folded into the MTM catalog in 2025.

typefaces.name: Graviola
typefaces.desc: With semi-rounded terminals, Graviola is soft and friendly. Produced in eight weights, in upright and italics.

typefaces.name: Graviola Soft
typefaces.desc: Graviola Soft is a juicy type family. It is based on my Graviola typeface, but I didn’t just round its corners. I redrew every stem and terminal so they would look just right. Combined with curved diagonal strokes and alternate glyphs, Graviola Soft makes for a super friendly typeface. Produced in eight weights, in upright and italics.

typefaces.name: Grecia
typefaces.desc: Traditionally, the design of serif typefaces has been rooted in early typographic models, influenced heavily by calligraphic ink pens that produce thin and thick strokes with oblique emphasis. These early designs were shaped by the tools used, creating a clear link between calligraphy and serif typefaces. However, with technological advancements, the objectives and applications of type design have significantly evolved. Serif typefaces, once confined primarily to reading contexts, are now more versatile, pushing the boundaries of typographic conventions and exploring creative, imaginative realms. PF Grecia exemplifies this evolution by blending blackletter sharpness with Roman attributes in a unique, idiosyncratic manner. It is a variable serif typeface that draws inspiration from Darley, a typeface originally designed for the National Geographic maps by cartographer Charles E. Riddiford in the 1930s. [ parachutefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Greed [Positype]
typefaces.desc: Greed is unapologetically opulent. Inspired by the intricate lettering of U.S. currency, this typeface amplifies every flourish, elevating the familiar into a bold expression of excess. Its exaggerated serifs, extravagant curves, and commanding presence embody decadence and ambition. Greed doesn’t whisper—it declares its dominance, making it the perfect choice for designs that demand attention and revel in unapologetic extravagance. [ positype.com ]

typefaces.name: Griffith Gothic
typefaces.desc: Griffith Gothic re-imagines a classic American design, paired with unorthodox details. Its story begins with Bell Gothic, C. H. Griffith’s 1937 custom design for telephone directories. To anticipate ink spread on press, Griffith thinned and flattened lowercase joins, blunted sharp corners, and enlarged counterforms. The result was an object lesson in defensive typeface design. Graphic designers would later become enamored of Bell Gothic’s unusual rhythm and drastic moves, and use it for eye-catching headlines well outside its original target size of six to eight point. Patrick Mitchell at Fast Company commissioned a full headline series based on Bell Gothic with extra weights and a condensed width, and a wholly new italic. More recently, Fred Shallcrass carefully revised and updated the family. [ frerejones.com ] Originally released by Font Bureau in 1997 and moved to Frere–Jones Type in 2020 [ fontsinuse.com ], available through Type Network. An updated version was published on the foundry’s website in December 2024.

typefaces.name: Grigio Serif
typefaces.desc: Grigio Serif is a sprightly and slender display serif bearing Art Nouveau influences and elegant calligraphic notions. Grigio’s narrow, tailored proportions and optimistic voice lend themselves perfectly to regal headlines with a confident air. Perfect for display uses, Grigio can deliver a playful yet refined attitude to brand packaging and ad campaigns — from wine & cheese to jams & jellies. [ badsontype.com ]

typefaces.name: Grollera
typefaces.desc: Grollera, an exciting, expansive sans serif font family, exists at the intersection of tradition and innovation. The typeface embraces contradictions. Modern, squarish inner shapes contrast with outer forms inspired by early grotesques to create a surprising and wholly new typographic language. Grollera’s outer forms can be traced back to the first nineteenth-century sans serifs, which were full of character. Their raw power and vitality disappeared in later designs like Helvetica—all of the personality was sandpapered out of the letterforms in a quest for polished perfection. [ tipografies.com ]

typefaces.name: Gronland
typefaces.desc: Gronland is a sans serif typeface, re-designed between 2022 and 2023. The goal was to create a font that isn’t tied to any specific inspiration, allowing it to stand on its own with a clean and functional design. Gronland excels in providing easy-to-read letterforms that are both practical and aesthetically pleasing, suitable for a wide range of applications. Its neutral yet modern appearance makes it an ideal choice for those seeking clarity and simplicity in their typography. [ gunesmuhittin.com ] Gronland is a sans serif typeface designed in 2018-2021. Gronland inspired by Swiss public transport signages, NYC way finding systems and Greenland. Designed for screen and medium sizes. [ dribbble.com ] Updated in 2024, then in 2025.

typefaces.name: GT Flaire
typefaces.desc: GT Flaire captures the pronounced curves created by calligraphic pens when applying ink to paper under pressure and translates this characteristic into a digital format. This typeface bridges the worlds of business and pleasure, breaking free from corporate rigidity by combining seriousness with playfulness and encouraging users to embrace both. [ grillitype.com ]

typefaces.name: GT Pantheon
typefaces.desc: GT Pantheon is an interpretation of historic shapes in a contemporary manner. It exhibits an expressive and dynamic character visible in every stroke. At its core is the conception of three optically-adjusted faces, each designed to best represent the same type at different sizes: Display, Text, and Micro. Within this spectrum, the family moves between elegance, sharpness, warmth and robustness, matching expression with functionality. [ grillitype.com ]

typefaces.name: Guyot Headline, Text & Press
typefaces.desc: Guyot is a type family inspired by the work of the punchcutter François Guyot, who lived and worked in Antwerp during the sixteenth century. Ramiro Espinoza got acquainted with the work of Guyot while attending the Expert Class in Type Design at Antwerp’s Plantin Institute for Typography. Researching French and Flemish punchcutters, Espinoza soon realized that the work of the most important masters of the period had already been digitized. However, he found the work of lesser-known punchcutters like Guyot, though perhaps not of the same superior quality as the others, equally compelling. And so a digital Guyot seemed in order. Espinoza decided early on that his Guyot was not going to be a facsimile typeface, but rather a modern interpretation aimed at the editorial market. He selected the most interesting elements from the Gros Canon and Ascendonica sizes and assembled them into a consistent family of contemporary detailing. During his year at the Plantin Institute for Typography, Espinoza researched several more punchcutters from the seventeenth century. Details common to the types of that period—like an increased contrast and an enlarged terminal in the a—were applied to Guyot to

typefaces.name: Guyot Sans
typefaces.desc: Guyot is a type family inspired by the work of the punchcutter François Guyot, who lived and worked in Antwerp during the sixteenth century. Ramiro Espinoza got acquainted with the work of Guyot while attending the Expert Class in Type Design at Antwerp’s Plantin Institute for Typography. Researching French and Flemish punchcutters, Espinoza soon realized that the work of the most important masters of the period had already been digitized. However, he found the work of lesser-known punchcutters like Guyot, though perhaps not of the same superior quality as the others, equally compelling. And so a digital Guyot seemed in order. The Guyot family was eventually divided into three subfamilies: Headline, Text and Press to take full advantage of the possibilities of these optical ranges. In the year 2023, Espinoza worked to expand the system with Guyot Sans, a refined, multipurpose sans family consisting of fourteen fonts. [ re-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Haas Recast
typefaces.desc: Haas Recast is our revival of a classic faux-Swiss grotesque sans typeface, originally designed in the 1950s by Max Miedinger and Eduard Hoffmann for the Haas Type Foundry. Our update brings Weight, Width, Italic, and Tracking axes to its versatile variable font. [ daltonmaag.com ]

typefaces.name: Habil
typefaces.desc: Inspired by the masterful works of António Jacinto de Araújo, introduced in his 1797 publication Nova Arte de Escrever , Habil reimagines the elegance of calligraphic forms for modern typography. We're developing Habil to capture the fluidity and sensitivity of Araújo's calligraphy, blending historical refinement with contemporary design to meet the needs of today's typographic applications. […] While Habil is not a direct replication of Araújo's original plates, it draws on his legacy, embodying the same spirit of innovation and artistry to bring calligraphic beauty into the modern era. [ dstype.com ]

typefaces.name: HAL Magic
typefaces.desc: HAL Magic is a true performer, an athlete and a keen entertainer, ready to run the show on the big stage. Loosely inspired by Joseph Churchward’s “Tranquility”, Magic has some additional tricks up its sleeve. The typeface comes in three subfamilies with variant x-heights: High, Mid and Low. Each subfamily brings its own distinct flavour and contains six weights plus corresponding obliques. All of these states are included in a spellbinding variable font, which allows for fluid transitions and enchanted shapeshifting. Rely on Magic to get the job done and make it look extremely easy.  Download Specimen [ type.hanli.eu ]

typefaces.name: Haltung
typefaces.desc: From the sans-serif lettering of Walter Käch to Frutiger’s Univers, to the students of the Basel school under Emil Ruder, Haltung is a neo-grotesk typeface inspired by a common attitude and design sensibility spanning these three generations. Conceptually, Haltung aims to bridge a gap between the teacher and student, taking their common approach to the sans-serif and re-imagines a robust, contemporary neo-grotesk that is refined yet retains the airy impression of its source material. Haltung’s namesake comes from a monograph of Schmid’s work—Gestaltung ist Haltung (Design is Attitude). [ order.design ]

typefaces.name: Hanae
typefaces.desc: Named after the trailblazing Japanese fashion designer, the first Asian woman to join a Haute-Couture house in Paris — Hanae Mori. Editorial in its heart, fashion in its soul, Hanae is a contemporary typeface that ties familiarity and beauty, elegance and fluidity. An evolution from the Old Style Antique, particularly Caslon, combined with the large x-height and wide proportions from Bookman, the classic aesthetic from Times New Roman, and some quirks from Baskerville. [ flaviazim.com ]

typefaces.name: Happy Times at the IKOB New Game Plus Edition
Hardanger
typefaces.desc: The Hardanger pixel typeface imitates the Norwegian embroidery of the same name. This blend of tradition and technology gives rise to a singular typeface, suitable for titling. From the precision of its pixels to the delicacy of its threads, Hardanger is both ornamental and refined. [ entravaux.framer.website ]

typefaces.name: Harmider
typefaces.desc: Harmider is a display, blocky typeface with shy serifs. The name comes from the polish word „Harmider” which means a type of noise – like when many things happen at once, for example. [ laic.pl ]

typefaces.name: Harry
typefaces.desc: Harry is based on a typeface with a strange name «Too Much» designed by William Bill Seifert in the 70’s for the VGC (Visual Graphics Corporation) foundry. This typeface appeared in the same years as the better-known Frankfurter, designed in its first versions by Bob Newman for Letraset. Too Much appeared at the time as an alternative to Frankfurter, but in a more contrasted version, less mono-linear in capitals only and with some letters showing a more unexpected drawing than its neighbour Frankfurter. Harry is therefore an interpretation that remains very close to the original design, but in which certain aspects and settings of weights, curves and proportions have been modified. [ eliottgrunewald.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Hauser
typefaces.desc: Hauser is a deep dive in the concept of constructed typography, following after the first exploration with Maxeville Construct. Formed by basic geometric shapes; circles, squares and lines are repurposed in multiple characters. Resulting in abstract individual characters that become legible when paired together. Built from repeating shapes on a fixed grid system, Hauser draws inspiration from the avant-garde architecture group Team 10; Structuralist- and later Metabolist architecture. Additionally Suprematism is a present theme when it comes to weights and compositions. [ s-m.nu ]

typefaces.name: Hauss
typefaces.desc: Introducing Hauss & Raum, a sans-serif work-horse and experimental display duet by Justin Sloane & Huw Williams. Hauss & Raum define distinctive polarities from the purely utilitarian to the bombastically deontological–a sturdy design tool and an exercise in psychedelic retrofuturism. While Hauss is Sloane’s meticulous creation, crafted over years of trial and refinement for his own graphic design practice, Raum represents a sort of destruction–pushing the contemporaneous “display inktrap” motif into uncharted territory. [ sharptype.co ]

typefaces.name: HD Koncert
typefaces.desc: Taking inspiration from lettering styles of 1960s music posters, characterized by its blocky shapes and wide proportions with geometric, sharp-edged letterforms create a sturdy, impactful aesthetic, while the wide proportion adds openness and enhances legibility, making it ideal for large-scale applications like headlines or posters. With balanced details such as open counters and consistent stroke widths. The design reflects the creative experimentation of mid-century typography, embracing attention-grabbing forms that evoke confidence and clarity. With the support of 4 scripts including Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, and Thai. [ holdontype.design ]

typefaces.name: HD Sinar
typefaces.desc: Sinar is previously known as Hailgen, a reversed contrast serif. Designed in 2019 and refined overtime. We decided to give it new name and purpose. The project aim is to study the reverse contrast nature and expand it to several scripts. With Indonesian and South East Asian on the Priority list, Javanese is on it’s development stage right now. Other than scripts, we also want to expand the style for a normal contrast to cater the text and editorial needs.

typefaces.name: Heaven can wait
typefaces.desc: Heaven can wait is a pseudo-pixel typeface, inspired by the titles of the film by Ernst Lubitsch. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Hebden Recut
typefaces.desc: Hebden is a ‘Northern’ font. Inspired by the town Hebden Bridge in Yorkshire, the family is a mix of a sign-painters' grotesque and Egyptian lettering. The uppercase is based on Victorian train station signage and the newly added lowercase is inspired by lettering manuals from the 19th century. Hebden has a nostalgic twist and is ideal for labelling, signage and memorable messages. The typeface with its robust angles and warm circular curves recalls the style of traditional English sans-serifs like Caslon’s 2-Line Egyptian. The weight range of the typeface has now spans eight thin to heavy styles with a slanted Roman for each weight. [ store.typenetwork.com ]

typefaces.name: Hekta
typefaces.desc: Hekta is a personal, experimental project of Arnaud Milliquet (ATMA World) and Nazareno Crea. This typeface provides a variation of styles in two weights. Every letter has its own respective alternate, sometimes inverting the contrast of thickness, sometimes reinventing its shape. The name derives from the Greek prefix "hekatón" (a hundred), hinting to the methodology applied in the design of this typeface where units of a hundred are alternatively subtracted or added to a fixed stroke to generate one design or its opposite. [ abc-etc.com ]

typefaces.name: Hela
typefaces.desc: Hela light is the first style of an upcoming grotesk font family. Despite its narrow and space-saving design, the typeface remains easily legible, making it suitable for longer texts. The design is grounded in geometrical shapes, complemented by rounded corners that provide a contrasting organic touch to its grid-based origins. [ moontype.de ]

typefaces.name: Helium (Dani Senso)
typefaces.desc: Helium is a slab typeface, designed for the Latin and Greek alphabet. It is wide and with generous interior spaces. It has a large x-height, and the ascenders are larger than the capital letters, to give it good legibility. A set of numbers and mathematical characters has an essential importance in the design, that it is oriented to scientific subjects. To use your special characters you must activate the basic ligatures or through the alternative character set ss20. [ danisenso.com ]

typefaces.name: Hellenic Typewriter
typefaces.desc: Hellenic Typewriter is a proportionally-spaced slab serif for text and display. The design combines the typewriter aesthetic’s balance of elegance and pragmatism with some of the extended western flavour of the style known as Antique Extended or Hellenic Wide, dating back to the 19th century. Rounded strokes, some unorthodox slab details and playful, looping tails all add to Hellenic Typewriter’s warmth and approachability, while its typewriter-inspired proportions and clean forms provide rythym and an honest, confident voice. The lightest weights, laying bare the simple, partly-geometric and optically-monolinear construction, embody an assertive elegance. Ball terminals feature extensively throughout the design, in both lower and uppercase. Expressive true italics elaborate upon and emphasise some of the freer, more decorative elements of the roman styles. [ polytype.co.uk ]

typefaces.name: Heltar
typefaces.desc: Originally published in 2011, updated in 2024. Heltar is a modern neo-grotesque typeface born from the legacy of Helvetica and refined for the digital age. Drawing inspiration from The Designers Republic’s treatment of Helvetica and the improvements of Hass Unica, Heltar strikes a balance between homage and innovation. Its meticulously crafted letterforms boast optical precision and subtle corrections, ensuring readability and rhythm, even under close tracking. But Heltar isn’t just about the past; it's also about the future. By incorporating ink-traps for a stylised, machine-like aesthetic, Heltar speaks to industries at the cutting edge of technology, making it ideal for brands in manufacturing and tech, seeking a sleek, futuristic vibe. [ thenorthernblock.co.uk ]

typefaces.name: Henmania
typefaces.desc: Henmania is a typeface where ingrown strokes form torqued, forward-leaning stencils. Its extra shapes and countershapes intermittently align between glyphs, twinkling with a crystalline delight. Henmania speaks to an unrelenting beat, and in all-caps, screams, COCK-A-DOODLE-DOOO! [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Herbik
typefaces.desc: Herbik is a warm, bouyant serif that explores the types of the Dutch Baroque, largely framed through the work of Miklos Kis — most commonly known as the Janson types. Herbik’s often top-heavy letterforms combine lively exuberance with more sober, tempered proportions and robust serifs to achieve a versatile and contemporary workhorse. [ counter-forms.com ]

typefaces.name: Hercules Neo
typefaces.desc: Contrast combined with smooth transitions and attention to detail are the magic features of Hercules family. Everything works up to present times – the power of good craft, clean, simple construction and elementar beauty are grounds for digital typography as well. Large x-height is also a legacy of the steam age, as display typefaces were primarily developed for the industrial revolution. Even in the age of artificial intelligence, nothing has changed, we need simplistic communication more than ever. Hercules is no more a revival, but an attractive, unique design, no matter it was “modern” some 150 years ago. Subhead designs have been corrected for small sizes. The range of its use is, therefore, quite extensive – from dictionaries and technical literature through magazines to art posters and advertising mate- rials. Regular: where Modern is too fragile and Century too boring, Hercules comes with its elegant forms and, at the same time, with sufficient firmness to be usable for longer texts. In its heavy, bold designs it approaches Falstaff, while in the Eco ones it has some fea- tures which are borrowed from Didot. The Text styles are perfectly adapted for sizes about 10 pt., for

typefaces.name: Hermanos
typefaces.desc: Hermanos is a dedication to the hand painted signs found in the Mission District of San Francisco. It's flared serifs, narrow stature and cheerful spirit make Hermanos a perfect compliment for packaging, restaurants, and creepy halloween headlines. [ nuformtype.com ]

typefaces.name: Hetskelet
typefaces.desc: Hetskelet combines a flared body with a sans inline and explores new shapes grown from an interaction between a bulbous tilted axis and a humanist upright one. This is a dance between the body and the bones, between the flesh and the skeleton. This is Hetskelet. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: HEX Franklin
typefaces.desc: An interpretation of Franklin Gothic , News Gothic , and Lightline Gothic produced as a variable font with weight and width axes. Also includes a ‘Tyght’ variant for typesetting in the ‘tight not touching’ style popular in the phototype era.

typefaces.name: Hexcess
typefaces.desc: Hexcess began as a sketch for a sci-fi heavy metal band logo but the project didn't move forward and the sketch sat in my sketchbook for years. After re-discovering it, I realized how much I still wanted to explore these letterforms and set about making an entire typeface out of it. Design-wise, this is an experiment using hexagons and novel forms derived from them to construct a condensed blackletter on a grid — a similar approach to that of Albrecht Dürer’s Constructed Textura of 1538. Several styles of blackletter were referenced to find forms that fit into the constraints of the design grid in a pleasing manner and with enough differentiation between glyphs (e.g. U-V) that would otherwise be too similar. In addition, Hexcess has high contrast, strong verticals, and swash glyphs, which altogether place this design light-years inside the display fonts quadrant (perhaps it should be named Janeway). [ delvefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Hightower
typefaces.desc: Hightower is a soft and inky take on the “Venetian” genre of text faces, which began with Nicholas Jenson’s roman of 1470. Hightower’s wide proportions and deep color were calibrated for small text sizes. Its organic forms and details also work well in headlines, adding complexity and subtlety. [ store.typenetwork.com ] Originally released by Font Bureau in 1996 and moved to Frere–Jones Type in 2020 [ fontsinuse.com ], available through Type Network and added to the foundry’s website in December 2024.

typefaces.name: Hilbertus Gill
typefaces.desc: Appears to be an interpretation of Albertus (Monotype, 1936).

typefaces.name: Hipsterpotamus
typefaces.desc: This typeface has me bamboozled to frazzle in attempts to describe it. In trying to fill as much of the available linear space with ink (or pixels [light]), it has become ballooned with squodge (but to avoid the kind of squodge that is evident in Gagarin , it has been given a few sharp corners). In doing so, it must abandon interior space; so – no counters. Some of the shapes incorporate the superellipse, a beautiful shape with a good story attached to it, which I really do recommend you read. I could see it being very satisfyingly cut from metal, but also made into squishy biscuits. I like that the vees – and possibly the M – look like an opened book; that the lowercase k looks like a churlish crow (or PacMan™ emerging from the bathroom); that the lowercase f looks like that famous criminal penguin with a pompadour in a wind-tunnel; and the asterisk, a lotus blossom. [ shapesforcash.com ]

typefaces.name: HLC Metra
typefaces.desc: HLC Metra seamlessly merges the boundaries between two iconic typographic archetypes known as “Grotesk” and “Geometric”, establishing its DNA predominantly within these two genres. Originating as an extension of my thesis at ECAL titled “Typographic Survivals: The Diachronic Evolution of Typographic Forms”, aimed at reimagining typographic classification and establishing links between influences, HLC Metra was conceived as a “mixed-breed” typeface, assimilating distinctive shapes from both worlds into a singular typeface. Drawing inspiration from Akzidenz Grotesk, Neue Haas Grotesk as well as Twentieth Century, its harmonious proportions and flowing rhythm evoke a seamless and modern sensibility, tailored for contemporary usage. [ hugolecorre.fr ]

typefaces.name: Hoffmann
typefaces.desc: Richard Lipton designed the Hoffmann family from letters drawn and then cut out of paper as free-standing forms by contemporary Michigan lettering artist Lothar Hoffmann. Lipton follows the creative development of contemporary lettering forms closely, searching for ideas that will yield type series. He digitized Hoffmann with Font Bureau in 1993, preparing four total weights, each supported by an expert set, plus a titling. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Hofmann
typefaces.desc: A display typeface based on a grid system by Swiss designer Armin Hofmann.

typefaces.name: Hofmann Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Inspired by the work of Swiss designer Armin Hofmann.

typefaces.name: Holise
typefaces.desc: Holise is a versatile typeface that masterfully blends modern and vintage aesthetics. Its condensed form is adorned with distinctive, spicy details on the serifs, giving it a unique and captivating character. This elegant font exudes sophistication, making it a perfect choice for adding flair and distinction to your titles and large-scale text. Whether you're aiming for a contemporary look or a classic feel, Holise brings originality and charm to any design, ensuring your work stands out with a touch of refinement. [ blazetype.eu ] Originally designed in 2021 and released with Blaze Type in September 2024.

typefaces.name: Hollywood Star
typefaces.desc: A typeface inspired by the Walk of Fame in Hollywood, Los Angeles, initially released in 2020. An updated version was released in 2025.

typefaces.name: Honeymoon
typefaces.desc: A true Dinamo-style monospaced Script typeface for all our friends and lovers. Containing romantic features such as single-width uppercase alternates, extravagant swashes, and other celebratory alternates.

typefaces.name: Horizon
typefaces.desc: Horizon is a strong, condensed display slab font with a wooden type feeling, commonly associated with American Old West folklore. Its shapes can also be classified as Antique, Egyptian, French Clarendon, or Italian Clarendon. In the 19th century, these designs were referred to as “Italian” due to the exotic appearance of their reverse-contrast serifs, despite having no clear connection to Italy. Beyond this arbitrary naming debate, Horizon is a stylistic synthesis of various archetypal sources from the early 20th century to the present day. It embodies the defining characteristics of these classic letterforms, widely used in large formats such as broadside posters, circus and carnival advertising, Western movie titles, street signage, basketball jerseys, and university logos. By blending a contemporary aesthetic with the attributes of a modern, functional Latin-script font, Horizon bridges the past and present. [ ott-foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Host Grotesk
typefaces.desc: A uniwidth sans serif based on Poppins , released as open-source and available on GitHub .

typefaces.name: Hour
typefaces.desc: Hour, designed by Federico Parra Barrios, is an original typeface that presents both conceptual and technical challenges. It proposes a contemporary interpretation of engraved letters, exploring how we perceive their forms based on the angle of incidence of the sun and the ambient light. This typeface breaks with a two-dimensional representation of the alphabet. One of the main challenges of Hour was how to portray the texture and depth of lapidary engraving, along with its shadows, under the constraints of Bézier curves. The illusion is created through an interplay of rasters with varying values. Though actually only drawn in black, each letter appears to contain tones of gray. Hour is a particularly accomplished variable font, despite having only two axes. The first axis, “hour,” determines the angle at which light strikes the surfaces of the letters, similar to a sundial. This axis evolves logically from 0 to 12, with the light appearing to revolve around the letters, generating an infinite number of variations. The second axis, “okta,” borrows the measurement of cloud cover from meteorology. By varying it, the designer gives the sensation of modifying the intensity of the incid

typefaces.name: House of Cassandre
typefaces.desc: Accessible by enrollment into Production Type’s Beta program.

typefaces.name: Hubano
typefaces.desc: Hubano is an all-caps display serif inspired by some lettering found on a Cuban cigar box (don't worry, we bought legally while in Jamaica ;-) The decorative and unconventional wacky crossbars of the A and H set the tone for a unique typeface rooted in Caribbean history. The premium cigar world has long been steeped in craftsmanship, tradition, and design. We're honoring that handmade legacy with this handmade font. [ simplebits.shop ]

typefaces.name: Hublot
typefaces.desc: Originally designed for the visual identity of La Fenêtre, an art center based in Montpellier, Hublot is a playful, sans-serif and monospaced family.
