Created by Sandrine Nugue, it comes in 11 styles, 5 weights and 5 italics, with a display version featuring much more radical shapes completing the family. Hublot’s visual concept plays on the contrast and graphic rhythm between very round shapes and triangular endings. Now it’s your turn to play! [ lift-type.fr ]

typefaces.name: Huemul Slab
typefaces.desc: Huemul Slab is a homage to Clarendon and Rockwell. While both typefaces feature powerful slab serifs, their proportions differ significantly. Clarendon has proportions based on transitional typefaces, giving it a more even and wider structure, whereas Rockwell follows classic proportions, resulting in greater variation between letterforms. Huemul Slab bridges the character of Rockwell with the more modern proportions typical of transitional typefaces, achieving a contemporary look. The result is a low-contrast typeface with aligned heights, ready for modern use but with a touch of classic elegance. [ wtypefoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Human Max
typefaces.desc: Human Max is a revival of the typeface known as ‘study for a typeface for machines and humans’, originally designed by Max Bill. This font complements Hofmann Grotesk , based on its proportions and sharing its origin, but adapted with a contemporary geometric finish.

typefaces.name: Humant
typefaces.desc: Humant is a geometric typeface inspired by the iconic Bauhaus design movement. It features clean, minimalist lines and circular shapes, emphasizing balance and symmetry. With its modular structure, Humant conveys a modern yet timeless aesthetic, making it ideal for branding, posters, and editorial design. The typeface combines functionality and art, evoking the Bauhaus principle of merging art and technology. [ tipotype.com ]

typefaces.name: Humus
typefaces.desc: Ukrainian humanistic semiserif of universal purpose. Thanks to humanistic proportions and somewhat calligraphic sharpness, the typeface unobtrusively disturbs the eye, while remaining at the same time a “strong” modern grotesque. Asymmetric serifs, distinctive letters and alternative glyphs give the font a Ukrainian flavor. The character set includes Slavic Cyrillic, European Latin and Monotonic Greek. Humus contains traditional and original ligatures, numeral variants, fractions, stylistic and historical alternatives. [ zakznak.com ]

typefaces.name: Hupaisa
typefaces.desc: Hupaisa is a geometric sans serif font that has a casual, hand-drawn appearance. It comes in six weights, including thin, light, regular, medium, bold, and black. Despite being a display font, Hupaisa is highly readable even in smaller sizes, making it an ideal choice for design projects. You can use it for both titles and body text and create captivating typography. Hupaisa also includes numerous alternate characters, ligatures, and swashes, allowing you to experiment and create unique titles, wordmarks, quotes, or logos.

typefaces.name: HWT Aetna
typefaces.desc: HWT Aetna is a revival of the sturdy Roman style of wood type most often called simply Aetna. This new digital version by Aaron Bell features four widths all based on those variations commonly offered by 19th Century wood type manufacturers. In addition, there is a four-layer all-caps version of Aetna based on the famous Wm. Page Chromatic Types. These allow designers to effortlessly create colorful chromatic streamer and shadow effects for their various projects. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT American
typefaces.desc: HWT American is a multilayered family. The source material was a 19th-century chromatic family that only included two fonts. This digital version includes eight, and they are designed to be set and arranged, one on top of the other, allowing thousands of imaginable color and pattern combinations. Five of the eight fonts in the set can be used individually as variations of the classic Tuscan style of wood type, defined by its concave stems and serifs. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Antique Tuscan 9
typefaces.desc: It is not an exaggeration to say that HWT Antique Tuscan is a very condensed 19th-century Tuscan design. This subtly detailed wood type was first shown by Wm H Page Co in 1859. Thanks to Miranda Roth Kirchmeyer’s work, this is the first digital version to include a lowercase and extended European character set. As lanky as Antique Tuscan is, it can make quite a statement when used at large sizes. Graphic designers everywhere! Imagine the dramatic headlines, posters, book covers, and packaging! [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Arabesque
typefaces.desc: HWT Arabesque is a long-lost Art Nouveau wood type from the Hamilton Museum Collection that evokes the excesses of Victorian design and the equally quirky ’60s Psychedelic era revival of Victorian type styles. Free-flowing designs flourished with Art Nouveau in the late 1800s and were directly referenced and further distorted with phototype in the late ’60s. Arabesque defies most of the basic tenets of type design and what comes to mind when one thinks “wood type.” [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Archimedes
typefaces.desc: HWT Archimedes is a wood type design sometimes known as Mansard. Virgin Wood Type brought this version to life as a wood type font. The variation with screw heads in the design was first seen in 1879 by William H. Page Co. This new digital version features a variety of styles, including the standard screw head option. The result is a sturdy, industrial font with a certain “joie de vivre” attitude. Not for every designer, but you know this is for YOU! [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Artz
typefaces.desc: HWT Artz evokes bold early 20th-century European poster lettering. It was designed by Erik Spiekermann for his own print studio, P98a, in Berlin. The rounded corners and robust shapes stand up to the punishing world of backlit signs and bring a bit of levity to all cap texts. At smaller sizes, the softer shapes radiate friendliness without straying toward whimsy. The outside curves are largely clothoidal and always find the smoothest transition from straight to curved. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Bernice
typefaces.desc: HWT Bernice is a system of ornaments designed by graphic artist Marian Bantjes. Aptly named for Bernice Schwahert, the first female type trimmer at Hamilton Manufacturing, known for her precision. The individual elements are asymmetrical, so symmetry, if that’s what you’re looking for, is found in rotation. Cover art, book endpapers, and fabrics are only a few possible applications. Equally enticing if you go big with wallpaper patterns and stenciled floors. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Bon Air
typefaces.desc: HWT Bon Air is a Mad Men-era advertising script for streamlined cars, exotic destinations, and boutique motels branded as resorts. Trademarked in 1961, it was one of the last new designs cut by Hamilton until the museum revival this century. Richard Kegler had only photographs and rubbings on which to base his digitization. A photostat proof was found after the project was finished. Bon Air was revived from the past, but it’s just as effective as a foil for the future. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Borders One
typefaces.desc: HWT Borders One is a revival of 19th-century typographic borders offering a spectrum from simple to ornate. It features ten decorative borders and eight streamer styles. It has versatility for playbills, certificates, warranties, shop signs, or tiny tickets. The modular construction allows seamless adaptation with the option to enlarge single elements for captivating backgrounds. Borders One showcases Richard Kegler’s appreciation for ornamental type in this concise yet versatile collection. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Brylski
typefaces.desc: Brylski is a typeface designed for the Hamilton Wood Type & Printing Museum, to be produced as wood type. Named for wood type worker Norb Brylski, the design is based on poster styles from the 19th century, particularly one offered as phototype by Dan X Solo under the name Midway Ornate. Brylski diverges notably from the original models, with adjustments to the proportions and serif style, plus other design optimizations for the wood type production process. [ hex.xyz ] HWT Brylski is Nick Sherman’s blend of 19th-century typographic motifs. Named for type cutter and Hamilton Printing Museum volunteer Norb Brylski, it features bifurcated serifs, extended width, with bold tops and bottoms. The mansard sides give the hefty serifs a jaunty air, while the very thin middles showcase the weight they both hold and anchor. Made with an understanding of the era, clever decisions have been taken to incorporate more modern letterforms into the character set. Use it boldly! [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Bulletin Script
typefaces.desc: Paul D. Hunt’s HWT Bulletin Script, inspired by the 60s psychedelic style and sourced from the Hamilton Collection, boasts a unique blend of contrasting elements. The heavy bottom halves of its letters sweep into crisp concavity, punctuated by energetic spikes. In contrast, the thin top halves feature intricate details like ball terminals and looped endings. This harmonious fusion of bold and delicate forms produces a coherent, flowing script. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Catchwords
typefaces.desc: Fonts like HWT Catchwords have always been offered alongside standard alphabets in wood type catalogs. They appear so often on posters as a decorative punch that they have become part of the wood type vernacular. These words could be inserted into a design along with decorative ornaments when space was tight or to add variety to the design. Catchwords features over 80 words based directly on designs offered by Hamilton and other wood type manufacturers of the 19th and early 20th Century. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Etta
typefaces.desc: HWT Etta is a display typeface with two distinctive styles: Etta East and Etta West. These offer versatility in conveying wood type aesthetics, drawing inspiration from the 19th-century wood type era, infused with 1960s phototype sensibilities, and adapted for contemporary design demands. Despite their differences, both fonts are intended for impactful display use, so embrace their individuality and combine them boldly. HWT Etta is a tribute to Etta Shove Hamilton, J.E. Hamilton’s wife. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Geometric
typefaces.desc: HWT Geometric is a 19th-century design that conjures up early 20th-century Dutch DeStijl lettering with mostly strict adherence to right angles and minimal stroke modulation. Geometric began life as a metal typeface from the Central Type Foundry, circa 1884. After many adaptations by various foundries, James Grieshaber digitized and expanded it for modern use. Geometric could be considered a quirky slab serif perfect for any more rebellious typographic use. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Gothic Round
typefaces.desc: HWT Gothic Round is a bold, rounded sans digitized by Miguel Sousa. He took inspiration from eight different wood type sources dating back to 1838. Despite its tubular appearance, this typeface surprises with carefully crafted details. Distinct characteristics were emphasized or subdued, resulting in a fun hybrid. Notice the flat top of the ‘j,’ the dimple on ‘1,’ and the solution for minimizing descenders in the ‘g.’ Given its small counters, this face shines when used in larger sizes. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Konop
typefaces.desc: HWT Konop would have been a head-scratcher for old-world printers, but modern-day designers will find inspiration in its modular and rotational features. Mark Simonson named the family for Hamilton Manufacturing retiree and museum volunteer Don Konop. Not only are the letters monospaced, but they are square. They can be arranged tabularly, offering a lot of creative freedom. They adapt to their limitations in charming ways, and the numbers have a lot of personality. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Lustig Elements
typefaces.desc: HWT Lustig Elements is a testament to innovative design. Over five years, Craig Welsh meticulously crafted this typeface inspired by the mid-century designer Alvin Lustig’s Euclid. This name also pays tribute to designer Elaine Lustig Cohen, who collaborated on its development. Lustig Elements defies rigidity with unconventional shapes, resulting in unexpected quarter-circle accents and a vibrant neon inline style, adding a touch of surprise to its geometric foundation. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Mardell
typefaces.desc: Louise Fili did a remarkable thing with her first-ever typeface, the Italian Futurist-inspired HWT Mardell. She made a geometric design without strictly adhering to a system. Fili allowed herself to play, resulting in innovative solutions to problematic characters. Have a look at: E F J K 3 & $. With its angular, constructed letterforms, the no-nonsense design is also a fitting tribute to the woman it was named for: veteran Hamilton Manufacturing type cutter Mardell Doubek. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Republic Gothic
typefaces.desc: Originally issued in six sizes as one of the last Hamilton Manufacturing Co. wood types, the digital HWT Republic Gothic is now a single-style affair. Miranda Roth and Richard Kegler based their design on the extended width, creating solid and outline versions. They can be used separately or overlayed to create color effects. The playful nature of Republic Gothic, with its handful of quirky characters, will add levity to any design, making it a lively alternative to every day sans serifs. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Roman Extended
typefaces.desc: HWT Roman Extended is a pairing of opposites in heft, but comrades in expansion. Fatface is a super-high contrast design, while Lightface offers delicate elegance. What they have in common is width. With Fatface, rather than reviving one version, designer Jim Lyles combined the best historical details. Lightface, a rare find in print shops, was recreated by Miranda Roth, maintaining grace and showcasing subtle contrast and wide, bracketed serifs. Both faces are eye-popping in large sizes! [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Showcard Script
typefaces.desc: HWT Showcard Script is a dynamic vintage typeface that hints at its origins from the mid-1900s, designed for shop owners to create in-house promotional material. Its brushstroke-based glyphs emulate skilled sign painting, with bold uppercase letters and unique details like the looping in B, E, and R, and open-dot i and j. Designer Terry Wüdenbachs digitized it from the Hamilton Wood Type & Printing Museum, extending the character set so you can create an authentic shop card aesthetic, too! [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Slab
typefaces.desc: The HWT Slab family, comprising Slab Antique and Slab Columbian, embodies robust slab serif designs, reminiscent of Dutch’ chocoladeletters.’ Both fonts share traits such as low contrast, a high x-height, short descenders, and occasional rounded endings with a lowercase ‘j’ notch. The only difference you’ll actually find is in the serif structure. Designer Tim Martin meticulously sourced material from various manufacturers and supplemented it with additional characters, punctuation, and accents. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Star Ornaments
typefaces.desc: HWT Star Ornaments, curated by typographic sage Richard Kegler, offers a mixed collection of historical ornaments ideal for modern design. With dozens of stars in two orientations, typographic whirligigs, ornamental brackets, and a versatile modular border system, these elements can be used for illustrations, patterns, or map markers. The modular border pieces, including stars and stripes, come with connectors and endings for creating intricate designs, from letters to free-form frames. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Tangent
typefaces.desc: HWT Tangent, a modern font with a 200-year-old legacy, features nesting letters, numerous alternates, and double-Os. Inspired by the 1800s wood type Tangent from the Cary Graphic Arts Collection at RIT, designer Patrick Griffin expanded it to over 500 glyphs, including ten alternates for the letter A. The font’s ascenders and descenders support smaller letters, allowing for creative spacing and versatility. The dynamism of Tangent lies in its unique letterforms and your skill in combining them. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Tuscan Extended
typefaces.desc: HWT Tuscan Extended is an exercise in exuberance: bifurcated terminals, stem spikes, crossbars, and that ampersand… oh my! There are some relatively simple letters (o, c, s), but ornamentation is otherwise omnipresent, especially in the w, x, and z. At least four different versions of this 19th-century typeface were made, so designer Frank Grießhammer had a lot of material to work with as he expanded the character set so Tuscan Extended would function in a modern, multi-lingual world. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT Unit Gothic
typefaces.desc: HWT Unit Gothic, originally published in 1907 by Hamilton Manufacturing Co., is, historically speaking, one of the first multi-height typefaces with seven fonts ranging from sturdy and small to thin and tall. This revolutionary design allowed for various lengths of harmonious text and headline compositions, pre-dating Adrian Frutiger’s system by fifty years. James Todd’s digital revival includes alternate characters, Greek and Cyrillic sets, and punctuation, totaling 600 glyphs per font. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: HWT VanLanen
typefaces.desc: Sturdy triangular serifs yet light on its feet, HWT Van Lanen is a modern classic. Originally commissioned in 2002, it was Matthew Carter’s first foray into wood type production after a half-century of designing typefaces. With a low contrast, boxy design and inspiration from the interplay of positive and negative forms, Carter imagined how two versions might be used together. You can create chromatics by layering the two or stacking lines on top of each other to create lively blocks of text. [ p22.com ]

typefaces.name: iA Writer
typefaces.desc: iA Writer Duo started as a slight customization of IBM Plex Mono to offer some characters ( MmWw ) 1.5x space. More thoroughly redesigned in 2018 with the introduction of iA Writer Quattro . Released as open-source on GitHub.

typefaces.name: Ice Tray
typefaces.desc: A grid-based display face inspired by the freezing of water and the frozen water “bridges” formed in ice cube trays. It’s designed for display use—being comprised of wild unorthodox letterforms set on a rigid grid. [ tofutype.ca ]

typefaces.name: Icona Serif
typefaces.desc: Icona Serif is a neutral typeface with a high x-height, a wide range of weights with adequate italics, and an extensive character set covering Latin, Cyrillic, and Greek. Many alternative characters find use in changes of typesetting character, but they stand out especially in display sizes, where they can attract attention even in a seemingly serious presentation. [ suitcasetype.com ]

typefaces.name: Idyll
typefaces.desc: Idyll is inspired by my time with my dear friend C at her organic farm, Terrafranta, in the hills near Florence—a place so beautiful, so unreal. I drew these letters last spring and summer as a love letter. A love letter to starry nights and midday heat. To sage, lavender, orchids, and bees. To our friendship, and to what might one day be lost forever. [ celine-hurka.com ]

typefaces.name: Image Future
typefaces.desc: Accessible by enrollment into Production Type’s Beta program.

typefaces.name: Imenso
typefaces.desc: A compressed typeface with subtle serifs offers a sophisticated balance between elegance and intensity, ideal for high-impact headlines. Its condensed letterforms make it well-suited for settings where space is limited yet presence is critical, allowing for bold messaging without sacrificing readability. The subtle serifs add a touch of refinement, giving the typeface a unique character that stands out from traditional sans-serifs or more pronounced, decorative serif fonts. This typeface delivers a commanding visual effect while maintaining a timeless and polished look, making it perfect for editorial designs, magazine covers, or advertising materials where a strong but stylish impression is necessary. The delicacy of the serifs adds a whisper of classicism to an otherwise modern and streamlined design, creating a sense of authority and sophistication. When paired with well-considered spacing and contrast, the compressed proportions emphasize power and elegance, drawing the reader’s eye to the message with immediate impact. [ dstype.com ]

typefaces.name: Immortel
typefaces.desc: Immortel, designed by Clément Le Tulle-Neyret, is a type family with four variants developed according to the Hippocratic theory of humors that explains these latter through the presence of one of the four principal fluids. Each one is the cause behind the development of a character trait: phlegm represents a lymphatic, sluggish, slow character (Immortel Infra); yellow bile, an angry and prideful character (Immortel Colera); blood, a jovial and warm character (Immortel Vena); and black bile provokes hopelessness and melancholy (Immortel Acedia). This type family is envisaged like a human being, able to reveal different temperaments through the forms that it adopts. Each variant can be substituted for another without causing any change in the bulkiness of the text, as the metric system, which provides a structural link between the variants—set width, x-heights, the length of ascenders and descenders, height of capitals—is constant. Typographically, each variant is inspired by the work of type designers, following the course of history: Immortel Infra finds its source in the work of Robert Granjon, a typeface engraver from the 16th century; Immortel Colera in the work of Jean Jannon,

typefaces.name: Impura
typefaces.desc: Impura is the result of a deep exploration into the Blackletter style and its diverse sub-genres. Blackletters have always fascinated us with their striking visual impact, rich historical roots, and broad range of sub-genres, each carrying distinctive stylistic nuances. Impura was designed to embody this versatility. Through a series of OpenType features, this typeface allows users to navigate between a wide array of stylistic sets and alternate forms inspired by iconic Blackletter sub-genres. This enables the typeface to adopt different personalities, from the flowing, humanistic curves of Fraktur to the rigid, angular forms of Textura, as well as other sets influenced by lesser-known sub-genres and modern reinterpretations. Additionally, Impura offers an extensive range of weights — a rarity for this genre — which adds even greater versatility. The result is a unique typeface that blends sharp angles, geometric precision, and smooth curves, creating a distinctive aesthetic characterized by its brooding elegance, unorthodox charm and raw energy. This multi-faceted approach gives Impura the ability to straddle historical authenticity and progressive creativity. [ fuertetype.com ]

typefaces.name: Inclusive Sans
typefaces.desc: Inclusive Sans is a text font designed for accessibility and readability. It is inspired by the friendly personality of contemporary neo-grotesques while incorporating key features to make it highly legible in all uses. [ oliviaking.com ] Updated in February 2025.

typefaces.name: Indecisive Mono
typefaces.desc: How to create an original Geometric Mono? Indecisive Mono takes on a more playful and approach than most geometric Monos. Indecisive Mono isn’t based off of one source of inspiration, but merges elements from various Sans Serifs, such as Bernhard Gothic, Nobel Antieke and Spartan. Equally, Indecisive Mono comes with a set of alternate, swash characters derived from Old-Style italic Serifs such as Granjon. This merger has resulted in a joyful and distinct Geometric Mono with plenty of character, perfect for any setting. It comes in 20 styles, from Thin to Heavy, with slanted counterparts providing the user with plenty of versatility for any design. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Indecisive Sans
typefaces.desc: How to create an original Geometric Sans? Indecisive Sans takes on a more playful and approach than most Geometric Sans. Indecisive Sans isn’t based off of one source of inspiration, but merges elements from various Sans Serifs, such as Bernhard Gothic, Nobel Antieke and Spartan. Equally, Indecisive Sans comes with a set of alternate, swash characters derived from Old-Style italic Serifs from punchcutters like Granjon. This merger has resulted in a joyful and distinct Geometric Sans perfect for any setting. It comes in 20 styles, from Thin to Heavy, with slanted counterparts providing the user with plenty of versatility for any design. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Indicate Mono
typefaces.desc: While preserving the strict order of a monospace typeface, Indicate Mono partly moves away from the typical technical aesthetics of fixed-width typefaces. The interplay of expected mechanical-looking characters and more warm and friendly letterforms create a unique dissonance.

typefaces.name: Indoor Kid
typefaces.desc: Updated with a lowercase in March 2025.

typefaces.name: Inknut Antiqua
typefaces.desc: Released as open-source on GitHub .

typefaces.name: Innovator Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Innovator Grotesk got its name because it’s tailored to the needs of startup founders and indie hackers. It praises entrepreneurship and all the crazy ones building today’s web and mobile apps that will change the world tomorrow. Innovator is meant to be for your startup what the San Francisco font is for Apple and Roboto is for Google. It’s a highly versatile neo-grotesque typeface perfect for user interface design. Its well-tailored vertical metrics ensure that text is centered on buttons and aligned with icons. Additionally, this setup means writing less code and ultimately achieving a reliable and maintainable design system on the frontend. [ yeptype.com ]

typefaces.name: Instant
typefaces.desc: Originally released in 2012 with BAT .

typefaces.name: Inter
typefaces.desc: Released as open-source on GitHub.

typefaces.name: Interact
typefaces.desc: Interact was originally designed by 8vo in 1994 as part of an invited submission to the American Center of Design Journal. It was first implemented as a system of grid-based bitmap typefaces, in lowercase characters only, for screen use. Taking as a starting point the optical characteristics of the stroke junctions in Wim Crouwel’s ‘vormgevers’ lettering of 1968, Interact employs horizontal and vertical lines as well as 45-degree pixel steps to modulate a set of stroke junctions which have the effect of optically rounding the letterforms. Interact has been extensively expanded and revised by MuirMcNeil as a system of 23 typefaces in 4 scaleable groups with a comprehensive range of 12 calibrated weights. A complete set of capital letters, punctuation marks and accented characters for Western European languages have also been added. The Interact typefaces follow a mathematical progression in which type size hierarchies are scaled in exact proportion to a constant pixel resolution. There are four resolutions in the Interact system: 06, 04, 03 and 02. These numbers refer to the scale ratios of the bitmap contours. When used in size relationships which are relative to these proportions,

typefaces.name: Interlock
typefaces.desc: Interlock is a geometric bitmap type system in four styles each in six weights. In Interlock, the relationship between inked and uninked parts of letters is broken down into even patterns of parallel horizontal or vertical lines. Where traditional type designs are configured in binary contrasts of form and counterform, Interlock’s lines are progressively incremented in weight to provide tonal pattern densities within the body of the type. [ muirmcneil.com ]

typefaces.name: Intermedial Slab
typefaces.desc: Intermedial Slab is a highly versatile and robust type family that offers both high-contrast and low-contrast slab serif styles, catering to a wide range of design needs. Each style is meticulously crafted with a humanistic touch, bringing warmth, precision, and an approachable quality to the typeface. The humanistic design approach ensures that each character feels balanced and natural, enhancing readability while maintaining a distinctive aesthetic. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Intern
typefaces.desc: A geometric sans serif produced as a color font.

typefaces.name: Intern Sans
typefaces.desc: Intern is a linear geometric sans serif family, a curious combination of simple shapes with a raw character. Type family is carefully constructed to create the very basic forms of letters and developed with minimal optical corrections to maintain the blunt and playful character. Letters get their dynamic proportions and huge x-height from construction of 5x5 grid of squares, inspired by sketches on a checkered notebook. This results a unique geometric typeface with a powerful appearance. The new and updated version of the Intern version 2.0, reworked and released with upgrades using the color font technology. All Intern license holders starting from 2022 will be eligible for a free Intern v2.0 Family license. [ elementtype.co ]

typefaces.name: Intersect
typefaces.desc: MuirMcNeil Intersect is a type system which subverts typographic weight — the relationship between inked and uninked parts of letters and word forms. Where traditional type designs can only provide a binary contrast of black and white, form and counterform, Intersect typefaces exceed this limitation by emulating a successive range of linear screens to give the illusion of tint densities within the body of the type. Because Intersect contours and spaces map onto each other precisely, a wide range of design options is possible using layers. Intersect is available in ‘A’ and ‘B’ contour variants (analogous to regular and bold). These share 16 common screen patterns, arranged in four groups each with four weights. Intersect A and B have been designed to interact with one another by layering (in 256 possible combinations). Using page layout, bitmap or vector design software, the designer can explore the potential for enhancing the layering effects by applying colour, tint and transparency / opacity as appropriate. [ muirmcneil.com ]

typefaces.name: Interstate
typefaces.desc: Starting in 1949, a team of road engineers and sign painters developed a new and clearer style of lettering for highway signs. A scientist’s rigor and a tradesman’s common sense merged—not always smoothly—to create Highway Gothic , which became the federal standard for road signage and a pervasive feature of the American landscape. The original alphabets were developed for the California Division of Highways by Dr. Theodore W. Forbes, assisted by J.E. Penton and E.E. Radek. Interstate began as a personal challenge to build a typeface from the unlikely source of highway lettering. By traditional precepts, this design is full of shapes that are “wrong” but essential to its personality, like the uppercase letters which range from oddly cramped to strangely wide or the abrupt descender of the lowercase g. Frere-Jones redesigned every original shape and extrapolated missing characters such as ampersands and foreign accents, using a light touch throughout to preserve both durability and the stumbling, dissonant charm. Contributions by Cyrus Highsmith, Nina Stössinger, Davy Dai, Richard Lipton [ frerejones.com ] Originally released by Font Bureau in 1993 and moved to Frere–Jones Type in 2

typefaces.name: Interstate Mono
typefaces.desc: Originally released by Font Bureau in 2000 and moved to Frere–Jones Type in 2020 [ fontsinuse.com ], available through Type Network and added to the foundry’s website in December 2024.

typefaces.name: Invert
typefaces.desc: Invert is an experimental variable typeface with interpolation between shapes and counter shapes. It consists of four styles: Black and White roman styles are complemented by the italics. Black and White styles are the complete opposite of each other. The Black style is based on a stencil construction, and the White is created from the counter forms of the Black. The styles can work separately but the magic happens in the movement between them. The need for smooth interpolation greatly influences the design of the original masters. The straight geometric shapes provide better control, while the stencilled Black style helps to avoid sloppy shapes. Enjoy the dynamic of black-to-white transformation! [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Ipar
typefaces.desc: Ipar is a new experimental-, conceptual typeface that features two widths and seven weights, making it a versatile option for a range of design applications. The most unique aspect of Ipar is that all stems are the same size and there are no optical corrections, resulting in a clean and modern look. The shapes of the letters are mathematically constructed using the most commonly used measurement tool, resulting in a precise and geometric aesthetic. The inspiration for Ipar comes from Austrian street and city signs, with the designer first encountering this style in Schladming. The typeface also draws on design movements such as Bauhaus and Constructivism, incorporating principles of geometry and simplicity. The overall effect is an experimental and concrete typeface that is both sleek and visually engaging. [ hungarumlaut.com ]

typefaces.name: Isola
typefaces.desc: An interpretation of Venus , including a backslanted style, with the addition of semi-monospaced and monospaced variants. The proportional family is produced as a variable font with weight and slant axes, and the monospaced family as a variable font with weight and monospace axes. Static fonts are also available.

typefaces.name: Items
typefaces.desc: Items is a contemporary typeface that ties in with the pervasive serifs of the early digital period. Reconciling familiarity with beauty, it seeks to overcome the limitations of Times & co. Its design is more consistent, featuring a contrast axis and top serifs that exhibit the same angle across all weights. Drawn with a focus on carefully modulated blacks and shapely whites, Items achieves an even typographic color. […] Each facet conjures distinct associations. The Condensed Black, for example, has qualities similar to the punchy Times variant seen on paperback designs by Fleckhaus. The other end of the weight spectrum echoes the days when the Macintosh boasted a narrow Garamond. Items Wide opens up a whole new dimension, exploring what a transitional serif would look like if freed from space constraints. On top of that, each subfamily has a Monospace style that is awkward and alluring at once. Characterized by fixed proportions and rather spindly strokes, this extension references the Latin glyphs included in fonts made for Chinese and Japanese scripts.

typefaces.name: IvyBodoni
typefaces.desc: IvyBodoni is an homage to the modern serif designs of the ’60s and ’70s. Typefaces like Pistilli Roman, Didi, and CBS Didot and lettering artists such as Mortimer Leach and Tommy Thompson informed Jan Maack’s choices when drawing the crisp hairlines, distinct ball terminals, and precise curves. This 21st-century Bodoni was made for fashion and editorial design and is ready for all your display typography needs. [ ivyfoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: IvyGothic
typefaces.desc: IvyGothic is a rationalized redesign of Times Gothic from the American Specimen Book of Type Styles, a catalog from American Type Founders (1912). Jan Maack aimed to preserve the original’s subtle warmth while refining its irregularities to improve readability, clarity, and simplicity — a bit of polish, if you will, to make this forgotten American grotesque shine in modern use. [ ivyfoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: IvySoft
typefaces.desc: IvySoft is an unpretentious, rounded sans balancing work and play. The skeletal structure is no-nonsense, keeping your text tight and easy to read. While the overall look is warm with tapered tails, rounded terminals, and a bit of contrast. The design began with IvyEpic material, making these two families an intriguing opportunity for a font pairing. [ ivyfoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Jack
typefaces.desc: Jack is a typeface born from the Tavern, the creative and experimental wavy tool crafted by Gaëtan Baehr. With its roots in brutalist design, Jack embodies a strikingly bold, robust, and modern aesthetic. Its simplified forms strip away unnecessary details, creating a raw yet refined structure that commands attention. Jack's unapologetic weight and clarity give it a powerful, expressive voice, perfect for making strong, assertive statements. Jack is designed exclusively in capitals, allowing for optimized wave effects with the Tavern tool. To further enhance its creative possibilities, the font includes a width variation axis and four corner axes—top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right—that enable precise control over each letter's shape. These features make it possible to craft unexpected and visually striking effects. [ black-foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: JAF Lapture
typefaces.desc: Updated in March 2025 with condensed and black styles, as well as with support for the Cyrillic script.

typefaces.name: Jäger
typefaces.desc: Jäger is a display typeface, useful for headlines or short to medium-length texts. It was designed in 2020 by Jérémy Schneider for VJ Type. The font’s release falls five years after the first drawings were developed for an exhibition at the Musées des Arts Décoratifs in Paris dedicated to contemporary art crafts. Jäger is a tribute to fine craftsmanship. The font is very directly inspired by techniques mastered by craftsmen in their work. We thus see the hollowed-out counter forms reminiscent of engravings, sculptures or working with chisels. The angles give the impression of having been cut in wood, the contours are rounded, never sharp. Each weight offers two versions: the Jäger Master version which is the original, most advanced, most daring design, and the Jäger Classic version in which the counter forms at the tops of the letters have been filled in to offer a smoother and more versatile option. [ vj-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Jargon
typefaces.desc: Jargon is a typeface that shows the influence of both Dutch newspaper types and the work of Francois Ganeau and Roger Excoffon. Completed at the beginning of 2025, this family grew out of a single condensed style of Thomas Bouillet’s degree project at Type]Media in the Netherlands in 2020. [ vault.commercialtype.com ]

typefaces.name: Jarlath
typefaces.desc: Though it had only a limited release as dry transfer type in 1974, Jarlath Hayes’s Tuam Uncial became an icon of Irish Modernism. Its design was based on hacked Helvetica Bold; Hayes sliced off the tops and bottoms of the letters to produce forms reminiscent of the wide, pen-formed scripts of old Insular texts. This digital revival, designed by Max Phillips under the supervision of Hayes’s daughter, supports over 150 languages and features ligatures, directional arrows, and a fuller range of punctuation. To improve readability, we’ve tempered the extreme squarishness of the original forms, reduced their contrast, and provided more generous letterspacing. Early drafts of the original Tuam Uncial lacked the published version’s semiserifs, so we’ve added a sans version, as well as italic and sans italic styles. [ signalfoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Jaws
typefaces.desc: Jaws is a reverse contrast unlike any you've ever seen. Named after and inspired by the iconic James Bond henchman, this type uses brute strength and clever solutions in a similar, yet completely unrelated fashion. Initially started as a new take on broad nib calligraphy, this type sheds its classic roots and takes firm footing in the contemporary landscape… [ nuformtype.com ]

typefaces.name: Jazzman
typefaces.desc: I am a big fan of Jazz and of Mid Modern Century design and I already created a few fonts about that style, but this time I wanted to create something a bit more functional that could many uses in a vintage way. So here is Jazzman. Inspiration comes from old 50/60s lettering, mostly from the US, with a Hand Drawn style. This is something important for me: you can see this is hand made. It is not perfect, it is human, and this is my thing. [ francischouquet.com ]

typefaces.name: Jester
typefaces.desc: A fork of Trickster .

typefaces.name: JL Impact Nieuw
typefaces.desc: Impact Nieuw is reinterpreted version of Impact originally designed by Geoffrey Lee in 1965 by adopting modern values. Its daring flowery cursive lines, ink-traps, and different width variations are the most significant change from the previously rigid look with its united set of straight-lined letters and condensed fixed width. [ j-ltf.com ]

typefaces.name: JL Joseleen
typefaces.desc: Joseleen is a serif typeface, developed from ‘Permeke’ originally drawn by Josse Pyl in 2013, now paired with an Italic. It has 3 sets of stylistic alternates besides its default set. Joseleen’s prominent wedge-shaped serifs sit heavy and walk with confidence, yet its floriated nature - looks almost like a ponytail, seen in the ‘K’, ‘R’, ‘Q’, and the ‘r’ - gives an elegant edge to the default set and the stylistic figure 2. However, the alternates of these letters in the figure set 1 and 3 with the hard-down sloping legs nuance a straightforward nature. [ j-ltf.com ]

typefaces.name: JL Jungka
typefaces.desc: Jungka is a typeface made collaboratively between Karel Martens and Jungmyung Lee. It derives from the most widely used fonts; Akzidenz Grotesk, Helvetica and Univers. We wanted to make a grotesk font positioned somewhere between Akzidenz grotesk, Helvetica and Univers - not as dry and distant as Univers, but devoid of the quirky uniformity of Helvetica. Jungka is more reminiscent of Akzidenz grotesk than the other two typefaces. Like Akzidenz grotesk its letterforms are autonomous in width and have a contemporary feel in their curves and straight lines. Yet Junka’s accentuated circular curves evoke a soft, friendly, and rhythmical atmosphere. Jungka shares the quality of a classically crafted sans serif typeface by taking its formal cues from these historic predecessors. However, fine-tuning its space for text enhances legibility with a modern touch. [ j-ltf.com ]

typefaces.name: JL Limpet Granite
typefaces.desc: JL Limpet Granite is a serif typeface, reinterpreted from a classic typeface Plantin. Like Plantin, it retains the robust structure of the strokes, the serifs, and generous letter widths, resulting in a rich texture and a visually substantial appearance. However, JL Limpet Granite enhances Plantin’s timeless and elegant essence by infusing a touch of femininity into the letterforms. Yet, its bold and contemporary characteristics are carefully balanced with the exaggerated cursive lines and daringly abrupt cuts, notably in letters such as ‘K’, ‘M’, ‘V’, ‘W’, and the ‘g’. The family includes eight text weights and is complemented by the standalone italicised version, JL Limpet Intertidal. [ j-ltf.com ]

typefaces.name: JL Limpet Intertidal
typefaces.desc: JL Limpet Intertidal, a compatible italicised pair to JL Limpet Granite, shares a tint of handwriting-like feature—not only appearing to be condensed for textural support to the regular style but also serving as a standalone typeface. Inspired by Cross-writing as a practice of writing sideways on top of the first side of text, various directional axes seamlessly coexist. Dissonance finds HARMONY. JL Limpet Intertidal has loosely defined axes and an unconventional adoption of letter width, particularly in characters like C, e, g, r, s, v, w, and y, which create a textural dissonance when written. Yet, as a whole, JL Limpet Intertidal meanders, crafting fluid tidal flourishes where diverse directional axes harmoniously coalesce. [ j-ltf.com ]

typefaces.name: JL Pirelli
typefaces.desc: Pirelli is the second typeface developed collaboratively between Karel Martens and Jungmyung Lee following Jungka. Pirelli is a revival of an anonymous grotesk typeface that Karel Martens once came across. Its mostly horizontal and vertical features with a mono-line structure and an absence of flourishes give it a concise expression. Yet, it has the distinctive motif of unusually high-waisted capitals, visible in all letters with bars, such as ‘E’, ‘F’, and ’P’. This feature gives Pirelli the atmosphere of earlier Art Nouveau and Secessionist lettering. However, the radically considered high contrast between uppercase and lowercase in its width talks of today’s time. [ j-ltf.com ]

typefaces.name: Jobim
typefaces.desc: Jobim draws its primary inspiration from the French classic Vendome (likely the most famous modern Old Face), designed by Francois Ganeua in 1951, but drifts away from a historical revival infusing a vernacular approach based on the lettering from the poster of Orfeu Negro. Replacing the dynamic, expressive flow of Vendome with a simpler, more orthogonal axis, Jobim manages to be both brutal and elegant. Suitable for big sizes, the Compressed Black is just the first of a family planned with 48 styles that will include up-right and italics. [ flaviazim.com ]

typefaces.name: Joc
typefaces.desc: The first letters of Joc typeface were designed to accompany Sara San Gregorio’s exhibition: Juguetoría a l’altura del joc curated by Helena Ayuso Moli y Anna Roigé Barrull at La Panera Art Center LLeida, Spain. The exhibition playground encourages children from age 5 to 9 to create their own toys by combining together different shapes. These shapes were the main inspiration for the concept of the letters and have been translated into symbols for the character set. The name of the typeface itself is a link between the same matching word in Catalan and Romanian – Joc = Game. A description of the personality of the typeface and the place where its’ design was born and my own native roots. [ futurefonts.com ] Released through Future Fonts in 2023, from which it graduated in August 2024 and reissued with Type-Ø-Tones.

typefaces.name: Joie Grotesk
typefaces.desc: A clean overall design, it borrows somewhat from pioneering sans-serif concepts of the early 19th century, adding quirks and warmth to a regular and balanced rhythm. These traits can be enhanced with various Stylistic Sets, e. g., by adding more expressive ears and hooks to “r” and “f”, respectively. Joie Grotesk gives you a confident and optimistic voice with wit and team spirit. It adapts to your requirements. In bolder weights, Joie Grotesk’s relationship to its old-style Grotesque ancestors is more evident. These styles are optimized for display sizes and short texts. Here, their unobtrusive quirks can be wholly appreciated. The regular and lighter weights, on the other hand, are optimized for longer copy. They make for a comfortable reading experience in all sizes. [ identity-letters.com ]

typefaces.name: Jt Multona
typefaces.desc: A boxy sans serif, initially an interpretation of Gigant (Genzsch & Heyse). Produced in five weights of increasing width, with uprights and two italics of different slants, as well as a variable font.

typefaces.name: Jt Picolo
typefaces.desc: A sans serif informed by 19th-century Grotesque typefaces. Produced in four weights in upright and italic, as well as a variable font.

typefaces.name: Jubel
typefaces.desc: Jubel is a feeling of exuberant expressions of joy and celebration, often accompanied by a sense of pride and accomplishment. The letters in Jubel are bold and capture the happiness and enthusiasm of a festive celebration. The thick strokes and lively curves exude excitement, reflecting the jubilant mood. [ typeoffeeling.com ]

typefaces.name: Julia
typefaces.desc: A cursive typeface inspired by calligraphy.

typefaces.name: Juma
typefaces.desc: Juma is a super display color font made to be used HUGE. Created by brazilian lettering artist extraordinaire Cyla Costa, Juma is a deep exploration of shapes and served as the path to push the boundaries of her work’s visual language. The shapes and colors of Juma remind us of natural beauties like tropical birds or a slab of marble, its twists and turns almost hypnotic. On the page, Juma can work as a beautifully decorated drop cap, a striking headline, or even in abstract compositions like patterns, but outside the page into the physical world, each individual letter has a sculptural quality to it that invites us to imagine it as an object. Juma is playful, daring, and powerful and we’re thrilled to have it in Naipe Foundry’s library.

typefaces.name: Jupette
typefaces.desc: A cheeky slightly soft sans serif with the spirit of the Côte d’Azur in the late fifties. [ store.typenetwork.com ]

typefaces.name: Kablammo
typefaces.desc: Kablammo is a hyperactive, doodad, maximalist typeface inspired by the energies of Jokerman, toys, and cartoons from the 80s and 90s and the Memphis Group. It’s a variable font with a Morph axis, allowing you to bounce between four predefined alternates for each glyph or anything in between. [ vectrotype.com ] Commissioned by Google Fonts and released as open-source on GitHub.

typefaces.name: Kade
typefaces.desc: Kade is a display/semi display sans family of fonts based on vernacular lettering photographed over the last ten years in and around the harbours of Amsterdam and Rotterdam. Hence the name Kade that translates into English as ‘quay’, also the name of its designer. Kade grew slowly from many different ideas and elements. The letters reflects the industrial method in which they are cut for the side of ships from large steel plates. Frequently subtleties of curves are compromised due to the cutting tools and the fact engineers are in control. Kade’s italics have an experimental character and were produced in an unorthodox manner by rotating 8 degrees, rather than slanting the roman characters, a method sometimes employed in shipyards. Kade constructed character is ideal for contemporary editorial works, architecture magazines, museums communication and posters. [ re-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Kaio
typefaces.desc: Kaio a new family of humanist-inspired sans serif fonts. Influenced by classics like “Gill Sans” and “Antique Olive”, but with a contemporary twist. It takes its name from Master Kaio (KingKai or Kaiō-sama) of Dragon Ball Z, who embodies wisdom and power, but is also zany and grotesque. The generous and piquant shapes of the font evoke the character’s personality. Available in 6 weights and a Display version, with more extreme shapes and round counter-forms, called “Krilin”. [ lift-type.fr ]

typefaces.name: Kalev
typefaces.desc: Kalev covers Latin, Cyrillic and Georgian and is designed for use in running text, display, logos and headlines. It is a take on the architectural idealism of twentieth century Estonian sans serif type. Georgian script is included in Kalev as a nod to the mutual affection between Estonia and Georgia. The lighter weights of Kalev are sleek, formal and confident, without novelty or decoration. While, the heavy weights take reference from later photo-type interpretations of geometric types like. These bolder styles are tightly packed while the terminals open up, reducing the relative width of certain letters making these heavy weights great for logos and headlines. For variety, the weight names are in Estonian and in-translation are impressionistic takes on body weight – Vormis (Normal), Musklis (Medium), Turske (Semibold), Paks (Bold), Tais (X Bold), Kogukas (Ultra). [ eastofrome.com ]

typefaces.name: Kante
typefaces.desc: Kante (german for edge) tries to be a balancing between digital and human forms. [ type.design ]

typefaces.name: Kanton Gothic
typefaces.desc: Inspired by the work of Morris Fuller Benton.

typefaces.name: Karl
typefaces.desc: Karl Ultra released in 2023. Italics added in May 2025. Karl Mono, available in a single weight and originally a separate release, was folded into the Karl family.

typefaces.name: Karloff Neutral
typefaces.desc: Karloff Neutral is an interpolation of two diametrically opposite styles, one capturing the idea of beauty (Karloff Positive) and the other expressing the idea of ugliness (reversed-contrast Karloff Negative), producing a surprisingly neutral, low-contrast typewriter typeface.

typefaces.name: Kicker
typefaces.desc: Kicker is designed to be layered. Mix and match the various thicknesses to create outlines, inlines, and double inlines. The variable font gives you even more variety, with the ability to fine tune the line thicknesses. Kicker was originally designed for Design Week Portland, back in 2012. The city’s wealth of neon signs, such as the Roseway Theater served as the initial inspiration. A sporty flair was brought in to highlight the friendly competition side of the design community. [ vectrotype.com ] Released in 2018 through Future Fonts, from which it graduated in 2019.

typefaces.name: Kiperman
typefaces.desc: Kiperman is a text typeface designed in honor of Henrique Leão Kiperman, founder of the publishing house Artmed, now Grupo A. The inspiration for the design came from the personality of the honoree. Just as Henrique always wanted to stay away from spotlights, the Kiperman typeface was designed so that it would not call attention to itself or impose any obstacles in the understanding of the text. In this way, the fonts revere Henrique’s legacy by respecting and honoring the published content. Its forms are simple and straightforward, with no unnecessary embellishments that could disturb the reading. The fonts are slightly narrower than normal, which yields higher efficiency without compromising reading comfort. Besides that, its italics are not just a slanted version of the romans, but rather a separate drawing. With a slope of 8°, its calligraphic structure provides the right amount of emphasis when necessary. The Kiperman type family has been commissioned by Grupo A and is available for licensing from Harbor Type. This was the way found for the fonts to be read by more people, spreading some of his spirit around the world. Available in four styles.

typefaces.name: Kleber
typefaces.desc: A display typeface extrapolated from type used for a 1960s magazine ad, later identified as Paul Renner’s Futura Display (1932).

typefaces.name: Kobe
typefaces.desc: Kobe is our new classic. First released as a one-weight font in 2018, it quickly became a house favorite: its straight-forward, well-proportioned modular structure made it as usable in text as its playful terminals and many alternates made it fit for display versions. Kobe is versatile yet timeless, which is why it defines the studio so well and is often present in our communication. The numerous ligatures and stylistic sets take inspiration from Japanese writing shapes. The regular version has just undergone a subtle makeover and now exists in 5 additional weights, perfect for text. The daring slant of its oblique makes the letters stand out in large paragraphs and is a clear testimony of our studio’s quirky approach at designing fonts. [ vj-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Kolding
typefaces.desc: Appears to be retired as of January 2025.

typefaces.name: Komuna
typefaces.desc: A fixed-width dot matrix typeface produced as a variable font.

typefaces.name: Kopius
typefaces.desc: The Kopius family is a contemporary serif type that features friendly characteristics with round, open counters conveying a relaxed ambiance. The robustness of the characters supports a wide variety of applications including editorial and display use. The uniquely defined glyph construction and serif shapes convey an allusion to a brush stroke that bestows a texture-rich appearance entirely in tune with functionality. The top and bottom slightly curved stems help the flow of the reading direction. Kopius is an exuberant family with a multifaceted repertoire. The upbeat type comes with a multitude of weights to satisfy any fanciful appetite for a colorful typographic palette. With packaging solutions in mind the family includes sets of expandable and combinable box heading material for a boundless range of adjusted composites. In addition, pertinent labels, weight-adjusted arrows, and word logos complete the Kopius family. OpenType provides advanced layout features including figure sets, small caps, fractions, and more. Herbert Thannhaeuser’s Liberta, an Antiqua type family designed for the East German type foundry VEB Typoart between the middle to end 1950s, has stirred the initial

typefaces.name: Kornel
typefaces.desc: Kornel is a seriffed type family designed for long texts. Its confident appearance derives from classic proportions and sharp details, both of which allow excellent performances for print and web. With the design priority of producing texts with a harmonious rhythm, inspiration for Kornel came from Renaissance typography in general, rather than any specific typeface. Treatment of terminals and diagonal strokes produce a distinguished contemporary twist and the gently slanted Italics are the perfect complement to the Roman. Sharp entry and exit strokes and oblique strokes of the Italics make for the simplified shapes of letters such as R, K, k, v, x, y, w. Produced in seven weights across upright and italics.

typefaces.name: Kotik
typefaces.desc: Kotik is a handmade sans with a bold personality—created for both text and display. It’s authentic yet modern, offering a fresh, playful twist on the classic sans aesthetic. Designed for the digital age, Kotik thrives in social media, branding, and beyond—striking the perfect balance between character and versatility. If you’re drawn to the clean appeal of Helvetica but want something with a little more charm, Kotik is ready to play. [ inhousetype.com ]

typefaces.name: Kranto
typefaces.desc: Kranto, a sans serif superfamily composed of 144 fonts designed by Ramiro Espinoza, draws inspiration from a group of mainly British and German grotesque typefaces from the first half of the twentieth century. Its three subfamilies—Kranto Normal, SemiCond, and Condensed—grow progressively narrower. Each subfamily comes in seven weights, from Thin to Black—and, for maximum typesetting and typographic flexibility, each weight is available in three different x-heights: Text, Normal, and Display. Brimming with subtly original design details, Kranto is a solid, trustworthy, and readable typeface that strives for objectivity and neutrality. Its unassuming nature makes Kranto an ideal choice not only for a broad assortment of corporate, editorial, and digital jobs, but also for environmental uses like signage and wayfinding systems. [ re-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Krasz
typefaces.desc: Italics added in June 2025.

typefaces.name: Krata
typefaces.desc: A titling typeface comprised of overlapped horizontal and vertical lines, inspired by Karl Gerstner’s Designing Programmes and Donald Knuth’s Metafont. Produced as a variable font with a weight axis.

typefaces.name: Krul
typefaces.desc: ‘Krul’ is a typographic interpretation of the lettering style created by Dutch letter painter Jan Willem Joseph Visser at the end of the 1940s, which decorated the traditional brown bars of Amsterdam. In the beginning, these letters were strongly associated with the pubs connected to the Amstel brewery. In the 1970s and 1980s, Leo Beukeboom, another talented letter painter, continued and expanded this lettering tradition. Conscious of the cultural issues that arise in reviving an unique style, and concerned about the speed with which the lettering style was disappearing, Ramiro Espinoza focused the project of designing ‘Krul’ on digitally recreating the calligraphic complexity of these beautiful letters. Created through several years of research, ‘Krul’ is not a direct digitization of the Amsterdamse Krulletter, but instead, an interpretation that incorporates numerous alternative characters absent in the original model, and improves upon details where necessary, resulting in an optimal performance on the printed page. The typeface is presented in Open Type format, with an abundance of intricate ligatures, fleurons, and swashes, which permit the creation of numerous calligraphic ef

typefaces.name: KTF Cirk
typefaces.desc: KTF Cirk is a free interpretation drawn after anonymous lettering found in an art exhibition catalog Світ і Молодь (World and Youth), most likely from 1985. Based on what was at hand, a private font was made to be used in the LP cover design for Alex Chumak (our friend and co-author of KTF Olivier ) band Sojuz. A simple geometric idea of crossing circles and lines and a free choice of Cyrillic letterforms (mixing upper and lowercase) for a unicase solution was an instant pleasure to work on. After its first successful use, we decided to expand it into a full release. At the end of its production, with all the drawings set, we stumbled upon its source called “Cirkulus”. It was made by Austrian designer Michael Neugebauer in 1970 for Letraset (LG118, 72pt 15.2 mm), and was used for Aretha Franklin’s 7-inch single on Atlantic Records. A Letraset catalog reveals a few similar fonts being in fashion between 1969–71: Horatio (Harry) Light, Fino, Premier Lightline, Linear, and a classic Avant Garde Gothic, a genre-defining face for layouts competing in using the thinnest possible lines. By closer examination of the mentioned cover, we spotted figures that didn’t match the original Neugeba

typefaces.name: KTF Compact
typefaces.desc: KTF Compact is simple, effective, and sparks joy. KTF Compact has been drawn based on a rare movie poster “Влюблен по Собственному Желанию”, found by Kirill Gluschenko, issued by Reklamizdat in 1982. Its further use cases were never found. Compact is a display typeface of ultimate heaviness, that exists on the edge of readability. Its shapes are mostly made of vertically set narrow rectangles of the same width, slightly rounded, and spaced most tightly. When typeset, Compact reminds on wooden blocks from the toy set, strictly arranged in lines. If you want, Compact is a typographic Roland 909: you type it, and a sequence comes into being. It takes the space and inverts it, becoming a surface. All the life then happens in black on white, or between the letters, depending on the usage. And don’t forget, it does its job perfectly only when being big, just like BelAZ in the mine. An Israeli-born designer Matan Iontef accomplished the Hebrew part of KTF Compact in 2023. He took inspiration from his research in wood type culture across Israel, adapting and remixing the found forms within the given system. Working with the script almost contradicting the nature of Compact, and accepting t

typefaces.name: KTF Jermilov
typefaces.desc: KTF Jermilov is a modular display font following the typographical practice of Kharkiv avant-garde artist and designer Vasyl Jermilov. As a representative of its era, it shares constructivist ideals of “the struggle against superfluity”, striving for universality and convenience. The font consists of two utilitarian principles: a) uppercase letters composed of limited geometric elements based on a 3x5 square grid, b) lowercase signature letter “a”. The authors' estate has been thoroughly analyzed and translated in font of two cuts (solid and stencil) with ten interchangeable stylistic sets enhancing the initial idea of a “font-constructor” and generating countless variations. This typographic style started in the 1920s as a modernist attempt of creating a universal typeface that could be easily reproduced and used by everyone with no previous experience*. It was also a follow-up of an elementary idea of a “square as a key module of art” (Malevich's suprematist manifesto) with its heralds El Lissitsky, Herbert Beyer, Joost Schmidt, and Jan Tschichold to name a few. Jermilov's letters aligned with this agenda and were used by the author throughout all his life in various printed matt

typefaces.name: KTF Metro Fonts
typefaces.desc: Echoing WWII events, in 2022 Kyiv Metro became the bomb shelter for thousands of its inhabitants. This sad fact is another big milestone in its rich history, which continues to be written. Built six decades ago, it carries 1.32 mln. passengers a day (2016) and is one of the most beautiful manmade creations in Ukraine. As part of station architecture, the letters of the Kyiv metro tell us a lot about its history. It’s a book. You can read it in many directions. Exiting on each station, you'll notice different letterings. “Look at them, analyze and make fonts on their basis”, we told to our students in our summer 2023 workshop called “Kyiv Metro Fonts”. So they did it within a week, and we took and carefully finished 5 most representative of them. The result is a family release called KTF Metro, aiming to preserve the typographic memory of the city. Additionally, Yevgen Anfalov interviewed Oleg Totsky, a metro historian. His answers open up a context in which Kyiv Metro letters emerged and supplement the showcased typefaces respectively. KTF Metro is free for Ukrainians. For the rest of the world: as Ukraine is still in the state of emergency, we'd like to ask you for a donation. Use

typefaces.name: KTF Olivier
typefaces.desc: KTF Olivier is based on a font called «Оливье» found in a book «Шрифты для художников-оформителей» («Fonts for design artists») issued in Minsk in 1979. This was a handbook for Soviet designers, featuring many fonts, most of which were drawn by the author himself, Rygor Klikushyn. Klikushyn was an outstanding figure in Belarusian art, a multifaceted man who lived a long and interesting life. He graduated from theatre school in the late 1930s, where, among other things, he taught himself to play the piano, and was then called up to the front as a cartographer and telegrapher and fought in World War II until the end, leaving behind numerous diaries that include maps of the battles he drew. After the war, he taught at the Viciebsk Institute of Art and Graphics. He was very interested in foreign art and always bought American and English magazines when possible. His daughter tells us that once he used a typewriter to reproduce a book by one of the unpopular foreign authors in the Soviet Union and gave copies to his acquaintances. At the time the typewriter was considered an ideological weapon, and Klikushyn was summoned to the KGB, accused of anti-Soviet propaganda and questioning his

typefaces.name: KTF Rublena
typefaces.desc: Rublena is the most used black grotesk on the ex-USSR terrain. It originated at the end of the XIX century in the city of Danzig (German Empire) as Zeitungs-Grotesque. Ever since this metal type was copied and distributed all around the globe in a broad variety of names and versions: Zeitungs-Grotesque, Fette Steinschrift, Breite fette Grotesque or Газетный Древній Черный to name a few. According to researcher Dr. Dan Reynolds, “it was once the protype for a heavy sans serif in German type-making.” [ typeoff.de ] Rublena is an “orphan child” of the metal type era. This type came out just one year before copyright law (“Geschmacksmustergesetz”) went into effect in 1876, which predestined the font to be bootlegged by different foundries, let alone the designer’s name remained unknown. Due to the high commercial success, some foundries cut Cyrillic versions, and the font quickly became popular in the Russian Empire. After the October Revolution of 1917, all the types were expropriated from private enterprises and became state property. According to the newly established plan-based economy, all the industries including printing and type-making were revised. Not only to save lead but al

typefaces.name: Kurversbrug
typefaces.desc: Since there is little or no true typographic expression of the ‘Amsterdam School’ of architecture, we have always felt there was a need for fonts that expressed this particular aesthetic. ‘Kurversbrug’ is a revival of the Amsterdam’s bridge letters. The original alphabet was probably designed by Anton Kurvers around 1930. Ramiro Espinoza solved many inconsistencies in the original model, completely redefined several letters, added punctuation marks, designed new weights and turned a simple alphabet into a family suitable for posters and standing flyers. [ re-type.com ] Moved to the Brutal Types catalog in 2025.

typefaces.name: Kuunari
typefaces.desc: Kuunari is a structured square sans type family of 42 fonts. It has three widths and seven weights in both upright and italic versions. The base form is a round-cornered rectangle, and this form constructs the glyphs throughout the fonts. Kuunari is a straightforward sans serif. It doesn't make any fuss about itself; it just does the job proudly and confidently. It is versatile; it can be used for titles and logos to make a statement or, more delicately, for body text and lead paragraphs. All in all, you can achieve diverse and rich typography with the Kuunari type family.

typefaces.name: KWINC Grotesk
typefaces.desc: A collaboration between New York design studio Karlssonwilker and Sudtipos. Inspired by vernacular dimensional letters found in U.S. home improvement stores, KWINC Grotesk offers a playful yet functional type experience. Its uppercase design is strikingly expressive, while the lowercase introduces an old-style aesthetic enriched with a multitude of typographic features. [ sudtipos.com ]

typefaces.name: Kyle Mono
typefaces.desc: Kyle Mono is a non proportional, monoline serif font family. It is a sibling to the font family Kyle, that changes its character with increasing weight. Kyles and Kyle Monos glyphs have sharp, triangular serifs that gain momentum as the weight grows, becoming almost slab-like. Both families have a quirky style - friendly, accessible and yet very individual, supporting legibility and expression. […] On the practical side, Kyle-Mono is great for use in coding, flight arrival displays, comparing amino acids or writing dadaist poetry. On a more expressive level, it offers us its own specific, edgy design-flavour. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Kyrios
typefaces.desc: Kyrios is a curious, slightly psychedelic blackletter family. Though it may seem like a modern idea, it is an interpretation of lettering from a grave monument carved in the late 1800s, located in Green-Wood Cemetery in Brooklyn, NY. This family is a study in contrasts – not just of thick/thin strokes, but of history and aesthetics. It pairs geometric simplicity with Art Nouveau curves and a blackletter lowercase with a Lombardic uppercase. (Also included is an alternate blackletter uppercase, which can be deployed for a more consistent appearance). [ arrowtype.com ]

typefaces.name: La Grotesque
typefaces.desc: La Grotesque is an effort to create Arabic & Latin in collaboration, like a conversation among friends, like a meal you prepare together. La Grotesque is a fun summer trip from Marseille (France) to La Marsa (Tunisia) via Marsala (Italy), celebrating the interconnectedness of the Mediterranean triangle that forms our cultural heritages. The Latin script is rooted in the warm, rounded forms of early 20th century wood type sans serifs. Maghrebi seems to follow its own rules, with letterforms and proportions varying significantly from one manuscript to the other and even within the same page in an unconventional, somehow grotesque manner. This trait parallels with the early Latin sans serif from the 20th century, allowing us to see Maghrebi as the grotesque of Arabic calligraphic styles. [ tptq-arabic.com ]

typefaces.name: Lab DJR
typefaces.desc: Lab DJR is a variable color pixel font with variable axes that lets you morph its default square element into a circle, a diamond, and a sparkle. On top of that, you can adjust their size in a variety of ways and even “split the atom” to divide each shape into four similar shapes. But the real fun comes when you mix the axes together and the outlines start to glitch out. When you use two at a time, the transformations are usually somewhat predictable, but after three or more, chaos reigns. [ djr.com ]

typefaces.name: Label
typefaces.desc: A sans serif of British inspiration. Produced in five weights, in upright and italic.

typefaces.name: Laconia Cherokee
typefaces.desc: Laconia Cherokee is an extension of the Laconia typeface for the Cherokee syllabic writing system. The design follows the humanist sans serif style of Laconia Latin, with the same weight range from thin to extra bold, with companions italics. In addition to the standard unicameral orthography characters, the fonts also include a set of lowercase syllabics as found in some historical publications and occasional modern use. A basic Latin subset is included. [ tiro.com ]

typefaces.name: Lagos
typefaces.desc: Lagos is a rough stencil design inspired by seaside signs touting boat trips photographed in Lagos, Portugal. The high stroke contrast lends it an elegance unusual in stencil designs. Lagos is part of a series exploring vernacular stencil designs from around the world that includes Las Perdidas (Peru), Kelly Twenty (UK) and Battery Park (US).

typefaces.name: Lalola
typefaces.desc: Lalola (first released as Lola in 1997) is a display typeface inspired by a lettering model found in the book Schriftschreiben Schriftzeichnen by Eugen Nerdinger and Lisa Beck. Lalola takes the few letters available from that model, as a starting point and becomes a single style typeface with strong character. [ type-o-tones.com ]

typefaces.name: Lapidar
typefaces.desc: An interpretation of Lapidar (Genzsch & Heyse, ~1874).

typefaces.name: Lasagna
typefaces.desc: Originally released by ReType in 2008, moved to the Brutal Types catalog in 2025.

typefaces.name: Laski Sans
typefaces.desc: In 2014 Paula Mastrangelo presented her first type family, Laski Slab. Over the last year, Ramiro Espinoza worked to expand the system and the outcome was Laski Sans, a refined humanistic sans addressing many of today’s design requirements, specifically optimized for editorial and corporate use. Laski Sans is a family of 20 fonts with weights finely balanced so that they can be easily combined in a wide range of environments. Its open forms and solid structure grant a high legibility on paper and on screen. The moderate, legible proportions and neutral appearance make Laski Sans especially well suited for commercial publications like marketing collateral and advertising campaigns. The type’s generally reserved tone opens up in 2 showy stencil variants – Stencil Black & Stencil Black Italic – which considerably expand Laski’s creative potential for expressive headlines. [ re-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Laski Slab
typefaces.desc: Laski Slab is a comprehensive suite of 20 fonts conceived for editorial purposes. The type family was designed by Paula Mastrangelo, an Art Director with extensive experience in editorial design specialized in corporate communication. Originally developed for an online children’s magazine, Laski was expanded into a multipurpose type family with the technical assistance of Ramiro Espinoza. Belying the intrinsic robustness of the slab serif genre, Laski’s humanistic construction and subtle calligraphic details lend it a friendly appearance. Round, open letter forms and generous horizontal proportions make it easy to read. The regular weights perform impeccably in text sizes, while the bolder versions produce expressive and very effective subheadings and headlines. Two idiosyncratic stencil variants considerably expand Laski’s creative potential. […] Laski Slab received a “Certificate of Excellence” at the 2014 Tipos Latinos Biennale. [ re-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Lavigne Nova
typefaces.desc: Lavigne is a type-family aimed at publications such as interior design and women magazines – anywhere a touch of distinction is to be desired. In the opinion of its designer, glossy magazines have been setting the same type families for years, with only a small group of fonts being used to denote refinement and sophistication. So the philosophy behind the Lavigne type family is to achieve the refinements observed in classic ‘modern serif’ typefaces, without borrowing too much from history. [ re-type.com ] Originally released as Lavigne , expanded and renamed (in 2024?) to Lavigne Nova .

typefaces.name: Lavishe
typefaces.desc: Lavishe is a dedication that was polished to fill in the Vietnamese's type library, which doesn't have many glyphic/incised choices or uses. It blends traditional details from the Roman, carved letters into a contemporary touch. Along with the flourish serif, the lowercase terminal was distinctively curved to give a calm, organic texture. When researched Vietnamese typography in the past, I realized how few times glyphic serifs are used or created. The examples discovered were just some versions of Friz Quadrata, Albertus,... Now, back in the modern-day, we have more fonts, but if prioritize the "Made in Vietnam" tag, there's still a lot of room. That's why Lavishe was delivered to give one more option for Vietnamese designers. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: LD Elly
typefaces.desc: LD Elly was designed by Bente Baseler as part of her MA Type Design studies at the University of Reading. The transitional type family is a friendly, calm and clean multi-script font family for continuous text setting in literature and editorial surroundings. LD Elly is named after Bente’s great grandmother, Elisabeth, who lived in Bavaria. She gives this typeface her character and attitude: stable serifs connected to the baseline, almost straight stems meet connecting strokes with contrast, and subtle elegance. [ lazydogs.de ]

typefaces.name: League Gothic
typefaces.desc: A revival of Alternate Gothic #1 by Morris Fuller Benton.

typefaces.name: Lentiform
typefaces.desc: Lentiform is a Lombardic for supporting text, contrasting convex curves with angular cuts, and spiky serifs with curling ball terminals. It was inspired by a plaque that I encountered at the Leeds Industrial Museum. I was struck by how the Lombardic on that plaque offered a lowkey blast of flavor for small headings, setting itself apart while not drawing undue attention. [ djr.com ]

typefaces.name: Leopardo
typefaces.desc: Leopardo, designed by Alexandre Bassi, draws inspiration from rich chancery models created by writing masters of the 16th and 17th centuries, offering a boldly contemporary interpretation. Alexandre Bassi developed a deep fascination for these calligraphic models, captivated by the complexity and freedom of their shapes, sometimes pushing them to the limits of exuberance. Originally drawn with thin nibs and engraved on copper, these works significantly affected the initial sketches of Round hand script. Leopardo takes its name from the writing manual De caratteri di Leopardo Antonozzi, which greatly influenced the type designer. Leopardo captures the vitality of the calligraphic gesture while maintaining the stability and coherence of a typographic system. The design reveals a rich variety of details, characterized by a quick ductus, pronounced contrast, sharp terminals, and recurring drops, which liven up the typographic colour. [ 205.tf ]

typefaces.name: Letters
typefaces.desc: Released by Velvetyne in May 2025.

typefaces.name: Lettra Mono
typefaces.desc: Lettra is a monospaced serif typeface that explores the design challenges of modular spacing, with each character individually crafted to ensure consistent weight and proportion across the set. The design draws inspiration from the classic aesthetics of serif typewriter fonts and the detailed classifications seen in botanical drawings.
