Its round and generous shapes offer a counterweight to the technical tone of fixed-width characters. [ ma-ma-type.com ] Originally designed in 2013 and made available when the foundry launched.

typefaces.name: Pahin
typefaces.desc: Pahin is an expressive flared serif that combines sharp forms with intricate contours. Its plasticity is inspired by the graceful curves of stems and flowers, creating vibrant and organic forms. Sharp elements contrast with soft and flowing lines, reminiscent of thorny thorns protecting delicate flowers or fruits. At the same time, Pahin inherits and is based on the tradition of calligraphy. The name of the typeface comes from the Ukrainian word «Пагін», which means “plant shoot”. [ blazetype.eu ] Expanded in August 2024 to three optical sizes. Available as a variable font with three axes (weight, optical size, and italic).

typefaces.name: Pantasia
typefaces.desc: Pantasia is a monospaced counterpart to Times New Roman. Times New Roman is one of the world’s most ubiquitous typefaces, conceived in 1931 by Stanley Morison in collaboration with Victor Lardent and perhaps William Starling Burgess for British newspaper ‘The Times’. Pantasia is roughly based on the ‘Wide 427’ cut of Times New Roman which was first issued in 1938 and intended as an ‘uncondensed’ version for book printing. The creation of Pantasia was motivated by my passionate interest in Times New Roman, and was drawn as a means to understand Times’ proportion, rhythms as well as a way to study the essence of its ‘Timesness’ beyond its association as a ubiquitous and default typeface. Pantasia is named after a bakery in ‘Yakitate!! Japan’, the anime I was watching when I first started drawing Pantasia in Berlin in 2016. Italic and other widths and rhythms of Pantasia are forthcoming. [ counter-forms.com ]

typefaces.name: Paquito
typefaces.desc: Appears to be retired as of 2025.

typefaces.name: Paragraf
typefaces.desc: Paragraf is a serif typeface with high-waisted structures, a tall x-height, and slightly narrow proportions. Its clean, straight lines and sharp details establish a clear, rational personality. The design features geometric simplicity, evident in elements like the rectangular and parallelogram-shaped terminals of the ‘r’ and the tails of the ‘y.’ The bottom serifs on letters such as ‘a,’ ‘d,’ and ‘u’ reflect this geometric foundation. Details like the tail of ‘Q,’ the legs of ‘R,’ ‘K,’ and ‘k,’ and the ear of ‘g’ showcase crisp, structured forms that reinforce its refined aesthetic. Horizontally and vertically cut terminals, seen in ‘c,’ ‘e,’ and ‘t,’ add a sharp, confident finish, while the 90-degree bracketed serifs, with smooth curves transitioning into the main strokes, achieve a balance between modern precision and classic elegance. Ideal for editorial design, Paragraf is also a strong choice as a brand font, offering a unique personality. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Paramount
typefaces.desc: Paramount is a study in humanist geometry. The typeface family begins with a rational, grounded tone, from which neofuturistic branches emerge. While ahistorical in nature, Paramount balances forward-looking atmospheres with the legacy of iconic, pseudogeometrical typefaces like Bauhaus . [ productiontype.com ]

typefaces.name: Parch
typefaces.desc: Parch is a variable type family designed by Kel Troughton, based on the deterioration of vinyl signs in the California sunshine. This type family was created in reverse, leaving behind letterforms in the negative space. Parch is an unicase and uniwidth design made with a few simple building blocks. These building blocks give Parch a distinct and rigid feel in the regular weight, and allows the variable font to morph as those blocks change shape. It was designed to use in reverse with a decaying variable axis, with the lightest and heaviest weights showing the most deterioration. [ store.overlaptype.com ]

typefaces.name: Parque Chas ht
typefaces.desc: Unreleased as of 2025.

typefaces.name: Parsimonia
typefaces.desc: Initially designed during the lockdown period caused by the COVID-19 health crisis, Parsimonia is inspired by the shapes of Romanesque letters to achieve an aesthetic and decorative purpose, where legibility and conventional letterforms were set aside to prioritize the final design’s shape. Parsimonia is a unicase, versatile, and variable typeface that ranges from light to bold weights. [ rubenprol.gal ]

typefaces.name: Pearl
typefaces.desc: Pearl wanted to be a micro from its first badly-drawn letter. I was reading Fred Smeijers at the time; He introduced me to Pierre Haultin’s body of hastily cut romans and as a point of contrast put up the rationale behind Linotype’s “Legibility Group” or Matthew Carter’s Verdana: Text for small sizes needs a loose fit, room to breathe. ‘But does it?’ Fred counters. With the first twenty or so letters of my stripling italic I was off to find out. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Peasy
typefaces.desc: Peasy is a friendly, modern sans serif typeface, designed for extended reading and medium-sized display settings. It is well balanced, low-contrast, and has a neutral but refreshing personality with a gestural, soft quality. Peasy has open apertures and stroke endings paired with a comfortable x-height for the lowercase and works well both in print and on screen. [ delvefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Péix
typefaces.desc: Peix is a variable display font named phonetically after the pixel unit (px). Peix's first iterations were carried out as a part of a master's degree diploma in graphic design. It has since been revised, completed and corrected. Its condensed look and serifs set it apart from the more classic pixel fonts. Peix was made by and for experimenting with type. Feel free to stretch, displace, distort and destroy it, mess around with all the possibilities given by its four variable axes (round, black, long and void), beyond legibility. Its extended set of miscellaneous icons, symbols, circled & squared numerals and ligatures makes it even more easy and satisfying to play with. [ entravaux.framer.website ]

typefaces.name: Pelikan
typefaces.desc: Pelikan is an unpolished sans with a special unicase feature baked inside, which lets you extend all letters—big or small—to the same height. Modernists in the 1920s waged a “fight against capital letters,” writing all their messages strictly in lowercase characters. In the ’70s, the search for an “egalitarian” type treatment continued, leading designers to the short-lived concept of the unicase. Pelikan throws a same height party for the 21st Century with its raw and blunt yet approachable feel. Its unusually large x-height gives it a confident stance and presence. Pelikan has two unicase features available via Stylistic Sets, letting you jump between the default look and our same height variations. Unicase 1 is uppercase heavy, with only a few lowercase letterforms sprinkled in. This setting feels solid and sturdy in text blocks. Unicase 2, on the other hand, is jumbled and playful, a happy mismatch of uppercase and lowercase forms of the same height. [ abcdinamo.com ]

typefaces.name: Pennsylvania
typefaces.desc: Living in Pittsburgh in the 1990s, Christian Schwartz registered the industrial grit in the forms of capitals and numbers on license plates in Pennsylvania—the rhythms of vertical and horizontal alignment without implications of typewriter or lineprinter. His monospaced interpretation appeared in 2000. Using Schwartz’s early 2000s sketches for a planned expansion as a jumping off point, Inga Plönnigs revisited the family in 2024, devising both a soft-edged sans and slab from the eccentric approach to serifs found in the stamped-metal inspiration. [ vault.commercialtype.com ] Originally released with Font Bureau in 2000.

typefaces.name: Perforat
typefaces.desc: Perforat is a typeface inspired by hardboard pegboard and perforated hardwood boards. This typeface doesn't have any spacing so every letter connects to the other, creating unique word strips. It is functional at very small sizes and experimental and playful at large scale. Designed by Jacob Grönbech Jensen and Nazareno Crea, Perforat is a small family of two: regular and wide, with the italics styles in the works. [ abc-etc.com ]

typefaces.name: Performa
typefaces.desc: Meet Performa, a versatile sans-serif font family that seamlessly unites the structured aesthetics of geometric typefaces with the subtle sophistication of grotesque designs. [ rsztype.com ]

typefaces.name: Peridia
typefaces.desc: Peridia is a mycelian display serif named after the Gasteroid, a puffy variety of fungi. With expressive caps and organic curves, its bold proportions and tight spacing allow for playful and mycelian interconnections between letters and character itself. As organic as mycelium, the x-height varies depending on characters and displays a unique ligature set. [ entravaux.framer.website ]

typefaces.name: Persona
typefaces.desc: Persona is a display sans serif based on Hans Möhring’s Florida (c. 1931) – best known for its appearance in Ingmar Bergman’s film titles – and inspired by Renaissance letterforms characteristic of the Florentine architecture, painting and sculpture of the fifteenth century. [ abyme.net ]

typefaces.name: Pétanque
typefaces.desc: What happens if you replace a ball terminal with a sport ball? Pétanque is a display sans serif with rational geometry and irrational pizzazz. Its distinctive feature is to play with the exact same circle on lowercase and uppercase letters, as well as on diacritic and punctuation marks. Inspired by the early experimental stages of Fat Faces (Robert Thorne & William Thorowgood circa 1820), Pétanque characters are drawn so all the balls can fit in a fun yet judicious way. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Petit Frère
typefaces.desc: Petit Frère is a surprising duo, of both rivals and accomplices. It is the quiet sibling to some more outspoken designs from the Plain Form catalogue. Distilled from these sources, namely Grandmaster for the Narrow cuts and Nostra Sett for the Wide, Petit Frère proposes the two extremes of a centerless design space, two takes on the sans-serif genre meant to complement each other. [ plain-form.com ]

typefaces.name: PF Centura
typefaces.desc: The evolution of typefaces has always been shaped by practical needs and aesthetic desires. Two notable 19th-century styles, Clarendon and Antique, illustrate this dynamic. Clarendons, with their bracketed serifs and moderate stroke contrast, were decorative and impactful, ideal for posters and headlines. However, their softer forms lacked legibility at smaller sizes and durability for industrial printing demands. Antique typefaces, also known as Slab Serifs, emerged as a functional response. Featuring unbracketed, blocky serifs and low stroke contrast, they were sturdier, highly legible, and better suited for rough printing conditions. Their bold, geometric design reflected the Industrial Revolution’s utilitarian values, offering versatility for both display and text uses. While Clarendons brought elegance, Antiques prioritized functionality and durability. This legacy inspired the creation of PF Centura, a variable typeface that reimagines these classic styles for modern use. An early version of PF Centura was introduced in 1999 as Centura 3D, a two-style 3D design showcasing its innovative potential. This version, now part of the Archive collection, laid the groundwork for the c

typefaces.name: PF Centura 3D
typefaces.desc: Created at a time when no magic 3D filters were around for font editors and all was done by hand, PF Centura-3D is a slab-serif typeface with a balanced, forceful attitude. Designed circa 1998 whilst experimenting with italics for Clarendon, and inspired by the iconic Rolling Stone magazine logo design of the era, the typeface’s memorable design is boldly providing results when visual brevity is a demand. Ideal for branding projects and updated to avoid feeling dated, PF Centura-3D meets the wide-ranging modern needs of design practitioners who opt for type that reminisces typography’s hand-crafted roots. Supports Latin and Greek. [ parachutefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Phlegm
typefaces.desc: Informed by American typography of the 1970s, in particular Ed Benguiat’s ITC Benguiat.

typefaces.name: Phonk
typefaces.desc: This typeface draws inspiration from J.M. Bergling’s untitled “modern alphabet” featured in his Art Alphabets and Lettering (1914). The Phonk typeface family features a sharp design with Contextual Swashes and Multiple Alternates. It will be available in seven weights, each accompanied by italic styles. [ instagram.com ] We discovered the work of Chicago-based designer J. M. Bergling (1866-1933) and our interest into the fine balance existing between the decorative / Art Nouveau aesthetic and something that would feel almost futuristic kept growing. We were also inspired by underground and alternative press from different protest and countercultural movement and thought that all of those influences could be brought together and lo create a type family. That's how the Phonk project started. [Yearbook of Type #7]

typefaces.name: Piegraf
typefaces.desc: Piegraf is a dangerously geometric font family meant for the world's boldest headlines. Despite its strict reliance on circles and squares, Piegraf features just enough legibility and warmth to save it from being reduced to a novelty. Piegraf was inspired by a handful of vintage geometric fonts that all mined similar territory. Some specific examples include Peter Steiner's Black Body (1973) and Black Pepper (1972), Charles Papirtis' Pink Mouse (1970) and Albert Boton's Black Boton (1970). All of these typefaces featured simplified, chunky outlines that delighted in reducing letters to their simplest forms. In many cases, doing away with counters all together. Piegraf lands somewhere in between a "Bauhaus" style geometric sans and a simplified, "Pacman" style font. There are even a few OpenType Alternates to experiment with (try it out below). For added versatility, an Italic weight is also available. [ centraltype.com ]

typefaces.name: Piet
typefaces.desc: Inspired by Finnish license plates.

typefaces.name: Pilot [VJ Type]
typefaces.desc: Pilot might just be a font for devoted fashion enthusiasts. This font was born from the desire to create a contemporary extended typeface of undeniable elegance. We picture it perfectly fitting into fashion editorials and photo shoots. But there’s no way it’s a one-season wonder : Pilot was designed to stand the test of time. Like timeless wardrobe staples, every detail has been carefully designed to achieve a high sense of balance, equally blending both feminine and masculine accents. The roman style embodies Pilot’s stately side: mature, elegant, and forward-thinking. The italic, on the other hand, is more experimental, even boldly expressive. In fact, this is our first deep dive into italic design—and we didn’t hold back. […] It combines angular, pointed ends with smooth, comfortable curves and fluid transitions in the diagonals. [ vj-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Pilsner
typefaces.desc: Sitting in a Paris cafe with a bottle of beer, Tobias Frere-Jones gave his attention to the label. It was set in a roman design wearing blackletter-like clothes, probably to suggest an origin in Alsace or points to the East. Unable to forget the design, with its blocky, straight line emphasis, Tobias designed Pilsner, an exercise in straight lines in an angle-centered scheme. Pilsner offers a truly adventurous typographic texture. [ store.typenetwork.com ] Originally released by Font Bureau in 1995 and moved to Frere–Jones Type in 2020 [ fontsinuse.com ], available through Type Network and added to the foundry’s website in December 2024.

typefaces.name: Pim
typefaces.desc: https://boldmonday.moosend.com/show_campaign/6c16acf6-9de3-41e8-9ddf-910263446147/4dd6606f-2dfc-67bb-52d2-7ee063e24520/ https://page-online.de/typografie/be-happy-be-pim/

typefaces.name: Pincar
typefaces.desc: The origins of Pincar represent an exercise in writing with unconventional tools—in this case, tweezers were modified to leave a trace of ink on paper. The resulting strokes unexpectedly overlapped in different ways, creating dramatic dynamics amidst the various rounds and flats. You can tell that it stemmed from the art of calligraphy, but it deviates from any well-established rules when it comes to writing. [ hottype.co ]

typefaces.name: Ping Round
typefaces.desc: Also released by TPTQ Arabic in 2025.

typefaces.name: Pitch
typefaces.desc: Pitch is a love letter to the typewriter. A typewriter has a singular purpose: putting letters onto a page. Put the paper in, stab away at the keys and letters instantly appear. It’s tactile, analogue, immediate. Pitch captures this aesthetic atmosphere: it’s a synthesis of digital and analogue that evokes — not emulates — typewritten text.

typefaces.name: Pivot Grotesk
typefaces.desc: A subtly modulated grotesque sans serif, NN Pivot Grotesk draws inspiration from two key visual principles: the radiation lines seen in timekeeping and walking, and the logarithmic spiral found in hand movements and the Milky Way’s rotation [ nouvellenoire.ch ]. Originally designed in 2020 for Theater Basel and released as a retail typeface in 2024.

typefaces.name: Piz Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Piz Grotesk is a modern reinterpretation of mid-century Swiss typography, inspired by the sharp beauty of glaciers. It blends technical precision with a unique character and is optimized for readability and complex technical work. [ serpentype.com ]

typefaces.name: Place
typefaces.desc: For our first release by French designer Julien Priez, we asked him to draw a wide serif typeface focusing on beauty and elegance. We thought this open-ended brief would perfectly suit his ability to look forward and create wildly inventive shapes while tapping into his deep historical knowledge of drawn, carved, and written letterforms. The result is Place, a display typeface for all sizes with both roman and blackletter capitals, and a particular talent for setting logotypes. [ commercialtype.com ]

typefaces.name: Plakaty
typefaces.desc: Plakaty is originally designed / showcased somewhere in the 50’s in the last century, in 1995 we digitized the main characters of the font. We completed the font in 2012. The font is inspired on the old wooden ‘biljetletters’ we found in an old typespecimen called ‘Arti letterboek’, typefaces designed by M. Meijer, former chief-draughtsman at De Bijenkorf Amsterdam, published by Uitgeverij Arti, Alkmaar. It can be considered as a homage to the anonymous typefaces we know from old printers before the offset era.

typefaces.name: Plasmid
typefaces.desc: Plasmid is a font inspired by mitosis [ daytonamess.com ]

typefaces.name: Play Extra
typefaces.desc: Play Extra began as a revival of “ Breite Fette Information ” and its genre of extra wide typefaces for titles and advertisement. In search for even more pronounced proportions, Play Extra developed into a variable font with a controllable “Stretch” axis. Play Extra takes up the idea of Adrian Frutiger’s concept for Icone and offers all the possibilities of a horizontally stretched font. By using variable font technology and a precise design with straight lines between the curves to maintain the original boxy character, Play Extra always retains its proper typographic expression. [ outofthedark.swiss ]

typefaces.name: Playfair
typefaces.desc: Produced as a variable font with three axes. Available as open-source on GitHub .

typefaces.name: Ploquine
typefaces.desc: A slab serif for editorial use, based on historical wood type designs. Produced in seven weights in upright and italic, as well as a pair of variable fonts with a weight axis.

typefaces.name: Plumbago
typefaces.desc: Plumbago prioritizes graphic form over typographic convention, with organic octagonal shapes fitted to a monospaced grid. A spirit of wide-eyed enthusiasm emerges from tapered strokes, sporadic sprawling slab serifs, an ample x-height, and unexpected structures that somehow feel completely at home. It’s a funky composition: within its rigid measured beat, each character has its own dynamic movement, with ovoid curves butting up against straight boundaries. Plumbago was originally commissioned by UnderConsideration as part of the identity system for Brand New Conference 2024, taking inspiration from Salt Lake City’s strict street grid and the style of lettering used for the streetcars that once ran on it. Currently encompassing a range of widths in one weight, the in-progress family has room for planned growth. [ xyztype.com ]

typefaces.name: Pointyhead
typefaces.desc: This thorny, spikey thing; this sharp and brutal collection of shards: it just about belongs to a large family of designs known as Blackletter. One wonders what people might do with these letters, maybe Norwegian Beard Metal or strong Czech beer will have need of their communicative skills. Fetish wear is another possibility. I wanted to have an O with serifs and I am delighted with the result. It has a second set of capitals, still sharp but less ornate and altogether more Roman. [ shapesforcash.com ]

typefaces.name: Polka
typefaces.desc: Polka is a re-interpretation of a character designed by Estonian typographer Villu Toots in 1972. It was found in a book he published called “Kirjakunsti abc” (meaning “Calligraphy abc”) part of a collection of sereval type specimen. The font was described by the author like this: “Because of the contrast in the letters, it resembles an antique. Suitable for advertising and propaganda tools and for use in consumer graphics”. This alphabet is also very close to Eugene Nerdinger’s grotesque typeface and seems to be a proper revival of the German designer's font as Nerdinger version is older. Toots developed several weight for this font, taking liberties and accentuating certain elements of identity in relation to Nerdinger's versions. Polka is even bolder than Villu Toots's boldest version, keeping some irregularities within the weight distribution and proportions. The x-height is voluntary pretty big, that’s how I like to use it, with a very small leading and spacing to make the silhouette of the text very compact and bold. [ eliottgrunewald.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Polliwog
typefaces.desc: Polliwog’s Art Nouveau-style capitals are inspired by the work of German artist Max Joseph Gradl. Rather than adopting the oranmental excess of Gradl’s original, this typeface suggests that all you need is a single drop of that proto-psychedelic Jugendstil energy to create a compelling rhythm. Intended for short bursts of novelty text, Polliwog juxtaposes straight stems with broad, swooping curves that flatten out abruptly as they hit the tops and bottoms of letters. This creates a clumping in weight that is echoed by the softened and tapered stroke endings, giving a lively wobble to an otherwise-skeletal design. [ djr.com ]

typefaces.name: Pompeji
typefaces.desc: Pompeji is inspired by the Pompeian Graffiti. Properties, forms and emotions of the graffiti translated into a contemporary context. Their accuracy and pointed shapes also indicate the use of the stylus and the act of scratching. At that time, these graffiti were scratched into walls with a pointed object. This is taken up again by the fine stroke width in Pompeji. It is geometrically constructed and at the same time odd and fluid. The main features of the font are its static and line-like attitude with breaks in ascenders and descenders and the many connections that can be made with neighboring letters. In addition, the numerous, ligatures and alternative letters create a unique typeface, as was seen in Pompeii at the time. [ skrr-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Pona
typefaces.desc: The classic-looking serif text family Pona is a free interpretation of some of the best-known serif fonts, including Times, Georgia, Plantin, Baskerville or Garamond. Its delicate letter forms possess a generous x-height and moderate contrast, so it performs well in small sizes or at low resolution. Text set in Pona has an even grey value and a warm, crunchy texture. This slightly idiosyncratic typeface reads smoothly and comfortably. Display Pona’s sister is drawn for use in large sizes. The increased contrast and the sophisticated characters shapes make this letters shine. Pona Display's lush curves lend a delicate elegance to short bursts of text and titles. [ tipografies.com ]

typefaces.name: Poolside
typefaces.desc: Poolside is inspired by popular serifs of the 80s & 90s used heavily in titles, headlines, and advertisements. Though familiar and nostalgic, certain expressive glyphs make Poolside stand out from alternatives. Whether it's for elegant editorial layouts or bold branding endeavors, Poolside rises to the occasion. The typeface's versatility shines through, proving useful for both sophisticated and edgy designs. Poolside is offered in two styles, Regular and Italic. [ doubledagger.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Poppins
typefaces.desc: Comissioned by Google Fonts and released as open-source on GitHub .

typefaces.name: Popular
typefaces.desc: Christian Schwartz drew Popular in 2004 for Robb Rice’s redesign of Popular Mechanics. Rice wanted a slab that would combine the clunky, mechanical charm of DIN with the power of Rockwell and Stymie. The family appeared in a few publications over the years before being finished for release in 2024 with help from TienMin Liao. [ vault.commercialtype.com ]

typefaces.name: Populus
typefaces.desc: This “variation on the Solperian theme” was created after the Areplos update as an attempt at a more robust monolinear counterpart. Roman capitals form the skeleton of all, even the decadent fonts we love. The goal of this experiment was playfulness based on the classics. The result is a number of alternative characters in a rich variety of cuts for wide use in visual systems. [ stormtype.com ]

typefaces.name: Porte Neue
typefaces.desc: Originally called Porte, updated in 2025 and renamed Porte Neue.

typefaces.name: Porter Sans
typefaces.desc: Porter Sans in an ultra-condensed engineered sans with an industrial pedigree. Optimized for deployments at large sizes, Porter packs a punch in a tight spot. All alphabetic characters are uniwidth — from caps to lowercase — so you can maximize your messaging in a controlled space. [ badsontype.com ]

typefaces.name: Portrait
typefaces.desc: An interpretation of French Renaissance types with triangular (Latin) serifs.

typefaces.name: Poseidon Sans
typefaces.desc: Loosely inspired by 20th century typewriter typefaces. Proportional but awkward. Designed for Darhil Crooks when he was at The Atlantic .

typefaces.name: Poster
typefaces.desc: We have subtly enhanced the family, a recreation of Didot excess, with additional styles. The following fonts comprise the family: Poster and Poster Italic, a bolder version named Poster Monster and Poster Monster Italic – a virtuoso exercise in counterforms and contrast, designed to unleash the full power of the font, as the name suggests. Poster Display, Poster Display Italic, Poster Display Monster, and Poster Display Monster Italic complete the family: four styles designed for even bigger sizes, with more contrast and visual impact. [ extratype.com ]

typefaces.name: Posthumous
typefaces.desc: Posthumous is a variable semi-connected blackletter script. It arose from a lettering sketch I was working on, just for fun—but when I started to connect the letters together and soften all of the joints, I knew it had to be a font. Of course, it quickly spiraled out of control and now includes six weights along a variable axis as well as two stylistic sets and a whole slew of OpenType features, like automatic arrows and various figure sets. [ prologuetype.co ]

typefaces.name: PoW Alara
typefaces.desc: PoW Alara is a wide sans serif which pays tribute to “ Pharaon ”, a slab serif published by Deberny & Peignot in the 1930s in France. In addition to its overall proportions and visible contrast, PoW Alara expresses some idiosyncracies from the roughness of 20th century slab serif fonts. It offers a hybrid mix between the expected simplicity of a sans serif typeface and old-school details like slab punctuation, symbols or quirky letter structures. The flared and enclosed terminals on open letters balance its distinct vertical contrast. [ proof-of-words.com ] Finalized in February 2025 with the addition of italic styles.

typefaces.name: PoW Covenant
typefaces.desc: PoW Covenant is a contemporary interpretation of the Scotch Roman typefaces of the early 19th century. If Scotch Roman were an intermediate stage between transitional and modern faces, PoW Covenant is “between” Display and Text. Its dry structure underlines the process of mechanization and standardization applied to text typefaces at that time. The removal of expected tear drops and the low contrast leaves only the skeletal construction to express the historical forms. The heavier weights refer more to Clarendons and slab serif typefaces, which are a continuation of this mechanization process. Italics are the contemporary counterpart to this reflection. They formally express all the simplification and construction principles of the design without any historical reference. The results are condensed and dynamic italics. [ proof-of-words.com ]

typefaces.name: PoW Covenant Mono
typefaces.desc: PoW Covenant Mono is a fixed-width companion to Pow Covenant, an interpretation of the Scotch Roman typefaces of the early 19th century. Its dry structure underlines the process of mechanization and standardization applied to text typefaces at that time. The removal of expected tear drops and its low contrast leaves only the skeletal construction to express the historical forms. In addition, the mono aspect of this sub-family interfers even more in the consistency of the typesetted texture and create unique effects. The heavier weights refer more to Clarendons and slab serif typefaces, which are a continuation of this mechanization process. Italics are the contemporary counterpart to this concept. They formally express all the simplification and construction principles of the design without historical reference. The visual paradox between a condensed italic design and the wide fixed-width makes the italics stand out in texts. [ proof-of-words.com ]

typefaces.name: PoW Garnier
typefaces.desc: PoW Garnier is formally inspired by the work of punchcutter Joan M. Fleischmann, and its digital adaptations. It has been completely redesigned to fit the width and proportions of Times New Roman, one of the most widely used typefaces. The adaptation to this familiar proportions is bringing new stylistic solutions and evolutions to Fleishmann’s shapes. PoW Garnier is designed to typeset long text. Nevertheless it is not without offering character with its forked serifs and exuberant details. Echoing the Paris Opéra Garnier, from which its name is taken, it is an eclectic typeface that mixes and blends periods and styles with a strong Baroque influence. Intended to be both discreet and present, its proportions make Garnier a paradoxical synthesis of Baroque eclecticism adapted for contemporary use. [ proof-of-words.com ]

typefaces.name: PoW Limerick
typefaces.desc: PoW Limerick is a pixel font deriving from the ABCs cross-stitch charts. At the crossroads of traditional craft and technology, its letter structures are composed of variable pixels, giving each variation a special texture. PoW Limerick is an all-caps font enhanced by a full set of vignettes. Behind its naive look hides a total revised version of past century’s alphabet. This display typeface is completed and extended with a set of accents, numerals, punctuation, math symbols, and arrows. PoW Limerick is heavily ornamented with multiple combinations of ornaments and vignettes that will take you back to the rich cross-stitch universe. [ proof-of-words.com ]

typefaces.name: PoW Savon
typefaces.desc: Savon is a work in progress. It is a classic Garamond inspired typeface. In addition to a few anachronistic details present in the Regular, the fancy Italic with its generous Swashes will give it a modern and offbeat look. [ proof-of-words.com ]

typefaces.name: PP Model
typefaces.desc: Model pays tribute to the world of plastic model kits, drawing inspiration from the iconic Japanese brand Tamiya. Renowned worldwide for its highly detailed and precise assembly kits, Tamiya’s legacy serves as the foundation for this design, celebrating the meticulous art of model-making. The typeface blends nostalgia with modern precision, capturing the essence of the assembly process through its clean, modular forms and mechanical aesthetic. [ pangrampangram.com ] Finalized in February 2025.

typefaces.name: PP Museum
typefaces.desc: PP Museum is a masterfully crafted humanist sans-serif typeface, embodying the perfect blend of elegance and versatility. This remarkable typeface draws inspiration from the meticulous sketches of Optima found on aged banknotes, reinterpreted with a modern sensibility that enhances both readability and sophistication. While technically a sans-serif, Museum’s subtle terminal flares echo a glyphic quality rarely seen in contemporary type design, imbuing it with a distinct personality. Its conceptual foundation is further enriched by extensive research into the typography of vintage tomes, book covers, spines and museum-centric objects — an homage embedded in its very name. [ pangrampangram.com ]

typefaces.name: PragmataPro
typefaces.desc: A condensed monospaced typeface with no interline spacing, optimized for coding, math and engineering. Release annoucement . A variable variant was released in 2025 .

typefaces.name: PragmataPro Fraktur
typefaces.desc: A monospaced blackletter typeface, expanded from the set of math symbols in PragmataPro .

typefaces.name: Principio
typefaces.desc: Principio is a free typographic interpretation of the capitals found on the title pages of illuminated Irish and English manuscripts dating back to the 7th century. These typographic compositions, with their interwoven and ornate characters, are of breathtaking graphic richness. Among the most beautiful manuscripts that have come down to us are the Book of Durrow (664–700), the Lindisfarne Gospels (700), and the Book of Kells (Iona and Kells, 800). Principio seeks to capture the spirit of early medieval art through a geometric interpretation adapted for contemporary use. Capitals, lowercase, and small caps can be used separately or combined to create a wide variety of tones and styles. The typeface also includes an extensive set of intricate ligatures and uncial alternates, offering a rich diversity of forms to explore. [ skritur.eu ]

typefaces.name: Profane
typefaces.desc: Rooted in gothic tradition, Profane evokes a modern interpretation of 14th-century inscriptions found in the Metz Cathedral (France). Blending angularity and softness, this display typeface preserves the medieval spirit with gargoyle-like terminals and diamond-shaped counterforms while adding a melted quality with rounded serifs and gooey ligatures. A striking graphic tension that grants distinctive and expressive texture to your scriptural needs. [ flaviazim.com ]

typefaces.name: Proportional
typefaces.desc: Proportional is inspired by Alan Bartram's article "Typewriter typefaces" presented in Footnotes, issue A (2016, pp. 14–33) and the idea of proportionally spaced typewriter fonts. All characters use one of the following spacing values: 80, 160, 240, 320, 400 or 480 UPMs. The result is a typeface with a strong technical look (close to that of a monospaced typeface) but with a more balanced, semi-organic spacing. Even though Bartram refers to specific units for each letter of the latin alphabet, some changes were made so as to (a) create a more balanced result, and (b) apply the same idea on the Greek alphabet (something that hasn't been done before... as far as I am aware of).

typefaces.name: PS Times
typefaces.desc: PS Times is a reimagining of the classic Times New Roman. Designed in collaboration with Jesse Amborn to be used as Parker Studio's proprietary brand font. The typeface is packed with a range of ligatures, stylistic sets, and playful symbols. Currently produced in a single weight, with more styles planned.

typefaces.name: Psilo
typefaces.desc: Charged with the semblance of psychedelia, Psilo fearlessly flaunts shapes that defy convention — an enthralling visual odyssey! This typeface springs to life with its 'breathe' variable axis, pulsating, expanding, and contracting at the extremes, in styles 'inhale' and 'exhale'. At its base, the 'rest' style strikes a rational balance while radiating a friendly and playful vibe. The initial idea was to achieve a typeface with generously-rounded shapes that are well-suited for 3D extrusion and can survive erosion of edges, offering a delightful base for volume experimentations. Emanating both a modern and vintage allure, Psilo is a mesmerizing fusion of sinuous curves, alluding to the lettering styles of the '60s.

typefaces.name: PT Schimetrik
typefaces.desc: PT Schimetrik is a modern grotesque typeface that adapts effortlessly to both print and digital mediums. Featuring clean geometry, versatile functionality and timeless aesthetic, making PT Schimetrik an ideal choice for a wide range of design applications. [ paavolatype.com ]

typefaces.name: Pulso
typefaces.desc: Pulso was designed to withstand various printing conditions. Developed to provide durability and consistency, Pulso excels in intensive text settings, even under the most challenging circumstances. With its three grades and two sets of italics, Pulso ensures flawless performance, thanks to its generous x-height and open shapes. [ dstype.com ] The collection is comprised of four optical sizes, initially made available as early-access versions in 2024. In January 2025, it was moved to the foundry’s retail catalogue. The preview image and links for this entry refer to the text optical size.

typefaces.name: Punch
typefaces.desc: An interpretation of Miller & Richard’s News Bill series (1880s).

typefaces.name: Quadro
typefaces.desc: Quadro is a squared variable sans-serif typeface designed for exceptional versatility across a wide range of contexts. With five widths (Compressed, Narrow, Normal, Moderate, and Wide) and six weights (Thin, Light, Regular, Medium, Bold, and ExtraBold), it is ideal for various design applications from corporate communications to fashion design, retail visual identity creation to digital interfaces for mobile devices. Its clean, geometric structure ensures a powerful visual impact, whether in smaller text or large, high-visibility headlines. [[blazetype.eu]]

typefaces.name: Quasimoda
typefaces.desc: Quasimoda is the “almost fashionable” sans serif family with 11 weights and matching italics. It combines fashionable geometric forms with old-fashioned classical proportions. We designed Quasimoda so that the lighter weights give off a fresh, modern feel, the middle weights provide excellent readability and elegance for longer texts, while the boldest weights introduce a slightly antiquated flair. Partly geometric, partly grotesque, Quasimoda is a versatile beast. It follows the current fashions but does not completely give into them, retaining classical proportions and the slight ugliness of the 19th-century grotesques. With its long descenders and its small x-height, Quasimoda combines well with Renaissance serif fonts such as Garamond’s, or it can serve itself as a leading body font for longer texts, as well as a variety of branding, headline and display purposes. Quasimoda´s extended Latin character set supports more than 80 languages, a Bulgarian Cyrillic extension is already included to the character set.

typefaces.name: R41 Monza
typefaces.desc: R41 Monza is a revival of a Nebiolo series designed about 1925 — a condensed sans serif with “liberty style” echoes in certain letters. Its particular structure makes it suitable when a limited space must show text only. [ store.typenetwork.com ]

typefaces.name: Radion
typefaces.desc: An interpretation of Rudolf Koch’s geometric sans serif Kabel (Klingspor, 1927). Some glyphs with alternate forms ( G , a , e , g , w , 2 ) are given different defaults to produce the two flavors of the typeface, Radion A and Radion B , which are otherwise identical. Each flavor is produced in eight weights, in upright and italics.

typefaces.name: Raïm
typefaces.desc: Raïm is a contemporary Didone typeface designed by Valerio Monopoli . Inspired by the art of wine, Raïm features a high x-height and is available in three styles: Text, Standard, and Display, each with varying contrasts. It also features a set of ligatures, which resemble vine tendrils, adding a unique and spontaneous touch. [ lift-type.fr ]

typefaces.name: Rainer
typefaces.desc: A tightly compressed sans with ever so closed apertures, a fairly large x-height, short ascenders and even shorter descenders. The overall design is mostly subtle with infrequent outbursts of lavish peculiarities; like a rather high waist, that is featured throughout some letters as a somewhat flavourful ingredient. The overall appearance lives off its reduced character. [ vectrotype.com ] Released on Future Fonts in 2018, from which it graduated in 2021. Re-released with Vectro in 2022.

typefaces.name: Raketa
typefaces.desc: Raketa is a display sans-serif type family with a subtle 4° incline and playful, energetic letterforms. It features seven weights, ranging from the delicate Thin to the robust Black. Inspired by mid-20th-century hand lettering, Raketa’s design draws from the study of expressive calligraphic brushwork, translating its fluidity into clean, structured forms. The typeface pays homage to the masterful works of Roger Excoffon, Oscar Ogg, and Oldřich Menhart, seamlessly blending historical influences with a contemporary aesthetic. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Ramboia
typefaces.desc: Ramboia is a playful and joyful take on the French Old-Style tradition. Combining approachability with elegance, the type family of five weights is crafted entirely from loose, flowing curves, free of angles, for a smooth and relaxed feel. [ r-typography.com ]

typefaces.name: Rare
typefaces.desc: Rare is a display, single-case typeface inspired by hypnotic shapes and moods. [ carmen-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Rascal Script
typefaces.desc: Rascal Script is an exhuberant broad-brush connected script. With wild calligraphic strokes and reckless speed, Rascal brings an irreverent voice to display settings. Rascal Script’s connective architecture allows for an economy of forms. Instead of a huge suite of alternate characters, it mimics the casual rhythm of handwriting with just three ligatures – fr, fs, and tt – and an alternate lowercase s. [ abstractoffice.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Raum
typefaces.desc: Introducing Hauss & Raum, a sans-serif work-horse and experimental display duet by Justin Sloane & Huw Williams. Hauss & Raum define distinctive polarities from the purely utilitarian to the bombastically deontological–a sturdy design tool and an exercise in psychedelic retrofuturism. While Hauss is Sloane’s meticulous creation, crafted over years of trial and refinement for his own graphic design practice, Raum represents a sort of destruction–pushing the contemporaneous “display inktrap” motif into uncharted territory. [ sharptype.co ]

typefaces.name: Rawest
typefaces.desc: A geometric sans-serif.

typefaces.name: Realise
typefaces.desc: Realise Slab is a serif typeface family that refers in spirit to the Scotch Modern aesthetic in a decidedly modern and brutalist form. Sharp details meet high contrast and experimental details in minuscule. [ capitalics.wtf ]

typefaces.name: Realm
typefaces.desc: Realm is a gracefully flared typeface in seven weights. It takes inspiration in a disparate selection of old English engraved and hand-painted pieces of lettering and merges proportions based on Roman capitals with loops and flourishes borrowed from roundhand calligraphy. These elements sums up a typeface well suited for headlines while a tall x-height and large, open counters makes it a viable option for running text as well. Produced in seven upright weights.

typefaces.name: Record
typefaces.desc: How to take a contemporary look at the futuristic aesthetics of the 1980s? Record represents a balance between an update and a testimony. Not only does it take us back to a time when music was transmitted over cables and collected on shelves, it also brings this aesthetic up to date with contemporary standards of typographic design. As the process moved forward, we decided to create two distinct families: Record Laser, with its sharp, unapologetically retro-futuristic aesthetic, and Record Disc, softer, more refined and suited to a variety of applications. Certain historic fonts, ubiquitous in our cities laid the foundations of Record, specifically Antique Olive Nord by Roger Excoffon and Serpentine, by Dick Jensen. [ sharptype.co ] The sample image and the links on this entry refer to Record Laser .

typefaces.name: Recursive Sans & Mono
typefaces.desc: Started as Stephen Nixon’s thesis project at KABK TypeMedia in The Hague, released as open-source on commission by Google Fonts. Produced as a variable font with five axes: weight, slant, casual, monospace, and cursive.

typefaces.name: Redondo Ave
typefaces.desc: Redondo Ave script font is an organic, casual, yet sumptuously extra font that you can dress up or down. [ hoodzpahdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Regards
typefaces.desc: Sometimes typefaces start to mature and develop with us. In 2013, on my return from London, having been hugely impressed by the work of Edward Johnston and Eric Gill, I designed the typeface Picadilly – which was to be a kind of postcard with an afterimage record. Pretty soon some things started to bother me about it, a version appeared, new, Neue, next, 2.0.... Over these 10 years I have often returned to the form of letters we know so well from the London Underground and decided to explore it again. This time the changes have gone so far that even the name has also changed.... Regards is a kind of homage to the aesthetics of the streets of London, in which the works of the greatest masters of typography are interwoven alongside neo-Gothic architecture or Brutalist insets. The whole family has a sharp character with humanistic detail – and is accompanied by a many alternative versions of the each glyph allowing for visual experimentation. Under the creative direction of Mateusz Machalski also participated in the project: Małgorzata Bartosik, Weronika Kanigowska, Borys Kosmynka. [ capitalics.wtf ]

typefaces.name: Reiher
typefaces.desc: Reiher Headline is a type family inspired by two fonts displayed in the famous Ploos van Amstel specimen, first printed in Amsterdam in 1767. Ramiro Espinoza’s affinity for Baroque types and his desire to study their characteristics in detail were the driving forces behind this new type family. As is typical of his revivals, Reiher Headline does not faithfully follow the forms of historical sources. Espinoza made numerous updates and modifications to the design so that it would better suit the tastes and requirements of contemporary type users. The Reiher Headline romans were based on the handsome N° 1 Groote Paragon Romein, a rather condensed typeface whose punchcutter has not yet been identified. These types are almost certainly of German origin, having appeared in such seventeenth-century books as Scrutinium chimicum vitrioli [Jena, 1666] and in the 1671 specimen produced by the Anton Janson foundry in Leipzig. Reiher Headline’s italics were based on the Aszendonica attributed to Nicholas Kis that can be found in the Ploos van Amstel specimen, as well as in numerous books and catalogues printed in the Netherlands in the seventeenth century. Several of the ornaments included in t

typefaces.name: Relaate
typefaces.desc: Relaate is a multi-genre type family. It’s a group of fonts which share certain features, but each of them is much more independent and unique than you would expect from a type family. Each member of Relaate family is an individual: elegant Serif, brutal Slab and quirky tall Grotesque. They treat the family characteristics in different ways, which are more natural for each genre. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Remorker
typefaces.desc: Stencil letters happen to be a common sight on maritime vessels, and this rings particularly true in regards to “Jadrolinija”, our home country’s most famous seafaring liner. Inspired by the intricate wayfinding and warning signs painted on surfaces in and on their ships—often done off the top of one’s head, without any predefined matrix—Remorker embodies the spirit of nautical endeavors. The amalgamation of its almost raw, geometric shapes forms an unmistakable aesthetic specific to cargo and passenger transport. Still, the typeface works just as well in a broad spectrum of environments that call for an industrial look and feel. [ hottype.co ]

typefaces.name: Renotype
typefaces.desc: Renotype, designed by Radim Peško, began as a formal exercise seven years ago. The objective was to create a simple, low-contrast typeface that could serve as an archetype or mould for characters of the Latin alphabet. Based on proportions as they were developed, changed, and established over the centuries, it responds with letter shapes that are not connected to any specific epoch or tool but are instead aesthetically functional—like a bathroom. The Renotype family includes a variety of styles, going from traditional (Regular, Italic), standardised (Mono), playful (Quasitalic) or speculative (Medieval). These styles do not expand Renotype through weights but rather through the flexibility of its construction and plain character. They are establishing the narration and, at the same time, indicate more possibilities and explorations. [ 205.tf ]

typefaces.name: Renwick
typefaces.desc: Inspired by the British humanist sans serifs of the 1920s (such as Johnston Sans, Gill Sans, and Granby) Renwick is a typeface optimized for body copy at 9pt size. Its open apertures, calligraphic influenced lowercase, and generous letterspacing ensure that it’s always comfortable to read. Language support spans over 200 different languages, from Vietnamese to Greenlandic. Renwick’s book style also features a complete set of OpenType small caps—perfect for typesetting novels. [ tofutype.ca ]

typefaces.name: Resist Mono
typefaces.desc: Also distributed by Fontfabric starting April 2025.

typefaces.name: Responder P
typefaces.desc: Petr’s personal handwriting stood model for this typeface, supporting Latin, Cyrillic and Greek. The random shapes and sizes, characteristic for handwriting, are simulated by giving each character 3 alternates, sometimes clearly different and sometimes there are just subtle changes, enough for the “random feeling” of a hand written text. By default the characters are connected where possible. Use OpenType features to disable the various types of connectors. The typeface comes in an upright and slanted italic variant. [ store.typenetwork.com ]

typefaces.name: Resum
typefaces.desc: This latest font is about summarizing resolution: by a delicate dots move, resolution decreases as fat increases. Similar themes are explored with the multi-axis Harber (2023) and the modular Moki (2021).

typefaces.name: Reverie
typefaces.desc: It was a reverie in summer. Calmness, clarity, after the mists of winter and spring. A reverie in summer. Fennel flowers and sea buckthorn. Bees and butterflies. Anticipation of years, excitement. Sunlight gradually gracing trees. A choreography, rehearsed and subtle. A longing (finally satisfied). An afternoon in August. Unreal. Unexpected (despite being dreamt of many times). Lilies of the day, only blooming once, to be consumed. A reverie in summer. Fleeting and enticing. Gradients of subtle blues and greens and yellows over calm waters. Preludes of darkness. A bouquet of wildflowers, freshly picked. A reverie in summer, long gone, remembered in sweetness. Reverie is a single style monospaced typeface with floral ornaments, encapsulating the dreamlike state of summer. [ celine-hurka.com ]

typefaces.name: Revetra
typefaces.desc: Revetra is a contemporary typeface characterized by its modernist aesthetic. Its high-contrast design elements contribute to a striking visual appeal, rendering it particularly effective for display and editorial applications. While rooted in contemporary design principles, Revetra incorporates subtle retro influences, offering a unique blend of modern sophistication and timeless charm. This makes it an ideal choice for projects seeking to evoke an air of modern luxury. [ wearegradient.net ] Originally released in 2024 as a single style through the designer’s own label, reissued by Gradient in January 2025 as a four-weight family.

typefaces.name: Review Mono
typefaces.desc: Review Mono is a monospaced text typefaces well suited for editorial use. Inspired by the spirit of the classical book typeface Garamond, it offers a typewriter version with a contemporary take on the historical style. Playing with proportions to fit a strict grid system, Review Mono is an atypical typeface performing best with texts in medium to small sizes. Using exactly half of the normal monospaced glyph width, the Ultracondensed allows new exciting typesetting possibilities. [ ecal-typefaces.ch ]

typefaces.name: Revolute
typefaces.desc: Inspired by the Resolut font designed by H. Brünnel for Fonderie Nebiolo in Torino in 1937, Revolute features letterforms with clean lines and subtle curves, creating a balanced and harmonious stencil. This design reflects a timeless aesthetic, blending historical influence with modern sensibilities, making it a versatile choice for various design projects. Whether you're working on branding, signage, or any project that requires a striking display font, Revolute offers a unique blend of elegance and functionality. The stencil design, characterized by its cut-out sections, adds an element of intrigue and creativity, making it stand out from traditional solid fonts. [ rsztype.com ]

typefaces.name: Rialta
typefaces.desc: A neo-grotesque sans serif.

typefaces.name: Richmond
typefaces.desc: Matthew Carter’s Richmond is a striking serif family made for setting text in all sizes. Initially commissioned for a major daily British newspaper redesign, it has been expanded into a comprehensive family with contributions from Jill Pichotta and Richard Lipton of The Type Founders. The quietly assertive curves and ideal weight range offer countless means to invigorate editorial typography. Available in Display (Ultra Light to Ultra Black) and Text (Regular to Black) with matching Italics. [ carterandcone.com ]

typefaces.name: Rifugio
typefaces.desc: The starting point for Rifugio was coming across Nebiolo’s 407 Bastone series, a quirky wide caps-only grotesque with unusual proportions and very unsubtle traits, as if Helvetica had ventured south through the Alps and indulged in one too many Campari cocktails… Rifugio takes it from there, revisiting the bold heritage of Aldo Novarese and the vitality of the ’50s and ’60s Italian typography. High-waisted capitals and carefully crafted pseudo-naive whimsical letterforms give Rifugio its warm, charming, and distinctive personality, adding a touch of vernacular typography and backcountry signage vibes to an otherwise well-balanced functional sans. Rifugio offers a comprehensive set of weights ranging from Thin to Black—as well as a variable font format—allowing its unique personality to shine in all demanding situations. Well-equipped with a variety of OpenType features (including small caps, superiors, inferiors, four types of figures, ligatures…) and a bunch of alternates, Rifugio provides a rich typographic palette to meet the needs of contemporary design. Friendly, dynamic and charismatic, Rifugio is a dazzling fusion of Italian flair and modern flexibility which undoubtedly off

typefaces.name: Rigatoni
typefaces.desc: Rigatoni is a didone display family with exceptional readability. Based on a German mid-century lettering specimen by Nerdinger, designer Alejandro Paul expanded the face into an extensive family, with 5 weights, italics, and a 2 weights stencil version. Its tall letterforms and sturdy serifs give it a noble bearing when set in all caps; in the lower case its large x-height and spacious counters imbue it with a welcoming tone. A plethora of alternate and swash characters let you create distinctive settings for identities, labels, titles, and headlines. Use the shorter ascender and descender variants for aesthetic effects, or to prevent collisions in tightly stacked text. [ sudtipos.com ]

typefaces.name: Rigby
typefaces.desc: Updated in 2025 with a monospaced variant.

typefaces.name: Rigor
typefaces.desc: Rigor embodies the balance between neutrality and sophisticated design. We are developing this seamless typeface utilizing the latest advancements in type design technology to excel in both clarity and performance. Drawing inspiration from early 18th-century Grotesk and Antique styles, Rigor aims to blend historical significance with modern functionality. [ dstype.com ]

typefaces.name: Rimmer Pro
typefaces.desc: This is the typeface Jim Rimmer was working on before his passing in early 2010. Its working title was Dubloon, and it was intended for use in a private press edition of Robert Louis Stevenson’s Treasure Island. While undergoing cancer treatment, and upon being informed that the work on the face would be resumed by colleagues, Jim, who had never titled any of his typefaces eponymously, requested that its name be changed to Rimmer. He left us with clear guidelines for a roman with small caps, and a basic italic. Upon Canada Type’s repatriation of Jim’s work in 2012, plans were drawn up to issue this face as a two-weight family with italics, for a total of four fonts. Its production was to be part of a comprehensive remastering project of the entirety of Jim’s type work, though for practical and logistical reasons it was placed way down the queue. The remastering project proved to be quite time-consuming, taking a few detours and side turns, and the Rimmer family completion languished with it. When the work resumed on it a few years later, the family was re-envisioned in an expanded framework, with more weights and many additional features within a modern interpolation environment. T

typefaces.name: Ringi
typefaces.desc: I am using the Berlin public transport a lot, especially the Ringbahn. I have even nicknamed it, it’s not “Ringbahn”, sometimes it’s just Ringi. This typeface is inspired by the LED typeface of Berlin S-Bahn displays. I’ve been looking at it for years, and what I liked about it is the engineered and pragmatic look of it. I always felt that with just a few tweaks it could look so so much better, even within the limits of the LED grid it was stuck to. Anyway, the person – probably an engineer – who made this, inspired me to design less and be more pragmatic on this project. So, Ringi is a sans serif design whose horizontal as well as vertical strokes have the same width – a true monolinear design (although there are some few exceptions, where it was really really needed). Ringi’s (very) slanted styles are truly just slanted without any correction of the curves, matching the rest of the stoically engineered aesthetic. The font package includes a variable font, too, making every style across the slant axis accessible. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Riquet
typefaces.desc: Richard Lipton’s Riquet is a display slab serif design. Wide, round, and quirky, it was inspired by the typographic letterforms from the nineteen-twenties and early thirties flourishing in Europe, where poster design set a high creative standard. Richard expanded a handful of freehand capital and lowercase letters on posters designed by artist Ludwig Hohlwein. Riquet is a delightfully casual typeface with 6 weights and the perfect selection of alternates. All of these give an expressive look of precisely inked letters that are perfect for any packaging or branding project. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Ritualist
typefaces.desc: Ritualist by Justin Penner takes inspiration from high-contrast wedge serif designs, like the 19th century typeface De Vinne, but viewed through a macabre lens. This seriously fascinating design is defined by its infinitely sharp points, and some dangerous curves that accelerate like the edge of a blade. Occupying a surreptitious space between beauty and darkness, Ritualist is elegant, alluring, vaguely exotic, and don’t look now but it might be suspiciously watching from across the street. [ delvefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: RL Aqva
typefaces.desc: RL Aqva is a vibrant, single-style typeface designed with display use in mind. With its cheerful personality, it blends a modern graphic sensibility with historical influences, drawing inspiration from iconic humanist typefaces and the golden era of phototypesetting. It pays homage to representatives like Revue, Marvin, or ITC Busorama. The typeface features organic yet simplified forms that create a strong visual impact. This bold design language is further emphasised in the capital letters, where the asymmetric construction of characters like ‘A’ and ‘Y’ adds a playful dynamic, balanced by the forward-reaching shapes of ‘R’, ‘S’, ‘D’, and ‘B’. RL Aqva does not fear occasional overlapping characters to create dense, cohesive blocks of display text, perfect for eye-catching headlines or bold visual statements. True to its name, RL Aqva also evokes the calm and soothing presence of water. The flowing, wave-like shapes within its letterforms are inspired by the tranquillity of coastal environments, from the peaceful shores of seas and lakes to the quietude of ponds. It reflects the sense of relaxation and leisure that these natural settings offer, with its fluid lines serving as a vi

typefaces.name: RL Folklor
typefaces.desc: RL Folklor is a distinctive display typeface designed around the dynamic interplay of positive and negative space. This approach results in bold, blocky letterforms with a carved aesthetic. The balance of straight segments, curves, and cuts maintains an energetic character, embodying artisanal simplicity. Like other typefaces in the collection, such as RL Aqva and RL Limo, RL Folklor challenges the conventions of sans-serif design by borrowing influences from serif traditions. Rather than drawing inspiration from specific typefaces, it takes cues from traditional craftsmanship, particularly woodcut aesthetics. Deeply rooted in the idea of memory, RL Folklor features interconnected shapes where negative space creates both harmony and tension. Its unique personality is defined by terminals that blend a rare combination of low-contrast humanist elements with echoes of ball terminals, as seen in letters like ‘C’, ‘J’, ‘S’, ‘a’, ‘c’, and ‘s’. Additionally, sharp pinch points strategically align, visually locking characters together for a cohesive and structured appearance. This typeface is a perfect tool for creating strong typographic impressions, excelling in large sizes, as well as i

typefaces.name: RL Grot
typefaces.desc: Inspired by early 20th-century designs like Franklin Gothic by Morris Fuller Benton and Grotesk No. 9 by Eleisha Pechey, RL Grot forges its own path, pushing contrast and embracing East-European vernacular influences. With a wide weight range from Hairline to Black, RL Grot balances compact proportions and tight spacing, particularly in its heaviest weights. Distinctive features, such as the simplified base of ‘t’, the confidently stepping left stem of ‘M’, and the egg-shaped forms of ‘U’, ‘o’, and ‘0’, highlight its character. Other nuances include emphasized shoulders on ‘h’, ‘m,’ and ‘n’, as well as the weight distribution in ‘c’ and ‘e’, which soften the strong vertical rhythm typical of headline type. While RL Grot excels in headlines and large sizes, its relaxed proportions in lighter weights make it equally suitable for extended text. This typeface strikes a balance between mechanical precision and humanist warmth — maybe it’s a “halfway grotesk,” maybe that’s why it’s the Grot. [ radluka.com ]

typefaces.name: RL Limo
typefaces.desc: RL Limo is a humanist typeface that defies strict classification as a sans serif, blending sharpness and softness. Its defining feature lies in the contrast between sharp, spiky terminals and generously rounded forms seen in characters like ‘O’, ‘C’, ‘d’, ‘p’, and ‘g’. This dynamic tension between angular and curved elements creates a bold, graphic impression, particularly in its heavier weights. The family consists of six upright styles, ranging from Regular to Black, with its lighter weights suitable for paragraph text while still leaning toward display use. As the weights increase, the counters grow tighter, enhancing its dramatic, high-impact appearance. The design holds true to humanist proportions, infusing organic, curved details within the counters, while the outer shapes maintain clean, straight lines for a more structured, graphic look. Inspired by contrasts between sharp and delicate forms — like the tension in a balloon before it pops, metal cutouts, or cutting pasta with scissors — it plays with visual tension in a way that feels experimental yet rooted in tradition. While not adhering strictly to any single type model, it borrows influences from Art Nouveau typography

typefaces.name: RL Refusit
typefaces.desc: Refusit is a typeface that is based on the popular typeface Futura Black. Futura Black is a sans-serif font that was designed by Paul Renner in 1929, and it became popular for its geometric shapes and clean lines. Refusit builds upon this foundation, but introduces some key differences that make it unique. Firstly, Refusit has a slightly more condensed design than Futura Black. This means that each letter is slightly narrower, which can make it appear more compact and modern. Additionally, Refusit has some slight variations in letter shapes, particularly in the curves and angles of the characters. These variations give the typeface a more organic, hand-drawn feel, while still maintaining the clean lines and modern sensibility of Futura Black. Another key difference between Refusit and Futura Black is in the overall tone and personality of the typeface. While Futura Black has a straightforward, no-nonsense feel, Refusit has a more playful and experimental quality. This is particularly true in the bold weight of the font, where the thick strokes and exaggerated shapes can create a dynamic and energetic effect. Overall, Refusit is a typeface that builds upon the strengths of Futura Bl

typefaces.name: RL Sezon
typefaces.desc: RL Sezon is a Grotesk type family inspired by early examples of the genre, known for its flexibility and adaptability. Historically, Grotesk typefaces were loosely connected collections that could expand and evolve — a quality that Sezon embraces. Its design strikes a balance between industrial precision and mechanical warmth, making it versatile for a wide range of applications. It follows measurements taken by both ruler and eye, rather than by laser. The typeface features semi-open terminals and generous proportions, paired with fully rounded counters allowing it to perform well in large display settings and longer paragraphs. While Sezon takes cues from early Grotesks like Venus, it also incorporates modern influences, such as the geometric simplicity of Futura. This combination gives the typeface a timeless yet contemporary feel, suitable for both traditional and forward-looking design applications. RL Sezon is available in a range of weights and italics, offering versatility for different contexts. It is packaged as both static fonts and a variable format, enhancing its flexibility. The name “Sezon” (Polish for season) reflects its all-year-round usability — whether for brand

typefaces.name: RL Slack
typefaces.desc: Discover the captivating fusion of history and the future with the Slack "Retro-Future Blocks" typeface. Crafted using a block-like construction kit, it seamlessly blends classic and modern aesthetics, offering a truly unique and versatile typographic experience. Inspired by early techno and house music visuals, this typeface emanates electric energy and dynamic movement. Its bold, geometric forms draw from 90s retro-futuristic games, paying homage to the past while presenting a distinct futuristic vibe. With its carefully crafted block-like design, it commands attention and suits various creative applications. Slack embodies a timeless journey, capturing the essence of historical architecture like Stonehenge, while embracing contemporary sleekness. Uppercase letters exude strength and authority from monumental civilizations, while lowercase letters maintain modern minimalism, reflecting the aspirations of the future. Its numerals boast unmistakable retro flair, evoking pixel art and digital innovation. Whether designing posters for futuristic events or seeking a touch of retro-futuristic charm, Slack is your go-to choice. [ regularlines.com ]

typefaces.name: RL Unno
typefaces.desc: The Unno typeface's versatility is evident in its ability to look great in various media formats such as magazines from Los Angeles to South Korea. Its perfect contrast of curves and strokes and clean lines are critical elements that make it a must-have font in any world-class font format. Unno typeface has a unique quality that makes it suitable for any design project that demands elegance, style, and sophistication. In conclusion, Unno typeface is a highly sophisticated and elegant typographic design that is perfect for any project that requires a touch of luxury and sophistication. Its clean lines, perfect contrast of curves and strokes, and versatility make it a must-have font for any world-class format. Unno typeface is a true testament to the art of typography, and its attention to detail and commitment to quality is evident in every character. [ regularlines.com ]

typefaces.name: RL Wit
typefaces.desc: RL Wit is a serif typeface designed for display use, drawing inspiration from the Renaissance epitaphs found on churches in the city of Wrocław. After World War II, Wrocław became part of Poland, but for nearly 500 years prior, it was a German city known as Breslau. Because of the significant historical upheavals of the 20th century, little of Breslau’s historical lettering has survived. Fortunately, some epitaphs carved during the late Renaissance remain preserved in the city, offering a glimpse into the artistry of the time. These epitaphs often feature Latin inscriptions framed by German texts engraved in Fraktur or Schwabacher styles. The interplay of these styles reveals their mutual influence: while the Latin inscriptions exhibit the refined elegance of the Renaissance, they still retain echoes of a medieval feel. The workshop responsible for these epitaphs was run by the sculptor Gerhard Hendrik and his assistants. Hendrik, born in the Netherlands, traveled before settling in Breslau, where he created numerous sculptures in city churches and surrounding areas. Since the lettering was likely delegated to Hendrik’s assistants, pinpointing the exact letter carvers is challengin

typefaces.name: RL Zeta
typefaces.desc: RL Zeta is a monospaced typeface that pays homage to the rich history of metal type printing. Designed to bridge the gap between the mechanical precision of traditional typesetting and the versatility required in modern digital contexts, Zeta embodies a blend of historical reverence and contemporary utility. Zeta’s monospaced design ensures uniformity and alignment, making it an excellent choice for coding, tabular data, and any application where consistency is paramount. This characteristic harks back to the utilitarian nature of typewriters, which employed monospaced fonts to ensure that each letter occupied the same amount of horizontal space. However, Zeta elevates this concept by adding nuances that reflect the sophistication of historical typefaces. [ regularlines.com ]

typefaces.name: Roboto Serif
typefaces.desc: Commissioned by Google Fonts.

typefaces.name: Rocher Color
typefaces.desc: Produced as a varilable color font.

typefaces.name: Rodger
typefaces.desc: Rodger is an 18 weight, rounded sans serif family. Its organic, yet refined curves walk a fine line between casualness and formality. The Rodger font family’s main source of inspiration came from rounded display faces of the 1960s and 70s, but it also references rounded typefaces found in wood type collections of the 19th century. Despite its vintage roots, Rodger is not a revival, but rather a contemporary interpretation of a classic style. Rodger’s 18 styles range from the delicate yet sturdy Rodger Thin, to the vaguely psychedelic and plump Rodger Black. [ centraltype.com ] Expanded in 2024 to seven weights in upright and italics, available as individual styles or as a variable font with weight and slant axes.

typefaces.name: Roko
typefaces.desc: Roko, A 5 weight display that loves to be set tight and party late. Drawn in the spirit of the tigthly letterspaced Lubalin/Carnase geo-sans era with an updated touch. [ nuformtype.com ]

typefaces.name: Romie
typefaces.desc: The font family was completed in June 2024 with the addition of italic styles across all weights.

typefaces.name: Rondette
typefaces.desc: Rondette's design is steeped in historical references, bridging the timeless and the modern. Inspired by Joseph Churchward’s iconic Churchward Design 70 (No-End version) and the striking work of Unimark International for Agip in the 1970s, it also pays homage to the bold, geometric style of Herbert Bayer's Universal alphabet and the clean, functional forms of 1930s sans-serifs like Futura and Kabel. From these roots, Rondette extends into the contemporary sports world, capturing the energy and precision of modern athletic aesthetics. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Ronzino
typefaces.desc: Ronzino rises from the ashes of our former brand typeface (Arial, sigh) to bring a new spin on the cult classic, improving on its (many) while retaining a similar information-driven feeling – anonymous and nondescript. [ collletttivo.it ]

typefaces.name: Roobert
typefaces.desc: Updated in 2024: Roobert – Our trusty workhorse for any occasion got even better last year! We expanded it with Mono and SemiMono families and added Vietnamese support. Plus, thanks to our brilliant friend Ilya Bazhanov, we’re thrilled to now include Cyrillic and Greek as well.

typefaces.name: Rootzin
typefaces.desc: Rootzin is a reverse contrast slab serif typeface destined for headlines and use in large sizes. Despite being only one weight, the typeface exploits Opentype features to expand the layout solutions by offering a set of small capitals and a range of numeral styles that can add real flexibility to the design. With an expanded character set covering latin, Greek and Cyrillic, this typeface aims to be a bold voice that will grab attention. [ typogama.com ]

typefaces.name: Roquefort
typefaces.desc: Roquefort (the typeface) is a quirky expanded grotesque, which, like Roquefort (the cheese), is pongy and full of flavour. However, where Roquefort (the cheese) develops its pungent tang through a lengthy maturation process, Roquefort (the typeface) takes the opposite approach. With the desire to avoid the over-thinking and over-refinement that can slowly sanitise a typeface design over time, Roquefort (the typeface) was produced hastily, with the hope of creating a grotesque with all the wonky inconsistencies that give a grot its distinct flavour. Roquefort (the typeface) is likely to be expanded and improved over time, and, as with all Polytype fonts, future updates will be free for existing licensees. [ polytype.co.uk ]

typefaces.name: Rosalie
typefaces.desc: Rosalie is a contemporary display serif by My-Lan Thuong, born from a medieval mural in Guérande, France. Rosalie is a study in polarities; it is both sharp and round, calligraphic and constructed, historic and futuristic, narrow and wide. With its unusual proportions and exuberant swashes, high contrast, and innovative shapes, Rosalie contains a unique mix of simultaneously complimentary and contradictory forms. The typeface’s development tracks the creative evolution of Thuong’s type design practice through many years of development. After 6 years in the making, Rosalie is now available as a duo of complementary Roman and Italic styles, both including OmniLatin language support. [ sharptype.co ]

typefaces.name: Roshan
typefaces.desc: Roshan is a high contrast multiscript typeface with close connections to calligraphic traditions. While the Arabic is inspired by the rounded forms of Persian Naskh and Maghrebi writing styles, its Latin is incised, in contrast with the more common practice of pairing a serif typeface counterpart to a high contrast Arabic. This makes the two scripts even more distinct in a multiscript context. Roshan is Persian for bright as well as enlightenment. In its name lies the description of one of its main characteristics. To let in more light into the counterforms, Roshan introduces subtle stencilling rather than enlarging the white of the letterforms. On the other hand, for the wide shapes of Arabic that do let it a lot of light, the terminuses were tapered to make the black and white balance on the reading line more consistent. [ tptq-arabic.com ]

typefaces.name: Roslindale Compressed
typefaces.desc: The compressed version of Roslindale Display , offered along with an Extra Condensed width as part of the Font of the Month Club in July 2024.

typefaces.name: Rosso
typefaces.desc: [ Release announcement ]

typefaces.name: Round
typefaces.desc: If you run around the rounded long enough, you might be inclined to make it square. And that’s exactly what has transpired with the “Round” typeface. The visually impactful cut angled terminals and stylishly rounded simplicity evoke a modern geometrical fluid approach to design, going to round then square, and back again. Unique characteristics of this typeface can be seen in the lowercase b, d, p, and q where the vertical bars cut through the rounds with sharp precision to create a graphically eye catching font, perfect for developing logos and any branding project. This font is optimised for text and graphic fluidity, when used in small text size, optically the corners transform right before your eyes into a rounded caress. The “Round” is not round, nor really a geometric, nor a humanist typeface, it’s something in between and more complex, It’s an exploration in design where a physical object, in this case a marker has determined the digital form, and type design imitates life and influences the way we look at the world around us. [ bureaubrut.com ]

typefaces.name: Round Condensed
typefaces.desc: If you run around the rounded long enough, you might be inclined to make it square. And that’s exactly what has transpired with the “Round” typeface. The visually impactful cut angled terminals and stylishly rounded simplicity evoke a modern geometrical fluid approach to design, going to round then square, and back again.
