Unique characteristics of this typeface can be seen in the lowercase b, d, p, and q where the vertical bars cut through the rounds with sharp precision to create a graphically eye catching font, perfect for developing logos and any branding project. This font is optimised for text and graphic fluidity, when used in small text size, optically the corners transform right before your eyes into a rounded caress. The “Round” is not round, nor really a geometric, nor a humanist typeface, it’s something in between and more complex, It’s an exploration in design where a physical object, in this case a marker has determined the digital form, and type design imitates life and influences the way we look at the world around us. [ bureaubrut.com ]

typefaces.name: Royalis
typefaces.desc: Royalis is an expressive and extravagant serif typeface family. It is characterized by a high contrast and dynamic features in the details, such as long terminals or deep inktraps. Royalis is available in three versions: a display version in six weights, a corresponding condensed version also for display applications, and a text version for body text in four weights. [ fontcuisine.com ]

typefaces.name: RP Crest
typefaces.desc: Crest is a striking 2-in-1 typeface that draws its inspiration from the world of cylinders, engine oil and the rubber of worn tires. It is available in 2 complementary styles, Crest and Crest Twice, which are built on the same extended skeleton. Crest Twice is distinguished by its double line and has a higher x-height than its little sister, making it the perfect tool for creating impactful short logos and lettering. Both fonts feature a multitude of ligatures that will give your designs the twists and edginess they deserve. [ robinpitchon.com ]

typefaces.name: RP Triliad
typefaces.desc: Triliad is the perfect asset for creatives looking to develop bespoke logos and lettering. Careful craft of spacing and kerning and its elegant swashes and ligatures ensures that each character fits harmoniously together in various aesthetically pleasing letter combinations, giving a distinctive touch to ones creations. [ robinpitchon.com ]

typefaces.name: RST Brother
typefaces.desc: RST Brother is the evolutionary successor to Brother 1816 & Brother XS/XL, now presented as a variable font. This comprehensive update extends functionality with an expansive range of characters, widths and weights. This typeface blends history, geometry and calligraphy, ensuring legibility across different sizes—ideal for branding, editorial, and signage. Its geometric nature works for larger applications lending distinctive character to headlines and posters; while its humanist nature makes it readable in small sizes. The condensed styles were engineered for space efficiency, ensuring uncompromised clarity in restricted spaces. The expanded versions offer a strong presence for display uses maintaining functionality without sacrificing style. Designed with adaptability in mind, Brother transcends stylistic eras, with the flexibility to complement both retro and contemporary atmospheres, seamlessly integrating into text or titles, whether in print or on digital platforms. [ reset-type.com ]

typefaces.name: RST Liberdad
typefaces.desc: RST Libertad is a humanist sans-serif typeface designed with legibility and efficiency as primary goals. Designed for a wide range of applications such as wayfinding, editorial, web, packaging, and branding. The typeface pays tribute to the works of 16th-century figures: Nicola Jenson, Claude Garamond, and Aldus Manutius, shaping its letterforms, proportions, and italics. One of the most distinctive features is the striking contrast between regular and italic shapes, which provide a distinct voice and personality. Its low-contrast strokes and ample counters ensure clarity and legibility, making it an excellent choice for wayfinding. Its short proportions make it an efficient and space-saving solution for text-heavy applications and ideal for web design, where vertical space is limited. Libertad's variable capacities allows designers to adjust its weight to fit specific needs, making it an ideal choice for digital design applications that require responsive design to fit different screen sizes and resolutions. [ reset-type.com ]

typefaces.name: RST Mazumbá
typefaces.desc: Rhythmically wild, aggressive, of resistance, Mazumbá unfolds as a symphony of form, inspired by the beats of Candombe drums, an Afro-Uruguayan rhythm enshrined as humanity's intangible heritage. A variable weight typeface with dramatic extremes and subtle midpoints, full of personality. This font, in perpetual motion, echoes the spirited African dance that accompanies the vibrant music. It's a project infused with profound meaning, rooted in history, culture, and tradition. Mazumbá’s versatility at its extremes enables you to craft eye-catching, dynamic headlines that captivate the eye. Meanwhile, its intermediates are finely tuned for immersive reading, upholding classic proportions with robust terminals, focusing on legibility. The lighter style (stencil) embodies the "chico" drum, characterized by its sharp, precise notes that cut through the air. In contrast, the heaviest (black) resonates with the depths of the "piano" drum, offering a sound so rich and deep that it completely envelops. In the middle (regular), the drum "repique" creates a harmonious dialogue between them. This is how Mazumbá takes shape, a typeface that dances freely, losing its endings, expanding and tensin

typefaces.name: RST Reactor
typefaces.desc: RST Reactor is a typeface that explores extremes and pushes them to their limit. Designed to coexist in all types of design pieces, it adapts to the environment without losing its essence. Reactor is a variable font with two axes: weight and width. Both axes take shapes to the limit to form a family of great versatility. The condensed styles evoke 19th century woodtype, while the wider versions breathe modernity. In between, a classic grotesque type, discreet, modern, and simple. Regarding weight, Reactor gives a sensation of cleanliness and minimalism in its lighter weights. On the heavy end, it fills the spaces to compose strong messages with high visual impact. In the middle, it remains silent and neutral. [ reset-type.com ]

typefaces.name: RST Silvestre
typefaces.desc: RST Silvestre is an innovative variable typeface with two principal axes: vertical and horizontal weight. The groundbreaking aspect of Silvestre is its horizontal weight which offers the unique ability to modify and explore the typeface's serif contrast. The distinct personality of Silvestre is most evident at its most extreme weights, on the other hand, the intermediate styles encourage users to engage with the typeface, discovering its experimental and playful typographic expressions. […] Silvestre's aesthetic is heavily influenced by two contrasting sources. The first is the industrial robustness of 19th-century wood type, which lends the typeface a sense of timeless strength. The second key influence is the psychedelic posters of the 1960s, which infuse the typeface with a funky essence. This combination results in Silvestre’s defining playful and energetic character. [ reset-type.com ]

typefaces.name: RST Thermal
typefaces.desc: RST Thermal is an exploration of balance and contrast. Combining the elegance of classical typography with the sharpness of contemporary design. It was conceived to be a variable font with two axes: weight & optical size, providing a wide range of options for texts & display applications. The regular and italic text weights breathe a warm atmosphere, their design inspiration is a relaxed interpretation of the work of 16th-century French type designer Robert Granjon, evoking a comforting rhythm and a sense of familiarity that makes reading enjoyable. On the other end of Thermal's design spectrum lie the extreme weights – thin and heavy –, specifically designed for larger sizes. These weights borrow stylistic cues from several distinct influences: the characteristic woodtype from the 19th century, the sharp lettering styles from the 70s, and the bold work of Oscar Ogg. One of Thermal's disctint features is its italic's 20° inclination, an significant inclination by all standards, this design choice finds its roots in the Ascendonica Cursive of 1571, but is a contemporary interpretation that generates a captivating contrast with the regular version. Thermal studies the past and analyz

typefaces.name: RST Transandina
typefaces.desc: RST Trasandina is a variable font with weight axis. Its letterforms are defined by a blend between humanist and geometric sans-serif models. This provides a mixture of broad open shapes with sharp, square and decisive curves that gives Trasandina a unique typographic presence. It draws inspiration from different sources: on one hand mechanical 20th-century German type, specifically industrial wood type such as DIN, and on the other, vibrant and futuristic sci-fi book covers from the 70s and 80s. This dichotomy is visible in the contrast between the mechanical, sturdy, precise and neutral atmosphere from the regular versions, and the organic and dynamic italics. The progression of weights was carefully explored, culminating in a powerful black weight which is remarkably robust and conveys an intense visual impact. [ reset-type.com ]

typefaces.name: RT Dromo
typefaces.desc: RT Dromo first appeared as a custom typeface project in the book Die Not hat ein Ende: The Swiss Art of Rock , which showcases various printed ephemera from the Swiss music scene. The design grew out of the context of its first application and is therefore based on double-gothic typefaces used for impact printing concert tickets during the 1980s. Since then it has been extended to a contemporary grotesque type family consisting of 9 weights.

typefaces.name: RT Rondelle
typefaces.desc: RT Rondelle is the result of an exploration into public transport signage typefaces. While building on this foundation it incorporates the distinctive characteristics of a highly specialized genre to become a versatile grotesque family with a balanced geometrical touch. Leaving behind the restrictions of its heritage RT Rondelle forms a consistent type family suited for a wide range of applications.

typefaces.name: RT Vitrine
typefaces.desc: RT Vitrine is a high-contrast Display Sans achieving a see-through quality through formal reduction while its crystal- clear shapes convey the air of effortless elegance. In his article “Through thick and thin: Fashion and type” first published in EYE No.65, Vol.17, 2007, Abott Miller writes: “[...] It has an almost see-through quality. Because of its radical thick-thin structure, the mass of the letterforms are greatly diminished: words typeset in Didone fonts act as a typographic veil over photography.” Having a visual characteristic compressed in clear words can have a revealing effect. With the serifs cut and the weight removed from the stroke endings altogether this typeface takes the translucence to the next level. Started as an exploration into the field of display type and the Didone genre, RT Vitrine has become a typeface stripped back to its essence, revealing the beauty in simplicity.

typefaces.name: Rube
typefaces.desc: Initially named Unie.

typefaces.name: Rules
typefaces.desc: Updated in 2024.

typefaces.name: Rules Gothic
typefaces.desc: Rules Gothic is the Gothic renewal of the Rules font family. Thought has the "go to" typeface for any designers who love to use contrasted, gothic, humanist inspired sans fonts in their project. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Rumpus Extended
typefaces.desc: Rumpus Extended is a super-wide typeface with sharp Latin serifs. It is descended from Stephenson Blake’s 1883 Wide Latin, which contrasts super-pointy serifs with super-round forms. Rumpus keeps a bit of the wild side of other Latins, but isn’t as overtly circuslike. Unlike its predecessors, Rumpus has a distinctly humanist structure, evidenced by its interior corners and punctuated by its diamond shaped dots. And the sheer width of Rumpus Extended is enough to give significant heft to any message, no matter how short it may be. [ djr.com ]

typefaces.name: RunRun
typefaces.desc: RunRun is an austere typeface family for handwritten style text with a relaxed rhythm, composed of three weights that subtly vary in thickness. Despite its casual look, RunRun was designed to perform in texts for immersive reading, so it has an extensive glyph set that includes many typographic refinements, such as small caps, different kinds of figures, ligatures, and contextual alternates. [ quintana-font.cl ] A condensed handwritten typeface produced in three weights.

typefaces.name: Rupta
typefaces.desc: Amnes is a sans-serif typeface released in 2024. It features a total of fourteen styles—seven Upright and seven Inktrap weights—offering a wide range of typographic possibilities. The Upright variant focuses on clarity and simplicity, while the Inktrap variant incorporates functional cutouts that improve legibility, especially at smaller sizes. Available in regular and Inktrap styles. The sample image shows the latter. Renamed Rupta later in 2025.

typefaces.name: Ryman Gothic
typefaces.desc: Inspired by American wood type and gothic typefaces. Cites the influence of Edwin Allen and Morris Fuller Benton.

typefaces.name: Saggi
typefaces.desc: We* made Saggi because Janson felt so dusty… So here it is: a fresh interpretation of Nicholas Kis’ sweet, rationalist, transitional letterforms, based on the meticulous research of a splendid Florentine folio.** Saggi is serious and lively while retaining the understated quirks of the metal type. It is geared for complex texts with broad language support and opentype features, yet it is not afraid of poster-size use. This typeface is relatively compact without abandoning its classical proportions: contemporary, Baroque and unintentionally beautiful. * Designed by Géza Sipos & Nóra Békés ** This revival was based on Saggi di naturali esperienze [Essays of natural experiments, Firenze, 1691] [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Saiga
typefaces.desc: Finalized in 2023.

typefaces.name: Sakkal Saad
typefaces.desc: https://www.sakkal.com/type/saad.html

typefaces.name: Salish
typefaces.desc: Salish was originally conceived in response to a Request for Proposals from the City of Seattle for a new typeface to be used for logos and general branding. The design draws from the concept of the 'Ovoid' (a shape rounder on the top and flatter on the bottom) which is a central part of Formline art developed by tribes along the Pacific Northwest coastline. It is believed that the unique shape of the Ovoid originated in the way a salmon egg looks when resting on a flat, dry surface. In developing this design, I studied Bill Holm's "Northwest Coast Indian Art" book as well as other art books. [ sajatypeworks.com ]

typefaces.name: Salvaje Display
typefaces.desc: Originally released with Coppers and Brasses in 2018, reissued by Typozon in 2022. Updated to 2.0 in January 2025.

typefaces.name: Sancta
typefaces.desc: Featuring clean lines, sharp corners, and a distinct geometric style, Sancta embodies the essence of Gaelic calligraphy while embracing the demands of contemporary design. This Celtic display font is carefully crafted to strike the perfect balance between tradition and readability, making it a versatile choice for a wide range of design projects. [ doubledagger.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Sans Norm
typefaces.desc: MuirMcNeil Sans Norm is a sans serif type system that emphasises rhythms of straight vertical strokes to give the impression of a blocky, condensed script. It has been constructed on a skeleton corresponding closely to that of MuirMcNeil Sans Sans , a ‘neutral’ type family where the characters of the latin alphabet are distilled into a system of variable components intended for extensive reconfiguration. Sans Norm’s more mechanised and stripped-down forms refer to utilitarian twentieth century geometric designs like DIN 1451, Isonorm and OCR-A. [ muirmcneil.com ]

typefaces.name: Sanscise
typefaces.desc: Sanscise is a compact font family for general use. The typeface was initially commissioned by creative agency Mucho as a bespoke typeface for a leading 100-year-old European business law firm. This inspired us to draw a modern, dignified alphabet. Sanscise is a humanist sans serif that looks decidedly contemporary, but with classical roots. Its narrow proportions allow you to fit more words on a line, while the open letterforms guarantee the typeface remains perfectly readable in even the smallest sizes. Sanscise sports flared stroke endings inspired by letters carved in stone. While not actual serifs, they provide a firm footing for the characters. The reader barely notices them when Sanscise is used for body copy. However, they make the typeface shine when set large. [ tipografies.com ]

typefaces.name: Santa Ana Sans
typefaces.desc: Santa Ana Sans is inspired by the perfectly imperfect typography on vintage and retro storefront signage and marquees. This semi-condensed typeface comes in 6 weights plus italics. It’s a workhorse typeface that you can set heavier text in, but don’t get it wrong, it knows how to play just as hard and has enough personality for headline copy, logos, and other display usages. Track it tight, track it wide…versatility is its middle name. [ hoodzpahdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Santiag
typefaces.desc: Santiag, designed by Clement Cases, is a contemporary western typeface, inspired by the reversal of stress in the character strokes of the mythic Italian typefaces from the 19th century. This typeface is a modern take on the genre, attempting to incorporate geometric shapes into the counter forms. Featuring bold shapes that relate to serifs, the half-circle is key to creating the rhythm and distinct character of the typeface. The height of the base is adjustable, giving the overall typography a cartoonish feel. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Satori
typefaces.desc: Satori is a geometric Sans Serif typeface inspired by feelings of sudden enlightenment or spiritual awakening. The type design blends inspiration from the circular journey of life and self-discovery, contrasted with the flat planes to represent the moment of realization and awakening. [ typeoffeeling.com ]

typefaces.name: Sature
typefaces.desc: Designed from large-print lettering drawn on paper, the Sature font family came from a desire to create a complete family that unfolds. The letters are the result of an adjustment of hand-made lettering. All styles can be used together to create contrasts in the layout. The name of the font comes from the french word «Saturer», meaning to overtake with excess. Feel free to maximise. With its 5 heights and 10 styles with the slant, the family offers a wealth of possibilities for creating saturation effects. A variable font that gives the impression that between each style appears a doubling of the letter, like a felt-tip marker that enlarges the letter. Horizontal processing was carried out to give the letters their fullness, making it easy for use in large sizes and high-impact messages [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Savanna Script
typefaces.desc: Richard Lipton is a master of the calligraphic script, transforming the elegance of pen-on-paper into beautiful, functional fonts. For Savanna Script, he channeled Friedrich Neugebauer and Martin Wilke, modern calligraphers whose square-edged pen updated 16th-century styles. Tight and taut, Savanna dances with a rapid yet effortless energy. Three weights and multiple cap styles offer flexibility rare in formal scripts. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Scatch
typefaces.desc: What would a Scotch Roman look like if it were a sans? Scatch is a modulated grotesque that taps into historical models from a different genre: it explores the question of what happens to a Scotch Roman when it has no serifs. Scatch is a Scotch Sans – a Roman minus the serifs. Some of the earliest sans serifs were derived from existing types by cutting away the serifs. The design process of Scatch was not quite that simple and straightforward. It pursued a similar objective, though: the long serifs had to go, but many other characteristics of the genre were to be preserved. [ tipografies.com ]

typefaces.name: Scatterplot
typefaces.desc: A variable slab serif made of dots.

typefaces.name: Scena
typefaces.desc: Scena is a sans-serif typeface crafted with a broad range of styles and proportions, making it equally suitable for extended text and large-scale display applications. The design began with a simple sketch exploring lowercase letters with bottom loops. From this concept, we developed both normal and wide character sets. Our initial focus was on the Slanted styles, but as we explored various graphic applications, it became clear that expanding the range to include Roman styles was essential to fully capture Scena’s expressive potential. The original characters are preserved as Stylistic Sets 2, 3, and 4, while the default set was refined and simplified of certain eccentric features. [ store.typenetwork.com ]

typefaces.name: Scenik
typefaces.desc: Scenik is a typeface inspired by the modernist typography of Margate, a coastal town in the UK. Drawing on influences from the 1930s to the present day, it merges heritage and contemporary design features to create a versatile type family. The typeface offers an extensive array of options, including 142 styles, 13 weights, and 3 families. Its versatile range is designed for use in any application, regardless of size or scope. The standard cut of Scenik is designed specifically for punchy headlines and word marks, while the text cut is tailored for more subtle word marks and smaller body copy. The mono cut is ideal for monospaced applications and smaller body copy. [ frostype.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Scope
typefaces.desc: Scope is a monolinear typeface designed with typographic interaction in mind. Its letters are constructed to function as mechanical variations and follow a strict set of rules: Closed forms are rounded, open forms are angular. This balance breaks the technical aesthetic with a soft, human touch. [ jonastype.com ]

typefaces.name: Scorpione
typefaces.desc: Debuted on Future Fonts in 2022, graduated in 2023.

typefaces.name: Scotus Sans
typefaces.desc: Scotus Sans is a low-contrast sanserif family available in a wide range of weights and styles. It performs excellently for long reading text in printing and on web pages, as well as on any kind of screen and device. Its name and its overall proportions come from a highly successful roman type which first appeared in the printing office of Octavianus Scotus, in Venice in 1481 – about ten years after Nicolas Jenson’s masterful roman type. Among the many imitations of Jenson’s roman available at the time, the roman used by Octavianus Scotus achieved the greatest commercial success. In fact, it was used by more than 100 printers in Italy and elsewhere in Europe. Nonetheless, Scotus Sans is not a revival of a 15th-century roman; it is a new sans based on the skeleton of the original roman and embodies ‘simplicity of form which does not reject traditional forms’ while maintaining ‘clarity and readability’. Galli, Olocco and Perondi designed Scotus Sans following in the footsteps of early 20th-century milestones such as Edward Johnston’s typeface for the London Underground and notably Monotype Sans Serif no. 231 (later known as Gill Sans), in which the designer tried ‘to work out the norm

typefaces.name: Scriber
typefaces.desc: Scriber is a meticulously crafted geometric stencil typeface that merges precision with contemporary aesthetics. Perfect for both digital and print media, Scriber brings a unique blend of structure and creativity to your work. With its clean, straight lines and sharp angles, Scriber ensures a balanced, uniform look that stands out in any context. The distinctive breaks within the strokes of each letter add an industrial flair, making Scriber ideal for projects that require a modern, technical feel. [ thenorthernblock.co.uk ] Originally an octagonal display typeface , it was reissued in February 2025 as a stencil typeface.

typefaces.name: Scuto Sans
typefaces.desc: Scuto Sans is a modern sans-serif typeface ideal for a wide range of applications, from branding and advertising to digital content and print media. Its well-proportioned letters and consistent stroke widths ensure readability at any size, making it ideal for user interfaces, corporate communications, and editorial layouts. [ minttype.com ]

typefaces.name: Scuto Soft
typefaces.desc: Scuto Soft is the softened counterpart of Scuto Sans, a modern sans-serif typeface ideal for a wide range of applications. Its rounded corners add friendliness and bring display characteristics to an otherwise neutral font family, making it suitable for branding, headlines, callouts, and other types of typographic emphasis. [ minttype.com ]

typefaces.name: Seabass
typefaces.desc: Seabass is a wide, modern sans serif with slight reverse contrast. The distinctive design blends eye-catching style with function. Look closely; it’s got California vibes. Think beach culture, skate parks, shopping malls, and boardwalk energy. It’s crafted to create typographic interest and visual texture, especially when set in all caps. This family is ideal for display but still intriguing and useful when small. Available in 14 styles—Extra Light to Black—including italics or 2 variable fonts. [ ladd-design.com ]

typefaces.name: Seabirds
typefaces.desc: The Seabirds is an homage to the historical legacy of lineals, combining different sub-genres of the sans-serif category within a single typeface. The project emerged through the study of book covers from the first half of the 20th century—particularly those crafted in the 1930s for the renowned publisher Albatross. They were featuring new and “modern” sans-serifs, most probably contributing to their growing world-wide popularity. Initially conceived as a revival of several well-known typefaces, the evolution of this project involved numerous redesigns to thoroughly appropriate and refine forms that have contributed to the History of Typography. The references that inspired the Seabirds are ultimately plural, diverse, and harmoniously blended for a consistent and contemporary design. The default set is predominantly geometrical, while the use of OpenType stylistic sets enables a transition from orthogonal to flat terminals, guiding the design to a more humanistic style. The uppercases maintain proportions reminiscent of classic Roman capitals, while revisions to the lowercases have been made to achieve a more balanced and cohesive rhythm. The ratio between ascender height and x-hei

typefaces.name: Seaford
typefaces.desc: Seaford is a sturdy, sophisticated, and energetic sansserif for reading and writing. Its design is rooted in long-form text serifs and evokes their familiarity and comfort. Resisting modernist homogenization, Seaford’s gently asymmetric, organic forms help reading by emphasizing the differences between letters, creating recognizable word shapes. A range of alternates and four sets of numbers further increase its versatility. Originally designed for Microsoft, Seaford is one of five new sansserifs included in Office 365 subscriptions. [ frerejones.com ]

typefaces.name: Seamus
typefaces.desc: İbrahim Kaçtıoğlu designed the extremely thick unicase typeface Seamus with humor, drawing his inspiration from the earliest American comics. The design of Seamus is exuberant, exaggerated, and caricatural. Its generous forms balloon out like Popeye’s biceps. Its massive strokes contrast with its particularly thin crossbars, and the “overinflated” curves are enhanced by tiny counters. Yet its particularly expressive letters fit together perfectly, making Seamus a display typeface with a particularly distinct style. [ 205.tf ]

typefaces.name: Season
typefaces.desc: The exploration of the transformation from sans to serif (or serif to sans) and the stages in between is at the heart of our Season typeface. Just as you enjoy the changing seasons, we hope you’ll appreciate each phase of Season. With the variable font format, you can experience even more stages in this dynamic sans-to-serif collection.

typefaces.name: Seasummer
typefaces.desc: Seasummer is a variable handwriting font with a single axis. The typeface was collaboratively designed by Céline Hurka and Stefaniia Bodnia. The project originally drew inspiration from the handwriting of illustrator Adrian Pourviseh, found in his diaries. In 2021, Adrian spent several weeks in the Mediterranean, participating in the rescue of refugees with Sea-Watch E.V.. While at sea, he processed these traumatic experiences at Europe's deadliest borders through his writing, later transforming them into a graphic novel. The novel, titled "Das Schimmern der See," was published in 2023 by Avant Verlag and designed by Moritz Schottmüller and Calvin Kudufia. The project received high acclaim by various news channels such as Arte TV and SWR and was supported generously by Stimuleringsfonds Creative Industries. Seasummer was specifically developed for this graphic novel, aiming to capture the emotional journey of its writer from tranquility to intensity. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Seitu
typefaces.desc: A geometric sans serif informed by Futura and Gill Sans, and inspired by the Coop logo (Bob Noorda, 1985). Produced as a variable font with a weight axis. Updated in 2025 with support for the Cyrillic script.

typefaces.name: Selawik
typefaces.desc: Selawik is an OpenSource, metrics-compatible, Segoe UI replacement font available on GitHub. Segoe UI is Microsoft’s core UI and branding typeface. Given the importance of this typeface, Microsoft wants to keep tight control over its use. However, increasingly there were situations where an app developer created a cross-platform app, or an OpenSource app, and wanted to use Segoe UI across all of them. Microsoft did not want to permit use of the font in these scenairos, but needed to provide a solution for these use cases—thus Selawik was born. The major challenge of this project was to design a typeface that matched the metrics, style, and feel of Segoe UI while being sufficiently different. [ sajatypeworks.com ] Released as open-source on GitHub.

typefaces.name: Seminario
typefaces.desc: Seminario is an all-caps typeface originally created for the Latin American restaurant Curiosa by Jean-Georges in Doha's Four Seasons Hotel. Inspired by a 1912 headline from Mexico's national weekly magazine La Revista de Revistas, its Art Nouveau spirit lives on in its discreet but distinctive flared serifs, elegant ligatures, and unusual alternate sets. With its feather-light weight and low contrast, Seminario shines at large sizes and short lengths. [ muccatypo.com ]

typefaces.name: Seraphine
typefaces.desc: Seraphine is a versatile Didone-style typeface that combines classic elegance with modern functionality. Available in 9 distinct weights, from Thin to Black, Seraphine offers a wide range of options for any design need. The font is meticulously crafted in 4 different optical sizes, ensuring excellent readability across both small and large text. It also includes true italics, preserving the sophisticated slant and flow characteristic of traditional Didone design. In addition to its extensive weight and optical size options, Seraphine is a fully variable font, allowing users to fine-tune its weight, width, and slant to achieve the perfect typographic balance for any project. The font also includes a set of decorative stylistic sets, which expand its creative potential, making it suitable for both classic editorial designs and modern branding or packaging work. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Serein
typefaces.desc: Serein is a sophisticated typeface inspired by the French term “serein,” which signifies a serene and refined ambiance. This harmoniously elegant font features Roman Capital Proportions, rooted in the timeless beauty of Old Style typography with classic yet contemporary charm. Serein’s high-contrast design, with its tapered calligraphic terminals and delicately impaled counters, brings an aura of elegance and sophistication to any project. [ typeoffeeling.com ]

typefaces.name: Server Mono
typefaces.desc: Server Mono is a typeface inspired by typewriters, Apple's San Francisco Mono, ASCII art, command-line interfaces, and programming tools. Server Mono continues the long tradition of monospace fonts, renowned for their versatility in command-line interfaces due to their clear readability and uniform character width. You'll notice our own preferences reflected in the design, as we value how it performs across various viewing contexts. Server Mono offers excellent readability and pairs well with its uniform, predictable, and orderly appearance. We anticipate that Server Mono will be a valuable choice for your websites, game worlds, and custom desktop application interfaces, especially where precise alignment is essential. [ servermono.com ] Comissioned by Internet Development Studio and released as open-source on GitHub.

typefaces.name: Sharf
typefaces.desc: Finalized in January 2024.

typefaces.name: Sharp Roman
typefaces.desc: Sharp Roman Display is the calligraphic convergence of two distinct origin stories. The roman uppercase forms are Lucas’s take on the Trajan Monumental Roman Capitals via Edward Catich, while the Italic is based on the work of Pedro Diaz “El Maestro” Morante. Sharp Roman Display becomes more than the sum of its parts, offering a wealth of typographic potential: instantly indelible, elegant in its expressiveness, and full of bravura. Sharp Roman skillfully connects the work of two masters who were separated by continents and centuries into a single family sharing a calligraphic framework, making for a typeface that is classical in its construction and contemporary in its execution. [ sharptype.co ]

typefaces.name: Shentox
typefaces.desc: Variable version released in June 2025.

typefaces.name: Shimano
typefaces.desc: This sharp-edged, industrial design from the hand of Richard Lipton was initially inspired by the logotype of the Shimano bicycle company. Shimano Square and Shimano Round are each drawn in four styles, Light & Black for Wide & Narrow widths. Shimano provides starkly geometric images in contrasting combinations of weight, width, and size. Intended for logos, posters, advertising, display, and covers for books and records. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Shogun
typefaces.desc: Shogun is part of a six-part wide, ornamental headline series of three weights in regular and extended widths. Richard Lipton began with a few characters drawn for a striking contemporary logotype designed by Los Angeles graphic designer Margo Chase. The size of the series allows Chase’s ideas to be applied to a variety of display uses, offering a set of weights and widths that repeat unusually similar shapes and themes. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Signa Set
typefaces.desc: The result of continuous practice in pursuit of perfection, Team’77 presents Signa in a digitalized version. With a unique warmth and finesse, Signa Set can be seen as an evolution of modernist typography with organic inflections. Placing first in the Bobst Graphic’s Lettre d’Or 1978 competition, Signa was originally developed for phototypesetting technology by the legendary Team’77 (André Gürtler, Christian Mengelt, and Erich Gschwind). As Team’77 had witnessed the transition from metal type to its dematerialization first-hand, they knew how to leverage the technology effectively. Signa was created in perfect accordance with the technology of the time and has, now, been skillfully revitalized and adapted for contemporary typesetting. A transition from mid-century archetype to the 1970s, Signa Set is a typeface with a substantial rigor yet is infused with a certain fluidity in its ductus. Reminiscent of calligraphy, Signa Set has subtle flares at the end of its strokes, a characteristic that gives the typeface a certain charm. The design gestures that are brought together in Signa Set make it perfectly suited for elegant headlines and for embellishing compositions, while also being

typefaces.name: Silvana Text
typefaces.desc: A contemporary text serif typeface influenced by 19th-century transitional typefaces, with less contrast and wider proportions than its counterpart Silvana Display (2022).

typefaces.name: Silver Coil
typefaces.desc: With this font, Edgar flies solo. Inspired by the rotating letters of Daniël, he dug out an old concept developed during the MultipleMaster era. Silver Coil mixes his expertise from variable font engineering, with knowledge gained by creating animated GIFs. To animate Silver Coil one best loops from 100 to 700 ♾️. By looping from 700 to 100 in the background, one can create the illusion of a full 360° tube. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Silverknife
typefaces.desc: Graduated from Future Fonts in 2023.

typefaces.name: Siruca
typefaces.desc: A stencil sans serif with matching pictograms, originally designed for wayfinding in the Al Hamra Complex, Kuwait.

typefaces.name: Sirucanorm
typefaces.desc: The solid variant of Siruca , informed by DIN and Isonorm typefaces, with mathematically-derived proportions.

typefaces.name: Sisters
typefaces.desc: Sisters is a lively set of stencil display typefaces designed by Type-Ø-Tones’ co-founder Laura Meseguer. The family features four fresh fonts that share foundational principles of construction yet complement each other—as sisters do—by celebrating their differences. Variations in contrast, weight, and design characteristics result in four distinct styles dubbed One through Four. This cool quartet contains no lowercase, asserting the family’s rightful place in the titling typography space. [ type-o-tones.com ]

typefaces.name: Sizek
typefaces.desc: Sizek is an experimental display typeface that reimagines and deconstructs the classical calligraphic structure of letters. It takes inspiration from the digital age's glitches, lags, and damaged or half-loaded files, reflecting the challenges and quirks of working with technology. Sizek presents a fractured, harsh, and edgy aesthetic. Letters are disrupted by intentional breaks and divisions, reassembled into unconventional shapes and counters. These irregular forms also evoke a sense of human nervousness and tics, reflecting the chaotic beauty and unpredictability of the digital age. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: Skia CC
typefaces.desc: Skia CC is a humanist sans serif initially designed by Matthew Carter for Apple Computer in 1994. It was the first of the QuickDraw GX fonts and the first single font to offer variations in design. The letterforms take inspiration from 1st-century Greek stone carvings. The family has a flexible range of use because of its open counters, large x-height, and distinctly angled terminals. The Type Founders updated and re-engineered the original data and it is now available in 5 widths and 5 weights or as a single variable font. [ carterandcone.com ]

typefaces.name: Skin & Bones
typefaces.desc: Originally designed by Douglas F. Jones and released in 1927 with VGC (Visual Graphics Corporation).

typefaces.name: Skolar Sans Hebrew
typefaces.desc: We developed Skolar Sans to accommodate contemporary typographers and the challenges they confront: an ever-changing spectrum of outputs and devices, in which serious typography can get lost. Skolar Sans is designed for comfortable reading and engineered to cope with complex editorial texts and data-rich interfaces. Skolar Sans Hebrew, designed by Eran Ben Barak, brings this adaptability to the Hebrew script. Through a systematic grouping of the letterforms, he achieved a consistent rhythm that helps to retain the conventional forms and natural proportions of the Hebrew script while matching the density of the Latin counterpart. The result is a contemporary low-contrast family tuned for legibility, spanning a range of weights and italic styles. [ rosettatype.com ]

typefaces.name: Slimak
typefaces.desc: The fatface genre originated in the early 19th century during the Industrial Revolution in Britain. As industries and cities rapidly grew, so did the demand for eye-catching advertising materials. This led to the creation of bold, high-contrast typefaces designed to capture attention from afar on posters, signs, and other printed materials. Slimak is a fatface type family with strong terminals, designed in three optical sizes to ensure perfect readability across various contexts. It features rounded corners, which add a friendly and approachable touch to its bold and dramatic letterforms. The typeface is enriched with calligraphic details, offering a subtle elegance that contrasts beautifully with its high-impact weight. One of the distinguishing characteristics of this type family is its very high x-height, which enhances legibility and gives the typeface a modern, robust appearance. This high x-height also ensures that text remains readable even at smaller sizes. [ thedesignersfoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Sloop Script
typefaces.desc: Sloop Script is elegant calligraphy, bringing typography to life with its sweeping gestural strokes, swashes, and alternates. Richard Lipton originally released Sloop Script in 1994 through Font Bureau. Sloop Script Pro is the new, improved, rethought version, offering expanded language support and more typographic features. Sloop Script sets beautifully out of the box or can become even more audacious with entry and exit swashes, small caps, ligatures, and alternates. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Smilena
typefaces.desc: Smilena is a stunning brush script font that has a modern touch. It can be used in various design projects, including package design. Smilena offers alternate characters, such as initial and final forms for lowercase letters, as well as swash characters. These features can be conveniently utilized in design software that supports Opentype capabilities.

typefaces.name: Solar
typefaces.desc: ABC Solar is a highly customizable geometric sans with a large weight spectrum and matching italics. You can change how it looks by selecting from a huge range of alternates — and by choosing between straight or angled cuts. It’s giving Kabel , Vogue , Metro No. 2 , Johnston , and Erbar-Grotesque plus Futura of course, but if I’m calling it what it is, Solar lives in that space between Remix and Homage of all the above—with a dash of poetic license thrown in. One of Solar’s defining characteristics is its round shapes, like its almost circular capital O. Some of its letters are simple in their construction—think single-storey a and cross-like t. But the open counters and straight terminals in characters like c and s break from this geometry, creating a sense of fluidity. Solar’s 18 stylistic sets reference various geometric and humanistic typefaces from the early 20th century: switch them up to switch up the typeface’s look. While Solar subfamily is made for legibility and functionality, Solar Display has been imagined for tight and punchy headlines. [ abcdinamo.com ]

typefaces.name: Sole Serif Rounded
typefaces.desc: Sole Serif Rounded is the new cut of CAST’s most successful typeface for newspapers. Compared with its closest competitor Sole Serif Display, it features rounded edges, lighter joints, shorter bracketed serifs. With its peculiar design it works specifically as a display face providing users with the best results on magazine and newspaper headlines, and on packaging, posters and other similar applications. [ c-a-s-t.com ]

typefaces.name: Soleto
typefaces.desc: Weight range expanded and variable font version made available in February 2025.

typefaces.name: Sorella
typefaces.desc: Sorella is a seriffed roman and italic with a big x-height suitable for headlines, bodies of text and brand identities. It comes in the regular weight with matching italic, and in three optical sizes. Its soft and slightly compact letters are carefully crafted and together with the sharp serifs and the bulbous terminals evoke an 18th-century atmosphere – a perception enhanced by some mannerist touches that reveal its engraved calligraphic origins, such as the unconnected parts of E, F, e and g. Other unconnected strokes are scattered throughout the alphabet and P, B and R also have open counters which contribute to a notable feeling of openness and lightness. The lowercase of Sorella Italic is an autonomous design though it follows the same design parameters as the roman and works very well with it. The extreme 20-degree slope of this italic adds even more dynamism to its already dynamic characters. Sorella is based on the texts written and engraved by Angela Baroni for an exquisite book of hours of 400 pages, Beatae Mariae Virginis officium (Venice, 1740). In this rare volume, printed from engraved copper plates, Baroni opted for Fleischmann-like forms of serif in the capitals (su

typefaces.name: Spaceland
typefaces.desc: Not to be confused with NaN Spaceland .

typefaces.name: Spagetty
typefaces.desc: Spagetty started with the urge to create the quintessential, slab serif, capital R—with its handlebar mustache curly leg. I've always loved how much personality lives in that one character. The rest filled in, inspired by the Wild East West, Ennio Morricone's spring-reverb-laden Spaghetti Western scores, sasparilla, swinging saloon doors, and 80s cartoons. Includes Regular and Rough styles.

typefaces.name: Spalla
typefaces.desc: A typeface that carries the weight of tradition on its shoulders — and the lightness of style. Spalla is an all-caps display typeface designed in 9 styles plus a variable version, gliding between the delicate and the bold without missing a beat. With classical proportions, touches of Italian Art Deco, and a spirit that shifts between the dramatic and the elegant, it was made to stand out. Its name comes from Italian: “spalla,” meaning shoulder. In opera, in theatre, in music — the “spalla” is the one who holds, supports, and guides. And that’s exactly what this typeface does: it offers visual structure with personality and poise. Spalla’s construction carries an architectural flair, but its soul is performative. Think golden signs in a café in Milan. Vintage film posters in Rome. The graphic flourishes that make everyday Italian life a typographic delight. [ plau.design ]

typefaces.name: Spektra Tekst
typefaces.desc: Originally published by Dotless type in 2024, reissued by Type Salon in 2025.

typefaces.name: Spiegel Slab
typefaces.desc: Spiegel Slab shares the features of its sibling, Spiegel Sans , including the shapes and proportions of an industrial-style gothic, combined with subtle diagonal stress and almost imperceptible traces of handwriting. Low contrast and robust serifs help Spiegel Slab confidently hold its ground on the page for subheads in the lighter weights, as well as being extremely striking in the heavier weights. [ lucasfonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Spitzkant
typefaces.desc: Spitzkant is a serif typeface family that is characterized by strong contrasts. Pointed, sharp serifs and edges contrast with round and fine forms, making it very individual and expressive. [ fontcuisine.com ] Made into a variable font in 2022.

typefaces.name: Splinter
typefaces.desc: Splinter is a display typeface designed and developed by Namrata Goyal and Frederik Berlaen in collaboration with Universal Thirst . It explores variable axes in a grid-based, modular design, pushing legibility to the extremes and creating letterforms that can be used beyond text such as patterns, or other graphic elements. The seed of this design lies in a piece of lettering found in a long-forgotten book from Goyal’s aunt’s library – which is filled with 1960s and 70s titles, many of them in Hindi. Over time, and with ongoing exploration of the design possibilities, Splinter found the light of day. At the centre of Splinter’s design space is a pliable, pixel font source. This source stretches into 5 variable axes and 3 ‘inline’ binaries– Splinter Single, Double, Triple. Further, each binary has interpolatable instances to help you navigate the design space. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Spoof
typefaces.desc: A slightly irreverent contribution to the geometric sans genre, Spoof takes cues from rationalist predecessors like Futura, Neuzeit Grotesk and Avant Garde, but subverts the style with some exaggerated proportions and more grotesque elements. Strict geometry and orthogonal terminals lend the illusion of calm uniformity; uncomfortably tight aperatures, some unbalanced forms, and an ungainly underbite in the open-bowled glyphs undermine that feeling of precision, creating a gawkish look. [ polytype.co.uk ]

typefaces.name: Spritz
typefaces.desc: Spritz is a typeface born from the Tavern, the creative and experimental wavy tool crafted by Gaëtan Baehr. This shadow-only font is defined not by its filled forms but by the ethereal silhouettes its letters cast, leaving the characters themselves transparent and open to interpretation. Entirely rounded and capitalized, Spritz evokes an airy, lightweight quality, resonating with a sense of three-dimensional depth and movement. While its readability takes a back seat, its visual intrigue shines, creating captivating and unexpected effects. Spritz features a width variation axis and four adjustable corner axes—top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right—offering unparalleled control for creating mesmerizing wave patterns and unexpected designs. Perfect for experimental projects or artistic explorations, Spritz invites you to discover the elegance of what lies in the shadows. [ black-foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Squadra
typefaces.desc: Squadra is a contemporary sans-serif family consisting of 18 styles: 9 Regular weights and 9 corresponding Italics. Inspired by the iconic Eurostile by Aldo Novarese and Alessandro Butti, the design reinterprets its geometric elegance and modernist essence with a refined touch suited for today's typographic needs. [ rsztype.com ]

typefaces.name: Ssonder
typefaces.desc: Ssonder is a Serif typeface inspired by the feeling of profound realization that each person you encounter has their own intricate and unique life, forming a delicate web of experiences and memories. With this in mind, Ssonder has been crafted to reflect the interconnectedness of individual stories through its design. The beautiful ligature stylistic sets and unconventional proportions create connections and unique flow within and between characters, symbolizing the connections that bind us all. Each letter is designed to maintain a sense of depth and sophistication. [ typeoffeeling.com ]

typefaces.name: ST Guust
typefaces.desc: Guust is part of ‘Typo Belgiëque’, a practice oriented scientific research & type design project examining the visual design identity of Belgium in the nineteenth and twentieth century that breathes new life into Belgium’s historical typeface families. Guust is a respectful contemporary interpretation of an extraordinary typeface for posters and pamphlets that originates from the type collection of Fonderie Typographique A. Vanderborght & Dumont, a 19th century Belgian type foundry in Brussels. [ studiotype.be ]

typefaces.name: ST Toone
typefaces.desc: Toone is a new original font family inspired by a thin wooden, elongated poster typeface from the printing type collection of Fonderie Typographique A. Vanderborght & Dumont, a 19th century Belgian type foundry in Brussels. The Toone font family includes a tall spiky serif & a sans serif version of the same regular type style. The slender and condensed look delivers a clean & contemporary style which makes Toone very suitable for logo’s, editorial & poster design, film credits, advertising, branding and packaging design. Toone is part of ‘Typo Belgiëque’, a practice oriented scientific research & type design project examining the visual design identity of Belgium in the nineteenth and twentieth century that breathes new life into Belgium’s historical typeface families. [ studiotype.be ]

typefaces.name: Staten
typefaces.desc: Inspired by the timeless catalogue of the masterful Sanborn Insurance Maps, Staten honors the past while adding copious amounts of utility. Similar to one of the mryiad tertiary typefaces seen in many of Sanborn’s maps, Staten maintains the authentic adaptability of its luminary counterpart. Whether it be the triple condensed or triple expanded weights to its oblique and reverse oblique angles, or the myriad alternative glyphs imbuing charm and customizability, Staten stands shoulders apart from revivalist typefaces and maps a new road into the future. [ cantrelltype.com ]

typefaces.name: Staten Sans
typefaces.desc: Inspired by the timeless catalogue of the masterful Sanborn Insurance Maps, Staten Sans honors the past while adding copious amounts of utility. Similar to one of the mryiad tertiary typefaces seen in many of Sanborn’s maps, Staten maintains the authentic adaptability of its luminary counterpart. Whether it be the triple condensed or triple expanded weights to its oblique and reverse oblique angles, or the myriad alternative glyphs imbuing charm and customizability, Staten stands shoulders apart from revivalist typefaces and maps a new road into the future. [ cantrelltype.com ]

typefaces.name: Stellar
typefaces.desc: The serif font Stellar arose from the desire to respond to the change in language through design and to promote the use of gender-equitable formulations. Stellar contains various gender characters such as the asterisk, which can be seamlessly varied in size and position thanks to variable font technology. Inktraps and calligraphic endings give Stellar its character. As a text font, Stellar is also easy to read in small point sizes. [ moontype.de ]

typefaces.name: Sticky
typefaces.desc: Sticky is a typeface utilizing the limitation of writing with masking tape. Sticky was inspired by sign painting, classical italics, and pichação style graffiti. The typeface has multiple ligatures and automatic alternative letters to create tight spacing and a convincing sign painting feeling. With simple strokes and economic structures, the typeface is perfect for headlines and call for actions. Sticky was initiated by Simon Memel, Lucrezia Noro and Eran Ben Barak in the class of Kai Bernau and finalised by Eran Ben Barak in 2023.

typefaces.name: STK Bureau Sans
typefaces.desc: Bureau is a cross-genre sans and serif type family. Stylistically the families lend from modern giants and idols, while firmly establishing an identity within their boundaries and language. STK Bureau comes in 2 styles (Sans + Serif), with four matching weights (Light, Book, Medium, Bold). The two styles can intertwine across applications because of its matching skeleton. Bureau is a workhorse, yet strongwilled – like the stallion in 'Spirit’ (Dreamworks, 2002). [ typekiosk.smuss.studio ]

typefaces.name: STK Bureau Serif
typefaces.desc: Bureau is a cross-genre sans and serif type family. Stylistically the families lend from modern giants and idols, while firmly establishing an identity within their boundaries and language. STK Bureau comes in 2 styles (Sans + Serif), with four matching weights (Light, Book, Medium, Bold). The two styles can intertwine across applications because of its matching skeleton. Bureau is a workhorse, yet strongwilled – like the stallion in 'Spirit’ (Dreamworks, 2002). [ typekiosk.smuss.studio ]

typefaces.name: STK Earl
typefaces.desc: There’s a new sherif in town. Earl is our slab serif with swagger. Bold but playful, it packs a punch with regressive ball-terminals and unexpected finials. Beneath its eye-catching personality lies a treasure trove of features and ligatures. [ typekiosk.smuss.studio ]

typefaces.name: STK Gerhard
typefaces.desc: Gerhard is a no-nonsense monospaced family, from 'Light' to 'Bold'. With slits in its joints for improved legibility and clearer construction, it takes its democratic cues from its namesake - Norway's post-war prime minister Einar Gerhardsen. In true social democratic fashion, every character gets exactly the same space. [ typekiosk.smuss.studio ]

typefaces.name: STK Hugo
typefaces.desc: Hugo is a new typeface based on traditional antiquas, and it gets its personality from its exaggerated serifs and the letter shapes' links and terminals. The character varies distinctively through the weights. Hugo acts as a dramatized antiqua with contemporary features in the display cut, best suited for modern usage. 'Hugo Book' is the rational counterpart to the 'Display' cut. With traits and qualities that ensure comfortable reading and delivery on a high functional level. In between sits the 'Regular' cut that borrows from both – a flamboyant pragmatic, you dare say. [ typekiosk.smuss.studio ] Appears to be retired as of January 2025.

typefaces.name: STK Miso
typefaces.desc: Miso is a round and wide sans serif that comes in six weights. Like our studio dog Billie, it's sturdy, friendly, and impossible not to love. Use Miso when you need a sans serif that makes everyone smile while getting the job done. [ typekiosk.smuss.studio ]

typefaces.name: STK Rom
typefaces.desc: Rom is a typeface drawn in the spirits of Univers, designed by Adrian Frutiger. The project started as a revival – but evolved into an exercise of controlling the temperament, yet keeping the apparent contrast and character known from Univers. The project resulted in a versatile family suited for editorial use and complex typesetting. [ typekiosk.smuss.studio ] Appears to be retired as of January 2025.

typefaces.name: STK Saga
typefaces.desc: Saga is our take on a modern classic. At reading size, it's all about comfort and clarity, but zoom in and you'll spot its playful side - from low-riding x-heights to bouncy ball-terminals. A cheerful, yet serious partner in crime. [ typekiosk.smuss.studio ]

typefaces.name: Stop
typefaces.desc: Originally designed by Aldo Novarese in 1971.

typefaces.name: Stornoway
typefaces.desc: Elegant fonts usually have extremely high contrast and crisp delicate shapes, but Stornoway’s version of elegance is a little more sturdy than that—it won’t fall apart from being too delicate. Inspired by the charm of Scotch Roman faces and Dwiggins’ Caledonia, Stornoway brings the style a bit further into the modern era with a higher x-height, flared terminals, and no serifs. The name “Stornoway” comes from an Island town in the Outer Hebrides in Northern Scotland, a town where my ancestors come from. The high contrast styles are great for display work and can effortlessly express Art Deco, the ideals of modern architecture and interior design, or graceful menus and signage. The low contrast styles are based closely on the same structure but with enough mass to perform very nicely in body text situations. The heavier weights in the low contrast style offer a unique chunky character that would be right at home on food and drink packaging. True italics provide sparkling, expressive styles that provide more ways to include the concept of sturdy elegance into your projects. [ arcanetype.com ] Produced as a variable font with weight and contrast axes.

typefaces.name: Stratum 1 & 2 Condensed
typefaces.desc: Infused with the energy and modernity of the original width, Stratum Condensed is a family of six space-saving fonts. Designed for the narrow confines of mobile phones and display headline environments, the typeface remains legible through the entire weight range. In addition to tabular numerals and directional arrows, Stratum Condensed supports the Greek and Cyrillic scripts. Like its regular-width companion Stratum, Stratum Condensed is offered in two distinct flavors: Stratum 1 Condensed features sharp, angled terminations, whereas Stratum 2 Condensed has flat terminations for a uniform feel. [ processtypefoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Striated
typefaces.desc: Support for the Cyrillic script added in February 2025.

typefaces.name: Subito
typefaces.desc: Subito is a contemporary almost monolinear geometric typeface inspired by the classics like AvantGarde and Century Gothic , but designed with more versatility in mind. Well-proportioned and balanced, it shares a generous x-height with these. Its narrower width makes it great for longer texts, not just titles. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: SubSans
typefaces.desc: SubSans emerged from research dedicated to exploring new shapes for a subtitling typeface tailored to the demands of the streaming services era, particularly for the fields of film and television. Quickly developing a fascination with the humanist sans-serif genre, the typeface is drawing inspiration in its construction from the timeless directional signage fonts of the 1960s and 1970s by Adrian Frutiger such as Concorde and Alphabet Roissy, as well as the display characteristics and memorability of Ernst Friz’s Friz Quadrata. Especially its dynamic contrast, curved stroke endings as well as short ascenders and descenders have proved to be an influence. Despite its historical influences, Subtype strives for an original, non-nostalgic feel. This typeface excels in delivering high legibility and a distinct, memorable character, even on the smallest screens, thanks to its dynamic curves, low contrast, and uniquely angled-cut stroke endings. The outcome is a robust humanist sans-serif font family offering a wide spectrum of weights, ranging from Hairline and Thin to Light, Regular, Medium, Semibold, Bold, and Black. The inclusion of italic cuts - created with a calligraphic approach to

typefaces.name: Sud
typefaces.desc: Sud was designed in 2015 by Jérémy Schneider as part of the 2015-2016 identity of the « Théâtre des Bouffes du Nord » in Paris. The font is particular for its unlikely widths, where some letters tend to surprisingly expand or trim themselves. It was conceived together with Nord, a bolder sister version, both intending to harmoniously co-exist in the graphic identity of the theater. [ vj-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Sudo
typefaces.desc: Sudo is a font designed for terminals, programming, and user interfaces. Use at 16 pixels size for optimal results. It has a monospaced variant, simply called Sudo, and a proportional variant, called Sudo UI. A Variable Font version is available. It has an extra variation axis to modify the length of descenders. [ github.com ] Released as open-source.

typefaces.name: Sulfite
typefaces.desc: Sulfite is a purposefully imperfect typeface with warmth and friendliness key to its distinction. Drawing of the typeface began with an intuitive approach with its character evolving in an organic manner. As the typeface started to define itself, references were sought out to solidify coherency. The process of development started around the heavier weights. With their respective ‘bulk’ it was more clear where opportunities lay in defining the personality of Sulfite. The extreme heavy weight was a priority early on. Oppose to being treated as a ‘heavier’ version of a lighter weight, considerations were given to the Extra Black to ensure it could stand alone as much as it could be part of a family. With the identity of Sulfite defined, personality traits worked their way down through the spectrum with consideration allowing the lighter styles to play a more pratical role in application. In the spirit of character, alternate letterforms are included to extend the dynamics of the typeface. [ luxtypo.com ]

typefaces.name: Summerford
typefaces.desc: Appears to be retired as of 2025.

typefaces.name: Super Castel
typefaces.desc: Accessible by enrollment into Production Type’s Beta program.

typefaces.name: SuperBlue
typefaces.desc: SuperBlue is a casual, cheerful sans serif family designed by Seán Donohoe, a Danish type designer and sign painter. Seán crafted the first version of the family during his time in the TypeMedia master’s program in type design at the Royal School of Art (KABK) in The Hague. While making initial sketches, he took advantage of his sign-painting skills, using two flat brushes to define SuperBlue’s basic forms. Despite its spontaneous appearance, SuperBlue does not break with the canon of traditional letterforms. Designers can readily use it to set text on paper and screens without encountering any legibility issues. Moreover, the incised appearance of its stems give words set in capital letters or small caps a remarkable elegance. [ re-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Superficial
typefaces.desc: Superficial is a display typeface inspired by liquid materials, bubbly shapes and happy summerly moods. [ carmen-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Supermassive
typefaces.desc: Hefty and idiosyncratic, Supermassive squeezes maximal weight and density out of the available space without sacrificing subtlety or soul. Responding to themes from 1960s handlettering styles, it presents long superelliptical curves and a teetering balance of vertical and horizontal weights. Minimal negative spaces push mass to a precarious extreme. In three cap-only styles drawn for headline sizes — and larger! — Supermassive is not quite stable, but always forceful.

typefaces.name: SUSE
typefaces.desc: Comissioned by the SUSE software company and released as open-source on GitHub.

typefaces.name: Svatopluk
typefaces.desc: Sans serif fonts, especially the neo-grotesques, have become a timeless favorite in the design world. They are praised for their clean lines, simplicity, and adaptability. Svatopluk is just a little curlier than everyone else. What sets Svatopluk apart is its unique, playful curves, all while maintaining a highly functional design. This font was inspired by a remarkable 7-year-old boy who has a deep fascination with technical things, from trains and planes to trams and engineering marvels. And let’s not forget, he’s also a dedicated Lego builder. [ superiortype.com ]

typefaces.name: Swanstone
typefaces.desc: Expanded in October 2024 to several weights, matching italics and support for the Cyrillic script [ newsletter ].

typefaces.name: Swiza
typefaces.desc: We’re excited to introduce Swiza, a sans-serif font family inspired by the timeless principles of Swiss design, reimagined for today’s needs.

typefaces.name: Synch
typefaces.desc: A contemporary, reverse-contrast, psychedelic typeface blowing in the wind. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Sys
typefaces.desc: A condensed typeface, originally designed to replace Verdana as a system font. Updated as Sys 2.0 .

typefaces.name: Sys 2.0
typefaces.desc: A revisiting of Sys (2002), produced in eight weights in upright and italics.

typefaces.name: Systm
typefaces.desc: SYSTM is a modular and metric font family built by two components – a quadrant and a square — displayed on a grid. Its design has been made to satisfy any grid obsession while echoing pavement’s principles, brutalist architecture, early interface designs and modular design in the broadest sense. Featuring one variable axis, applying to the outlines’ thickness, SYSTM lets designers reach any kind of style, weight and text grayness. Above all, SYSTM has been designed to provide an efficient and versatile visual identity tool – including over 1000 glyphs, multiple stylistic sets and grids both for latin and cyrillic letters. Make SYSTM your system. [ blazetype.eu ]

typefaces.name: T1 Korium
typefaces.desc: T1 Korium is a powerful, contemporary sans serif font family of 5 separate cuts equipped with variable font technology. Packing a punch with its dynamic rhythm, beginning with the highly stressed Ss, definitive features, like the angular terminals on letters like Kk and Ss, were designed to merge at the same height to keep a consistent texture across long words while remaining bold and expressive. T1 Korium’s namesake was inspired by corium, a deadly, lava-like material created in the core of a nuclear reactor during a meltdown incident. You can find the character set packed with symbols you would associate with a nuclear plant setting, like a complete set of wayfinding arrows, the Atom, Biohazard, Radioactivity symbols, chemical signs, and more Unicode easter eggs. [ t1-foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: T1 Robit
typefaces.desc: T1 ROBIT is a tech brutal typeface with huge ink traps and humanistic shapes. Drawing inspiration from sci-fi visual culture, futurism, and industrial design, T1 ROBIT consists of 5 styles with variable font technology, providing users with plenty of opportunities for experimentation. [ t1-foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: T1 Zirbal
typefaces.desc: The harsh weather of the subalpine zone sharpened the extremely resistant and yet vibrant Zirbal to what it is today. Zirbal is a robust display and headline typeface that can adapt to the most adverse conditions and formats. Whether in extra wide or very narrow environments, Zirbal is convertible and can expand from Condensed to Extended. Like its namesake the Swiss Pine, with its sinker roots that reach into the deepest crevices of rock and anchor the tree, Zirbal is distinguished primarily by its very narrow spacing, which makes the typeface appear so robust yet contemporary. Like the cone of the Swiss Pine, another focus of this typeface is the fluid gender. This focus is expressed in a special (gender) feature of the typeface, which automatically adjusts the asterisk to match the previously running letter. Born in the alpine region – ready for the big world – it spreads its lateral roots to find use in a wide variety of applications. From headlines in magazines to posters, labels, logos, and entire brand identities, Zirbal is an ideal companion for your next design expedition. [ t1-foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Tablet Gothic
typefaces.desc: Tablet Gothic is a sans serif family for digital and print publications needing both flexibility and graphic coherence amidst dense amounts of information. It delivers the sturdy, straightforward, and clean appearance expected from a grotesque while allowing its personality to stand out on the page. [ type-together.com ] Substantially updated in 2024 with increased character set, as a variable font with weight and width axes.

typefaces.name: Tac
typefaces.desc: Tac is the initial release of a single style, bold weight, sans serif typeface project that is inspired by the wordmark of one of the most significant festivals in Africa's post-colonial history, Festac '77. As an inspired revival, it expands upon the six lowercase letters, single quotes and numeral 7 in the festival's wordmark, resulting in a contemporary font with comprehensive language support for all African languages that are commonly written with the Latin writing system. [ afrotype.com ] Released as open-source on GitHub.

typefaces.name: Talkie
typefaces.desc: Introducing Talkie, a fresh and dynamic typeface that's ready to infuse personality into your projects. With a versatile range of weights and a variable font option for full family packs, this typeface offers endless creative possibilities. If you're seeking a touch of contemporary flair, Talkie effortlessly adds vibrancy and character to any project, whether you're crafting captivating branding materials or packaging projects, Talkie is your go-to choice. [ typeverything.com ]

typefaces.name: Talon
typefaces.desc: Talon is an ornamental condensed display typeface from the hand of Richard Lipton. The seed of the idea was a handful of characters drawn by the Los Angeles graphic designer Margo Chase. From this scattering of capitals, Lipton organized and designed a complete display typeface, capital and lowercase, figures, and punctuation, expanding and capturing the West Coast originality that characterizes the work of Margo Chase. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Tangier
typefaces.desc: With Tangier, Richard Lipton continues to explore the possibilities of the elegant Spencerian form in its infinite variety. Inspired by lettering on a catalog cover, Lipton developed this lively series, exuberant yet disciplined, with a black weight that pushes the boundaries for contrast in a script. Captivated by Tangier’s flair and sprightly joie de vivre, Glamour magazine incorporated two weights into their 2008 redesign. [ liptonletterdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: Tanja
typefaces.desc: Typefaces made from circles are an intriguing proposition for graphic designers. Many are created for technical reasons, such as for the dot matrix printers, or for large screens at sports events. Often they are simple sans serif forms, but Tanja is something unique; a Renaissance dot typeface. Based on the monolinear Marian 1554, Tanja began life as the proposed logo for a German publisher. Though the idea is simple, a seriffed dot typefaces, in its details it reveals a complexity as the dots vary gradually in size. Like Marian, it closely follows the historical models of Garamond and Granjon, but has a contemporary aesthethic, a remix of a remix of a classic. Designed as a display typeface for sizes above 30 point, it comes with various numeral styles, small capitals, swash letters and ligatures. [ commercialtype.com ]

typefaces.name: Tanklager
typefaces.desc: Tanklager ("tank farm" in German) is a typeface inspired by a weird hand-painted sign found on the side of an oil tank in Visp, Switzerland. Tanklager made its debut in the 9th issue of a review called Jef Klak, which was dedicated to ingestion and digestion. Its type design is a mixture of DIN and grotesk features, where capital and lowercase letters sometimes have different structures. Some shapes are blatantly recycled, like the f and the t; sometimes there aren't enough optical corrections and sometimes they are pushed too hard, like in the X or in the letter apexes. The diacritics are very geometrical and they're having a blast. The typeface comes in two cuts: Original (its width is similar to that of the original sign) and Kompakt (for more effective titles). The category is: all the dirty tricks at once. [ tunera.xyz ]

typefaces.name: Tasman
typefaces.desc: Originally published by OurType, Dan Milne’s Tasman has found a new home at Retype. Milne first conceived Tasman as a typeface for newspapers. This influenced the proportions and look of the face considerably: the goal was to keep the personality as warm and playful as possible without losing the credible tone required to deliver all kinds of news. A sturdy, warm type family that is neither mechanical nor fragile. It borrows its name from Abel Janszoon Tasman (1603–1659), a Dutch seafarer, explorer, and merchant who mapped parts of Australia in 1642, including Van Diemen’s Land (now known as Tasmania). Tasman’s primary purpose is an unbiased presentation of information; it strives for neutrality over elegance. Its characters are sturdy and unambiguous, sporting strong serifs, punctuation, and diacritics, as well as generously sized small caps and hybrid figures. Rationalized letterforms give the face enough robustness to withstand the stress of screen applications and laser printing. The figures’ three-quarter x-height makes them considerably larger than traditional oldstyle numerals, yet they still integrate with the lowercase much better than lining figures do. [ re-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Taurus Grotesk
typefaces.desc: An interpretation of Venus .

typefaces.name: Tausend
typefaces.desc: https://www.commarts.com/exhibit/tausend + https://www.commarts.com/exhibit/tausend

typefaces.name: TDN Dingbats
typefaces.desc: As a big dingbat fan and user, I had to create my own set. [ typedunord.com ]

typefaces.name: Tegner
typefaces.desc: Tegner was inspired by a visit to the Museum of Rudolph Tegner. A poster from an exhibition at the Independent Artspace Den Frie in Copenhagen from 1911 featured very special letters that resonated with the roughness of the museum's concrete building. Square on the outside and organic on the inside, with a set of unicase lowercase, smaller captials, a triangular space character and an owl. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Tekio Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Despite being an idiosyncratic grotesk with a raw character it is drawn on an eight point grid which makes its rhythm, vertical and horizontal dimensions highly organised. [ store.tekio.work ]

typefaces.name: Teléfono
typefaces.desc: Teléfono is a cute and thin connected script, with a handwritten flow and a versatile simplicity. Inspired by curly telephone wires and wall climbing vines, it effortlessly connects words to big feelings and, hopefully, to people. The lowercase is charming and simple, making any word look clean and distinctive. And when adding an initial capital, it evokes 20th century business writing, but with a modern twist. As a confident script should, Teléfono has extreme vertical proportions: A reduced x-height allows ascenders and descenders to own their fair share of space, giving an air of elegance to the lines of text. Teléfono shines when set big, and when given space to play. We hope you enjoy it! [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Teletext
typefaces.desc: Teletext is a humanist pixel typeface designed by Adrian Frutiger in 1979, and released by Maxitype in 2025. While consulting the extensive Frutiger archive at the Museum für Gestaltung’s Graphics Collection in Zürich, Maximage’s interest was piqued by a mysterious bundle named [Caractères TVP / Teletext]. The folder contained a large quantity of sheets featuring pixel letters drawn by hand onto a 16 × 16 xeroxed grid. Its matrices had an unusual ratio of 1:2 which created narrow vertical proportions. The folder also contained various optical correction tests, alternative glyphs and even attempts to simulate the effect of screen glow on the typeface. Every single piece of paper punctiliously bore the refrain of Frutiger’s initials—AF—which gave it the air of a quality-control stamp by the master. The screen typeface was commissioned around 1979 by the French electronics manufacturer Thomson-CSF for the new Paris Charles de Gaulle airport, which had opened in 1974. It was only a small addition to the wider signage of the airport, which was typeset in Alphabet Roissy, the main typeface that Frutiger had designed in 1970 (and which would later evolve into the “Frutiger” typeface). Alp

typefaces.name: Terrane
typefaces.desc: Terrane is a humanist typeface designed to open dialogues. It exemplifies the dualities inherent in humanist design by balancing apparent simplicity with subtle complexity. As a low-contrast sans-serif, Terrane projects clarity and openness with forms that feel culturally grounded and organic. While Terrane’s design roots are firmly planted in the humanist sans tradition, the serif counterpart explores more exotic, lesser-known traits. Methodical and modern, Terrane proposes a synthesis of warmth and exactitude. [ productiontype.com ]

typefaces.name: Terza
typefaces.desc: Greg Gazdowicz’s heuristic exploration of the various ways humans interact with digital text led him to design Terza, a typeface in three modes (or “speeds”). Terza Reader, the fastest variant, takes cues from Bembo, Centaur, and Poliphilus, all based on the Aldine text types cut by Griffo. Terza Author, ideal for composing new material on screen, decelerates the tempo by becoming wider and airier. And Terza Editor, the slowest variant, embraces the tradition of monospaced typewriter faces to create a steady, incantatory rhythm—perfect for writing on writing.
