[ commercialtype.com ] Updated with a Display family in October 2024.

typefaces.name: Thow
typefaces.desc: Thow is (going to be) a workhorse serif, that captures the essence of transitional mixed with modern genre while introducing unique and contemporary flourishes that evoke a heritage of historical elegance. Inspired by the design of the "Đông Dương Tạp Chí" newspaper (1913-1919), Thow draws from transitional serifs like Baskerville, Caslon, and Times New Roman, … It features a large x-height, open terminals, and distinct diacritics, creating a unique yet highly legible typeface suited for long-form text. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Tid
typefaces.desc: Tid, by Letters from Sweden and Stefania Malmsten, is an interpretation of The Best Typeface in the World, a typeface and an idea that Göran Söderström and Stefania have both been obsessed with throughout their working lives. Initially created for Moderna Museet in Stockholm, a first version of Tid was introduced during their extensive exhibition with Laurie Andersson – an artist who works with text and language – in the spring of 2023. [ lettersfromsweden.se ]

typefaces.name: Tifo
typefaces.desc: Tifo takes its inspiration from the lettering that can be found on the banners brandished by the most fervent tifosi (supporters) during football matches. Emerging in Italian stadiums in the early days of the Years of Lead, these supporters showed their support for their favorite team using banners, chants, and smoke bombs. Initiated by Roman Tronchin in 2021 as part of the ECAL’s Master’s degree in Type Design, the Tifo typeface comes in five styles: Roma, Venezia, Bologna, Palermo, and Milano. Romain Tronchin developed this typeface by carefully examining tifosi fanzines from the 1970s and 1980s, with each variant corresponding to a different style of lettering. Some “oddities” visible in these vernacular sources–which could rightly be considered as typographic errors–were intentionally conserved. They provide Tifo with a singular and authentic character that is part of a long-standing tradition of typically Italian public lettering. The five styles of Tifo share the same underlying frame, but each one “wears its own colors”! With a geometrical construction, and a design reduced to elementary forms, the Roma (with square counterforms), Venezia (with its rectangular outlines and c

typefaces.name: Timáukel
typefaces.desc: Timaukel is a Dutch-inspired serif typeface, with calligraphic-inspired shapes and more curved lines than its references. The name comes from the Selk'nam People, who lived and lives in Tierra del Fuego, in the south of the world; and their divinity is called Temáukel or Timáukel, it is also a place on the same island. It is a typeface in four variants: Regular, Italic, Black and Black Italic, in this second version. It also contains the basic set, its Small Caps, Swash Capitals, terminal forms, alternative k letter, oldstyle and lining figures, tabular numbers, as well as superscripts, subscripts, fractions and other OpenType characteristics to compose complex and long texts. [ futurefonts.com ] Updated November 2024 with Black and Black Italic styles.

typefaces.name: Tinta
typefaces.desc: The Tinta Typeface is a rebellion against sterility and cold perfection. In a time dominated by supersharp offset printing and screen typography, Tipografies embarks on a search of lost warmth. The goal is to recreate the mood of Renaissance printmaking. Tinta utilizes variable font technology to bring back the vulnerable quality of letterforms. A dynamic sans of classical proportions, Tinta is characterized by organic forms with curving contours and flared endings. The serifless roman is complemented by an animated italic. Rather than engaging in a digital copy of the types cut by Jenson or Griffo, Tinta is concerned with capturing the spirit found in works from the 15th century. [ tipografies.com ]

typefaces.name: Tiny Gothic
typefaces.desc: A sans serif typeface inspired by the ingenious solutions of punchcutters who crafted typefaces for optimal legibility at minute sizes . Not to be confused with Tiny Grotesk , released earlier by Tiny Type Co. .

typefaces.name: Tiny Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Not to be confused with Tiny Gothic , released later by Optimo .

typefaces.name: Tiro Malayalam
typefaces.desc: Tiro Malayalam is available in two orthographic flavours: the standard fonts supporting the traditional orthography for Malayalam, Sanskrit, and Pāli texts, and the ‘R’ fonts supporting the simplified, reformed orthography for Malayalam introduced in the early 1970s. The fonts share a common glyph set, and the default traditional or reformed behaviours can be overridden at the cluster level using formatting control characters as specified in the Unicode Standard. The design of Tiro Malayalam is inspired by the proportions and features of 19th Century metal types, including a slight slanting of vertical strokes that enliven text. [ tiro.com ]

typefaces.name: Tiro Sinhala
typefaces.desc: Tiro Sinhala is designed to be comparable in weight and proportion with other Tiro Indic fonts, and like them is especially well-suited to traditional literary publishing but also made with the needs of today’s multiple print and screen media in mind. The design is informed by the conventions of 19th Century metal types, but particularly inspired by handwritten and engraved lettering of that period, reflecting the transition from Sri Lankan palm leaf manuscripts to writing with European pens. The fonts support the modern, simplified orthography as defined as default behaviour in the Unicode Standard, but also use of the ZWJ formatting control character to affect traditional conjunct forms. In additional to Sinhala language, the fonts can be used for Sanskrit and Pāli texts. [ tiro.com ]

typefaces.name: Tlayuda
typefaces.desc: Born from a TypeCooker session, Tlayuda is a display typeface that has a very intense and contrasting vertical rhythm, this reverse contrast typeface was made for bold and extravagant moves. Tlayuda plays with the design space in unconventional ways, featuring two (future) vertical axes: waist and xHeight, and two (also future) horizontal axes: width and serif extensions. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Tofua
typefaces.desc: Appears to be retired as of January 2025.

typefaces.name: Tomate
typefaces.desc: ‘Tomate’ started in 2006 as a brush lettering exercise for a poster, and was later used for the ReType identity. In 2008 its author decided to turn it into a super fat typeface suitable for packaging and mass consumption products. The possibilities of ultra heavy forms are explored in this alphabet; trying to solve the design problems that these sort of forms present. ‘Tomate’ shows influences from the beautiful ‘Goudy Heavyface Italic’ which is a design the author admires. [ re-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Totokin
typefaces.desc: Totokin is a moderately reverse-contrast slab serif typeface, distinguished by its unique blend of soft curves, gentle forms, and sturdy structure. This defining style creates a harmonious balance between readability and visual appeal, making it a versatile choice for various design applications. The reverse-contrast feature, where horizontal strokes are thicker than vertical ones, lends Totokin a subtle but noticeable personality, setting it apart from traditional slab serif typefaces. [ inhousetype.com ]

typefaces.name: Tradition
typefaces.desc: Tradition is a caligraphic serif font, from the hands of Percy Delf Smith, and digitised by Mads Wildgaard in 2024. The design itself distills the principles from which Delf Smith gained recognition — open forms, subtle serifs but an expressive spirit. The shapes themselves aided the generation of gc16, which became a reinterpretation of these gentle expressions in a digital language.

typefaces.name: Tragic Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Tragic Grotesk is not neutral: On the contrary, it attempts to negotiate a mediating act between warmth and humanity on the one hand and technical directness on the other. The shapes and proportions of Tragic Grotesk were designed with the aim of balance and harmony. The openings such as a, c, e and s are semi-open and the stroke endings of these letters are slightly slanted. Furthermore elements from pre-Helvetica times were mixed in: references to the design of grotesque typefaces from the late 19th century. Further design properties: Technical, »DIN«-related straight lines have been injected into the round shapes. And finally the ever so slightly curved diagonal strokes as a nod to the calligraphic origins of type. In total Tragic Grotesk is not neutral: It conveys warmth and digital clarity. [ charactertype.com ]

typefaces.name: Tranemo
typefaces.desc: Tranemo is a geometric sans-serif. A modern interpretation of the typeface used on road signs in Sweden. For Swedish people, Tranemo brings to mind an authoritarian and credible – but friendly – voice. A typeface Swedish people have a relationship to. [ nymarktype.co ]

typefaces.name: Transept
typefaces.desc: Transept is a two masters, variable pixel typeface. It is inspired by the aesthetics of architectural floor plans of roman and gothic churches. The roman style serves as a bold or regular, and the gothic style can be seen as a light style. Its variable compatibility allows for some expressive and experimental styles. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Traviata
typefaces.desc: Traviata is a display font released in 2017 by Violaine & Jérémy. Designed for the 2017-2018 identity of the « Théâtre des Bouffes du Nord » in Paris, this font was directly inspired by the adaptation of the play La Traviata by Benjamin Lazar, Florent Hubert and Judith Chemla. Traviata starts with a large classical structure offering shy serifs and becomes an expressive force through its unusual details, such as a long apex and strokes, as well as the mix of a traditional construction and very geometrical shapes. The result is a well-balanced, contrasted and elegant font, perfect for display use, especially with a strong colorful palette. [ vj-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Trente Cinq
typefaces.desc: A geometric sans serif informed by the lettering found on vintage film posters and 1940s French cinema. Named after the 35mm film format used in traditional cinematography.

typefaces.name: Trola
typefaces.desc: The Trola family is related to the sans serif Bulo. They share the skeleton, but Trola has a completely different flavour. Its unusual proportions make it particularly recommended for generous sizes and still fit in tight spaces. It can also be considered a headline with a moderate contrast to gain presence and make a stronger screen display. Trola Text keeps the original spirit of Trola, but some of the letterform features have been modified so it can perfectly adapt to the needs of typefaces used in text of continued reading. [ tipografies.com ]

typefaces.name: True Sans
typefaces.desc: Extended styles added in July 2023.

typefaces.name: True Serif
typefaces.desc: After a blown engine in the valley of Vertical Metrics, we’ve finally arrived on the release day of True Serif. The sibling to True Sans, a family of fonts stuck somewhere between dreams of grandiosity, Seamless User-friendliness®, and utter vagueness. Despite these theatrical first few paragraphs, the fonts hail from a range of design principles I distilled from a few ’60s 70’s typefaces — some grand and which have served on a plethora of applications from then til now and for millennia to come, and some which sadly became forgotten despite their need to belong in the world. This family is a re-actualisation of these design traits that I admire so much and want to see used, despite the chance that this actual font family too will go into oblivion. [ instagram.com ]

typefaces.name: Trujillo BT
typefaces.desc: We had the opportunity to participate in the research and digitalization of the typographic revival project inspired by the work of the renowned Colombian artist Sergio Trujillo Magnenat. The 'typographic revival' is not just about replicating or scanning old forms; it also involves adapting and modernizing these forms to ensure they function in a contemporary context. Sergio Trujillo Magnenat, known for his prolific career as a visual artist in Colombia, left an artistic legacy that has endured through the decades. Born in Bogotá in 1911, his work ranged from illustrations and book covers to the creation of iconic logos and posters, such as those designed for the 'IX Centenary of the Bolivarian Games,' a sort of Latin American Olympic Games, held back in 1938. On the other hand, the creation of this typeface was part of a research and recovery project of alphabets and typefaces made in Colombia in the early 20th century, led by the Instituto Caro y Cuervo, a prestigious institution dedicated to the study and preservation of Colombia’s cultural heritage. Many letters were reinterpreted from Trujillo’s other works, or in some cases, created entirely from scratch. This is achieved by

typefaces.name: Trust Sans
typefaces.desc: Trust Sans is a friendly typeface, with a flowing ductus and humanistic construction that helps designers meet the challenges of everyday life. [ fonts.antoniolechuga.com ] Originally released with Latinotype in 2019 [ behance.net ], reissued in 2024.

typefaces.name: TT Biersal
typefaces.desc: TT Biersal is a display sans serif with a free-spirited, playful, and adventurous nature. The concept of this font was sparked by a German poster from the early 1930s. We aimed to maintain the proportions of the reference along with an unpolished, lively feel of its lettering. As a result, we got a vibrant, dense font with narrow proportions and asymmetrical forms. [ typetype.org ]

typefaces.name: TT Drugs
typefaces.desc: TT Drugs is a typeface that doesn’t feature serifs but stands out for its high contrast. Its narrow terminals lend an elegant and sophisticated appearance. Interestingly, the upper parts of stems in letters like ‘n’, ‘m’, ‘p’, ‘q’, ‘r’ and the lower elements of strokes in ‘a’ and ‘u’ are slightly curved. These details make the font unique and add refinement while maintaining its serious character. The typeface’s name reflects the story of its creation: the font family was initially intended to be used for the pharmaceutical industry. However, in practical use, the font revealed its multiple dimensions and seamlessly blended with differently themed projects. After the update, the typeface has become even more versatile, so now only its provocative title reminds us of the pharmaceutical past of TT Drugs. [ typetype.org ]

typefaces.name: TT Gertika
typefaces.desc: TT Gertika is a geometric sans serif with a dynamic character and a dancing rhythm. This font’s idea originates from the lettering featured on an American poster from the late 1930s. We saw many peculiar and eye-catching details in the letters and decided to reimagine them. As a result, we got a font that alludes to something ancient and primitive while still being modern. [ typetype.org ]

typefaces.name: TT Hoves Pro
typefaces.desc: Updated in 2024 with a monospaced version.

typefaces.name: TT Interphases Pro
typefaces.desc: Updated in March 2025.

typefaces.name: TT Modernoir
typefaces.desc: TT Modernoir is a display sans serif with dynamic proportions. Fluid lines and delicate Art Nouveau forms in this typeface blend seamlessly with the rhythmic flow and improvisational freedom of jazz. To design this font, we drew inspiration from the French typography of the XXth century and noir film aesthetics, which is reflected in its name. The key feature of TT Modernoir is a significant proportion difference between square and oval characters: the square ones are extremely narrow, and the ovals are very wide. The curved letter legs give the font an exquisite look, and the dynamic swirls infuse it with the feeling of musical rhythm and movement. [ typetype.org ]

typefaces.name: TT Paplane
typefaces.desc: TT Paplane is a squared-looking display sans serif. Its name, Paplane, comes from the phrase “paper plane.” This embodies the core idea of our font: the logic of letters is built in a way that makes them look like they are folded from a paper strip. So, this sans serif stands out for its squared forms, 45-degree cuts, flowing outer contours, and asymmetrical smoothing of stroke ends. A playful feel of the font is achieved by varying proportions of lowercase and uppercase characters. Other captivating details include the drops in the Cyrillic alphabet, the forms of the letter “i” and the Cyrillic letter “т,” the tails of “ц” and “щ,” and the serifs of the letters “i” and “l”. TT Paplane includes two font styles with different aesthetics: Regular and Thin. The Regular style is low-contrast and more paper-looking. The Thin style, in turn, features reverse contrast while having the same glyph forms, making the font’s design look like a barcode in use. Uppercase characters in both font styles are noticeably narrower than lowercase, and the letter proportions are closer to monospaced. In addition, the typeface includes a variable font with a weight variation axis. [ typetype.org ]

typefaces.name: Tuaf
typefaces.desc: Tuaf is an experimental Latin & Arabic type family designed for small sizes, started as an EsadType graduation project. The process began with sketches on 2 mm high lines, adhering to strict rules. This approach prompted an exploration of the interplay between the black and white shapes, shaping the writing rhythm over the individual letter details. Rather than a linear increase of weights in the family, the styles changed shape or structure to improve their performance at small sizes. [ futurefonts.com ] The initial version includes the Bold and Bold Italic styles.

typefaces.name: Tugev
typefaces.desc: Tugev is a jugendstil grotesk inspired by a thicket of late nineteenth and early twentieth century expressive sans-serifs. Tugev draws on the formalities of Breite Grotesk, the visual impact of Zeitungs Grotesk and the recherché curves of typefaces like Ronaldson Gothic, Secession, Chicago and Aviso. Specific details take reference from Berthold’s Venus while the height of the cross bars in uppercase letters like E G R draw influence from Jugendstil and Secessionist lettering. The modulation (the stroke contact from thick to thin) is pushed to the extreme in the heavier weights of the terminals of curved letters. These strokes run thin making Tugev firmly non-linear. For contrast the accompanying 'true' italic is inspired by Lining Gothic Italic No. 524 as seen in the 1906 American Line Type Book published by American Type Founders Co. The design of Lining Gothic is closer to true italic forms than a typical oblique italic. It is both flowing and rhythmical and enjoys a stark contrast with the awkward and robust formality of Tugev roman. [ futurefonts.com ] Known as Kapow prior to version 0.3 from September 2024.

typefaces.name: Tuplet
typefaces.desc: Tuplet is a MonoSpace Font. It features a rich set of alternates with Caps, Numbers and Special Characters in Regular und Double Widths. This allows for uniquely interesting options, when dealing with typography. It opens up new ways to fit a line of text. The double wide Caps also lends the text a unique blend of history and modernity. The playful shapes are derived from french renaissance type, with a lot of Jakob Fangmeier-esque charm on top. The outrageous serifs allow for even grey values in the extreme width differences. Overall Tuplet is a very contemporary companion for everything that has to stand out. [ type.design ]

typefaces.name: TWK Burns
typefaces.desc: Burns is a geometric sans serif typeface inspired by the work of Herb Lubalin and in particular his ITC Avant Garde Gothic typeface. Knowing the past while trying to write the future: Burns is a new take on this category of geometric typefaces, distilling a contemporary touch with a highly graphic approach and playful aesthetics. Burns’ design is characterised by its high x-height, minimal tapering and pure geometric shapes. The Ultra cut has become so bold that it allows overlapping strokes and clogged letters, making it unique and expressive. At its boldest weight, it becomes an instant logo generator! However, the font family remains consistent and covers a wide range of weights, from the extremely thin Hairline to the super swollen Ultra. Burns is simple in its geometric design and also versatile with a complete character set and numerous graphic alternates. [ weltkern.com ]

typefaces.name: TWK Continental
typefaces.desc: One of the first questions to answer when starting a design project is, “What will its function be?” Each project offers its unique response, shaping the constraints guiding the resulting design. The story of this typeface began with the idea of creating a signature for a studio—an emerging practice. It was meant to embody an idea, a way of designing. The question then became, Which historical moments should it reference?” TWK Continental is a sans-serif typeface whose DNA blends mechanical and constructed elements inspired by Akzidenz Grotesk with a subtle calligraphic touch, drawing from the teachings of Walter Käch and the Univers of Adrian Frutiger. In striving for a balance between these references, the design aims to produce dark, compact text blocks by reducing the capital height and shortening the ascenders. Through multiple iterations, a cohesive family of weights developed. Gradually, a compact character width was introduced, providing vast creative options. Its simple, honest, and refined forms, rooted in the Swiss graphic design tradition, give it the appearance of studious older sibling who can explain you all about the history of Brutalist architecture—only to find la

typefaces.name: TWK Everett
typefaces.desc: Everett emerged during Nolan Paparelli’s studies at ECAL/University of Art & Design Lausanne, resulting in his diploma work, and has been evolving ever since. Initially inspired by the work of the American photographer Daniel Everett, it quickly became more personal and resulted in his own take on the neogrotesque genre. Everett’s symmetrical structure is balanced with an organic drawing and a particular digital flavour. Strong typographic details at the apexes add a high visual tension while retaining a classic and timeless design, finding the right balance between a font that is graphic yet fluid. Low ascenders and descenders allow designers to set texts with tight line spacing, resulting in economizing space. The fonts are fully equipped with various stylistic sets, ligatures and case-sensitive forms among other features. The weight variation from Hairline to Super with corresponding Italics forms a coherent and versatile family offering various design solutions from book design to poster design, branding to signage systems and much more. [ weltkern.com ]

typefaces.name: TWK Everett Mono
typefaces.desc: Everett Mono is the monospace counterpart to the Everett typeface, designed by Nolan Paparelli. From the outset, a monospaced version of Everett has always been part of the project. Originally only available in Regular, the typographic programme then became more ambitious: how to translate Everett’s 20 weights - its broad proportions and distinctive cuts - into single blocks of fixed size? A real challenge! The design had to find creative ways of compressing and carefully adjusting the letterforms to maintain a high level of legibility while retaining the original Everett flavour. All weights are designed to be used together; each glyph in each weight shares the same width. A particular graphic feature of Everett Mono is its ligatures, which sometimes occupy two or even three blocks, giving it a mechanical feel. Ultimately, Everett Mono is an independent and complementary sub-family, offering a vast choice of typographic styles and features. [ weltkern.com ]

typefaces.name: TWK Ghost
typefaces.desc: Ghost is a carefully drawn, brutalist yet elegant serif typeface. First informed by street letterings and the sharp flow of honorific Wu-Tang Clan member Ghostface Killah, the typeface matured over time, from the street to the magazine cover, from graffiti markers to digital typography. Ghost’s calligraphic axis combined with sharp triangular serifs and low stroke contrast makes it robust and highly legible. Very edgy and spiky, it is a rather rational and constructed serif Roman with a tempered Italic. Ghost maintains a level of delicacy at small sizes while showing all its graphic peculiarities when used in big quotes or headlines. Therefore, it’s a perfect typeface for editorial design; magazines, newspapers, websites, book covers as well as short logotypes and letterings. [ weltkern.com ] Not to be confused with Ghost from Sharp Type.

typefaces.name: TWK Lausanne
typefaces.desc: Originally released by Nizar Kazan in 2019, updated and reissued with Weltkern in 2021. Some versions circulating prior to 2019 [ fontsinuse.com ]. Designed as a modern response to historical sans-serifs like Helvetica, Lausanne brings a contemporary edge shaped by the possibilities of digital typography. This includes the duality and adaptability of distinct “Text” and “Display” styles, ensuring optimal performance across different contexts. Its compact appearance, achieved through short ascenders and descenders, adds to its clean and structured feel, making it as functional as it is elegant. The letter “a” in Lausanne stands out with its distinctive features—particularly the subtle drop-like detail within its form. This organic approach extends to other characters, like the geometric yet almost Roman-inspired shapes found in the “s” or those contained within the “O.” The idea was to create a grotesque sans-serif that feels ultra-organic, almost psychedelic, but in a way that whispers rather than shouts. The inspiration came from the notion that typefaces often perceived as neutral or basic, like Helvetica, can sometimes be seen by designers as almost psychedelic due to their inte

typefaces.name: TwoSix
typefaces.desc: TwoSix is a modular typeface constructed using the stroke geometries of MuirMcNeil’s ThreeSix type system, published in 2014 and now a part of the Monotype collection. The armature of TwoSix has been adapted from the earlier design to correspond with the other typefaces in MuirMcNeil’s extensive Two Type System. The many subgroups that comprise the Two System have not been designed as independent alphabets but as the framework of an expansive design space in which individual glyphs are configured to collaborate with each other harmoniously. [ muirmcneil.com ]

typefaces.name: Typewriter
typefaces.desc: The inspiration for Typewriter came from a found object, namely an Olivetti Letterer 22 typewriter discarded by a tenant who previously occupied our studio. We used a single sheet type proof from the machine as a starting point to create our own distinctive digital typewriter font. Our version of Typewriter has been expanded to incorporate a new glyph set, additional weights, and complimentary italic styles.

typefaces.name: Typewriter Contrast
typefaces.desc: Typewriter Contrast is a quirky iteration of our A2 Typewriter font with square terminals and contrasted weight. The font is a stylish rethink of the typewriter model; contemporary, yet also evoking the mid-century modern era. Typewriter Contrast is an ideal font for setting headlines, pull-quotes, running text, folios, and captions.

typefaces.name: U_Pipe
typefaces.desc: U_Pipe is a multiline companion to U_Type , a collection of stencil typefaces constructed on a shared framework from a minimal set of component parts. In U_Type, every character serves as a blueprint onto which different arrangements of modules are configured automatically. [ muirmcneil.com ]

typefaces.name: U_Type
typefaces.desc: U_Type is a collection of stencil typefaces constructed on a shared framework from a minimal set of component parts. In U_Type, every character serves as a blueprint onto which different arrangements of modules are configured automatically. U_Type consists of six compatible type systems: U_Line, U_Quad, U_Hexa, U_Octo, U_Span. U_Type has been designed in two variant subsets. Set ‘A’ in each system features open intervals or stencil bridges between individual character subcomponents which are reduced to hairline spaces in Set ‘B’. U_Type fonts are designed to interact with one another. Using page layout, bitmap or vector design software, two or more fonts can be overlaid in precise registration or in calibrated offsets allowing the application of multiple outlines, tints, colours, textures, patterns or transparencies. [ muirmcneil.com ]

typefaces.name: Ubu
typefaces.desc: Ubu is a geometric type system in two versions, Ubu Block and Ubu Slab, each drawn in four individual styles that are also intended to correspond with one another in interlocking layers. The typeface is named after Ubu Roi, a dramatic production written by Alfred Jarry in 1896. [ muirmcneil.com ]

typefaces.name: Ubuntu
typefaces.desc: Originally designed by Dalton Maag for Canonical in 2010–2011 and expanded in 2015. In 2023, TypeNetwork and partner foundries Kerns & Cairns , DJR , and DualType were commissioned to create a variable version. Credits after the FONTLOG.txt document.

typefaces.name: Ubuntu Mono
typefaces.desc: The monospaced version of Ubuntu .

typefaces.name: Ultramarina
typefaces.desc: Halfway between nineteenth century display wood letters and the American grotesk sans-serif of the early twentieth, we can find Ultramarina, a novelty serif font for use in large body headlines, which shows its power of attraction to quality food, the country’s legume, and gentlemen with a mustache and apron. Ultramarina has been revamped in 2025 with a better design and wider language coverage. [ mtm.madrid ]

typefaces.name: Umiak
typefaces.desc: Umiak is a take on the Berthold's Corinna (1904) and the 1970s ITC revival Korinna with stylistic influences from typefaces like Cheltenham, New Text, Souvenir and Clearface. The lowercase of Umiak is slightly narrower than the broad face of Korinna but retains those awkward (but stylistically important) little serifs. Also, similar to the 1970s ITC revival, the x-height of Umiak is quite tall allowing generous vertical space for attention grabbing curves in letters like b d g q . However, in order to soften the uppercase and to help it gel with organic flourishes of the lowercase, Umiak has calligraphic touches and curves in high-frequency letters A S T as well as M N V W X Y. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: UN-11
typefaces.desc: Introducing UN-11, a rare cut of the Swiss classic by Adrian Frutiger faithfully digitized and carefully re-engineered for today’s typographic universe. In 1961, IBM unveiled the Selectric Typewriter, featuring a revolutionary type ‘golf ball’ that replaced the traditional typebar mechanism. To expand their font catalog and promote this new technology, IBM enlisted Adrian Frutiger to adapt his iconic Univers, modifying it to suit the machine’s specific constraints and metrics. The result was an alternate version of Univers with unit-based spacing, marking an exciting and distinct departure from conventional monospaced type. To Frutiger, the font’s charmingly uneven rhythm uniquely combined mechanical precision with a human touch. Today, UN-11’s idiosyncrasies stand out in a world of polished interfaces, rounded corners, and total easing. [ sourcetype.com ] For a related effort, see Jens Kutilek ’s article: Reviving the IBM Selectric Composer Fonts .

typefaces.name: Undo Sans
typefaces.desc: The history of inline and neon display typefaces are rich and wild, especially in Phototypesetting catalogues of the 70s. Undo’s construction is based on a geometric grotesque and tries to take it one step further by balancing dark and bright spots that arise from the pairing of sharp and round corner-details and separated stroke endings. [ deinwaller.com ]

typefaces.name: Unicaster
typefaces.desc: Unicaster is a grotesque typeface with a unified case height for both upper and lower case. This style, known as Unicase, provides a strong composition appropriate for short texts, titles, packaging and similar forms that fall into the ‘Display’ category. The original reference to the typography is found on the back cover of the album Part One by the psychedelic group West Coast Pop Art Experimental Band (WCPAEB), published in 1967, where the extensive name of the group appears written in these characters with an irresistible charm. We did some research on the original font and, finding no clues, we decided to offer our personal view of the model. [ type-o-tones.com ]

typefaces.name: Utile
typefaces.desc: Utile started out as an extensive study of numerous sans-serif typefaces that have their roots in the type classification of static Grotesks and Neo Grotesks. In parallel to this exploration and during the design process, divergent consideration came into play, such as maximum flat-open apertures in upper cases (C, G, S) and lower cases (c, s), a concept that was later abandoned to return to more measured apertures with moderately open humanist lower case forms to enhance the reading experience for smaller set text. Although the concept of flat-open apertures was set aside, it provoked an exploration of stroke contrast and an addition of glyphic details that led to lightly swelled terminals for both text and display styles. The asymmetrical incised stem definitions, applied with measure, help to render the type rhythmically animated with a touch of classical letter heritage. To keep reverberations of the pen at its lowest, the majority of upper cases are then also mostly spared of glyphic details generally maintaining a sans identity. The Utile collection is reminiscent of typefaces designed during the mid 20th century enunciating a certain elegance and fluidity. [ kontour.com ]

typefaces.name: Utile Display
typefaces.desc: Utile started out as an extensive study of numerous sans-serif typefaces that have their roots in the type classification of static Grotesks and Neo Grotesks. In parallel to this exploration and during the design process, divergent consideration came into play, such as maximum flat-open apertures in upper cases (C, G, S) and lower cases (c, s), a concept that was later abandoned to return to more measured apertures with moderately open humanist lower case forms to enhance the reading experience for smaller set text. Although the concept of flat-open apertures was set aside, it provoked an exploration of stroke contrast and an addition of glyphic details that led to lightly swelled terminals for both text and display styles. The asymmetrical incised stem definitions, applied with measure, help to render the type rhythmically animated with a touch of classical letter heritage. To keep reverberations of the pen at its lowest, the majority of upper cases are then also mostly spared of glyphic details generally maintaining a sans identity. The Utile collection is reminiscent of typefaces designed during the mid 20th century enunciating a certain elegance and fluidity. [ kontour.com ]

typefaces.name: V1olet
typefaces.desc: V1OLET is a display, single-case typeface that came out from experimenting with some effects on Illustrator. It was originally created in 2020 for a poster series called “Flowers” in which the letters were mirroring the petals of a water lily. [ carmen-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Vadelma
typefaces.desc: Vadelma is a script type family of four fonts. It is inspired by brush lettering and has soft and friendly looks. Vadelma can be used for branding, packaging and where ever you need a legible and smooth script font. Vadelma has lots of ligatures, swashes and alternative characters that will make your design unique and beautiful. You can also buy Vadelma as Variable Font and adjust the weight of Vadelma smoothly between Light and Bold weights. Notice that you need design software that supports Variable Fonts.

typefaces.name: Valve
typefaces.desc: Valve is a versatile typeface collection that blends grotesque, geometric, gestural, industrial, monospaced, and cursive sans serif styles into a unified, cohesive ensemble. Defying conventional classifications, Valve provides a wide range of typesetting options through its two distinct families: an ink-trapped workhorse designed for excellent readability at small sizes, and a striking stencil companion that reveals the font’s modular structure and underlying design connections. Valve features three main stylistic sets—a blocky semi-monospaced variant, a familiar humanist style, and a lively cursive option—each showcasing unique contextual ligatures that adapt to tracking for smooth text flow in any combination. With its adaptability and dynamic nature, Valve allows you to control and fine-tune the expressive qualities of your text, making it ideal for a variety of projects, from bold branding and impactful signage to refined editorial design. [ pangrampangram.com ]

typefaces.name: Vanilla Sans
typefaces.desc: Inspired by geometric forms, this type family is crafted for modern designers. Its clean design excels in various applications, offering high legibility and and an understated sophistication. With additional arrows, symbols, and circled numerals, Vanilla Sans simplifies creating hierarchies and enhancing UX design. The typeface includes several alternates for characters like a, g, l, G, and J, allowing for quick mood changes. As a bonus, Vanilla Sans features 26 unique patterns, assigned to uppercase letters (A–Z via Stylistic Set 7), sparking creative possibilities. [ blast-foundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Vanity
typefaces.desc: Vanity is an octic unicase typeface that captures the printed effect of letterforms on New Jersey license plates from the 1930s to the 1990s. The two-width family draws inspiration from the visual remnants of how embossed and painted plates were produced. Engineer-constructed letterforms and rounded corners form the foundation of the typeface. By embracing material ‘flaws’ in individual characters — such as paint bleeding over the edges of specific letters — the family finds rhythm in its irregularity.

typefaces.name: Varming
typefaces.desc: A custom font family originally designed for Steensen Varming (in 2013), an international building services consultancy with unrivalled expertise in mechanical and electrical engineering, lighting, and sustainable design. Varming is a geometric design with delicately chamfered corners; this feature is distinctive at a large scale yet appears soft and rounded at smaller sizes.

typefaces.name: VCTR Mono
typefaces.desc: This monospaced type design is warm, slightly goofy, and tactile. Inspired by text found on the lenses and bodies of manual cameras, specifically Leicas and Nikons. Originally named ISO and designed for our project exif.co . [ vectrotype.com ]

typefaces.name: Venice Blvd
typefaces.desc: Venice Blvd font is an amusing and unpretentious display sans-serif family with 4 weights and 8 styles. From the whimsical Regular weight all the way to the deep-fried-cronut that is the Black weight, there’s variety to suit most occasions (likely not funerals). 22+ Illustrative symbols also included to spice things up. [ hoodzpahdesign.com ]

typefaces.name: VentiQuattro
typefaces.desc: VentiQuattro is an elegant, distinct and expressive serif featuring all the bells and whistles we’ve come to expect from contemporary typefaces. The pronounced contrast, pointy terminals and sharp serifs is a subtle nod to the Italian classics. Referencing, but never replicating. [ playtype.com ] Originally released in 2009 [ fontsinuse.com ], reissued in November 2024 as a larger family.

typefaces.name: Verbo
typefaces.desc: Verbo presents a refreshing fusion of pure geometry and subtle warmth, reinterpreting the disciplined precision of Bauhaus typefaces through a humanist lens. With its slightly angled terminals and Art Deco-inspired architectural elements, Verbo balances modernity and timeless elegance. This versatile type family is tailor-made for corporate design, signage, and packaging, delivering both sophistication and readability. To fully harness the potential of the Verbo family, we created the bold and expressive Verbo XL. This striking display typeface features an exceptionally large x-height, ensuring maximum visual impact. Verbo XL introduces several alternate characters, drawing inspiration from a rich tapestry of historical styles, including blackletter, uncial, and geometric forms. This seamless blending of diverse influences results in a typeface that feels innovative and familiar, perfect for projects that demand attention and artistic flair. [ dstype.com ] Sample image and links refer to the Verbo sub-family.

typefaces.name: Verdana Pro
typefaces.desc: Matthew Carter originally designed Verdana for Microsoft specifically for the screen. Its clarity and versatility — and hinting from Tom Rickner — have withstood the medium’s limitations. More than 20 years later, now Verdana Pro, it is still among the most legible, usable fonts on the Web. David Berlow has since expanded the family with help from David Jonathan Ross, adding three new weights, a Condensed width of five weights, and small caps in Roman and Italic, totaling 20 styles. Verdana Pro includes a character set that supports all languages using Latin, Cyrillic, and Greek alphabets. This makes Carter & Cone’s Verdana Pro an intriguingly adaptable, modern sans fit for print and mobile use. [ carterandcone.com ]

typefaces.name: Vieno
typefaces.desc: The goal in designing Vieno was to modernise classically elegant shapes so that the the end result would be an up to date typeface combining old and new design elements. The typeface has its roots solidly in tradition but with a bold and modern execution. Vieno plays with the juxtaposition of classical proportions and contrast, organic shapes and rough mechanical details. The design combines elements that feel conventional and clear those that are surprising and slightly out of place. Great care was given in making these contrasting elements work together in a harmonised whole. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Virna
typefaces.desc: Originally commissioned for the MTV Italy identity. Featuring interline ligatures.

typefaces.name: Voyage
typefaces.desc: In 2024, we have added 3 new weights to the family: light, medium and black. We have also refined certain minor details on all the weights in order to perfect stylistic consistency. Voyage is a romantic and curvy display typeface, useful for headlines, or short to medium lengths texts. From the adventurous eye of the lowercase ‘e’ to the curly ‘h’, Voyage features delicate hairlines for maximum contrasts. We designed 55 stylistic ligatures, 26 variants, which are open-type programmed, the user decides which glyph to alternate. Bon Voyage. [ vj-type.com ]

typefaces.name: VZWO Choreo
typefaces.desc: Sample image shows VZWO Choreo Display Thin .

typefaces.name: Waverse
typefaces.desc: Graduated from Future Fonts in 2024.

typefaces.name: Wayle
typefaces.desc: Meet Wayle, a sans-serif takes inspiration from classic lineal fonts, but with a little more flare. A direct and detailed letterorms, gliding gracefully. With its large capitals, low x-height, and distinctive, slightly bulging characters like the "a" and "s", its flat endings, Wayle procures an optimal flow. And of course, it incorporates all the contemporary OpenType features, making it flexible. Ideal for all types of text, Wayle makes your text stand out without overdoing it. It's all about readability, with just the right amount of whale-sized charm. [ typefaces.pizza ]

typefaces.name: Weird Serif
typefaces.desc: Weird Serif is a freaky take on the fancy Didone typefaces commonly used in the fashion industry. The solemnity of that genre is jazzed up with weird hanging down serifs (see V, W, K and so on). The typeface also features a dramatic contrast and extra large x-height. Despite the name, the usability and legibility are not disrupted with too much wackiness. Weird Serif was initially designed on day 23 of 36 Days of Type, my challenge of making a whole font every day. [ futurefonts.com ]

typefaces.name: Werkdruck
typefaces.desc: Its rooting in rational designs means Werkdruck is decidedly drawn, not written. This typeface has the regular appearance of a Didone typeface, with vertical stress and symmetrical construction, but it comes with much less sparkling stroke contrast and bracketed serifs, true to the 19th-century saying: “Less spice, more meat.” The appearance of Werkdruck isn’t mechanic, though, with details like the organic drop terminals deviating visibly from the ruler-and-compass ideal of more stylized designs and infusing the modest character of this typeface with life. Werkdruck reminisces popular turn-of-the-century typefaces built upon the Scotch Modern genre that were cast into economic proportions to accommodate print shop requirements of the time. Unlike those predecessors, though, Werkdruck opts for more generous shapes with contemporary digital needs in mind, making each character exude confidence in modern branding while remaining legible in small sizes on high-resolution displays. [ identity-letters.com ] First preliminary version released in 2021, finalized in January 2025.

typefaces.name: Werksatz
typefaces.desc: Inspired by early grotesque typefaces such as Akzidenz Grotesk and Venus, Werksatz is our contemporary interpretation of this beloved genre. [ identity-letters.com ] First preliminary version released in December 2020, finalized in April 2021.

typefaces.name: WHOA
typefaces.desc: WHOA is an experimental variable font, named after the sound commonly heard after dragging the slider for the first time. Use four sliders to expand the outlines into a three dimensional hyperspace. It also comes with a filled ‘top’ style, that can be layered on top to help with readability. [ vectrotype.com ]

typefaces.name: Wildberry
typefaces.desc: Wildberry is based on the brushy lettering found on U.S. National Wilderness signage. Keeping the energy and playfulness of the source material, we worked out many of the awkward and inconsistent moments of the design. The joins have been opened up a little bit, to even out the color, and a more consistent, slightly reversed contrast system is also used in Wildberry. [ vectrotype.com ] Released on Future Fonts in 2018, from which it graduated in 2022.

typefaces.name: Williamson Italic
typefaces.desc: Williamson Italic is a distinctive display typeface originally crafted for a series of Franz Kafka book covers that never happened. Created by Paul Barnes, it draws inspiration from his own lettering, blending influences from Eastern European design, Berthold Wolpe’s lesser-known Hyperion , and the stone-carving traditions of western Scotland. Its condensed form, with a subtle six-degree angle, features robust slab serifs and a dynamic tension between rounded curves and sharp joints. Designed in a single weight, Williamson Italic is ideal for book covers, menus, and logos, offering a striking and versatile aesthetic. [ vault.commercialtype.com ]

typefaces.name: Wimaria Gotisch
typefaces.desc: This typeface was digitized from an original letterpress font of “Element” originally published in the 1930s by the Bauer type foundry. [ fdi-type.de ] Offered in January 2025 to supporters of the non-profit organization running the printing museum Pavillon-Presse and to supporters of the Schriftkontor community websites Typography.Guru and Typografie.info . Not available for general licensing.

typefaces.name: Wince
typefaces.desc: A pixelated reverse-contrast sans serif.

typefaces.name: Winco
typefaces.desc: While conceiving Winco, Ramiro Espinoza studied the work of the masters of postwar book cover design: Helmut Salden, Boudewijn Ietswaart, Berthold Wolpe; among others. He also looked into German and Czech traditions of expressive printing types that had such a strong presence in the earliest decades of the 20th century. Having established a stylistic framework, Espinoza designed the typeface from scratch. The process has resulted in a typeface that successfully combines the high legibility and seriousness of a text face with the expressiveness, dynamism and subtle irreverence of the original hand-rendered alphabets. [ re-type.com ]

typefaces.name: Work Sans
typefaces.desc: Released as open source on GitHub.

typefaces.name: Workhorse Saboneta
typefaces.desc: Some of the most gorgeous type on earth is calligraphic blackletter, hand-drawn by devout masters in the age of mystical folklore. Saboneta aims at a new renaissance of blacklettering that combines classicism with technology for an innovative approach to blackletters. A full range of weights brings out a spectrum of character and utility rarely found in blackletter typefaces. The elaborate and excessive illuminated letters found in historical manuscripts are re-envisioned with 3 capital styles & small caps. [ workhorse.studio ]

typefaces.name: Worm
typefaces.desc: MuirMcNeil Worm is a modular type system designed in seven compatible weights. Each Worm glyph has been shaped individually rather than being predetermined as the product of an overarching design code. The result is a type family that is co-ordinated as a loose association of idiosyncratic characters rather than a strictly regimented alphabet. However, the Worm letterforms are balanced harmoniously as a system by means of a consistent geometric framework that determines the construction of every contour, space and alignment. All seven Worm weights are designed to interact with one another in calibrated layers so that outlines can be mapped onto each other to generate a range of visual options when applied in print and interactive media or motion graphics. [ muirmcneil.com ]

typefaces.name: Worm Variable
typefaces.desc: Worm Variable is a development of MuirMcNeil’s Worm type system. Designed for Variable Font technology, its weights extend on a sliding scale from Thin to Fat with eight intermediate weight presets. Worm Variable’s contours precisely match the letterforms of Worm, each of which have been shaped individually rather than being predetermined as the product of an overarching design code. The result is a type family that is co-ordinated as a loose association of idiosyncratic characters rather than a strictly regimented alphabet. However, the Worm letterforms are balanced harmoniously as a system by means of a consistent geometric framework that determines the construction of every contour, space and alignment. [ muirmcneil.com ]

typefaces.name: Wormhole
typefaces.desc: MuirMcNeil Wormhole is a modular type system designed in seven styles. All seven Wormhole typefaces are designed to be combined, interacting in multiple layers with each other and with all of the weights of the MuirMcNeil Worm type system. Contours across the range are fully compatible so they can be mapped onto each other by the user working with page layout or vector drawing software. A huge range of visual options can be easily generated and applied in print, interactive or motion graphics environments.

typefaces.name: Wraith Mono
typefaces.desc: Wraith Mono is an all-caps, monospaced font that is simple in form and function. Chunky yet soft, it works for both large, strong headings as well as smaller tabular uses. [ doubledagger.xyz ]

typefaces.name: WT Skrappa
typefaces.desc: Updated in 2024.

typefaces.name: Wulkan
typefaces.desc: The origins of Wulkan date back to a decade ago when designer Jan Estrada-Osmycki was searching for an expressive serif typeface for use in a personal project. Unable to satisfy his specific needs, Jan decided to create his own, taking inspiration from the likes of Caslon Graphique, ITC Grouch and the lettering work of Tom Carnase and Herb Lubalin to name a few. The result was a highly expressive display typeface with a strong personality built upon spiky serif details, ball terminals and calligraphic like flow. [ thedesignersfoundry.com ] An update to Wulkan Display (2019): The end result in addition to redesigning the Display family includes the new Text and Headline families, variable font support, a new Black weight, optimisation of the design for longer texts and new OpenType features like small caps and swashes. [ thedesignersfoundry.com ]

typefaces.name: Xanti Typewriter
typefaces.desc: Xanti Typewriter is a monospaced type family. Its strong and geometric construction is based on the logo designed in the mid-1930s for Olivetti by Xanti Schawinsky, a Bauhaus disciple and a pioneer of what later became the Swiss Style. Beyond the influence of Bauhaus typography, what makes Xanti Typewriter interesting is that, by increasing the weight of the letters almost all glyphs lose their serifs. This design decision allowed Xanti Typewriter to become a type family with eight weights from Hairline to ExtraBold and matching italics, and to cover many applications, from packaging to editorial design and coding. Lastly, Xanti Typewriter is fully equipped with lining and old style numerals, slashed zero, and alternates. [ c-a-s-t.com ]

typefaces.name: Yet Grotesk
typefaces.desc: Yet Grotesk is a multitool sans serif typeface designed with functionality in mind. It seeks balance, stays humble, and aims to straightforwardly convey its intended message. Inspired by great typefaces like Akzidenz Grotesk, Record Gothic, and Gerstner Program, it also takes features from more mainstream forms like Arial, embracing accessibility and everyday appeal. The shapes feel familiar yet distinctive in some details. Capitals are drawn wide to provide for strong titles or all-caps composition. The spacing leans to the tight end which allows for dark and robust text blocks. [ formagari.com ]

typefaces.name: Yolker
typefaces.desc: Yolker began in 2021 as a part of my 52 Fonts Project. It has become one of my favorites and is lovingly referred to as "egg font." This typeface is designed to look like eggs just dropped into a pan. Each letter is meant to feel like it approximates the same volume as the average egg. Yolker forgos the usual straight lines, counters, and sharp corners which causes it to playfully skirt the limits of legibility. [ typedunord.com ]

typefaces.name: Yorick
typefaces.desc: Yorick is based on a monospace typewriter font (model 3402U) found in the Campionario caratteri e fregi tipografici (specimen book) of the Nebiolo typefoundry, dated 1920 – but the font might probably be older. The source is a slab serif form very common in typewriter fonts (Pica, according to Olivetti naming system) with a little touch of classical flavour from the Imperial style (i.e. with thick and thin contrasts). Start in 2016, Yorick keeps the essence of the original design, and avoid to make it look too digital or constructed. It’s a gentle industrial font: a font of engineers in Oxford shirt and tweed suits, not in white blouse. A precision tool with eleganza torinese, not showing off. Its italic is a proper one, not a slanted roman. It comes in a simple family of 4 styles, but with a large character set which includes bot Latin and Cyrillic scripts — each completed by localised alternates for Romanian, Moldovan, Serbian, Macedonian and Bulgarian. [ 205.tf ]

typefaces.name: ZC Casual
typefaces.desc: The single stroke style, also known as "speed stroke", has been used by sign painters for more than 60 years. Based on real painted letters by Caetano Calomino, ZC Casual offers a modern twist to this classic with soft entries and crisp exit strokes, capturing the authentic feel of hand-lettered signage. Including Swash Capitals & sparkles to uplift most show card aficionados. [ flaviazim.com ]

typefaces.name: Zed
typefaces.desc: Designing Type for Accessibility with Peter Biľak, Héctor Mangas Afonso, and Benjamin Ribeau .

typefaces.name: Zeist
typefaces.desc: Luzi Types quintessential geometric sans serif typeface, Zeist embodies the principles of early 20th-century modernism while incorporating dynamic, customisable features. It nods to Futura with a less rigid approach, honours Neuzeit Grotesk with a more cohesive form language, and salutes Avenir with a more constructed aesthetic. Characterised by clean lines, uniform stroke weight, and consistent letter shapes, Zeist reflects a minimalist aesthetic that feels meticulously crafted. Its logical construction gives the impression that every element is purposefully designed, creating an almost calculated appearance. The typeface introduces innovative features across four dynamic axes: the Terminal Axis, which adjusts letter terminals from Angular to Horizontal styles; the x‑Height Axis, modifying the x‑height from Low to Tall, particularly beneficial for small font sizes; the Weight Axis, ranging from Hairline to Black; and the Italic Axis, enabling a slant from 1 to 12 degrees. [ luzi-type.ch ]

typefaces.name: Zetal
typefaces.desc: Zetal is a Geometric Grotesk inspired by the industrial modernism of signage on water tanks and cargo containers, blending the strong typographic heritage of the Enschede foundry with mid-20th-century American influences. These latter influences, characterized by direct clarity and expressive strength, evoke the aesthetics of large urban and industrial structures, seamlessly integrating with European geometric precision. The forms of Zetal are built on a rigorous grid that emphasizes geometric harmony, with expanded horizontal proportions that give the typeface a solid, mechanical presence. The proportions are carefully crafted to convey balance and precision: the width of the letters ensures solidity without compromising legibility. The metric consistency between vertical and horizontal elements creates a regular, uniform rhythm, underscored by a structure that prioritizes geometric clarity. The robustness of the forms remains constant, providing the text with a technical, functional imprint. Every detail contributes to the overall perception of order and rationality, reflecting the essential and precise nature of Zetal. [ aieou.tools ]

typefaces.name: Zetkin
typefaces.desc: Determined diagonals, a strong slant and extended proportions make for a confident display typeface. Some of the most characteristic design features – like the high-waisted uppercase letters and flaring stroke endings – are a nod towards Venus, a typeface family released in 1907 by Bauersche Gießerei. With a wide range in weights and the wide display styles, Zetkin is useful for all kinds of text sizes and usages. [ futurefonts.com ] A sans serif typeface informed by Venus , started as a custom typeface with Dan Reynolds.

typefaces.name: Ziggy
typefaces.desc: Ziggy is a strong display typeface inspired by hand-painted letterings found on boat hulls. Odd details and awkwardness features have been preserved to give its letters their distinctive identity. [ ma-ma-type.com ] Originally designed in 2013 and made available when the foundry launched.

typefaces.name: Zingiber
typefaces.desc: Zingiber, an elegant yet relaxed script typeface, showcases the skilled touch of a handcrafted design. Its serifs ensure excellent readability, making it perfect for headlines and short texts in a variety of contexts—children’s books, historical publications, or even cookbooks. [ typofonderie.com ]

typefaces.name: zk Kamenyar
typefaces.desc: Kamenyar is a serif typeface but not the regular one. Its strong serifs and a little shaky stems make it playful and brisk. Polite and regular from afar but when your look closely it reveals its rebel mood. [ zakznak.com ]

typefaces.name: zk Trembita
typefaces.desc: Trembita — is a display typeface that has no curves. A bit clumsy and restless but remains warm and friendly. Inspired by carved words on trees in the carpathian woods. Typeface is named after “trembita” — an alpine horn which is common among Ukrainian highlanders Hutsuls who live in western Ukraine. [ zakznak.com ]

typefaces.name: Zug ETC
typefaces.desc: Zug is inspired by Alex Stocker's lettering drawings which appeared on: Lettera 1, published by Arthur Niggli (1954). This typeface merges soft outline curves and straight angled counterforms, alternating with the use of incredibly angular sharp diagonals. It was renamed after the city of Zug in Switzerland, where the former artist and designer lived and worked his whole life. The project expanded into a range of weights from Thin to Extra Bold. A custom version of Zug Light has been used for the logo of MATEK Technical Performance Intimates and the brand uses the font family for its visual identity. [ abc-etc.com ]

foundries.name: ABC ETC
foundries.desc: Established by Nazareno Crea . The foundry’s typeface catalog was launched at the end of 2022.

foundries.name: Aesthetic Type
foundries.desc: Aesthetic Type™ was founded in 2014 by multi-disciplinary creative Michael Jarboe alongside his partner Robin Jarboe. It is based in the same California locale that has originated numerous cultural institutions that have had an undeniable influence around the world. For the first time in 2019 the studio is public facing with the first of many select type releases now commercially available. [ aesthetictype.com ]

foundries.name: AllCaps
foundries.desc: Founded by Ondřej Báchor and Jan Novák .

foundries.name: APK Type
foundries.desc: APK Type is the independent type foundry founded by Dutch design studio Autograph Peter Korsman. We design and offer distinctive typefaces and font families (retail and custom) for use in print and the digital realm. [ apk-type.com ]

foundries.name: Arcane Type Foundry
foundries.desc: Established by Alanna Munro as Alanna Munro Type Foundry, renamed Arcane Type Foundry in 2025.

foundries.name: Babelfont
foundries.desc: Established in 2015 by Brahim Boucheikha and Gia Tran . Mostly focused on custom typefaces, the studio released its first collection of retail typefaces in 2025.

foundries.name: Badson Type Foundry
foundries.desc: The foundry arm of Badson Studio , officially launched in 2024 [ proofco.xyz ]. Founded by Kyle Read .

foundries.name: Beam Type
foundries.desc: Established by Cecilia Del Castillo and Felix Bamforth .

foundries.name: Bfgs.Studio
foundries.desc: Initially known as Brass Fonts, renamed Bfgs.Studio in 2025.

foundries.name: Big Fog Foundry
foundries.desc: Big Fog is a design studio founded by Valerie Burgess and Brian Dove in 2021. In April 2025 the studio spun up Big Fog Foundry as a semi-separate home for Brian’s growing retail font catalog , which had been previously released through the studio.

foundries.name: Black Foundry
foundries.desc: Black Foundry, styled Black[Foundry], was established by Grégori Vincens and Jérémie Hornus . In 2025, the catalogue was sold to The Type Founders, where it remains as an imprint as the original company winds down.

foundries.name: Boulevard LAB
foundries.desc: Early access typefaces available at Boulevard Beta LAB .

foundries.name: Brutal Types
foundries.desc: Established in 2025 by Paula Mastrangelo and Ramiro Espinoza of Retype to develop a catalog that centers on avant-garde alphabets created by architects, artisans, and designers during the interwar period of the 20th century .

foundries.name: Commercial Type
foundries.location: New York, United States; London, United Kingdom

foundries.name: Compañía Tipográfica de Chile
foundries.desc: Alexis Navarro , Gastón Uribe and Raúl Israel .

foundries.name: Contrast Foundry
foundries.location: Sunnyvale, California, United States; Moscow, Russia

foundries.name: Dogray
foundries.desc: Established by Sahar Afshar and José Solé .

foundries.name: Double B Type
foundries.desc: The type foundry arm of Brand Brothers , a studio founded by Johan Debit and Jean-Rémi Massery in 2010.

foundries.name: Double Zero
foundries.desc: Double Zero (styled D0uble Zer0) was founded in 2022 by Malou Verlomme. The entire catalogue is free to use for non-commercial projects.

foundries.name: DualType
foundries.desc: Founded by Zrinka Buljubašić and Gen Ramírez .

foundries.name: Edition.studio
foundries.desc: The collaborative practice of Victoire Coyon and Adrien Menard .

foundries.name: Element Type
foundries.desc: Founded by Doğukan Karapınar and İbrahim Kaçtıoğlu . Our name, Element, represents our approach to type design. It emerged from the idea of having our laboratory where we built tools and methods to experiment that could lead us to something exciting. We see our practice as a blend of science and art; instead of mass-producing, we aim to innovate, transform, and evolve our craft continuously.

foundries.name: En Travaux
foundries.desc: En Travaux is a french foundry by Julien Simon, Dorian Delavault, Audrey Aujoulat, Yann Valiani & friends. We aim to offer free fonts and experimental type works from and to a wide range of graphic and type designers. [ entravaux.framer.website ]

foundries.name: Extraset
foundries.desc: Extraset is an independent Swiss type foundry established in Geneva jointly led by Alex Dujet (Futur Neue), Xavier Erni (Neo Neo), Roger Gaillard (Cécile + Roger) and David Mamie (TM Todeschini + Mamie). Extraset publishes professional typefaces made by graphic designers for graphic designers.

foundries.name: Extratype
foundries.desc: Founded by Íñigo Jerez as Textaxis, later renamed Extratype.

foundries.name: Électro-bibliothèque
foundries.desc: Électro-bibliothèque was founded by Clément Le Tulle-Neyret & Thomas Leblond in 2021. Électro-bibliothèque publishes books and typefaces.

foundries.name: FaceType
foundries.desc: Founded by Marcus Sterz and Georg Herold-Wildfeller .

foundries.name: Fond de riz
foundries.desc: A foundry that distributes open-source typefaces by Justine Gagnaire, Marie Deloffre and Cédric Rossignol-Brunet.

foundries.name: Font Club Belgica
foundries.desc: Founded by Frederik Berlaen and Dries Wiewauters in 2024 [ fontclubbelgica.com ], officially launched in May 2025 .

foundries.name: Frere–Jones Type
foundries.desc: At the end of 2024, thirteen typefaces originally released with Font Bureau were added to the foundry’s retail library.

foundries.name: Fuerte Type

foundries.name: General Type Studio
foundries.desc: A type foundry founded by Stéphane Elbaz.

foundries.name: Gruppo Due
foundries.location: Berlin, Germany; Karlsruhe, Germany; Bern, Switzerland; London, United Kingdom

foundries.name: Hamilton Wood Type Collection
foundries.desc: See also: Hamilton Wood Type Legacy Project .

foundries.name: Heheh Type
foundries.desc: Founded by Nour El Shamy , Shahd El Sabbagh , and Manuel von Gebhardi .

foundries.name: Hoodzpah
foundries.desc: Founded by Amy Hood and Jen Hood .

foundries.name: Hypersand
foundries.desc: Formerly known as Range Left , renamed Hypersand in 2025.

foundries.name: Ivy Foundry
foundries.desc: Established by Jan Maack . The Ivy Foundry is a type design studio that makes fonts that fit the purpose of every designer’s unique needs. As a graphic designer, Jan Maack created these typefaces out of response to his own situational knowledge. Every family is for designers by a designer. All of the families are versatile and not easily pigeon-holed. [ ivyfoundry.com ]

foundries.name: Kyiv Type Foundry
foundries.location: Kyiv, Ukraine; Bar, Montenegro; Hanover, Germany; Barcelona, Spain
foundries.desc: Founded by Yevgeniy Anfalov and Oleś Gergun .

foundries.name: Laucke Siebein Type
foundries.location: Amsterdam, Netherlands; Offenbach am Main, Germany; Berlin, Germany
foundries.desc: Established by Dirk Laucke and Johanna Siebein (co-founders of Studio Laucke Siebein) together with Clemens Buchegger.

foundries.name: London Type Foundry
foundries.desc: Founded by Paul Harpin , Paul Hickson , and Joe Graham.

foundries.name: MA-MA Type
foundries.desc: Established by Maxime Fittes . Further reading: MA-MA Type, A Craftsman’s Approach to Type Design .

foundries.name: Manufacturas Tipográficas Madrileñas
foundries.desc: Established by Juanjo López . In 2025, typefaces released by the founder under Huy!Fonts were folded into the MTM catalog, which had been formerly dedicated to the Madriles collection.

foundries.name: Milletype Foundry
foundries.desc: Established by Corentin Echivard and Romain Marc .

foundries.name: Mint Type
foundries.desc: Founded by Andriy Konstantynov in 2004, becoming the first Ukrainian type foundry to present itself on the international digital type market. [ minttype.com ). Joined by Oleh Lishchuk in 2016.

foundries.name: Monkey Type
foundries.location: New York, United States; Chamonix, France

foundries.name: Moontype
foundries.desc: Co-founded by Pia Schröer and Julia Flomm .

foundries.name: Mota Italic
foundries.location: Berlin, Germany; Moline, Illinois, United States

foundries.name: MuirMcNeil

Off Type offers everyone free access to top-quality fonts for personal use, with commercial licenses available for purchase. This allows those who use typefaces the most (designers) to play and work with the free fonts in their entirety and when they are used in a commercial project, the client or employer (or you) can purchase the required license. foundries.name: Outline Online
foundries.desc: Co-founded by Samira Schneuwly and Laura Csocsán and launched in 2025. Outline Online is a collaborative practice that manifests itself as a constantly evolving platform for publishing ideas. This project encapsulates our collective vision of rendering typefaces accessible in the digital space to the public. Constantly shifting shape between shared screenshots and printouts, our files find a permanent place in the folders of this website. Founded by Samira Schneuwly and Laura Csocsán in 2023 and launched in 2025, Outline Online fuses a contemporary understanding of graphic design as a foundation to recontextualise the visual language of type design. Working from multiple locations in Switzerland, we are operating digitally, aiming to contribute to the current scene of the discipline. [ outline-online.com ]

foundries.name: Superness
foundries.desc: Established by Alessio D’Ellena . First appearance of the label is in 2016 as side project by Alessio D’Ellena. Established as unstable practice reflecting an idiosyncratic expression of typographic culture. Typefaces and writing systems are the focus of a line of research devoted to pushing the boundaries of tradition. Superness is an exercise in analogy. A typeface is at one time text, mathematics, writing system, software and could be even more than that. Research and self-reflective thinking on writing media —and its (re)production— are foundational themes in the Superness’ investigation around the role of design in relation to society. That means looking through the functions of a type system, how it operates in both technical and relational environment. [ superness.info ]

foundries.desc: Tunera is a transnational type foundry, that aims to present new and original typefaces for everyone. Tunera Type Foundry got its name from the Indian fig cactus, called “tunera” in Spanish, because it offers sharp font picks, rich curves and lots of flavor. Founded in January 2020 by Ariel Martín Pérez , joined by Anton Moglia soon after. The foundry distributes open-source typefaces, all the while facilitating donations to the typeface designers.

Born out of the design studio "Violaine & Jérémy" founded by creative partners Orsoni and Schneider, VJ-Type is an extension of their artistic and sensitive territory. The foundry's work is essentially guided by their irrepressible inclination for an expressive, elegant and impeccably balanced aesthetic. [ vj-type.com ]

tags.name: Chromatic Type
tags.desc: Typefaces that can produce multi-color effects using color font technology, or by layering separate styles or variable font instances.

tags.name: Coding fonts
tags.desc: Monospaced typefaces for writing and reading source code.

tags.name: Design process
tags.desc: The story behind the typeface. This tag currently lists all typefaces that have a design info URL attached to them. When the list grows unmanageably long, the entries will be curated.

tags.name: Dot matrix
tags.desc: Typefaces constructed from circles or dots aligned to an uniform grid. For dots arranged along the letter outlines, see Dotted .

tags.name: Dotted
tags.desc: Typefaces constructed from circles or dots arranged along the letter outlines. For dots aligned to an uniform grid, see Dot matrix .

tags.name: Early access
tags.desc: In-progress typefaces, offered early at a discounted price.

tags.name: Engraved calligraphy
tags.desc: Typefaces influenced by pointed-pen calligraphy, especially the English roundhand , known as “copperplate script” from the method of reproduction by way of engraved copper plates.

tags.name: Exotic axes
tags.desc: Variable fonts with interesting variation axes.

tags.name: Minisites
tags.desc: Typefaces with minisites. This tag currently lists all typefaces that have a Minisite URL attached to them. When the list grows unmanageably long, the entries will be curated.

tags.name: Patterns and ornaments
tags.desc: Tileable designs packaged as font files, either by themselves or as supplements to alphabets.

tags.name: Pedagogical
tags.desc: Typefaces used in education, often to teach young people how to read or write, or type inspired by educational materials. The tag also encompasses type that illustrates its own construction.

tags.name: Road signage
tags.desc: Typefaces influenced by the standardized type used for traffic signs, license plates, road markings, street signs. Archetypes include DIN 1451 , SNV , Caractères , Transport , Trafikkalfabetet , Tratex , Highway Gothic .

tags.name: Standardized lettering
tags.desc: Further reading:

tags.name: Stencil/Display
tags.desc: Stencil and modular typefaces based on abstracted shapes.

tags.name: Stencil/Sans
tags.desc: Stencil typefaces based on a sans serif model.

tags.name: Stencil/Script
tags.desc: Stencil typefaces based on a script model. By extension, unjoined scripts that create a similar impression.

tags.name: Stencil/Serif
tags.desc: Stencil typefaces based on a serif model.

tags.name: Stencil/Slab
tags.desc: Stencil typefaces based on a slab serif model.

tags.name: Tapes and tubes
tags.desc: Typefaces whose construction evokes ribbons, strips of adhesive tape, neon tubes, etc.

tags.name: Typewriter fonts
tags.desc: Typefaces inspired by fonts available to typewriters, modeled by the technical constraints imposed by the medium, or evoking the physical appearance of typewritten text.

tags.name: User interface
tags.desc: Typefaces designed with user interfaces in mind. While a variety of sans-serif fonts work well for UIs, this tag reflects the type designer’s declared intent towards this application.
